purpose: Academic quiz question bank for the Sharjah Expo app. Real delivered bank (question_bank_output/, generated per Abhi's spec) merged 2026-09-20: 65 major subjects across Indian/IB/British/American/SABIS/UAE MoE, 12 minor-curriculum PCMB sets, and a shared 300-question Aptitude pool used for occasional substitution (see js/questions.js maybeSubstituteAptitude). UAE MoE is a union of the uae_moe/ and uae_moe_current/ exports (600 records, each already covering both stream taxonomies) — see scripts/merge-question-bank.js. Every record has placeholder: false; reviewed_by is still null pending independent subject-teacher review, a separate decision for Abhi ahead of the live event. See data/QUESTION_BANK_SOURCES.md for the CC BY-adapted subset (Psychology, Political Science/Government). Regenerate via `node scripts/merge-question-bank.js`, edit nothing in this file by hand.
note_on_stream_ids: eligible_stream_ids values must match an 'id' inside data/curriculum_subjects.json's curricula[curriculum].streams[].id / .groups[].id / .combination_clusters[].id / .ap_categories[].id, or a synthetic 'track-N' id for .external_exam_tracks (see js/questions.js's getStreamOptions, the single canonical derivation both the registration stream-picker and this validator use). An empty array means the question applies to every stream/group/cluster within that curriculum. Curricula with no stream/group structure (SABIS, Aptitude, and the 'Other' bucket) should always use an empty array here.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: An owner pays for a personal holiday from the business bank account. How should this normally be treated in the sole trader's accounts?
options: As additional sales revenue
As a purchase of business inventory
As a reduction in the owner's personal spending outside the accounts
As drawings, not a business operating expense
questions.answer: As drawings, not a business operating expense
questions.explanation: The business entity concept separates the owner's private transactions from business expenses.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A sole trader puts personal cash into the business. What is the immediate accounting effect?
options: Business liabilities and drawings increase
Cash decreases while capital increases
Business cash and owner's capital increase
Sales revenue and operating profit increase
questions.answer: Business cash and owner's capital increase
questions.explanation: An owner's contribution increases the business's assets and equity without being trading income.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A business buys equipment on credit. What happens when the purchase is recorded?
options: Owner's drawings increase
An asset and a liability increase
An asset increases and a liability decreases
Cash increases and revenue increases
questions.answer: An asset and a liability increase
questions.explanation: The equipment is acquired while payment remains owed to the supplier.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A business buys equipment using cash. Ignoring other effects, what happens to total assets at purchase?
options: One asset replaces another, so the total is unchanged
Total assets necessarily double
Total assets fall by twice the price
The purchase immediately creates sales revenue
questions.answer: One asset replaces another, so the total is unchanged
questions.explanation: Cash decreases and equipment increases by the same transaction amount.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Services are completed this month, but the customer will pay next month. Under accrual accounting, what is recorded now?
options: Cash received and no revenue
A liability to the customer for the whole fee
An owner's capital contribution
Revenue and a receivable
questions.answer: Revenue and a receivable
questions.explanation: Revenue is recognised when earned, with a receivable representing the amount still due.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A business pays rent covering part of the next accounting period. How is the unused portion treated at the reporting date?
options: As sales revenue
As a payable already settled twice
As a prepayment asset
As an expense belonging entirely to the current period
questions.answer: As a prepayment asset
questions.explanation: The payment relates to a future benefit, so that portion is carried forward rather than charged to the current period.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Electricity has been used by year-end, but the bill has not yet been paid. What adjustment is needed?
options: Reduce the expense because payment is late
Recognise the expense and a liability
Ignore the cost until cash is paid
Recognise an asset and sales revenue
questions.answer: Recognise the expense and a liability
questions.explanation: Accrual accounting includes costs incurred in the period even when payment follows later.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A machine is purchased to be used for several years. Why is its full cost not normally charged as a one-day operating expense?
options: Its benefits extend over several accounting periods
Every cash payment must be recorded as revenue
Machines never lose service potential
Only inventory can be an asset
questions.answer: Its benefits extend over several accounting periods
questions.explanation: The machine is recognised as an asset and its depreciable cost is allocated over its useful life.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Equipment helps earn revenue over several years. What does depreciation allocate?
options: Cash into a separate replacement fund automatically
Its current selling price each day
Its owner's personal income
Its depreciable cost over those periods
questions.answer: Its depreciable cost over those periods
questions.explanation: Depreciation allocates cost; it is not itself a cash saving mechanism or a market valuation process.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Goods bought for resale remain unsold at year-end. Why are they not all included in the current cost of goods sold?
options: All purchases must be drawings
Inventory cannot appear in a statement of financial position
They remain an asset until sold or otherwise expensed
Unsold goods are automatically revenue
questions.answer: They remain an asset until sold or otherwise expensed
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold relates to goods sold, while qualifying unsold inventory is carried forward.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A trial balance totals equally on both sides. What does this establish?
options: Every account is classified correctly
Total recorded debit balances equal total recorded credit balances
Every transaction has been recorded correctly
No transaction has been omitted
questions.answer: Total recorded debit balances equal total recorded credit balances
questions.explanation: Equality is an arithmetic check, but some errors affect both sides equally or omit both entries.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A bank statement shows a charge not yet entered in the cash book. What should the business record?
options: A bank expense and a reduction in the bank balance
An increase in sales and cash
A reduction in the supplier's invoice price
A new capital contribution
questions.answer: A bank expense and a reduction in the bank balance
questions.explanation: The charge reduces the business's bank funds and is recorded as the relevant expense.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A customer's debt is confirmed irrecoverable. What should happen to that receivable?
options: It is retained as fully recoverable indefinitely
It becomes additional sales revenue
It is transferred to cash without collection
It is written off and the loss recognised
questions.answer: It is written off and the loss recognised
questions.explanation: A receivable with no recoverable amount should no longer remain as an asset at its original value.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A partnership agreement specifies unequal profit shares. Should profit automatically be divided equally?
options: Yes; profit must match each partner's age
No; all profit belongs to the partner who collected cash
No; the agreed sharing arrangement should be applied
Yes; every partnership must divide every profit equally
questions.answer: No; the agreed sharing arrangement should be applied
questions.explanation: An agreed profit-sharing arrangement governs allocation in the stated situation.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A partnership charges a partner interest on drawings under its agreement. What is the purpose of the charge?
options: To classify drawings as sales
To account for the partner's use of business funds for personal withdrawal
To record interest paid to a bank
To increase cash automatically without settlement
questions.answer: To account for the partner's use of business funds for personal withdrawal
questions.explanation: The charge adjusts the allocation between the partnership and the withdrawing partner under the agreement.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A new partner joins an established profitable firm. Why might goodwill be considered?
options: The incoming partner may gain a share of an existing business advantage
Goodwill always equals the cash in the bank
Admission makes all existing assets worthless
Goodwill is the same as an unpaid supplier invoice
questions.answer: The incoming partner may gain a share of an existing business advantage
questions.explanation: Goodwill reflects benefits such as reputation and earning capacity that can affect the partners' agreed settlement.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A company raises funds by issuing ordinary shares. How does this differ from taking a conventional loan?
options: The company must record every share receipt as sales
Ordinary shareholders become trade payables
The transaction necessarily creates an operating loss
The funds represent ownership capital rather than a repayable loan principal
questions.answer: The funds represent ownership capital rather than a repayable loan principal
questions.explanation: Share capital is equity funding; borrowing creates a creditor relationship and repayment obligations.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A company owes interest on its issued debentures for the period. How is this generally treated?
options: As additional share capital
As a customer advance
As a finance cost
As an ordinary shareholder's dividend
questions.answer: As a finance cost
questions.explanation: Debenture interest is a cost of borrowing, distinct from a distribution of profit to owners.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A business has valuable buildings but little cash to meet bills due tomorrow. What issue does this illustrate?
options: Long-term assets are the same as cash on demand
Asset wealth does not guarantee immediate liquidity
Owning buildings guarantees that every bill can be paid immediately
Profit and cash are always identical
questions.answer: Asset wealth does not guarantee immediate liquidity
questions.explanation: The ability to meet near-term obligations depends on accessible cash and liquid resources, not only total asset value.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Depreciation reduces reported profit. Does recording the depreciation entry itself pay cash to anyone?
options: No; the entry is a noncash allocation
Yes; cash is paid to the depreciation account
Yes; the asset's supplier receives the amount again
No; therefore it can never affect profit
questions.answer: No; the entry is a noncash allocation
questions.explanation: The cash acquisition and the later allocation of cost are separate accounting events.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A credit sale is omitted completely from the books. Why can the trial balance still agree?
options: The customer automatically records the sale in the seller's books
Trial balances do not contain any revenue accounts
Omission changes only the debit total
Both the debit and credit entries are missing
questions.answer: Both the debit and credit entries are missing
questions.explanation: An equal two-sided omission leaves debit and credit totals equal while understating the relevant accounts.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A cheque issued and recorded by the business has not yet been presented to the bank. Why do the cash book and statement differ?
options: The cheque is automatically a bank error
The payment must be treated as sales revenue
The business has recorded a payment that the bank has not yet processed
The business must record the same expense a second time
questions.answer: The business has recorded a payment that the bank has not yet processed
questions.explanation: An unpresented cheque is a timing difference between the two records.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Closing inventory is overstated while other figures are correct. What happens to cost of goods sold and gross profit?
options: Both remain unchanged
Cost of goods sold is understated and gross profit overstated
Both are overstated
Cost of goods sold is overstated and gross profit understated
questions.answer: Cost of goods sold is understated and gross profit overstated
questions.explanation: Closing inventory is deducted in calculating cost of goods sold, so overstating it lowers that cost and raises profit.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A fixed depreciation rate is applied to a declining carrying amount. Why does the annual charge normally fall?
options: The rate is applied to a smaller base each year
The rate must increase each year
The asset's original cost rises each year
Cash received from customers determines the charge
questions.answer: The rate is applied to a smaller base each year
questions.explanation: Under reducing-balance depreciation, the percentage stays fixed while the carrying amount declines.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: An expense incurred this year is paid next year. What happens if the year-end accrual is omitted?
options: Current profit is understated and liabilities overstated
Only cash changes
Assets and liabilities both increase correctly
Current profit is overstated and liabilities understated
questions.answer: Current profit is overstated and liabilities understated
questions.explanation: Omitting the expense increases reported profit and omitting the payable reduces reported liabilities.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Last year's rent prepayment is used during the current period. What should happen to that portion?
options: It becomes current-period sales revenue
It remains an asset forever
The prepayment asset decreases and rent expense is recognised
The prepayment asset increases again without payment
questions.answer: The prepayment asset decreases and rent expense is recognised
questions.explanation: As the prepaid benefit is consumed, its cost moves from the asset to the relevant period's expense.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Evidence suggests that some receivables may not be collected, but the exact debts are not yet known. What is the purpose of an allowance?
options: To guarantee the remaining customers will pay
To reflect estimated credit losses in the carrying amount
To cancel every customer debt automatically
To record cash already collected
questions.answer: To reflect estimated credit losses in the carrying amount
questions.explanation: An allowance accounts for estimated noncollection without treating every balance as individually confirmed irrecoverable.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A business describes profit as a percentage of selling price. Why is this not the same as markup on cost?
options: The two percentages use different denominators
Gross profit has a different cash value under each name
Selling price and cost must be equal
Markup excludes the cost of goods sold entirely
questions.answer: The two percentages use different denominators
questions.explanation: Margin relates gross profit to revenue; markup relates it to cost.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: When starting from profit in an indirect operating cash-flow calculation, why is depreciation added back?
options: It is a new cash receipt from customers
It increases the original cost of inventory
It is always a financing cash inflow
It reduced profit without causing a current operating cash payment
questions.answer: It reduced profit without causing a current operating cash payment
questions.explanation: The adjustment reverses a noncash expense included in the profit starting figure.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Revenue is recognised, but trade receivables increase during the period. All else equal, how does this affect cash from customers relative to revenue?
options: Revenue must be zero
Every receivable increase is a cash inflow
Cash collection is lower than recognised revenue
Cash collection must exceed revenue
questions.answer: Cash collection is lower than recognised revenue
questions.explanation: An increase in unpaid customer balances means part of recognised revenue has not yet been collected.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A company receives a new bank loan. Why does this increase cash without increasing profit at receipt?
options: The bank has purchased the company's inventory
It creates a liability rather than earned revenue
All cash receipts are excluded from accounting
The money becomes a depreciation charge
questions.answer: It creates a liability rather than earned revenue
questions.explanation: Borrowed funds must be repaid and are financing, not income earned from operations.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A company distributes part of its accumulated profit as a dividend. How is this different from paying an operating expense?
options: It is a distribution to owners rather than a cost of earning the period's revenue
It increases sales revenue
It is always interest on a loan
It is the purchase of a new productive asset
questions.answer: It is a distribution to owners rather than a cost of earning the period's revenue
questions.explanation: Dividends distribute equity returns, while operating expenses contribute to determining profit.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Assets are revalued immediately before a new partner joins. Why are the resulting gains usually allocated to the old partners under the old ratio?
options: The new partner automatically owns all earlier gains
Revaluation gains must always be shared equally
The old ratio applies only to cash expenses
They relate to value accumulated before the new profit-sharing arrangement
questions.answer: They relate to value accumulated before the new profit-sharing arrangement
questions.explanation: Pre-admission gains belong to the partners who held the business under the previous arrangement, subject to the agreement.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: An existing partner's share of future profits falls when a new partner is admitted. What does the decrease identify?
options: The business's cash loss for the year
A reduction in every recorded asset
That partner's sacrificed profit share
The new partner's entire capital contribution
questions.answer: That partner's sacrificed profit share
questions.explanation: The sacrificing share measures the portion of future profit entitlement given up.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: When one partner retires, another's share of future profit increases. Why is that increase relevant to goodwill adjustment?
options: It determines the legal age of retirement
It measures the benefit gained from the retiring partner's share
It proves the firm received cash immediately
It equals the retiring partner's unpaid supplier debts
questions.answer: It measures the benefit gained from the retiring partner's share
questions.explanation: Gaining partners may compensate the retiring partner for the goodwill benefit attached to the acquired share.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A partner advances a separate loan to the firm. Why distinguish it from the partner's capital?
options: The loan has a creditor relationship distinct from the ownership balance
Every amount supplied by a partner must be sales revenue
The loan cannot earn interest under any agreement
The loan automatically changes all profit shares
questions.answer: The loan has a creditor relationship distinct from the ownership balance
questions.explanation: A partner can be both owner and lender, with different accounting treatment for the two balances.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Shares are issued for more than their nominal value. What does the excess represent?
options: A trade discount on inventory
A loss on issuing the shares
An automatic dividend payable
Share premium rather than sales revenue
questions.answer: Share premium rather than sales revenue
questions.explanation: The excess forms a separate equity component associated with the capital issue.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Two firms have different sizes. Why may comparing profit margins be more informative than comparing profit totals alone?
options: A higher margin guarantees a larger total profit
Absolute profit cannot be measured
Margins relate profit to the scale of revenue
Margins remove every difference in accounting policies
questions.answer: Margins relate profit to the scale of revenue
questions.explanation: Relative measures support comparisons across scale, while business models and accounting choices still matter.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A loan instalment is due soon while the rest is due several years later. Why may the liability be split in the statement of financial position?
options: A loan cannot have more than one payment date
The portions have different settlement time horizons
Every loan must be recorded wholly as revenue
Splitting changes the total amount owed
questions.answer: The portions have different settlement time horizons
questions.explanation: Classification helps users distinguish near-term obligations from longer-term financing.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A business's workforce has valuable experience that is not shown as a separate asset in its accounts. What does this illustrate?
options: Financial statements do not capture every source of business value
Experienced staff have no economic value
Every unrecorded benefit is automatically a bookkeeping error
The balance sheet must equal the business's possible selling price
questions.answer: Financial statements do not capture every source of business value
questions.explanation: Recognition and measurement rules limit which resources appear as separately recorded assets.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: One expense is understated by 100 and another overstated by 100. Why can overall profit appear correct while the accounts still need correction?
options: Correct total profit proves every expense classification is correct
The two errors remove the need for reliable records
Offsetting errors necessarily make cash balances correct
The errors offset in total but misstate the individual categories
questions.answer: The errors offset in total but misstate the individual categories
questions.explanation: A correct aggregate can conceal incorrect components that affect analysis and decisions.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A machine purchase is debited to repairs expense and credited correctly to cash. Why can the trial balance agree despite the error?
options: Capital expenditure cannot be paid in cash
The cash credit corrects the classification automatically
Equal entries were made, but the debit was classified incorrectly
Every expense debit prevents a trial balance from balancing
questions.answer: Equal entries were made, but the debit was classified incorrectly
questions.explanation: The arithmetic balance does not distinguish an expense from an asset account.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A bank correctly deducted a direct debit that the business had not recorded. Should it remain only a reconciliation timing item?
options: No; the bank must reverse every direct debit not previously entered
No; the business should update its cash book for the actual transaction
Yes; every statement-only item is permanently ignored in the cash book
Yes; recording it would necessarily duplicate an existing entry
questions.answer: No; the business should update its cash book for the actual transaction
questions.explanation: The business's records are incomplete when an actual bank transaction has not been entered.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A business has a current ratio above 1 and pays a current liability using cash. Ignoring other changes, what happens to that ratio?
options: It increases
It decreases to exactly 1
It stays unchanged in every case
It becomes negative
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Subtracting the same amount from current assets and current liabilities increases their ratio when assets initially exceed liabilities.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A firm's current ratio improves because slow-moving inventory rises while cash falls. Why is the improvement not enough to establish stronger liquidity?
options: Every inventory increase is immediately spendable cash
A higher current ratio guarantees timely payment of every bill
Asset composition cannot affect liquidity
The current assets may be less readily convertible into cash
questions.answer: The current assets may be less readily convertible into cash
questions.explanation: A ratio's quality depends on the nature and recoverability of its components, not only the total.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A higher depreciation charge reduces profit, but the asset was paid for last year. Ignoring tax effects, what direct current cash-flow change is caused by the charge alone?
options: Cash rises by the full charge
The supplier receives a second payment
None
Cash falls by the full charge
questions.answer: None
questions.explanation: Depreciation is a noncash allocation; changing the charge alone does not create a current payment.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Closing inventory is overstated this year and becomes next year's opening inventory. If next year's closing figure is correct, what is the next-year profit effect?
options: Next-year revenue automatically rises to offset it
Next-year profit is understated
Next-year profit is overstated again
The error cannot affect next year
questions.answer: Next-year profit is understated
questions.explanation: Overstated opening inventory raises next year's cost of goods sold, lowering its profit.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Earned income not yet received is omitted at year-end. Which combined misstatement follows?
options: Profit and receivables are understated
Profit and liabilities are overstated
Cash and capital contributions are overstated
Expenses and payables are understated
questions.answer: Profit and receivables are understated
questions.explanation: The missing entry omits both earned income and the asset representing the amount due.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Reported profit rises mainly because of a one-off gain on selling a building. Why be cautious about forecasting higher recurring trading profit?
options: Every gain is automatically a cash loss
Selling a building guarantees higher future sales
One-off gains must be ignored in all financial statements
The gain may not recur and is separate from ongoing operating performance
questions.answer: The gain may not recur and is separate from ongoing operating performance
questions.explanation: Forecasting should distinguish sustainable operating earnings from unusual transactions.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Operating profit rises, but capital employed rises by a larger percentage. What happens to return on capital employed?
options: It remains unchanged regardless of capital growth
It becomes equal to cash at bank
It falls
It must rise because profit rose
questions.answer: It falls
questions.explanation: A ratio falls when its denominator grows proportionately faster than its numerator.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A partnership agreement guarantees one partner a minimum profit share and specifies which partner bears any shortfall. Why is the agreement needed in allocation?
options: A guarantee always means all partners receive equal amounts
The guarantee changes how the available profit is distributed
The guarantee creates additional trading profit automatically
Every shortfall must be paid by customers
questions.answer: The guarantee changes how the available profit is distributed
questions.explanation: A profit guarantee reallocates the existing amount according to the agreed responsibility for any deficiency.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A new partner joins after reserves were accumulated by the old partners. Why distinguish those reserves from future shared profits?
options: They arose under the previous ownership and sharing arrangement
All past reserves must automatically belong to the incoming partner
Reserves are always external liabilities
Reserves prove that an equal amount of cash is available
questions.answer: They arose under the previous ownership and sharing arrangement
questions.explanation: Pre-admission accumulated profits belong to the earlier partners according to the applicable arrangement.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A partnership uses fixed capital accounts and separate current accounts. Where would an ordinary drawings adjustment usually be recorded?
options: As sales revenue
As a permanent reduction of fixed capital in every case
In the supplier's control account
In the partner's current account
questions.answer: In the partner's current account
questions.explanation: The current account records routine drawings and profit allocations while the fixed capital balance remains separately maintained.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Partners adjust goodwill through their capital or current accounts without any cash transfer. What follows?
options: The adjustment guarantees new external funding
Goodwill must have been sold to a customer
Ownership balances can change without a cash movement
The bank balance must rise by the goodwill amount
questions.answer: Ownership balances can change without a cash movement
questions.explanation: An internal equity adjustment redistributes claims without necessarily causing a receipt or payment.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Two partners contribute different capital amounts but agree to equal profit shares. Why should allocation not automatically follow capital proportions?
options: Profit shares must always equal the partners' loan balances
Capital balances and agreed profit-sharing rights are distinct
Unequal capital makes the partnership accounts impossible
Equal shares require equal cash withdrawals every day
questions.answer: Capital balances and agreed profit-sharing rights are distinct
questions.explanation: The agreed entitlement to profit can differ from the proportions of capital invested.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A company has little profit but still owes interest under a borrowing agreement. Why is this different from treating interest as an ordinary dividend?
options: Interest is a finance obligation, while an ordinary dividend is an owner distribution
Interest can always be omitted whenever profit is low
Both payments are automatically classified as sales deductions
A lender becomes an ordinary shareholder whenever profit falls
questions.answer: Interest is a finance obligation, while an ordinary dividend is an owner distribution
questions.explanation: Debt service is not simply a discretionary allocation of the residual profit to owners.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Equipment is acquired by issuing shares directly to the seller, with no cash paid. How should this affect the cash-flow totals for the acquisition itself?
options: It must appear as an investing cash outflow equal to the equipment value
It must appear as operating cash paid to customers
It creates both a cash inflow and outflow despite no cash movement
It should not be included as a cash payment
questions.answer: It should not be included as a cash payment
questions.explanation: A noncash investing and financing transaction is distinguished from actual cash flows and disclosed appropriately.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Inventory cost exceeds the amount expected to be realised from sale after the necessary selling costs. Why is a write-down considered?
options: The write-down creates cash for buying replacement stock
A lower selling price automatically changes the original purchase invoice
The inventory should not remain carried above its recoverable sale value under the stated valuation basis
Expected losses are ignored until every item is sold
questions.answer: The inventory should not remain carried above its recoverable sale value under the stated valuation basis
questions.explanation: The lower-of-cost-and-net-realisable-value approach recognises a loss in the carrying amount when recovery falls below cost.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Operating cash flow is strong only because supplier payments have been delayed unusually. What should an analyst examine?
options: Whether profit must have increased by every unpaid amount
Whether the cash improvement is sustainable and obligations are building up
Whether delayed payments prove supplier costs disappeared
Only the positive cash total, ignoring payables
questions.answer: Whether the cash improvement is sustainable and obligations are building up
questions.explanation: Postponing payments can temporarily preserve cash while increasing liabilities and future cash demands.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Two similar firms use different reasonable useful-life estimates for similar equipment. Why compare those policies before comparing profit margins?
options: Different depreciation charges can affect reported profit without identical operating differences
Useful-life estimates never affect expenses
A longer life necessarily means the equipment performs better
Identical revenue guarantees identical profit under every estimate
questions.answer: Different depreciation charges can affect reported profit without identical operating differences
questions.explanation: Accounting estimates influence expense recognition, so apparent performance differences may partly reflect those choices.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two organisms share many inherited structural features. What does this most reasonably suggest?
options: They must be the same species
They cannot differ in DNA
A relatively close evolutionary relationship
Identical habitats are required
questions.answer: A relatively close evolutionary relationship
questions.explanation: Shared inherited features can indicate common ancestry, although convergent features must be distinguished.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A cell is placed in a solution with lower water potential than its cytoplasm. What tends to happen?
options: Water leaves the cell
Water enters the cell only
The cell instantly makes more water
Solute movement must stop
questions.answer: Water leaves the cell
questions.explanation: Water moves by osmosis toward the lower water potential across a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A cell grows much larger without changing shape. Why can exchange become less efficient relative to its needs?
options: Surface area disappears
Its membrane becomes nonselective automatically
Its enzymes stop existing
Volume increases faster than surface area
questions.answer: Volume increases faster than surface area
questions.explanation: A decreasing surface-area-to-volume ratio makes exchange less sufficient for the larger internal volume.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A tissue repairs a small wound by mitosis. What should daughter cells normally retain?
options: No DNA
The parent cell's chromosome number
Half the parent cell's chromosomes
A completely new genetic code
questions.answer: The parent cell's chromosome number
questions.explanation: Mitosis normally preserves chromosome number in genetically similar daughter cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Why does meiosis reduce chromosome number before fertilisation?
options: It prevents chromosome number doubling each generation
It makes gametes have no genes
It prevents all genetic variation
It makes every offspring identical
questions.answer: It prevents chromosome number doubling each generation
questions.explanation: Fusion of two haploid gametes restores diploidy without continually increasing chromosome number.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A leaf receives light but very little carbon dioxide. Why may increasing light fail to raise photosynthesis?
options: Light never affects photosynthesis
Oxygen replaces carbon dioxide in sugar synthesis
Carbon dioxide is limiting
Chlorophyll must be absent
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide is limiting
questions.explanation: Increasing a nonlimiting factor has little effect when another required factor restricts the rate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A working muscle's ATP demand rises. Why must ATP be continually regenerated?
options: ATP contains no transferable energy
Cells hold only a limited immediately available ATP supply
ATP cannot be broken down
All ATP is stored permanently in DNA
questions.answer: Cells hold only a limited immediately available ATP supply
questions.explanation: ATP is rapidly used and resynthesized to support continuing cellular work.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A shoot bends toward light. Why does unequal growth produce bending?
options: All cells shorten equally
The root changes into a leaf
The light physically pushes the shoot
Cells on one side elongate more
questions.answer: Cells on one side elongate more
questions.explanation: Differential elongation across the shoot causes curvature toward the light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Alveoli have thin walls and a large total surface area. What does this arrangement improve?
options: Filtration of red blood cells
Production of bone tissue
Diffusion of respiratory gases
Storage of undigested food
questions.answer: Diffusion of respiratory gases
questions.explanation: A short diffusion distance and large surface support rapid oxygen and carbon-dioxide exchange.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person produces a smaller volume of concentrated urine when conserving water. What kidney change contributes?
options: More water is reabsorbed from the filtrate
All filtration stops permanently
More water is secreted into the tubule
Blood cells pass freely into urine
questions.answer: More water is reabsorbed from the filtrate
questions.explanation: Greater tubular water reabsorption reduces urine volume and concentrates remaining solutes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A reflex withdraws a hand from a painful stimulus before deliberate action. What advantage does this offer?
options: Permanent loss of brain function
A response without any neurons
Proof that muscles detect every stimulus alone
A rapid protective response
questions.answer: A rapid protective response
questions.explanation: Reflex pathways allow quick responses without waiting for conscious planning.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A muscle pulls on a bone across a joint. Why is another muscle needed for the opposite movement?
options: Muscles have no force when shortening
Muscles actively pull rather than push
Bones contract independently
A single tendon can reverse its attachment
questions.answer: Muscles actively pull rather than push
questions.explanation: Antagonistic muscles create opposing joint movements by pulling in different directions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A flower receives pollen from another plant of the same species. What may this increase compared with self-pollination?
options: Genetic variation in offspring
The number of chromosomes in every gamete
The certainty that all seeds are identical
The elimination of fertilisation
questions.answer: Genetic variation in offspring
questions.explanation: Cross-pollination can combine alleles from different individuals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A recessive trait appears in a child of two unaffected parents in a simple autosomal model. What is a possible explanation?
options: The allele must be dominant
The child has no chromosomes
Both parents carry the recessive allele
Neither parent has the allele
questions.answer: Both parents carry the recessive allele
questions.explanation: Two heterozygous parents can each transmit the recessive allele.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Before cell division, DNA is copied. Why is accurate copying important?
options: Proteins cannot exist near DNA
Each daughter cell needs inherited genetic information
DNA supplies all the cell's oxygen
Copying removes every mutation from the species
questions.answer: Each daughter cell needs inherited genetic information
questions.explanation: Replication preserves genetic instructions for transmission to daughter cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Antibiotic treatment leaves a few resistant bacteria alive. Why can resistance become more common afterward?
options: Every bacterium deliberately chooses a mutation
The antibiotic teaches all bacteria to resist
Sensitive bacteria become mammals
Resistant survivors reproduce
questions.answer: Resistant survivors reproduce
questions.explanation: Selection favours resistant variants already present or arising through mutation and gene transfer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A population grows rapidly, then slows as food becomes scarce. What explains the slowdown?
options: The disappearance of reproduction in all species
A lack of any environmental effect
Density-dependent competition
An unlimited carrying capacity
questions.answer: Density-dependent competition
questions.explanation: Competition intensifies as population density approaches resource limits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Dead leaves decay and mineral nutrients return to soil. What ecological link is illustrated?
options: Decomposers recycle matter
Decomposers create sunlight
Energy cycles without any loss
Plants do not need nutrients
questions.answer: Decomposers recycle matter
questions.explanation: Decomposition releases nutrients from organic matter for reuse in ecosystems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A reserve protects several connected habitats instead of one tiny isolated patch. What advantage can connections provide?
options: Guaranteed extinction of predators
Elimination of all competition
Identical conditions everywhere
Movement and gene flow between populations
questions.answer: Movement and gene flow between populations
questions.explanation: Habitat connections can reduce isolation and support dispersal and genetic exchange.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A useful gene is introduced into a bacterial plasmid. Why can this help produce its protein?
options: The gene has to become a virus first
The plasmid can carry the gene into a suitable host
The plasmid directly becomes the protein
Bacteria do not require gene expression
questions.answer: The plasmid can carry the gene into a suitable host
questions.explanation: A vector can transfer a gene for expression in a compatible host system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two species look alike but their similarities evolved independently in similar environments. What should a classification study do?
options: Use additional inherited and molecular evidence
Assume identical appearance proves recent ancestry
Ignore DNA because appearance is always decisive
Treat similar environments as identical genomes
questions.answer: Use additional inherited and molecular evidence
questions.explanation: Convergence can imitate relatedness, so multiple lines of evidence are needed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A membrane protein moves ions against their concentration gradient. What additional requirement is likely?
options: Identical ion concentrations on both sides
Destruction of all membrane proteins
An energy source
A completely impermeable cell wall
questions.answer: An energy source
questions.explanation: Moving against an electrochemical gradient requires energy, directly or through coupling.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Adding more substrate reduces the effect of a reversible competitive inhibitor. Why?
options: The reaction no longer needs enzymes
Substrate competes more successfully for the active site
The inhibitor is converted into substrate
The enzyme is permanently denatured
questions.answer: Substrate competes more successfully for the active site
questions.explanation: Higher substrate concentration increases the likelihood of substrate occupying the shared binding site.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Homologous chromosomes exchange corresponding segments during meiosis. What can result?
options: A doubling of chromosome number in every gamete
Loss of all genes from both chromosomes
Identical copies of one parental chromosome only
New combinations of alleles on a chromosome
questions.answer: New combinations of alleles on a chromosome
questions.explanation: Crossing over recombines linked alleles between homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Light reactions stop supplying ATP and NADPH. Why does carbon fixation soon slow?
options: Carbon dioxide instantly disappears from the atmosphere
The chloroplast loses all membranes immediately
Carbon reduction needs their energy and reducing power
The Calvin cycle directly absorbs all required photons
questions.answer: Carbon reduction needs their energy and reducing power
questions.explanation: The Calvin cycle depends on ATP and NADPH generated by light-dependent reactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Oxygen becomes unavailable to aerobic cells. Why does the mitochondrial electron-transport chain stall?
options: Its final electron acceptor is missing
Glucose cannot contain carbon anymore
All glycolysis enzymes require oxygen directly
The Krebs cycle becomes a photosynthetic cycle
questions.answer: Its final electron acceptor is missing
questions.explanation: Without oxygen accepting electrons, electron carriers cannot be efficiently reoxidised.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Why can fermentation sustain glycolysis when oxygen is absent?
options: It produces oxygen for mitochondria
It makes ATP without any substrate
It eliminates the need for enzymes
It regenerates NAD+
questions.answer: It regenerates NAD+
questions.explanation: Regeneration of NAD+ allows the oxidation step in glycolysis to continue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two plants receive equal total light but different uninterrupted night lengths and flower differently. What does this suggest?
options: Photosynthesis stops in all long nights permanently
Night duration can regulate flowering
Only total light energy matters
Flowers never respond to timing
questions.answer: Night duration can regulate flowering
questions.explanation: Photoperiodic responses often depend on the duration of uninterrupted darkness.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Exercising tissue releases more carbon dioxide and becomes more acidic. How can this assist oxygen delivery?
options: Haemoglobin's oxygen affinity decreases locally
Haemoglobin binds oxygen irreversibly
Blood stops flowing to that tissue
Carbon dioxide replaces iron in every haem group
questions.answer: Haemoglobin's oxygen affinity decreases locally
questions.explanation: The Bohr effect promotes oxygen unloading where metabolic activity is high.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: ADH secretion rises when blood becomes more concentrated. What combined response is expected?
options: Complete cessation of filtration in all nephrons
Increased loss of water with no feedback
More collecting-duct water reabsorption and less urine
Less water reabsorption and more dilute urine
questions.answer: More collecting-duct water reabsorption and less urine
questions.explanation: ADH increases collecting-duct water permeability, helping conserve water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A chemical synapse normally transmits in one direction. Why?
options: The neurotransmitter destroys the receiving neuron
Vesicle release and postsynaptic receptors are arranged asymmetrically
Electrical charge can move only one way through all materials
Both neurons have identical release machinery at the same contact
questions.answer: Vesicle release and postsynaptic receptors are arranged asymmetrically
questions.explanation: The presynaptic terminal releases transmitter onto receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A skeletal muscle sarcomere shortens while actin and myosin filament lengths stay constant. How?
options: Both filaments are chemically dissolved
Actin converts completely into myosin
The muscle loses all ATP
The filaments slide past each other
questions.answer: The filaments slide past each other
questions.explanation: Cross-bridge cycling increases filament overlap without shortening individual filaments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: One sperm fuses with the egg while another fuses with the central cell in a typical angiosperm. What is produced?
options: Only pollen grains
A haploid seed coat
Embryo precursor and nutritive endosperm precursor
Two identical diploid embryos
questions.answer: Embryo precursor and nutritive endosperm precursor
questions.explanation: Double fertilisation forms the zygote and usually triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Red and white flowers produce pink heterozygotes in a simple inheritance model. What does this demonstrate?
options: The heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype
The parental alleles are permanently blended and lost
The trait has no genetic basis
Every allele is recessive
questions.answer: The heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance changes the heterozygote phenotype without erasing the separate alleles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A son inherits an X-linked allele from which parent in the usual XY model?
options: His father
Both parents through the same X chromosome
Neither parent
His mother
questions.answer: His mother
questions.explanation: A son normally receives his X chromosome from his mother and Y chromosome from his father.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A gene's mRNA is present but no protein is produced after ribosome function is blocked. Which stage is directly affected?
options: Chromosome segregation
Translation
DNA replication
Transcription initiation only
questions.answer: Translation
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA and assemble amino acids during translation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A population's allele frequencies shift sharply after a random disaster leaves few survivors. What process can explain this?
options: Genetic drift through a bottleneck
Directed mutation to help every survivor
Guaranteed stabilising selection
Inheritance of acquired injuries
questions.answer: Genetic drift through a bottleneck
questions.explanation: Chance sampling during a bottleneck can change allele frequencies independently of adaptive value.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A flowering plant gains pollination while an insect gains nectar. What makes this mutualism?
options: Neither species gains anything
Both must be the same species
Both species benefit
Only the insect benefits and the plant is harmed
questions.answer: Both species benefit
questions.explanation: Mutualism describes interactions with a benefit to each participating species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A pond can have less producer biomass than consumer biomass at one instant. How is this possible?
options: Biomass and productivity are identical measures
Producers reproduce and are consumed rapidly
Energy increases at every trophic transfer
Consumers perform all photosynthesis
questions.answer: Producers reproduce and are consumed rapidly
questions.explanation: Rapid producer turnover can sustain consumers despite low standing producer biomass.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A DNA sample is repeatedly heated, cooled with primers, and extended by polymerase. Why are primers needed?
options: They replace all template DNA
They cut every target molecule into amino acids
They convert RNA directly into protein
They provide starting points for DNA synthesis
questions.answer: They provide starting points for DNA synthesis
questions.explanation: DNA polymerase extends from an existing primer with a free 3-prime end.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two populations look different but interbreed and produce fertile offspring naturally. Under a biological species concept, what is strongest evidence they belong to one species?
options: Different local food sources alone
The fact that both have cells
Reproductive compatibility and gene flow
Different body colour alone
questions.answer: Reproductive compatibility and gene flow
questions.explanation: The biological species concept emphasizes reproductive connection rather than appearance alone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Plant and animal cells are placed in sufficiently dilute solutions. Why can the plant cell become turgid while the animal cell may burst?
options: The plant wall resists expansion and builds opposing pressure
Plant membranes are completely impermeable to water
Animal cells contain no solute
The plant cell has no osmotic gradient
questions.answer: The plant wall resists expansion and builds opposing pressure
questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall limits expansion, allowing pressure potential to oppose further water entry.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Homologous chromosomes fail to separate in meiosis I, but meiosis II proceeds normally. What is expected for that chromosome among the four products?
options: Only one product can be affected
Every product contains two complete diploid genomes
All have an abnormal number of it
All have the normal number
questions.answer: All have an abnormal number of it
questions.explanation: Meiosis-I nondisjunction sends both homologues to one cell, producing two n+1 and two n-1 products.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A leaf's photosynthesis increases with added CO2 at one light level but barely responds in dim light. What explains the contrast?
options: The limiting factor differs between conditions
CO2 is never a photosynthetic substrate
Dim light destroys every chloroplast instantly
Light and CO2 act independently at all levels
questions.answer: The limiting factor differs between conditions
questions.explanation: CO2 may limit at adequate light, whereas insufficient light limits the response in dim conditions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A stronger stimulus causes more frequent action potentials rather than proportionately taller action potentials in one axon. Why?
options: Stimulus strength changes the genetic code each time
Stronger stimuli eliminate refractory periods
Individual action potentials are all-or-none events
Axons cannot transmit repeated signals
questions.answer: Individual action potentials are all-or-none events
questions.explanation: Stimulus intensity can be encoded by firing frequency while action-potential amplitude remains broadly fixed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Blood hormone level is high but target cells lack functional receptors. Why might the expected response be absent?
options: Hormone presence alone does not ensure signal reception
Hormones act without any molecular interaction
The hormone must instantly turn into DNA
All cells respond identically to every hormone
questions.answer: Hormone presence alone does not ensure signal reception
questions.explanation: Target response depends on functional receptors and downstream signalling.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A trait follows mitochondrial inheritance in the usual human model. Why can affected mothers pass it on while affected fathers generally do not?
options: Fathers have no mitochondria
Mitochondrial DNA is carried on the Y chromosome
Only sons receive egg cytoplasm
Most embryonic mitochondria come from the egg
questions.answer: Most embryonic mitochondria come from the egg
questions.explanation: The egg supplies nearly all zygotic cytoplasm and mitochondria in typical human inheritance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A bacterium stops making an enzyme when the enzyme's end product is abundant. Why can this be advantageous?
options: It stops all metabolism permanently
It conserves resources when further synthesis is unnecessary
It removes every gene from the chromosome
It guarantees a higher mutation rate
questions.answer: It conserves resources when further synthesis is unnecessary
questions.explanation: Regulatory feedback can avoid spending energy and materials on unneeded enzyme synthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A trait is heritable and improves survival but reduces reproduction enough to lower total offspring contribution. What determines its evolutionary success?
options: Survival duration alone
The organism's desire to pass it on
Body size alone
Its net contribution to reproductive fitness
questions.answer: Its net contribution to reproductive fitness
questions.explanation: Selection depends on genetic contribution to future generations, integrating survival and reproduction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A food chain lengthens while primary production is unchanged. Why does adding a top consumer limit the biomass it can support?
options: Longer chains create energy
Repeated trophic transfers reduce available energy
Energy is fully recycled at each feeding step
All producers stop photosynthesising
questions.answer: Repeated trophic transfers reduce available energy
questions.explanation: Energy transfer is inefficient, leaving progressively less available to additional consumer levels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person receives ready-made antibodies. Why is protection usually immediate but less lasting than active immunisation?
options: The antibodies reproduce indefinitely
The recipient's genome is permanently replaced
Passive antibodies cannot bind antigens
Antibodies act directly but do not necessarily create the recipient's immune memory
questions.answer: Antibodies act directly but do not necessarily create the recipient's immune memory
questions.explanation: Passive immunity supplies effectors that decay without necessarily stimulating durable memory.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A DNA insert and vector have compatible sticky ends but are not ligated. What is missing for stable recombinant DNA formation?
options: Removal of the vector's origin of replication
Covalent sealing of the sugar-phosphate backbone
Conversion of DNA into protein
Destruction of all complementary bases
questions.answer: Covalent sealing of the sugar-phosphate backbone
questions.explanation: Base pairing can align fragments, while ligase seals backbone nicks to stabilize the construct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two parents both have blood group AB. Under the standard ABO model without rare exceptions, why can they not have a group O child?
options: Neither parent carries the recessive i allele
Their A and B alleles permanently blend into a new allele
Every child must have group AB
Group O requires an extra chromosome
questions.answer: Neither parent carries the recessive i allele
questions.explanation: Each AB parent transmits either the A or B allele; a group O genotype requires an i allele from each parent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Cells in a nephron's proximal tubule lose much of their brush border while remaining alive. What function is most directly impaired?
options: Initial pressure filtration by those same tubule cells
Production of all blood plasma proteins
Storage of urine in the bladder
Efficient reabsorption through reduced membrane surface area
questions.answer: Efficient reabsorption through reduced membrane surface area
questions.explanation: Proximal-tubule microvilli enlarge exchange area, so their loss can reduce reabsorptive capacity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: At the same oxygen partial pressure, a tissue becomes more acidic and richer in carbon dioxide. What happens to haemoglobin oxygen binding?
options: Haemoglobin instantly loses all iron
Binding becomes independent of local chemistry
Affinity falls, favouring oxygen release
Affinity rises, trapping more oxygen
questions.answer: Affinity falls, favouring oxygen release
questions.explanation: Higher CO2 and hydrogen-ion levels favour oxygen unloading through the Bohr effect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A recombinant product contains human proinsulin but retains its connecting peptide. Why is that not equivalent to fully processed mature insulin?
options: Bacterial production automatically completes every human processing step
The connecting peptide must be removed and the correct linked-chain structure retained
The connecting peptide is the entire active hormone
Mature insulin contains no covalent bonds
questions.answer: The connecting peptide must be removed and the correct linked-chain structure retained
questions.explanation: Maturation removes the C-peptide, leaving the A and B chains connected by disulfide bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Double-stranded RNA matching a target transcript suppresses production of its protein. Which interpretation fits RNA interference?
options: Expression is silenced by targeting matching RNA without necessarily altering the DNA sequence
The target gene must be permanently deleted from every chromosome
The RNA directly turns into the missing protein
Every unrelated transcript must be destroyed equally
questions.answer: Expression is silenced by targeting matching RNA without necessarily altering the DNA sequence
questions.explanation: RNA interference uses sequence-specific RNA targeting to reduce gene expression, distinct from editing the genomic sequence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A hormone increases sodium reabsorption in appropriate kidney tubules. Why can this help reduce water loss when water can follow osmotically?
options: Sodium reabsorption necessarily forces more water into urine
Water moves independently of all osmotic gradients
The hormone converts sodium into water
Retained solute promotes water reabsorption
questions.answer: Retained solute promotes water reabsorption
questions.explanation: Increased solute retention can support osmotic water recovery, depending on tubular water permeability.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two ecosystems have equal gross primary production, but producer respiration is greater in one. Which has more new producer biomass available after respiration?
options: They necessarily have equal net production
Neither can have any net production
The ecosystem with lower producer respiration
The ecosystem with higher producer respiration
questions.answer: The ecosystem with lower producer respiration
questions.explanation: Net primary production equals gross primary production minus producer respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A penguin and a dolphin have flipper-like structures suited to swimming. Why does this similarity alone not establish close recent ancestry?
options: Swimming removes all inherited differences
Similar selection pressures can produce analogous adaptations independently
Every similar structure must be inherited from an immediately shared ancestor
Both animals are necessarily fish
questions.answer: Similar selection pressures can produce analogous adaptations independently
questions.explanation: Convergent adaptation can generate similar functional forms in distantly related lineages.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A secretory cell produces large amounts of exported protein. Which feature would support this activity?
options: A permanently inactive nucleus
Abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum
Absence of ribosomes
No cell membrane
questions.answer: Abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum
questions.explanation: Ribosomes on rough endoplasmic reticulum synthesize proteins destined for secretion.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A cell is placed in a solution with lower water potential than its cytoplasm. What tends to happen?
options: Water leaves the cell
Water enters the cell only
The cell instantly makes more water
Solute movement must stop
questions.answer: Water leaves the cell
questions.explanation: Water moves by osmosis toward the lower water potential across a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A cell grows much larger without changing shape. Why can exchange become less efficient relative to its needs?
options: Surface area disappears
Its membrane becomes nonselective automatically
Its enzymes stop existing
Volume increases faster than surface area
questions.answer: Volume increases faster than surface area
questions.explanation: A decreasing surface-area-to-volume ratio makes exchange less sufficient for the larger internal volume.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: An enzyme works with one substrate but not a similarly sized molecule. What best explains this?
options: The enzyme becomes the product
The enzyme has no three-dimensional structure
The active site's chemistry and shape are selective
All molecules of the same size react identically
questions.answer: The active site's chemistry and shape are selective
questions.explanation: Substrate binding depends on chemical complementarity as well as shape.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A tissue repairs a small wound by mitosis. What should daughter cells normally retain?
options: No DNA
The parent cell's chromosome number
Half the parent cell's chromosomes
A completely new genetic code
questions.answer: The parent cell's chromosome number
questions.explanation: Mitosis normally preserves chromosome number in genetically similar daughter cells.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: Why does meiosis reduce chromosome number before fertilisation?
options: It prevents chromosome number doubling each generation
It makes gametes have no genes
It prevents all genetic variation
It makes every offspring identical
questions.answer: It prevents chromosome number doubling each generation
questions.explanation: Fusion of two haploid gametes restores diploidy without continually increasing chromosome number.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A plant stores excess glucose as starch. Why is an insoluble storage polymer useful?
options: It contains no chemical energy
It diffuses out of cells faster
It cannot be broken down
It has less osmotic effect than many free glucose molecules
questions.answer: It has less osmotic effect than many free glucose molecules
questions.explanation: An insoluble polymer stores many sugar units with less effect on water potential.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: An egg and sperm fuse. Which immediate genetic consequence follows?
options: The zygote has no nucleus
All paternal genes replace maternal genes
The zygote receives chromosomes from both parents
Only maternal chromosomes remain
questions.answer: The zygote receives chromosomes from both parents
questions.explanation: Fertilisation combines the two haploid chromosome sets into a diploid zygote.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A recessive trait appears in a child of two unaffected parents in a simple autosomal model. What is a possible explanation?
options: The child has no chromosomes
Both parents carry the recessive allele
Neither parent has the allele
The allele must be dominant
questions.answer: Both parents carry the recessive allele
questions.explanation: Two heterozygous parents can each transmit the recessive allele.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: Before cell division, DNA is copied. Why is accurate copying important?
options: Each daughter cell needs inherited genetic information
DNA supplies all the cell's oxygen
Copying removes every mutation from the species
Proteins cannot exist near DNA
questions.answer: Each daughter cell needs inherited genetic information
questions.explanation: Replication preserves genetic instructions for transmission to daughter cells.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A gene is active in one cell type but inactive in another from the same person. What can differ?
options: The person's species
The basic meaning of all DNA bases
The number of parents
The proteins produced
questions.answer: The proteins produced
questions.explanation: Differential gene expression lets cells with similar genomes develop different functions.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A second exposure to the same pathogen can trigger a faster specific response. Why?
options: The body no longer needs immune cells
Red blood cells remember the pathogen
Memory lymphocytes were formed earlier
All pathogens are identical
questions.answer: Memory lymphocytes were formed earlier
questions.explanation: Immunological memory allows a quicker and often stronger response to a previously encountered antigen.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A useful gene is introduced into a bacterial plasmid. Why can this help produce its protein?
options: The gene has to become a virus first
The plasmid can carry the gene into a suitable host
The plasmid directly becomes the protein
Bacteria do not require gene expression
questions.answer: The plasmid can carry the gene into a suitable host
questions.explanation: A vector can transfer a gene for expression in a compatible host system.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: Phospholipids placed in water form a bilayer. Which arrangement minimises unfavourable contact?
options: Hydrophobic tails face inward away from water
Hydrophilic heads face inward away from water
All tails remain individually exposed to water
Every phospholipid breaks into separate atoms
questions.answer: Hydrophobic tails face inward away from water
questions.explanation: Amphipathic phospholipids arrange polar heads toward water and nonpolar tails toward each other.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A mutation replaces a buried nonpolar amino acid with a charged one. Why might protein function change?
options: The mutation necessarily doubles the entire protein length
The genetic code stops being shared by cells
Every charged amino acid always improves function
The substitution can disrupt folding interactions
questions.answer: The substitution can disrupt folding interactions
questions.explanation: Changing side-chain properties can alter folding and the structure needed for function.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: An uninoculated culture-medium control develops microbial growth. What does this suggest?
options: All experimental samples must be genetically identical
No organisms can grow in the medium
Contamination occurred in the medium or handling process
The intended culture has definitely produced the desired product
questions.answer: Contamination occurred in the medium or handling process
questions.explanation: Growth in a control that received no intended cells indicates unintended biological contamination.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A culture grows well but produces little of the desired enzyme. Why measure product yield separately from cell growth?
options: Product concentration cannot change after growth begins
More cells do not necessarily mean proportionately more product
Every cell always makes the same amount of every protein
Growth measurements directly identify all secreted molecules
questions.answer: More cells do not necessarily mean proportionately more product
questions.explanation: Biomass and product formation are related but distinct outputs of a culture process.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A small plant-tissue sample regenerates into a plant under suitable conditions. What biological potential does this demonstrate?
options: Some plant cells can give rise to the tissues of a whole plant
Every isolated plant cell grows without any suitable environment
Plant cells lack genetic information after isolation
Regeneration requires the tissue to become an animal embryo
questions.answer: Some plant cells can give rise to the tissues of a whole plant
questions.explanation: Plant regeneration reflects developmental potential expressed under appropriate conditions, not automatic growth in every setting.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: Two DNA records have similar sequences. What is a useful first reason to compare them computationally?
options: To prove that their organisms are identical in every trait
To replace all need to interpret the alignment
To guarantee that every difference changes a protein
To identify matching regions and candidate differences
questions.answer: To identify matching regions and candidate differences
questions.explanation: Sequence comparisons reveal patterns of similarity and variation that require biological interpretation.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A protein measurement is interpreted against samples of known concentration. Why use those reference samples?
options: To remove every possible source of experimental error
To change the unknown's concentration automatically
To relate the measured signal to an established concentration scale
To ensure all unknown samples contain the same protein amount
questions.answer: To relate the measured signal to an established concentration scale
questions.explanation: Standards provide a calibration relationship between signal and the quantity being estimated.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A membrane protein moves ions against their concentration gradient. What additional requirement is likely?
options: Destruction of all membrane proteins
An energy source
A completely impermeable cell wall
Identical ion concentrations on both sides
questions.answer: An energy source
questions.explanation: Moving against an electrochemical gradient requires energy, directly or through coupling.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: Adding more substrate reduces the effect of a reversible competitive inhibitor. Why?
options: Substrate competes more successfully for the active site
The inhibitor is converted into substrate
The enzyme is permanently denatured
The reaction no longer needs enzymes
questions.answer: Substrate competes more successfully for the active site
questions.explanation: Higher substrate concentration increases the likelihood of substrate occupying the shared binding site.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A cell with damaged DNA pauses before replication or division. Why is this useful?
options: It removes the need for DNA
It guarantees faster uncontrolled growth
It changes the cell into a gamete
It allows repair before damage is passed on
questions.answer: It allows repair before damage is passed on
questions.explanation: Checkpoints can delay progression so damage can be repaired or the cell removed.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: Homologous chromosomes exchange corresponding segments during meiosis. What can result?
options: Loss of all genes from both chromosomes
Identical copies of one parental chromosome only
New combinations of alleles on a chromosome
A doubling of chromosome number in every gamete
questions.answer: New combinations of alleles on a chromosome
questions.explanation: Crossing over recombines linked alleles between homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: Red and white flowers produce pink heterozygotes in a simple inheritance model. What does this demonstrate?
options: Every allele is recessive
The heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype
The parental alleles are permanently blended and lost
The trait has no genetic basis
questions.answer: The heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance changes the heterozygote phenotype without erasing the separate alleles.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A DNA base changes but the encoded amino acid stays the same. What explains this?
options: Different codons can specify the same amino acid
Every mutation deletes a chromosome
Ribosomes ignore all RNA
Amino acids determine DNA bases in reverse
questions.answer: Different codons can specify the same amino acid
questions.explanation: The genetic code is degenerate, allowing some substitutions to be synonymous.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A gene's mRNA is present but no protein is produced after ribosome function is blocked. Which stage is directly affected?
options: DNA replication
Transcription initiation only
Chromosome segregation
Translation
questions.answer: Translation
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA and assemble amino acids during translation.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A vaccine against one pathogen does not automatically protect against every unrelated pathogen. Why?
options: All infections use the same antigens
Immunity cannot form memory
Adaptive recognition is antigen-specific
Vaccines remove all white blood cells
questions.answer: Adaptive recognition is antigen-specific
questions.explanation: Different antigens require appropriately matched immune receptors and memory responses.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A DNA sample is repeatedly heated, cooled with primers, and extended by polymerase. Why are primers needed?
options: They convert RNA directly into protein
They provide starting points for DNA synthesis
They replace all template DNA
They cut every target molecule into amino acids
questions.answer: They provide starting points for DNA synthesis
questions.explanation: DNA polymerase extends from an existing primer with a free 3-prime end.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: A solute's uptake rate levels off as external concentration rises, despite an increasing gradient. What can explain the plateau?
options: A limited number of transport proteins are saturated
Diffusion gradients have become irrelevant to all membranes
The solute must be converted into water
The membrane has acquired unlimited carriers
questions.answer: A limited number of transport proteins are saturated
questions.explanation: Carrier-mediated transport has a finite capacity when the available proteins are fully occupied.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
questions.q: An edit alters a gene's regulatory sequence without changing its protein-coding sequence. What can still change?
options: The genetic code used by every ribosome
The amino-acid sequence must always change
The number of protons in each DNA atom
When or how much of the protein is made
questions.answer: When or how much of the protein is made
questions.explanation: Regulatory DNA influences expression, so protein abundance or timing can change without altering its amino-acid sequence.

questions.subject: Biotechnology
