options: Repayment may fall due before the equipment generates enough cash
Long-lived equipment cannot be financed externally
Short-term finance never carries a repayment obligation
The equipment's useful life guarantees immediate cash recovery
questions.answer: Repayment may fall due before the equipment generates enough cash
questions.explanation: Funding maturity should be considered alongside the timing of the asset's expected cash benefits.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A forecast shows a temporary cash deficit two months ahead. What is its practical value?
options: It proves the business is permanently unprofitable
It records cash already received in that future month
It eliminates uncertainty about every forecast input
It gives time to arrange funding or adjust cash timing
questions.answer: It gives time to arrange funding or adjust cash timing
questions.explanation: Forecasting supports advance action, while its assumptions and predicted amounts remain uncertain.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A founder raises equity from a new investor instead of taking a loan. What trade-off may result?
options: No effect on ownership under any equity agreement
The removal of all future business risk
Less contractual debt repayment but a share of ownership and control given up
Guaranteed fixed interest payments to the investor
questions.answer: Less contractual debt repayment but a share of ownership and control given up
questions.explanation: Equity funding shares ownership and residual returns rather than simply creating a conventional loan obligation.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: Routine decisions must pass through many management layers. What problem can delegation help reduce?
options: The cost of every raw material
Delays in decisions that capable local staff could make
The need for any accountability
Every difference between departments
questions.answer: Delays in decisions that capable local staff could make
questions.explanation: Appropriate delegation moves decisions nearer the information and work, subject to clear limits and competence.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A business can train existing staff or recruit specialists for a new process. What should guide the choice?
options: The urgency, required skills and relative costs of each route
Only the number of current staff
A rule that recruitment is always cheaper
A rule that existing staff can master any task immediately
questions.answer: The urgency, required skills and relative costs of each route
questions.explanation: The best route depends on available time, skills gaps, resources and the business's longer-term needs.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A bonus rewards only the number of units produced. Quality falls. What explains the outcome?
options: Pay incentives cannot affect behaviour
More units always imply better customer value
The quality target was necessarily met because output rose
The measure can encourage output at the expense of unmeasured quality
questions.answer: The measure can encourage output at the expense of unmeasured quality
questions.explanation: People may focus on rewarded measures, so incentives should reflect important dimensions of performance.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: Holding less stock reduces storage costs but deliveries are unreliable. What trade-off follows?
options: Storage costs and stockouts are the same cost
Supplier reliability becomes irrelevant when inventory falls
Lower holding costs may come with greater stockout risk
Lower stock always improves service reliability
questions.answer: Lower holding costs may come with greater stockout risk
questions.explanation: Lean inventories reduce buffers, making dependable replenishment more important.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A firm increases output using spare existing capacity. Why might average fixed cost fall?
options: Every additional unit is costless
The same fixed cost is spread over more units
Total fixed cost must fall to zero
Variable cost per unit must double
questions.answer: The same fixed cost is spread over more units
questions.explanation: Within the relevant capacity range, fixed costs do not rise proportionately with output.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A supplier offers a lower production price, but the task is central to the brand's quality. What else matters?
options: Quality control, reliability and dependence on the supplier
Only the quoted unit price
Whether all internal expertise can be discarded immediately
A guarantee that external suppliers always outperform internal staff
questions.answer: Quality control, reliability and dependence on the supplier
questions.explanation: An outsourcing decision includes strategic and operational consequences as well as direct purchase cost.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A pilot succeeds only because the founder provides unpaid labour that would need paid staff at scale. What should be revised before expansion?
options: Only the pilot's sales total
The assumption that unpaid work has no economic cost
The conclusion that any successful pilot guarantees scalable profit
The cost model and feasibility under realistic staffing
questions.answer: The cost model and feasibility under realistic staffing
questions.explanation: Scaling can change the resource requirements; omitted labour costs can make the apparent model misleading.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A delivery firm rewards speed alone, and damaged parcels increase. What change best addresses the problem?
options: Count only the fastest delivery each week
Treat damaged parcels as unrelated to the incentive
Use a balanced performance measure including timely, undamaged delivery
Raise the speed target further without monitoring damage
questions.answer: Use a balanced performance measure including timely, undamaged delivery
questions.explanation: A measure should reflect the intended service outcome and avoid rewarding behaviour that undermines it.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: Buying a competitor expands market access quickly but joins firms with conflicting cultures. What makes the decision more complex than comparing purchase price with current profit?
options: Culture cannot affect operations or staff retention
Integration risks can change the expected future benefits
Past profit guarantees identical future profit after acquisition
Combining ownership automatically removes all duplication costs
questions.answer: Integration risks can change the expected future benefits
questions.explanation: Acquisition outcomes depend on integration, retention and coordination as well as the initial financial comparison.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A project has already spent money that cannot be recovered. Future cash benefits are now below avoidable future costs. Which reasoning is sound?
options: Assess continuation using the future costs and benefits affected by the decision
Continue solely to justify the irrecoverable spending
Count the sunk spending as a new cash payment each future month
Ignore all future costs because development has already begun
questions.answer: Assess continuation using the future costs and benefits affected by the decision
questions.explanation: Irrecoverable past expenditure is unchanged by the current choice; relevant future consequences should guide it.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: Customers say they would buy a product, but actual trial purchases are low. What should the business infer?
options: The survey must have been deliberately falsified
Actual purchases are irrelevant if opinions are positive
Every trial purchaser represents every future customer
Stated intentions may differ from behaviour under real purchasing conditions
questions.answer: Stated intentions may differ from behaviour under real purchasing conditions
questions.explanation: Purchasing evidence tests willingness to commit under real price and context constraints, complementing survey responses.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A price cut raises revenue because demand is elastic. Why can profit still fall?
options: Elastic demand guarantees zero variable cost
The price reduction removes all fixed costs
Extra volume and the lower margin can increase costs enough to outweigh revenue gains
Higher revenue always means higher profit
questions.answer: Extra volume and the lower margin can increase costs enough to outweigh revenue gains
questions.explanation: Revenue effects alone do not determine profit; the contribution and total cost consequences also matter.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A product has a small market share in a rapidly growing market. Why is immediate withdrawal not automatic?
options: A portfolio label determines the decision without context
It may offer growth potential, but the investment and competitive prospects need assessment
Every low-share product must already be highly profitable
Market growth guarantees that this product will become the leader
questions.answer: It may offer growth potential, but the investment and competitive prospects need assessment
questions.explanation: Portfolio categories inform analysis but do not replace judgement about resources, differentiation and expected returns.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A producer starts direct online sales below its retailers' prices. What longer-term issue should it assess?
options: Retailers may reduce support or stop carrying the product
Direct selling guarantees that retail support is no longer useful
Retailers' responses cannot affect total sales
Every channel serves exactly the same customers at the same cost
questions.answer: Retailers may reduce support or stop carrying the product
questions.explanation: A direct channel can affect partner incentives and the wider route to customers.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A firm's advantage comes only from a feature competitors can copy cheaply next month. What is the concern?
options: Low copying cost guarantees permanent differentiation
The feature cannot create any present customer value
A copied feature automatically reduces all industry demand to zero
The advantage may be difficult to sustain
questions.answer: The advantage may be difficult to sustain
questions.explanation: An easily imitated benefit may provide limited lasting protection from competition.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: Sales rise during a campaign, but a major competitor also closes temporarily. What is needed before crediting the campaign with the whole increase?
options: Only the campaign's total number of views
A rule that sales increases never have multiple causes
Evidence separating the campaign effect from other changes
An assumption that every simultaneous sale was caused by advertising
questions.answer: Evidence separating the campaign effect from other changes
questions.explanation: A before-and-after increase can reflect several influences, so attribution requires an appropriate comparison or supporting evidence.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A break-even chart assumes constant unit price and variable cost, but expansion requires discounts and overtime. What should be questioned?
options: Whether every chart must have a zero sales line
Whether the original contribution assumptions still apply at the higher output
Whether fixed costs can ever be measured
Whether break-even analysis always predicts demand
questions.answer: Whether the original contribution assumptions still apply at the higher output
questions.explanation: Changing prices or unit costs changes contribution and can make the original linear projection inappropriate.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A profitable wholesaler's receivables grow much faster than sales and customers pay increasingly late. What risk follows?
options: It may struggle to meet cash commitments despite reported profit
Receivables growth guarantees immediate cash availability
Accounting profit prevents any liquidity problem
Late collection necessarily increases every customer's demand
questions.answer: It may struggle to meet cash commitments despite reported profit
questions.explanation: Profit can be tied up in unpaid balances while cash payments still fall due.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A project is attractive only if its sales forecast is achieved exactly; a small shortfall makes it unattractive. What does this reveal?
options: The forecast has been proved accurate
The project has no risk because a calculation was completed
The sales forecast can be ignored once the initial result is positive
The decision is sensitive to the sales assumption
questions.answer: The decision is sensitive to the sales assumption
questions.explanation: Sensitivity analysis shows how conclusions change when uncertain assumptions move.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A founder rejects all outside equity to retain control, although internal funds cannot support a planned expansion. What is the real trade-off?
options: External equity must be accepted by every growing firm
Internal finance is unlimited when the founder remains sole owner
Retaining ownership may limit the speed or scale of growth
Control and funding availability are always independent
questions.answer: Retaining ownership may limit the speed or scale of growth
questions.explanation: Finance choices can affect both ownership and the resources available to pursue objectives.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A manager delegates an important task but gives neither adequate authority nor access to information. Why may delegation fail?
options: Assigning a title guarantees effective action
The employee lacks the means needed to fulfil the responsibility
Delegation requires the manager to abandon all oversight
Authority and information cannot affect task performance
questions.answer: The employee lacks the means needed to fulfil the responsibility
questions.explanation: Responsibility should be matched with suitable authority, information and support.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: New software is technically sound, but staff bypass it because the workflow is slower and training was rushed. What should management examine?
options: How implementation, training and workflow fit affect adoption
Only whether the software launches without crashing
Whether resistance proves every employee opposes improvement
Whether another announcement alone guarantees compliance
questions.answer: How implementation, training and workflow fit affect adoption
questions.explanation: Successful change requires practical integration and user capability as well as technical functionality.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: Two sales teams have different territory potential but are judged only on total revenue. Why can this distort appraisal?
options: Total revenue measures effort perfectly in every context
All teams must face identical demand because they share an employer
A larger territory always has a lower sales potential
Results may reflect territory differences as well as effort and skill
questions.answer: Results may reflect territory differences as well as effort and skill
questions.explanation: Performance measures need context to distinguish controllable contribution from differing opportunities.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: Packing can handle twice the output that assembly can produce. Why might faster packing equipment add little overall output?
options: The fastest stage determines the whole process's capacity
Packing speed always doubles assembly speed
Assembly remains the limiting stage
Overall capacity is the sum of every stage's capacity
questions.answer: Assembly remains the limiting stage
questions.explanation: A sequential process is constrained by its bottleneck unless the limiting stage or flow changes.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A firm inspects more finished goods, but the same defect keeps recurring. What additional approach targets the cause?
options: Treat rework as proof that the process is reliable
Improve the process that produces the defect
Inspect only the products that look attractive
Increase output while keeping the faulty process unchanged
questions.answer: Improve the process that produces the defect
questions.explanation: Inspection detects defects; process improvement and quality assurance seek to prevent them.

questions.subject: Entrepreneurship
questions.q: A package uses less material per unit, but total sales rise enough that material use increases overall. What distinction matters?
options: Per-unit efficiency and total resource use can move in different directions
A per-unit reduction guarantees lower total use
Higher total use proves no per-unit saving occurred
Only revenue can measure environmental resource use
questions.answer: Per-unit efficiency and total resource use can move in different directions
questions.explanation: Total consumption depends on both material per unit and the number of units produced.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A program must read marks, calculate averages and print reports. Why split these into separate tasks?
options: Each part can be developed and checked more clearly
Splitting guarantees that no errors remain
Each task must run on a different computer
Separate tasks remove the need to pass data
questions.answer: Each part can be developed and checked more clearly
questions.explanation: Decomposition breaks a problem into manageable components with identifiable responsibilities.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A variable total is 5. The program assigns total=total+2. What value does total then hold?
questions.explanation: The right-hand expression uses the previous value before assigning the new result.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Entry is allowed only when a ticket is valid AND the visitor meets the age requirement. A valid ticket alone is presented. What must still be checked?
options: Whether the ticket has the larger numerical value
Whether the two conditions have identical names
Whether the age requirement is met
Whether at least one condition is false
questions.answer: Whether the age requirement is met
questions.explanation: AND requires both conditions to be true.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A program must inspect every item in a known list once. Which approach directly fits?
options: Sort the list without inspecting its values
Loop through the list's items
Inspect only its first item
Repeat until an unrelated password changes
questions.answer: Loop through the list's items
questions.explanation: Traversal applies the required operation to each element of the collection.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A postcode begins with zero and is not used in arithmetic. Why store it as text?
options: To preserve its characters, including the leading zero
To make numerical addition faster
To force every postcode to have the same value
To prevent all invalid input automatically
questions.answer: To preserve its characters, including the leading zero
questions.explanation: An identifier's character representation matters; numeric conversion can discard leading zeros.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Two students have the same name. Why use a unique student ID as the primary key?
options: The ID makes every name unique
The ID removes the need to store any other field
Names cannot be stored in a database
The ID distinguishes their records reliably
questions.answer: The ID distinguishes their records reliably
questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies a row even when descriptive attributes repeat.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A table contains many classes, but a report needs only class 12A. What should a query's WHERE condition do?
options: Delete other classes from the stored table
Sort all names without filtering
Keep rows whose class equals 12A
Rename every row as class 12A
questions.answer: Keep rows whose class equals 12A
questions.explanation: A WHERE condition selects qualifying rows for the result without itself deleting the others.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A report should show the highest marks first. Which ordering is appropriate?
options: Insertion order regardless of marks
Descending order of marks
Ascending order of marks
Alphabetical order of student names
questions.answer: Descending order of marks
questions.explanation: Descending numerical order places larger values before smaller ones.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A message must reach a particular device on an IP network. Why does it need destination addressing information?
options: Network equipment uses it to direct the message toward the destination
It determines the font used in the message
It guarantees that the message contains no errors
It proves that the sender is trustworthy
questions.answer: Network equipment uses it to direct the message toward the destination
questions.explanation: Destination addresses support delivery; addressing alone does not establish integrity or trust.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A user types a website name instead of its IP address. What does name resolution help provide?
options: A guarantee that the site's claims are true
A copy of the user's password
Extra storage space on the user's device
The network address associated with the name
questions.answer: The network address associated with the name
questions.explanation: DNS resolves domain names to relevant network addressing information.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Which prompt best asks an AI for a usable school recycling announcement?
options: Write a school announcement without stating its topic or purpose
Write a 60-word announcement for students explaining where to place paper waste
Write a detailed research essay about worldwide recycling policy
List technical recycling terms for waste-management specialists
questions.answer: Write a 60-word announcement for students explaining where to place paper waste
questions.explanation: The specific audience, purpose and length make the intended output clearer.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Students need examples for an attendance dashboard demonstration. Which dataset best avoids exposing classmates' details?
options: Real records with phone numbers removed but names retained
Real records with names hidden but identifying absence notes retained
Invented records clearly marked as synthetic
Real records with names replaced but student numbers retained
questions.answer: Invented records clearly marked as synthetic
questions.explanation: Synthetic demonstration records can show the design without disclosing classmates' personal information.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A school chatbot is unsure about a student's unusual request. Which design best supports reliable service?
options: Ask the same question repeatedly until its answer sounds certain
Present the most common answer as applicable to every unusual case
Offer escalation to an authorised staff member
Choose its highest-scoring answer even when confidence is low
questions.answer: Offer escalation to an authorised staff member
questions.explanation: Escalation lets a responsible person handle cases outside the system's reliable coverage.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A speech recogniser performs poorly on accents missing from its training examples. Which improvement addresses that gap?
options: Evaluate and train with appropriately obtained diverse speech
Collect more examples only from the accents already recognised well
Lower the confidence threshold without checking transcription errors
Increase output length while keeping the speech data unchanged
questions.answer: Evaluate and train with appropriately obtained diverse speech
questions.explanation: Representative speech data and evaluation can expose and reduce the coverage gap.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: An AI learning app requires dragging objects but some learners cannot use that gesture. Which change improves access?
options: Make the drag targets larger while still requiring the same gesture
Extend the time limit while still requiring the same gesture
Add spoken instructions while still requiring the same gesture
Provide a keyboard or button alternative
questions.answer: Provide a keyboard or button alternative
questions.explanation: Alternative controls allow more learners to perform the same essential action.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A school stores one row per student and columns for class and mark. Which structure best represents this labelled table in Pandas?
options: A function name without data
A DataFrame
One unlabelled scalar
A single Boolean value
questions.answer: A DataFrame
questions.explanation: A DataFrame provides a two-dimensional labelled structure suitable for tabular records.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A DataFrame has columns Name and Mark. Why select its Mark column before calculating average achievement?
options: The operation should use the relevant numeric measurements
Names must first be converted into exam marks
Selecting one column sorts every row automatically
Column selection deletes the other data permanently
questions.answer: The operation should use the relevant numeric measurements
questions.explanation: Choosing the appropriate variable keeps the calculation focused on the quantity being summarised.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A class wants to compare enrolment counts across four clubs. Which plot directly supports that comparison?
options: A line implying a time sequence where none exists
A pie chart of the clubs' names converted into letter counts
A scatterplot with no defined numeric axes
A bar chart with one bar per club
questions.answer: A bar chart with one bar per club
questions.explanation: Separate bars represent and compare counts for distinct categories.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A CSV file has four fields per row, but import settings use the wrong separator. What problem can result?
options: The original file necessarily disappears
The data gain new observations from the separator alone
Fields may be combined or split incorrectly
All numbers automatically become correct dates
questions.answer: Fields may be combined or split incorrectly
questions.explanation: The delimiter determines where the importer recognises field boundaries.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Why inspect the first few rows after importing a dataset?
options: To remove all missing values automatically
To check that columns and sample values were interpreted as intended
To prove the entire dataset contains no errors
To calculate every possible statistic at once
questions.answer: To check that columns and sample values were interpreted as intended
questions.explanation: A small preview can reveal import problems, although it cannot establish full data quality.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A program sums a list but starts its total at 1 instead of 0. What error results?
options: The final sum is one too high
The final sum is multiplied by one
Only the last item is counted
The result is correct whenever the list has more than one item
questions.answer: The final sum is one too high
questions.explanation: The initial value is included in the accumulation, creating a constant extra one.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A value must be at least 10 and at most 20. Why is x>=10 OR x<=20 an incorrect validation condition?
options: It rejects every real x
It accepts only 10 and 20
It checks exactly the same condition as AND
It accepts every real x rather than only the intended interval
questions.answer: It accepts every real x rather than only the intended interval
questions.explanation: For any real number, at least one of those two inequalities holds; the interval requires both.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A loop runs while count<10, but count never changes inside it. If count starts at 0, what is the main problem?
options: The condition becomes false automatically after one pass
The loop must skip its body
The loop does not reach a terminating condition
The loop necessarily executes exactly ten times
questions.answer: The loop does not reach a terminating condition
questions.explanation: Without a change to the controlling state or another exit, the true condition remains true.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A search should treat School and school as equivalent. What preparation helps?
options: Compare their lengths as proof of equality
Apply the same case normalisation to both strings
Convert only one string to uppercase regardless of the other
Compare their first characters only
questions.answer: Apply the same case normalisation to both strings
questions.explanation: A consistent normalisation removes the intended case distinction while retaining the rest of the text.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A school wants the average mark for each class. What does grouping by class achieve?
options: A separate aggregate is computed for each class
The table becomes sorted by every student's mark automatically
Only one student from each class is retained in storage
Each student's mark becomes the whole-school average
questions.answer: A separate aggregate is computed for each class
questions.explanation: GROUP BY partitions rows into groups for aggregate calculations.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: In SQL, some email fields are NULL. Why can COUNT(email) be smaller than COUNT(*)?
options: COUNT(*) counts only rows with missing emails
COUNT(email) removes duplicates automatically
COUNT(*) counts columns rather than rows
COUNT(email) excludes NULL email values
questions.answer: COUNT(email) excludes NULL email values
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts rows, while counting an expression excludes rows where that expression is NULL.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: One course has several enrolments. Why can joining courses to enrolments return the course details several times?
options: Every join must return exactly one row per course
The database has physically duplicated the course table
The join produces one result row for each matching enrolment
The course's primary key has necessarily become invalid
questions.answer: The join produces one result row for each matching enrolment
questions.explanation: A one-to-many relationship can repeat parent details in a query result without duplicating the stored parent record.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A teacher's phone number is copied into every class record. What problem can arise when it changes?
options: Repeated storage guarantees consistent updates
Some copies may be updated while others remain stale
Every copy must change automatically without a relationship
The number can no longer be queried
questions.answer: Some copies may be updated while others remain stale
questions.explanation: Duplicated facts require coordinated changes; separating shared details helps maintain consistency.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A link's bandwidth rises, but a small request still waits on a long round-trip delay. What distinction explains this?
options: Transfer capacity and travel delay are different properties
Greater bandwidth guarantees zero latency
Latency is determined only by file size
Small messages require no network travel
questions.answer: Transfer capacity and travel delay are different properties
questions.explanation: Higher bandwidth can speed bulk transmission while propagation and response delays remain.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Data are encrypted in transit to a correctly authenticated server. What does this primarily protect against?
options: Every mistake made by the receiving application
All malicious actions by an authorised recipient
Every false claim on the website
An eavesdropper reading the transmitted content
questions.answer: An eavesdropper reading the transmitted content
questions.explanation: Transport encryption protects data on the connection, not every aspect of endpoint behaviour or content quality.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A leak alarm often sounds when there is no leak. Which error is occurring?
options: False negatives
Correct rejections
False positives
True positives
questions.answer: False positives
questions.explanation: The system predicts a leak when the actual condition is negative.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A recommender shows only content similar to previous clicks. What concern follows?
options: Users may encounter an increasingly narrow range of material
Past clicks establish that users prefer every item they have never seen
Personalisation guarantees equal exposure to opposing viewpoints
High click-through rates establish that the recommendations are educationally balanced
questions.answer: Users may encounter an increasingly narrow range of material
questions.explanation: Repeatedly selecting similar material can reinforce a restricted exposure pattern.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Students who cannot access an app are absent from its satisfaction survey. How might this affect results?
options: Randomising the order of survey questions eliminates access bias
App-user satisfaction directly estimates satisfaction among excluded students
The survey may overrepresent users with successful access
A large response count necessarily removes the exclusion problem
questions.answer: The survey may overrepresent users with successful access
questions.explanation: People excluded by access problems cannot report their experiences through that survey channel.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A message asks users to reveal passwords so an AI tool can personalise lessons. What should students recognise?
options: A familiar school logo makes it safe to disclose a password in chat
Personalisation does not justify sharing secret credentials
A personalisation benefit authorises any requested account access
An encrypted connection alone establishes the requester's authority
questions.answer: Personalisation does not justify sharing secret credentials
questions.explanation: Credentials control access and should not be disclosed in response to such a message.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: An AI summariser produces short, fluent text but omits the article's main limitation. Which criterion has failed?
options: Grammatical fluency
Conciseness
Consistency of writing style
Faithfulness to the source
questions.answer: Faithfulness to the source
questions.explanation: A useful summary must preserve important qualifications, not merely read smoothly.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A DataFrame's row labels are student IDs, not consecutive positions. Why distinguish label selection from position selection?
options: Row labels cannot contain numbers
An ID label and a row's ordinal position may identify different records
Labels must always equal row numbers starting at zero
Position selection always returns every matching name
questions.answer: An ID label and a row's ordinal position may identify different records
questions.explanation: Label-based and positional indexing refer to different properties of a row.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A report should include only rows whose Mark is at least 70. What should the filtering condition describe?
options: A true-or-false result for each row's mark comparison
The sum of every student's name
Only the DataFrame's number of columns
A command to replace every mark with 70
questions.answer: A true-or-false result for each row's mark comparison
questions.explanation: A Boolean mask selects rows according to whether each row satisfies the condition.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Some marks are missing. Why investigate their meaning before replacing every missing mark with zero?
options: A missing mark always proves absence from the course
Replacing values never changes an average
Zero cannot appear in a numeric column
Missing information may differ from an actual score of zero
questions.answer: Missing information may differ from an actual score of zero
questions.explanation: Unrecorded or unavailable marks are not automatically zero achievement, and replacement affects interpretation.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A graph compares weekly library visits over a term. Why place ordered weeks along the horizontal axis?
options: To convert visit counts into percentages automatically
To hide weeks with fewer visits
To preserve the sequence needed to interpret change over time
To guarantee visits rise each week
questions.answer: To preserve the sequence needed to interpret change over time
questions.explanation: Time order helps readers interpret trends and changes across successive observations.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Two Series store values using student IDs as labels but in different orders. Why consider label alignment when combining them?
options: Combining Series must always sort values numerically
Matching should follow the intended student identities
The first value in every Series necessarily belongs to the same student
Labels are decorative and can never affect operations
questions.answer: Matching should follow the intended student identities
questions.explanation: Pandas operations can align labelled data, so labels must correctly identify corresponding observations.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A maximum-finding algorithm starts its current maximum at zero. Why does it fail on a nonempty list containing only negative numbers?
options: Zero can remain the result even though it is not in the list
Negative numbers cannot be compared
The largest negative number is always zero
Initialisation does not affect a maximum search
questions.answer: Zero can remain the result even though it is not in the list
questions.explanation: The initial candidate must be compatible with the input domain, for example the list's first element.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Discount rules use an if-elif chain: spend>=100 gets 10%, then spend>=200 gets 20%. Why does spending 250 receive only 10%?
options: Both discounts are always added
The comparison 250>=200 is false
An elif branch always overrides the first branch
The first true branch prevents the later branch from being checked
questions.answer: The first true branch prevents the later branch from being checked
questions.explanation: An if-elif chain selects its first satisfied condition, so more restrictive thresholds should be considered appropriately.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A sorting program passes tests containing only distinct positive values. What is still poorly checked?
options: Whether every programming language sorts identically
Whether the program's title is unique
Its behaviour on duplicates, negative values and empty input
Whether positive numbers can be represented at all
questions.answer: Its behaviour on duplicates, negative values and empty input
questions.explanation: Successful tests establish behaviour for tested conditions, leaving other relevant input classes unresolved.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A query must show only classes whose average mark exceeds 70. Why use a condition on the grouped result?
options: Grouping automatically discards every class below the threshold
The criterion concerns a group aggregate rather than each original mark
Filtering individual marks above 70 gives the same class averages
Averages cannot appear in database queries
questions.answer: The criterion concerns a group aggregate rather than each original mark
questions.explanation: Filtering rows before averaging changes the data used; aggregate conditions are applied after groups are formed.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: An SQL field is NULL. Why is comparing it with =NULL not the proper test for missingness?
options: NULL represents an unknown value and needs an IS NULL test
NULL is always identical to the number zero
NULL is always identical to an empty string
An equality comparison converts every NULL to false data permanently
questions.answer: NULL represents an unknown value and needs an IS NULL test
questions.explanation: Ordinary comparisons with NULL evaluate to unknown in SQL's three-valued logic; IS NULL explicitly tests missingness.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A table has two rows matching a key, and another has three rows with that key. How many pairings does an equality join produce for that key?
options: Five
Three
One
Six
questions.answer: Six
questions.explanation: Each of the two rows pairs with each of the three matching rows, producing six combinations.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A database update is intended for one student but omits its WHERE condition. What is the main risk?
options: Only the row with the smallest primary key changes
The update automatically guesses the intended student
Every row in the target table can receive the update
No row can change without a WHERE condition
questions.answer: Every row in the target table can receive the update
questions.explanation: Without a restricting condition, an UPDATE applies its assignments to all rows in the target table.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A connection includes a very fast local link and a much slower external link. Why may upgrading only the local link barely improve large downloads?
options: A local upgrade automatically upgrades remote infrastructure
The external link can remain the limiting stage
End-to-end speed equals the sum of every link's capacity
The fastest link alone sets the full download speed
questions.answer: The external link can remain the limiting stage
questions.explanation: Throughput is constrained by bottlenecks along the path, so improving a nonlimiting stage can have little effect.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A user signs in successfully but is denied access to staff records. Why is this not necessarily an error?
options: Identity verification does not imply permission for every resource
A successful login must grant all database rights
Permission checks apply only to anonymous users
The password must therefore have been incorrect
questions.answer: Identity verification does not imply permission for every resource
questions.explanation: Authentication establishes identity; authorisation determines what that identity is permitted to do.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: An attacker cannot read an encrypted connection but controls the receiving device after decryption. What remains possible?
options: Encryption prevents all endpoint access forever
The endpoint never needs plaintext to use the message
The connection must have been unencrypted because an endpoint was compromised
The attacker can access plaintext at that endpoint
questions.answer: The attacker can access plaintext at that endpoint
questions.explanation: Protecting transmission does not protect data from a compromised endpoint that processes the decrypted content.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: An educational bot is rewarded only for keeping students chatting longer. What unintended result is plausible?
options: Time spent chatting directly measures retention after the session
Optimising engagement guarantees that explanations become more concise
It may prolong interaction without improving learning
The longest conversations necessarily produce the greatest learning gains
questions.answer: It may prolong interaction without improving learning
questions.explanation: Engagement duration is an imperfect proxy that can diverge from educational benefit.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Names are removed, but a dataset retains exact birth dates and rare class combinations. What remains possible?
options: A rare combination is less identifying because fewer records share it
Keeping indirect identifiers is harmless whenever names are stored elsewhere
Individuals may be identified by combining indirect details
Removing direct identifiers eliminates every possible link to individuals
questions.answer: Individuals may be identified by combining indirect details
questions.explanation: Combinations of indirect identifiers can uniquely or narrowly identify a person.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Two groups have similar overall accuracy but very different false-negative rates. What conclusion follows?
options: Equal accuracy establishes that missed cases have equal consequences
The different false-negative rates can be ignored if the overall scores match
Equal accuracy alone does not establish equal error impact
Equal accuracy implies equal false-negative rates
questions.answer: Equal accuracy alone does not establish equal error impact
questions.explanation: Different error distributions can produce the same total accuracy while affecting groups differently.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A visual explanation highlights a region in an image. What should a reviewer avoid assuming?
options: That the highlight can suggest what to investigate
That explanations can be compared across examples
That independent testing remains useful
That the highlight proves a correct causal reason for the prediction
questions.answer: That the highlight proves a correct causal reason for the prediction
questions.explanation: An explanation visualisation is evidence to examine, not automatic proof of causality or correctness.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A highly accurate attendance model requires continuous intrusive recording; a less intrusive method meets the school's stated need. What should designers compare?
options: Necessary benefit, data exposure and less intrusive alternatives
Accuracy gains alone without asking whether extra data are necessary
Data-storage cost alone without considering the recording's intrusiveness
User consent alone without considering whether a less intrusive method suffices
questions.answer: Necessary benefit, data exposure and less intrusive alternatives
questions.explanation: Responsible design considers proportionality and alternatives alongside predictive performance.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A file repeats some student records after two exports are combined. Why not blindly delete every row with a repeated name?
options: Duplicate removal cannot change any result
Different students can share a name
A repeated name always identifies a duplicate record
All records in the larger export must be discarded
questions.answer: Different students can share a name
questions.explanation: Deduplication needs a valid identity rule, such as an appropriate student identifier and record context.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A class summary reports mean marks, but one class has many unrecorded results. Why compare completion rates alongside the means?
options: The observed means may represent different proportions of each class
The larger mean proves all missing marks are high
An average automatically imputes every missing record correctly
Completion rates and sample composition cannot affect interpretation
questions.answer: The observed means may represent different proportions of each class
questions.explanation: Selective missingness can make comparisons of recorded marks misleading even when the arithmetic is correct.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Two bar charts use the same values, but one starts its vertical axis close to the minimum value. What should a reader notice?
options: The original counts necessarily changed
The chart with the shorter axis has more observations
Axis choices cannot affect visual comparison
The apparent size of differences can be exaggerated
questions.answer: The apparent size of differences can be exaggerated
questions.explanation: Bar lengths can visually overstate differences when a truncated baseline is overlooked.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: A table of registration codes loses leading zeros after conversion to numbers. Why is this a substantive problem?
options: Leading zeros necessarily represent missing students
The conversion improves all joins by definition
The codes' exact text may be needed to match records correctly
Every identifier must support multiplication
questions.answer: The codes' exact text may be needed to match records correctly
questions.explanation: Identifiers encode identity rather than magnitude, and altering their representation can break matching rules.

questions.subject: Informatics Practices
questions.q: Two files use the column label Score, but one records percentages and the other raw marks out of different totals. Why is direct averaging invalid?
options: Averaging automatically detects and corrects different scales
The measurements must first be interpreted on a comparable basis
Identical column names guarantee identical meaning
Both columns should be sorted alphabetically first
questions.answer: The measurements must first be interpreted on a comparable basis
questions.explanation: Shared labels do not ensure consistent units or definitions; combining values requires semantic as well as structural checks.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every member of set A is also in B, but B has extra members. Which statement follows?
options: A and B are disjoint
B is a proper subset of A
A equals B
A is a proper subset of B
questions.answer: A is a proper subset of B
questions.explanation: A is contained in B without being equal to it.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A real-valued rule contains the term 1/(x-3). Which input must be excluded?
questions.explanation: At x = 3 the denominator is zero, so the expression is undefined.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The graph of y = f(x) is changed to y = f(x)+4. What changes?
options: Every point moves upward by four units
Every point moves right by four units
All slopes double
The domain necessarily shrinks
questions.answer: Every point moves upward by four units
questions.explanation: Adding a constant to the output produces a vertical translation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An inequality is multiplied on both sides by a negative number. What must change?
options: The inequality becomes an equality
Only the larger side is multiplied
The inequality direction reverses
Both sides become zero
questions.answer: The inequality direction reverses
questions.explanation: Multiplication by a negative number reverses order on the number line.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An angle is increased by one full turn. What happens to its sine and cosine?
options: Both become zero
Both stay the same
Both change sign
Sine doubles while cosine stays fixed
questions.answer: Both stay the same
questions.explanation: Sine and cosine are periodic with a full-turn period.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A sequence increases by the same amount at every step. What feature does its term-number graph have?
options: A continuously doubling slope
A vertical line
A repeating circle
A constant slope
questions.answer: A constant slope
questions.explanation: A constant difference makes the term a linear function of its index.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A positive quantity grows by the same percentage each year. Which model is appropriate?
options: A fixed value with no change
A sequence with constant second difference necessarily
Geometric growth
A constant additive increase
questions.answer: Geometric growth
questions.explanation: Repeated multiplication by a fixed factor produces a geometric sequence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In expanding (1+x)^n for a positive integer n, why is the constant term 1?
options: It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
Every term contains x
The exponents must all be zero
All coefficients are equal to one
questions.answer: It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
questions.explanation: Only the product of all constant choices contributes to the x-to-the-zero term.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two distinct nonvertical lines have the same slope. What follows?
options: They are perpendicular
They meet exactly once
They must pass through the origin
They are parallel
questions.answer: They are parallel
questions.explanation: Equal slopes give the same direction; distinct intercepts keep the lines separate.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A point moves so its distances from two fixed points have a constant sum greater than their separation. What path results?
options: A parabola with that same definition
An ellipse
A hyperbola
A straight line in all cases
questions.answer: An ellipse
questions.explanation: An ellipse is defined by a constant sum of distances to two foci.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two vectors have equal magnitudes and opposite directions. What is their sum?
options: The zero vector
A vector twice as long
A unit vector
A scalar equal to their common magnitude
questions.answer: The zero vector
questions.explanation: Opposite equal vectors cancel component by component.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Values of f(x) approach 5 as x approaches 2, but f(2) is defined as 9. What is the limit at 2?
options: It must not exist
questions.explanation: A limit concerns nearby values, not the separately assigned value at the point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A graph has a jump at x = a. Why is the function not continuous there?
options: Its domain must contain only integers
Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
Its value must be negative
Its slope must be positive
questions.answer: Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
questions.explanation: Continuity requires the two-sided limit to exist and equal the function value.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A differentiable function has positive derivative throughout an interval. What does this imply?
options: Its values are all positive
It is constant
It must be linear
It is increasing on the interval
questions.answer: It is increasing on the interval
questions.explanation: Positive derivative gives increasing function values, regardless of their signs.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A nonnegative rate of water inflow is graphed against time. What does area under the graph represent?
options: The tank's initial volume alone
The elapsed time squared
Total water added over that time
The highest flow rate
questions.answer: Total water added over that time
questions.explanation: Integrating a rate over time gives the accumulated quantity.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A population's growth rate is proportional to its current size with a positive constant. What qualitative behaviour follows?
options: Exponential growth in the ideal model
Constant absolute growth
Linear decline
Immediate extinction
questions.answer: Exponential growth in the ideal model
questions.explanation: The differential equation dP/dt = kP gives exponential growth for positive k.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A matrix has two rows and three columns. Why cannot it be added directly to a three-by-two matrix?
options: Only square matrices can ever be added
Every entry must be positive
Their entries must first be determinants
Matrix addition requires matching dimensions
questions.answer: Matrix addition requires matching dimensions
questions.explanation: Elementwise addition requires corresponding entries in matrices of the same shape.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two events are mutually exclusive. What is impossible in one trial?
options: Their probabilities adding to less than one
Both occurring together
Either event occurring
Neither event occurring
questions.answer: Both occurring together
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events have an empty intersection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A bag contains red and blue counters. You learn the chosen counter is red. What happens to the relevant sample space?
options: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
It expands to all possible bags
Every original outcome remains equally relevant
It contains no outcomes
questions.answer: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
questions.explanation: Conditioning restricts attention to outcomes satisfying the given information.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A proposed solution violates one constraint in a linear programme. How is it classified?
options: A required corner point
Always unbounded
Infeasible
Automatically optimal
questions.answer: Infeasible
questions.explanation: Feasible solutions must satisfy all constraints simultaneously.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A student belongs to A or B, but not both. Which membership condition describes this?
options: Membership in the universal set only
Membership in their symmetric difference
Membership in their intersection
Membership in neither set
questions.answer: Membership in their symmetric difference
questions.explanation: The symmetric difference contains elements belonging to exactly one of the two sets.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two machines act in sequence: the first doubles an input, the second adds three. Why can reversing them change the result?
options: Addition always occurs before multiplication in any real process
Both machines must produce zero
The first machine has no output
The operations need not commute
questions.answer: The operations need not commute
questions.explanation: Doubling after adding three also doubles the added amount, unlike adding it afterward.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A quadratic's discriminant changes from positive to negative as a parameter varies. What changes?
options: Its leading coefficient must become zero
Every coefficient becomes negative
Two distinct real roots become no real roots
No real roots become two distinct real roots
questions.answer: Two distinct real roots become no real roots
questions.explanation: The discriminant's sign determines whether the roots are real and distinct, repeated, or nonreal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A sine equation has one solution in the first quadrant. Why can another occur in the second quadrant?
options: Supplementary angles have equal sine
Sine is one-to-one over a full turn
Cosine is positive in both quadrants
Every angle has the same sine
questions.answer: Supplementary angles have equal sine
questions.explanation: Reflection across the vertical axis preserves the unit-circle y-coordinate.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A complex number is multiplied by its conjugate. Why is the result real and nonnegative?
options: The imaginary part is always zero before multiplication
Conjugation changes its real part's sign
All complex products are nonnegative
It equals the square of its modulus
questions.answer: It equals the square of its modulus
questions.explanation: The imaginary cross terms cancel, leaving the sum of the squared real and imaginary parts.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A geometric sequence has ratio between zero and one. Why can the infinite sum be finite?
options: The terms eventually become negative
Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
There are only finitely many terms
Every term is zero
questions.answer: Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
questions.explanation: For absolute ratio below one, partial sums approach a finite limit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two committee roles are distinct. Why does assigning the same two people in exchanged roles create a different outcome?
options: The role assignment is part of the outcome
The membership becomes a different size
One person disappears
All arrangements are unordered
questions.answer: The role assignment is part of the outcome
questions.explanation: When positions or roles matter, permutations distinguish assignments with the same members.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two points lie on the same line parallel to another line. How do their perpendicular distances to the other line compare?
options: One distance must be zero
Distances depend only on x-coordinate
They are equal
The point farther right is always closer
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Parallel lines remain a constant perpendicular distance apart.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A line touches a circle at one point. How does it relate to the radius through that point?
options: It has the same length as the radius
It is perpendicular to the radius
It is parallel to the radius
It passes through the centre
questions.answer: It is perpendicular to the radius
questions.explanation: The tangent at a circle point is perpendicular to the radius there.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two nonzero vectors have zero dot product. What does this imply?
options: They are parallel in the same direction
They are equal
Their cross product must also be zero
They are perpendicular
questions.answer: They are perpendicular
questions.explanation: The dot product is proportional to the cosine of the angle, which is zero at a right angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two lines in three-dimensional space do not meet and are not parallel. What is possible?
options: They are the same line
Their direction vectors are zero
They are skew
They must lie in one plane
questions.answer: They are skew
questions.explanation: Skew lines are nonparallel, nonintersecting lines in different planes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The graph of absolute value of x has a sharp corner at zero. What is true there?
options: It is continuous but not differentiable
It is differentiable but not continuous
It has an infinite function value
It has the same tangent slope from both sides
questions.answer: It is continuous but not differentiable
questions.explanation: The left and right slopes differ although the function has no discontinuity.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function is increasing but its slope is becoming smaller. Which combination can describe it?
options: Negative first derivative and positive second derivative
Both derivatives negative necessarily
Zero first derivative throughout
Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.answer: Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.explanation: Increasing values require positive slope, while decreasing slope indicates concavity down.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A velocity-time graph has regions above and below the time axis. What does its signed integral represent?
options: Final acceleration
Net displacement
Total distance in every case
Maximum speed
questions.answer: Net displacement
questions.explanation: Positive and negative velocities contribute opposite signed displacements.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: F(x) is the area accumulated under a continuous function f from a fixed starting point to x. What does F'(x) measure?
options: The current value f(x)
The total area squared
Only the starting value of f
Always zero
questions.answer: The current value f(x)
questions.explanation: The derivative of accumulated area recovers the instantaneous integrand.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Matrices A and B can be multiplied in both orders. Why need AB not equal BA?
options: Both products must be undefined
All matrices represent the same transformation
Matrix multiplication generally depends on order
Only negative entries cause noncommutativity
questions.answer: Matrix multiplication generally depends on order
questions.explanation: Composing linear transformations in different orders can give different results.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two linear equations describe the same line. What is their solution set?
options: One point chosen by the larger coefficient
Infinitely many points on that line
No points
Exactly two points
questions.answer: Infinitely many points on that line
questions.explanation: Dependent equations impose the same condition rather than two independent constraints.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two counters are drawn without replacement from a mixed bag. Why can the second colour depend on the first?
options: The colours physically transform
All second draws are independent by definition
The first counter returns automatically
The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.answer: The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.explanation: Removing a counter changes the proportions remaining for the next selection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every value in a data set increases by the same constant. What happens to variance?
options: It becomes zero
It doubles
It stays unchanged
It rises by that constant
questions.answer: It stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The mean shifts by the same amount, leaving deviations from the mean unchanged.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A linear objective is maximised on a bounded polygonal feasible region. Where can at least one optimum be found?
options: At a vertex
Only at the region's centre
Only outside the feasible region
At every point necessarily
questions.answer: At a vertex
questions.explanation: A linear function on a bounded polygon attains an optimum at a vertex, possibly along an entire edge.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: To disprove the statement 'Every positive integer has property P', what is sufficient?
options: Many integers having P
One negative integer lacking P
No tested counterexample
One positive integer lacking P
questions.answer: One positive integer lacking P
questions.explanation: A single counterexample within the stated domain disproves a universal claim.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A piecewise function has equal left and right limits at a joining point, but its assigned value differs. What repairs continuity there?
options: Set the derivative to one without changing values
Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
Change every nearby value to zero
Remove both intervals entirely
questions.answer: Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
questions.explanation: A removable discontinuity is fixed by matching the point value to its existing limit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An upward-opening quadratic has two distinct real roots. Where is it negative?
options: Strictly between the roots
Outside both roots
Everywhere
Nowhere
questions.answer: Strictly between the roots
questions.explanation: The parabola lies below the axis between its crossings and above it outside them.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Multiplying a nonzero complex number by i changes its plane representation how?
options: Reflection only across the real axis
A quarter-turn clockwise with doubled modulus
A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
A doubling of modulus without rotation
questions.answer: A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
questions.explanation: Multiplication by i adds an angle of pi over two and has modulus one.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A series has terms that approach zero. Why does that alone not prove convergence?
options: A zero term forces every later term to vanish
The partial sums may still grow without bound
Every such series is finite
Terms approaching zero must alternate
questions.answer: The partial sums may still grow without bound
questions.explanation: Vanishing terms are necessary but not sufficient; the harmonic series is a standard counterexample.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair coin has produced several heads in independent tosses. Why is tails not made more likely on the next toss?
options: Tails becomes impossible after enough heads
The coin remembers its previous states
A balancing sequence is guaranteed immediately
The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
questions.answer: The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
questions.explanation: Independent trials retain the same probability regardless of previous outcomes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two lines have proportional x and y coefficients but nonproportional constants in their equations. What follows?
options: They intersect at the origin necessarily
They are perpendicular
They are distinct parallel lines
They are identical lines
questions.answer: They are distinct parallel lines
questions.explanation: Matching coefficient ratios give the same direction, while incompatible constants prevent intersection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Three nonzero coplanar vectors in three-dimensional space are considered. What must be true?
options: They are linearly dependent
They are mutually perpendicular
Their pairwise dot products are zero
They all have equal lengths
questions.answer: They are linearly dependent
questions.explanation: A plane through the origin spans at most two independent vector directions.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Three vectors have zero scalar triple product. What geometric conclusion follows?
options: They necessarily form a cube
They are all unit vectors
They are mutually perpendicular and nonzero
They are coplanar or linearly dependent
questions.answer: They are coplanar or linearly dependent
questions.explanation: The scalar triple product measures signed parallelepiped volume, which vanishes for dependence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function oscillates between values near -1 and 1 arbitrarily close to a point without narrowing its range. What happens to its limit there?
options: The limit equals the point's assigned value
No single limit exists
The limit must be zero by averaging
The limit must be one
questions.answer: No single limit exists
questions.explanation: Persistent full-amplitude oscillation prevents values from approaching one number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function is differentiable at an interior point. Which conclusion is guaranteed?
options: It is continuous there
Its derivative is positive there
It is locally linear exactly
It has a local extremum there
questions.answer: It is continuous there
questions.explanation: Differentiability implies continuity, but does not determine slope sign or the presence of an extremum.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For f(x)=x cubed, the derivative is zero at zero. Why is zero not a local maximum or minimum?
options: The derivative is undefined there
The function is constant nearby
The function keeps increasing through it
The function is discontinuous there
questions.answer: The function keeps increasing through it
questions.explanation: A zero derivative alone is insufficient; the function increases on both sides of the stationary point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A continuous odd function is integrated from -a to a. Why is the integral zero?
options: Every antiderivative is constant
Opposite signed contributions cancel
The function must be zero everywhere
The interval has zero length
questions.answer: Opposite signed contributions cancel
questions.explanation: Odd symmetry gives equal-magnitude contributions of opposite sign on symmetric intervals.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In dP/dt = kP(1-P/K), with k and K positive, a population is slightly below K. What does the model predict?
options: It decreases away from K
It immediately jumps to zero
It grows exponentially without limit at all sizes
It increases toward K
questions.answer: It increases toward K
questions.explanation: For 0<P<K the growth rate is positive and becomes smaller near the stable equilibrium K.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: AB equals the identity for square matrices of the same size. What follows?
options: B must equal A
A's determinant is zero
B is the inverse of A
A must have all positive entries
questions.answer: B is the inverse of A
questions.explanation: A square matrix with an inverse product is nonsingular, and B is its inverse.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A square coefficient matrix is invertible. What follows for a linear system with that matrix and any right-hand side?
options: There is exactly one solution
There are always no solutions
There are always infinitely many solutions
Only a zero right-hand side is allowed
questions.answer: There is exactly one solution
questions.explanation: Multiplying by the inverse determines a unique solution vector.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rare condition has a test with some false positives. Why need a positive result not make the condition highly likely?
options: Test accuracy is irrelevant
A positive result proves the condition is absent
Rare conditions cannot be tested
The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.answer: The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.explanation: The posterior probability depends on both test performance and the prior prevalence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two random variables have finite means but are dependent. Which statement still holds?
options: They must have identical distributions
The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
Their variances always add without a covariance term
Their product mean always equals the product of their means
questions.answer: The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
questions.explanation: Linearity of expectation does not require independence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every observation is multiplied by a constant c. Why is variance multiplied by c squared?
options: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
The mean is always unchanged
Variance counts observations without using values
Only negative constants affect variance
questions.answer: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
questions.explanation: Variance averages squared deviations, so scaling values squares the scale factor.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A linear objective is parallel to an edge where it reaches its optimal value on a feasible polygon. What follows?
options: No optimum exists
Only a point outside the polygon is optimal
Every feasible point on that edge is optimal
Only its midpoint is optimal
questions.answer: Every feasible point on that edge is optimal
questions.explanation: The objective is constant along that edge, producing multiple optimal solutions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A trolley moves forward while its velocity-time graph slopes downward. What is happening?
options: It is slowing down
It is moving backward
Its acceleration is zero
Its distance travelled is decreasing
questions.answer: It is slowing down
questions.explanation: A downward slope means negative acceleration; with positive velocity this reduces speed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A passenger leans forward when a bus brakes. Why?
options: The seat increases the passenger's speed
The passenger loses mass
The passenger's body tends to keep moving
A forward force from gravity appears
questions.answer: The passenger's body tends to keep moving
questions.explanation: Inertia resists the change from the body's original forward motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A box remains stationary while you push it gently on a rough floor. What balances your push?
options: An upward force from the floor
Static friction
Kinetic friction
The box's weight alone
questions.answer: Static friction
questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to oppose the push until its limiting value is reached.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two carts initially at rest push apart on a frictionless track. What must their momenta do?
options: Have equal velocities
Point in the same direction
Increase the total momentum
Add to zero
questions.answer: Add to zero
questions.explanation: With no external horizontal force, total momentum remains its initial value of zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone moves at constant speed in a circle. Why is it accelerating?
options: Its speed must be increasing
Its kinetic energy must increase
Its velocity changes direction
Its mass changes continuously
questions.answer: Its velocity changes direction
questions.explanation: Velocity includes direction, which changes throughout circular motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical springs support equal loads, one singly and two in parallel. Which arrangement stretches less?
options: The parallel pair
The single spring
Both stretch equally
Neither arrangement can stretch
questions.answer: The parallel pair
questions.explanation: The parallel springs share the load, increasing the effective stiffness.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sealed hydraulic system has connected pistons of different areas. Why can the larger piston exert more force?
options: Pressure must be larger at the larger piston
The fluid creates extra energy
The smaller piston has no displacement
The same pressure acts over a larger area
questions.answer: The same pressure acts over a larger area
questions.explanation: Transmitted pressure is the same at equal depth, while force equals pressure times area.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ice is melting at its melting point under constant pressure. Why can heat enter without raising temperature?
options: All added energy becomes light
Energy changes the phase
The ice has stopped absorbing energy
Its specific heat becomes zero
questions.answer: Energy changes the phase
questions.explanation: Latent heat changes intermolecular arrangement rather than increasing temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Gas expands and pushes a piston. What energy transfer occurs through the moving piston?
options: The gas does work on its surroundings
The surroundings always do positive work on the gas
The gas necessarily gains internal energy
No energy crosses the boundary
questions.answer: The gas does work on its surroundings
questions.explanation: An outward force acting through the piston's displacement transfers energy as work.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At the extreme position of a mass on an ideal spring, which quantity is zero?
options: Its acceleration magnitude
Its elastic potential energy
Its instantaneous speed
Its restoring force
questions.answer: Its instantaneous speed
questions.explanation: The mass reverses direction at the extreme, where its instantaneous velocity is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
