questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: A naturalistic study records genuine settings, but people know they are watched. What limitation remains?
options: Observation becomes a randomised experiment automatically
No behaviour can be recorded outside a laboratory
Awareness of observation can alter behaviour
A natural setting guarantees completely unaffected behaviour
questions.answer: Awareness of observation can alter behaviour
questions.explanation: Realistic settings can improve relevance, but observer awareness and measurement choices still affect validity.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: School records show a change in behaviour after a policy, but recording practices changed at the same time. What must be separated?
options: A causal effect that is already proven by chronology
Change in behaviour from change in how it was recorded
The school's name from its postal address only
The number of archived pages from their paper size
questions.answer: Change in behaviour from change in how it was recorded
questions.explanation: An apparent historical trend can partly reflect changes in measurement rather than the underlying behaviour.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: One study reports a correlation of −0.90 and another +0.40. Which has the stronger linear association?
options: The first, because strength depends on magnitude rather than sign
The second, because positive always means stronger
Both, because every nonzero correlation has equal strength
Neither, because negative correlations are impossible
questions.answer: The first, because strength depends on magnitude rather than sign
questions.explanation: The absolute coefficient is larger in the first study; the sign indicates direction.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: A dataset follows a strong curved pattern but has a linear correlation near zero. What follows?
options: The variables must be statistically independent
The curved pattern must be a graphing error
A zero coefficient proves a negative causal effect
Near-zero linear correlation need not mean no relationship
questions.answer: Near-zero linear correlation need not mean no relationship
questions.explanation: A linear correlation measures linear association and can miss systematic nonlinear patterns.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: Two studies claim to measure aggression, but one counts interruptions and the other physical acts. Why compare their definitions before combining results?
options: Any count is automatically a complete measure of aggression
Different definitions prove both studies have no value
They may measure different aspects of the broader concept
The same label guarantees identical measurement
questions.answer: They may measure different aspects of the broader concept
questions.explanation: Operational definitions determine what observations represent a construct and therefore affect interpretation and comparability.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: A proposed study conceals its purpose to reduce response bias. Why is scientific usefulness alone insufficient to justify the concealment?
options: A useful aim guarantees that all methods are acceptable
Ethical review must consider necessity, harm, consent arrangements and debriefing
Concealment automatically makes every result invalid
Avoiding response bias removes every duty to participants
questions.answer: Ethical review must consider necessity, harm, consent arrangements and debriefing
questions.explanation: Methodological benefits must be weighed alongside participants' rights and protections.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: A teacher says a research survey is optional but implies that refusal will damage a student's standing. What ethical issue arises?
options: The pressure undermines genuinely voluntary participation
The word optional removes all coercive influence
Survey length alone determines whether consent is free
Refusal proves that the student lacks research ability
questions.answer: The pressure undermines genuinely voluntary participation
questions.explanation: Consent can be compromised by pressure from someone with authority even when participation is formally described as optional.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: Two cells share the same DNA sequence but express different genes after different regulatory signals. What does this show?
options: Every difference in gene expression requires a new mutation
The cells cannot belong to the same organism
Environmental and regulatory influences cannot affect gene activity
Gene activity can differ without a difference in DNA sequence
questions.answer: Gene activity can differ without a difference in DNA sequence
questions.explanation: Regulation, including epigenetic mechanisms, can alter expression without changing the underlying base sequence.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: A conditioned response declines during extinction but briefly returns after a rest. Why is extinction not simply erasure of all prior learning?
options: Recovery proves that no extinction occurred
All learned responses must grow continuously without interruption
The earlier association can still influence responding under changed conditions
The original stimulus was never learned
questions.answer: The earlier association can still influence responding under changed conditions
questions.explanation: Spontaneous recovery indicates that reduced responding after extinction does not necessarily mean the original learning has vanished.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: One learner improves through rewards for closer attempts; another copies a demonstration. Why distinguish the methods?
options: Observing a model is the definition of negative punishment
The first emphasises consequences of successive approximations; the second observation of a model
Both require identical experience of direct rewards
Neither can influence a learned skill
questions.answer: The first emphasises consequences of successive approximations; the second observation of a model
questions.explanation: Shaping and observational learning describe different mechanisms that may also operate together.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: A familiar shortcut works well in one setting but fails when the underlying conditions change. What is the sound conclusion?
options: Its usefulness depends on how well its assumptions fit the setting
The shortcut is therefore useless in every setting
Success once guarantees success in every later problem
Heuristics always outperform systematic analysis
questions.answer: Its usefulness depends on how well its assumptions fit the setting
questions.explanation: Efficient heuristics can be valuable but are vulnerable when cues no longer predict outcomes reliably.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: A test predicts outcomes in its norming group but performs poorly in another group with different experiences. What needs evaluation?
options: Only whether the printed test title is unchanged
Whether identical scoring guarantees identical meaning
Whether the original group can be ignored in every analysis
Validity and fairness for the intended population
questions.answer: Validity and fairness for the intended population
questions.explanation: Evidence of validity is tied to the interpretation, purpose and population, not simply to a test's existence.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: Two people with similar inherited predispositions develop differently under different experiences. Which explanation best accommodates this?
options: Experience requires genes to have no influence
Different outcomes prove that neither genes nor environment matters
Development can reflect interactions between inherited factors and environment
Genes determine every outcome independently of experience
questions.answer: Development can reflect interactions between inherited factors and environment
questions.explanation: Biological predispositions and experience can work together in producing individual differences.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: A vivid, confidently reported memory changes in details across repeated accounts. What does this indicate?
options: Vivid memories cannot be reconstructed
Subjective vividness does not guarantee accuracy
Confidence makes every detail objectively correct
Changing an account proves deliberate dishonesty in every case
questions.answer: Subjective vividness does not guarantee accuracy
questions.explanation: Emotional or vivid recollection can still be affected by reconstruction and later information.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: Identical twins raised apart show similarities, but their environments were not assigned randomly. What should a careful interpretation avoid?
options: Treating similarity as proof that environment has no influence
Considering inherited influences at all
Comparing similarities with other evidence
Acknowledging that multiple influences may operate
questions.answer: Treating similarity as proof that environment has no influence
questions.explanation: Twin evidence can inform genetic contributions without excluding environmental similarities, selection or gene–environment processes.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: Workers change behaviour after researchers begin observing them, even without the planned treatment. What should the study consider?
options: Proof that the planned treatment caused every change
A guarantee that awareness never affects behaviour
The impossibility of measuring workplace behaviour
Effects of observation and expectations as alternative influences
questions.answer: Effects of observation and expectations as alternative influences
questions.explanation: Participation and attention may affect behaviour, so they must be considered when attributing change to a treatment.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: People in lower-control jobs report more stress-related problems, but their working and living conditions also differ. What conclusion is justified?
options: Job conditions cannot affect stress
The association rules out all environmental explanations
Perceived control is a candidate influence, but the association alone isolates no single cause
Control is proven to be the only cause
questions.answer: Perceived control is a candidate influence, but the association alone isolates no single cause
questions.explanation: Other correlated conditions can contribute to the relationship, so stronger designs are needed to isolate causal effects.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Every member of set A is also in B, but B has extra members. Which statement follows?
options: A equals B
A is a proper subset of B
A and B are disjoint
B is a proper subset of A
questions.answer: A is a proper subset of B
questions.explanation: A is contained in B without being equal to it.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A real-valued rule contains the term 1/(x-3). Which input must be excluded?
questions.explanation: At x = 3 the denominator is zero, so the expression is undefined.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: The graph of y = f(x) is changed to y = f(x)+4. What changes?
options: All slopes double
The domain necessarily shrinks
Every point moves upward by four units
Every point moves right by four units
questions.answer: Every point moves upward by four units
questions.explanation: Adding a constant to the output produces a vertical translation.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: An inequality is multiplied on both sides by a negative number. What must change?
options: The inequality direction reverses
Both sides become zero
The inequality becomes an equality
Only the larger side is multiplied
questions.answer: The inequality direction reverses
questions.explanation: Multiplication by a negative number reverses order on the number line.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: An angle is increased by one full turn. What happens to its sine and cosine?
options: Both change sign
Sine doubles while cosine stays fixed
Both become zero
Both stay the same
questions.answer: Both stay the same
questions.explanation: Sine and cosine are periodic with a full-turn period.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A sequence increases by the same amount at every step. What feature does its term-number graph have?
options: A repeating circle
A constant slope
A continuously doubling slope
A vertical line
questions.answer: A constant slope
questions.explanation: A constant difference makes the term a linear function of its index.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A positive quantity grows by the same percentage each year. Which model is appropriate?
options: Geometric growth
A constant additive increase
A fixed value with no change
A sequence with constant second difference necessarily
questions.answer: Geometric growth
questions.explanation: Repeated multiplication by a fixed factor produces a geometric sequence.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: In expanding (1+x)^n for a positive integer n, why is the constant term 1?
options: The exponents must all be zero
All coefficients are equal to one
It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
Every term contains x
questions.answer: It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
questions.explanation: Only the product of all constant choices contributes to the x-to-the-zero term.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two distinct nonvertical lines have the same slope. What follows?
options: They must pass through the origin
They are parallel
They are perpendicular
They meet exactly once
questions.answer: They are parallel
questions.explanation: Equal slopes give the same direction; distinct intercepts keep the lines separate.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two circles subtend the same central angle. Why is the intercepted arc longer on the larger circle?
options: The angle necessarily becomes larger on the larger circle
Arc length is independent of radius
The arc becomes a diameter in every larger circle
Arc length is proportional to radius for a fixed angle
questions.answer: Arc length is proportional to radius for a fixed angle
questions.explanation: The relation between arc length, radius and angle makes arc length scale with radius when angle is fixed.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two vectors have equal magnitudes and opposite directions. What is their sum?
options: A unit vector
A scalar equal to their common magnitude
The zero vector
A vector twice as long
questions.answer: The zero vector
questions.explanation: Opposite equal vectors cancel component by component.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Values of f(x) approach 5 as x approaches 2, but f(2) is defined as 9. What is the limit at 2?
options: It must not exist
questions.explanation: A limit concerns nearby values, not the separately assigned value at the point.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A graph has a jump at x = a. Why is the function not continuous there?
options: Its value must be negative
Its slope must be positive
Its domain must contain only integers
Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
questions.answer: Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
questions.explanation: Continuity requires the two-sided limit to exist and equal the function value.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A differentiable function has positive derivative throughout an interval. What does this imply?
options: It must be linear
It is increasing on the interval
Its values are all positive
It is constant
questions.answer: It is increasing on the interval
questions.explanation: Positive derivative gives increasing function values, regardless of their signs.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A nonnegative rate of water inflow is graphed against time. What does area under the graph represent?
options: Total water added over that time
The highest flow rate
The tank's initial volume alone
The elapsed time squared
questions.answer: Total water added over that time
questions.explanation: Integrating a rate over time gives the accumulated quantity.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A population's growth rate is proportional to its current size with a positive constant. What qualitative behaviour follows?
options: Linear decline
Immediate extinction
Exponential growth in the ideal model
Constant absolute growth
questions.answer: Exponential growth in the ideal model
questions.explanation: The differential equation dP/dt = kP gives exponential growth for positive k.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A continuous normal distribution is symmetric about its mean. What proportion lies above the mean?
options: A proportion determined only by its standard deviation
One half
All of it
None of it
questions.answer: One half
questions.explanation: Symmetry divides the total probability equally on either side, with zero probability at one exact value.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two events are mutually exclusive. What is impossible in one trial?
options: Either event occurring
Neither event occurring
Their probabilities adding to less than one
Both occurring together
questions.answer: Both occurring together
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events have an empty intersection.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A bag contains red and blue counters. You learn the chosen counter is red. What happens to the relevant sample space?
options: Every original outcome remains equally relevant
It contains no outcomes
It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
It expands to all possible bags
questions.answer: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
questions.explanation: Conditioning restricts attention to outcomes satisfying the given information.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: For a continuous random variable, probability over an interval is represented by what feature of its density graph?
options: Area over that interval
The value at just the left endpoint
The curve's total length
The number of turning points
questions.answer: Area over that interval
questions.explanation: Density accumulates into probability through area, rather than a single graph height.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A student belongs to A or B, but not both. Which membership condition describes this?
options: Membership in their intersection
Membership in neither set
Membership in the universal set only
Membership in their symmetric difference
questions.answer: Membership in their symmetric difference
questions.explanation: The symmetric difference contains elements belonging to exactly one of the two sets.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two machines act in sequence: the first doubles an input, the second adds three. Why can reversing them change the result?
options: The first machine has no output
The operations need not commute
Addition always occurs before multiplication in any real process
Both machines must produce zero
questions.answer: The operations need not commute
questions.explanation: Doubling after adding three also doubles the added amount, unlike adding it afterward.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A quadratic's discriminant changes from positive to negative as a parameter varies. What changes?
options: Two distinct real roots become no real roots
No real roots become two distinct real roots
Its leading coefficient must become zero
Every coefficient becomes negative
questions.answer: Two distinct real roots become no real roots
questions.explanation: The discriminant's sign determines whether the roots are real and distinct, repeated, or nonreal.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A sine equation has one solution in the first quadrant. Why can another occur in the second quadrant?
options: Cosine is positive in both quadrants
Every angle has the same sine
Supplementary angles have equal sine
Sine is one-to-one over a full turn
questions.answer: Supplementary angles have equal sine
questions.explanation: Reflection across the vertical axis preserves the unit-circle y-coordinate.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A complex number is multiplied by its conjugate. Why is the result real and nonnegative?
options: All complex products are nonnegative
It equals the square of its modulus
The imaginary part is always zero before multiplication
Conjugation changes its real part's sign
questions.answer: It equals the square of its modulus
questions.explanation: The imaginary cross terms cancel, leaving the sum of the squared real and imaginary parts.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A geometric sequence has ratio between zero and one. Why can the infinite sum be finite?
options: There are only finitely many terms
Every term is zero
The terms eventually become negative
Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
questions.answer: Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
questions.explanation: For absolute ratio below one, partial sums approach a finite limit.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two committee roles are distinct. Why does assigning the same two people in exchanged roles create a different outcome?
options: One person disappears
All arrangements are unordered
The role assignment is part of the outcome
The membership becomes a different size
questions.answer: The role assignment is part of the outcome
questions.explanation: When positions or roles matter, permutations distinguish assignments with the same members.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two points lie on the same line parallel to another line. How do their perpendicular distances to the other line compare?
options: They are equal
The point farther right is always closer
One distance must be zero
Distances depend only on x-coordinate
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Parallel lines remain a constant perpendicular distance apart.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A line touches a circle at one point. How does it relate to the radius through that point?
options: It is parallel to the radius
It passes through the centre
It has the same length as the radius
It is perpendicular to the radius
questions.answer: It is perpendicular to the radius
questions.explanation: The tangent at a circle point is perpendicular to the radius there.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two nonzero vectors have zero dot product. What does this imply?
options: Their cross product must also be zero
They are perpendicular
They are parallel in the same direction
They are equal
questions.answer: They are perpendicular
questions.explanation: The dot product is proportional to the cosine of the angle, which is zero at a right angle.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two lines in three-dimensional space do not meet and are not parallel. What is possible?
options: They are skew
They must lie in one plane
They are the same line
Their direction vectors are zero
questions.answer: They are skew
questions.explanation: Skew lines are nonparallel, nonintersecting lines in different planes.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: The graph of absolute value of x has a sharp corner at zero. What is true there?
options: It has an infinite function value
It has the same tangent slope from both sides
It is continuous but not differentiable
It is differentiable but not continuous
questions.answer: It is continuous but not differentiable
questions.explanation: The left and right slopes differ although the function has no discontinuity.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A function is increasing but its slope is becoming smaller. Which combination can describe it?
options: Zero first derivative throughout
Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
Negative first derivative and positive second derivative
Both derivatives negative necessarily
questions.answer: Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.explanation: Increasing values require positive slope, while decreasing slope indicates concavity down.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A velocity-time graph has regions above and below the time axis. What does its signed integral represent?
options: Total distance in every case
Maximum speed
Final acceleration
Net displacement
questions.answer: Net displacement
questions.explanation: Positive and negative velocities contribute opposite signed displacements.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: F(x) is the area accumulated under a continuous function f from a fixed starting point to x. What does F'(x) measure?
options: Only the starting value of f
Always zero
The current value f(x)
The total area squared
questions.answer: The current value f(x)
questions.explanation: The derivative of accumulated area recovers the instantaneous integrand.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A rational function with distinct linear factors in its denominator is split into simpler fractions. Why can this help integration?
options: Each simpler term may have a known antiderivative
The operation changes the value of the function
All resulting integrals must be polynomials
The denominator's zeros cease to matter
questions.answer: Each simpler term may have a known antiderivative
questions.explanation: An algebraically equivalent decomposition can expose standard integrals while retaining the original domain restrictions.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two linear equations describe the same line. What is their solution set?
options: No points
Exactly two points
One point chosen by the larger coefficient
Infinitely many points on that line
questions.answer: Infinitely many points on that line
questions.explanation: Dependent equations impose the same condition rather than two independent constraints.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two counters are drawn without replacement from a mixed bag. Why can the second colour depend on the first?
options: The first counter returns automatically
The bag's composition changes after the first draw
The colours physically transform
All second draws are independent by definition
questions.answer: The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.explanation: Removing a counter changes the proportions remaining for the next selection.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Every value in a data set increases by the same constant. What happens to variance?
options: It stays unchanged
It rises by that constant
It becomes zero
It doubles
questions.answer: It stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The mean shifts by the same amount, leaving deviations from the mean unchanged.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: An online school poll is answered only by students who volunteer. Why may a huge response count still give a biased estimate?
options: Every volunteer must give an incorrect response
The arithmetic mean cannot be calculated for volunteers
Volunteers may systematically differ from nonrespondents
Large samples always create bias automatically
questions.answer: Volunteers may systematically differ from nonrespondents
questions.explanation: More observations do not remove a selection mechanism that underrepresents parts of the target population.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: To disprove the statement 'Every positive integer has property P', what is sufficient?
options: No tested counterexample
One positive integer lacking P
Many integers having P
One negative integer lacking P
questions.answer: One positive integer lacking P
questions.explanation: A single counterexample within the stated domain disproves a universal claim.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A piecewise function has equal left and right limits at a joining point, but its assigned value differs. What repairs continuity there?
options: Change every nearby value to zero
Remove both intervals entirely
Set the derivative to one without changing values
Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
questions.answer: Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
questions.explanation: A removable discontinuity is fixed by matching the point value to its existing limit.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: An upward-opening quadratic has two distinct real roots. Where is it negative?
options: Everywhere
Nowhere
Strictly between the roots
Outside both roots
questions.answer: Strictly between the roots
questions.explanation: The parabola lies below the axis between its crossings and above it outside them.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Multiplying a nonzero complex number by i changes its plane representation how?
options: A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
A doubling of modulus without rotation
Reflection only across the real axis
A quarter-turn clockwise with doubled modulus
questions.answer: A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
questions.explanation: Multiplication by i adds an angle of pi over two and has modulus one.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A proof shows P(n) implies P(n+2) and checks only P(1). Why is that insufficient to establish P(n) for every positive integer?
options: It proves even cases but never odd ones
An implication can never be used in induction
P(1) automatically checks P(2)
It may establish odd cases while leaving even cases unproved
questions.answer: It may establish odd cases while leaving even cases unproved
questions.explanation: A step of two preserves parity, so separate starting cases or a different argument are needed to cover both chains.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A fair coin has produced several heads in independent tosses. Why is tails not made more likely on the next toss?
options: A balancing sequence is guaranteed immediately
The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
Tails becomes impossible after enough heads
The coin remembers its previous states
questions.answer: The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
questions.explanation: Independent trials retain the same probability regardless of previous outcomes.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two lines have proportional x and y coefficients but nonproportional constants in their equations. What follows?
options: They are distinct parallel lines
They are identical lines
They intersect at the origin necessarily
They are perpendicular
questions.answer: They are distinct parallel lines
questions.explanation: Matching coefficient ratios give the same direction, while incompatible constants prevent intersection.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A differentiable one-to-one function has a nonzero derivative at a point. Why is its inverse locally steep when the original is locally shallow?
options: Their derivatives add to zero
The inverse's derivative depends only on its intercept
Their corresponding derivatives are reciprocals
Their derivatives must be equal
questions.answer: Their corresponding derivatives are reciprocals
questions.explanation: The inverse reverses the input-output change, giving the reciprocal derivative where the original derivative is nonzero.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Three vectors have zero scalar triple product. What geometric conclusion follows?
options: They are mutually perpendicular and nonzero
They are coplanar or linearly dependent
They necessarily form a cube
They are all unit vectors
questions.answer: They are coplanar or linearly dependent
questions.explanation: The scalar triple product measures signed parallelepiped volume, which vanishes for dependence.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A function oscillates between values near -1 and 1 arbitrarily close to a point without narrowing its range. What happens to its limit there?
options: The limit must be zero by averaging
The limit must be one
The limit equals the point's assigned value
No single limit exists
questions.answer: No single limit exists
questions.explanation: Persistent full-amplitude oscillation prevents values from approaching one number.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A function is differentiable at an interior point. Which conclusion is guaranteed?
options: It is locally linear exactly
It has a local extremum there
It is continuous there
Its derivative is positive there
questions.answer: It is continuous there
questions.explanation: Differentiability implies continuity, but does not determine slope sign or the presence of an extremum.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: For f(x)=x cubed, the derivative is zero at zero. Why is zero not a local maximum or minimum?
options: The function keeps increasing through it
The function is discontinuous there
The derivative is undefined there
The function is constant nearby
questions.answer: The function keeps increasing through it
questions.explanation: A zero derivative alone is insufficient; the function increases on both sides of the stationary point.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A continuous odd function is integrated from -a to a. Why is the integral zero?
options: The function must be zero everywhere
The interval has zero length
Every antiderivative is constant
Opposite signed contributions cancel
questions.answer: Opposite signed contributions cancel
questions.explanation: Odd symmetry gives equal-magnitude contributions of opposite sign on symmetric intervals.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: In dP/dt = kP(1-P/K), with k and K positive, a population is slightly below K. What does the model predict?
options: It grows exponentially without limit at all sizes
It increases toward K
It decreases away from K
It immediately jumps to zero
questions.answer: It increases toward K
questions.explanation: For 0<P<K the growth rate is positive and becomes smaller near the stable equilibrium K.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A function changes sign across a vertical asymptote. Why does this not guarantee a root between the endpoints?
options: Continuity on the whole interval is missing
A sign change never gives any information
The intermediate value theorem requires differentiability everywhere
An asymptote must itself be a zero
questions.answer: Continuity on the whole interval is missing
questions.explanation: The intermediate value theorem requires continuity; a discontinuity can separate opposite signs without a zero.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A proof assumes a proposed claim is false and derives an impossibility using valid premises. What follows about the claim?
options: It is true only for the example used first
No conclusion is possible from any contradiction
It must be true under those premises
It must be false because it was assumed false
questions.answer: It must be true under those premises
questions.explanation: If the negation leads logically to a contradiction with valid premises, the negation cannot hold.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A rare condition has a test with some false positives. Why need a positive result not make the condition highly likely?
options: Rare conditions cannot be tested
The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
Test accuracy is irrelevant
A positive result proves the condition is absent
questions.answer: The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.explanation: The posterior probability depends on both test performance and the prior prevalence.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Two random variables have finite means but are dependent. Which statement still holds?
options: Their variances always add without a covariance term
Their product mean always equals the product of their means
They must have identical distributions
The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
questions.answer: The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
questions.explanation: Linearity of expectation does not require independence.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: Every observation is multiplied by a constant c. Why is variance multiplied by c squared?
options: Variance counts observations without using values
Only negative constants affect variance
Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
The mean is always unchanged
questions.answer: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
questions.explanation: Variance averages squared deviations, so scaling values squares the scale factor.

questions.subject: Analysis & Approaches
questions.q: A short Maclaurin polynomial matches a function closely near zero but poorly at a distant input. Why is this unsurprising?
options: Omitted higher-order terms may matter away from the expansion point
Matching derivatives at one point guarantees exact global equality
The function must have changed its formula
All polynomial approximations are equally accurate everywhere
questions.answer: Omitted higher-order terms may matter away from the expansion point
questions.explanation: A finite local expansion need not control error far away; higher-order contributions and convergence restrictions matter.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A survey measures a random sample of students to estimate the whole school's mean journey time. What is the sample mean used as?
options: The population size
Proof that all journeys take equally long
An estimate of the population mean
A guaranteed exact value for every student's journey
questions.answer: An estimate of the population mean
questions.explanation: A sample statistic provides an estimate of a population parameter, with sampling uncertainty.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A real-valued rule contains the term 1/(x-3). Which input must be excluded?
questions.explanation: At x = 3 the denominator is zero, so the expression is undefined.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: The graph of y = f(x) is changed to y = f(x)+4. What changes?
options: Every point moves right by four units
All slopes double
The domain necessarily shrinks
Every point moves upward by four units
questions.answer: Every point moves upward by four units
questions.explanation: Adding a constant to the output produces a vertical translation.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: An inequality is multiplied on both sides by a negative number. What must change?
options: Only the larger side is multiplied
The inequality direction reverses
Both sides become zero
The inequality becomes an equality
questions.answer: The inequality direction reverses
questions.explanation: Multiplication by a negative number reverses order on the number line.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: An angle is increased by one full turn. What happens to its sine and cosine?
options: Both stay the same
Both change sign
Sine doubles while cosine stays fixed
Both become zero
questions.answer: Both stay the same
questions.explanation: Sine and cosine are periodic with a full-turn period.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A sequence increases by the same amount at every step. What feature does its term-number graph have?
options: A vertical line
A repeating circle
A constant slope
A continuously doubling slope
questions.answer: A constant slope
questions.explanation: A constant difference makes the term a linear function of its index.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A positive quantity grows by the same percentage each year. Which model is appropriate?
options: A sequence with constant second difference necessarily
Geometric growth
A constant additive increase
A fixed value with no change
questions.answer: Geometric growth
questions.explanation: Repeated multiplication by a fixed factor produces a geometric sequence.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Equal deposits earn the same positive interest rate. Why does depositing at the start rather than end of each period build a larger final balance?
options: The nominal deposit amounts become larger
Interest stops applying to later deposits
The rate must become negative
Each deposit earns interest for an additional period
questions.answer: Each deposit earns interest for an additional period
questions.explanation: Earlier deposits have more time to accumulate interest, assuming the same payment schedule shifted earlier.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two distinct nonvertical lines have the same slope. What follows?
options: They meet exactly once
They must pass through the origin
They are parallel
They are perpendicular
questions.answer: They are parallel
questions.explanation: Equal slopes give the same direction; distinct intercepts keep the lines separate.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two routes have the same number of road segments but different total travel times. Which network feature is needed to compare journey times?
options: Edge weights representing time
The order in which the towns are alphabetised
Only the number of vertices
A requirement that every edge have weight one
questions.answer: Edge weights representing time
questions.explanation: Summing time weights measures journey cost; counting segments alone ignores unequal durations.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two vectors have equal magnitudes and opposite directions. What is their sum?
options: A vector twice as long
A unit vector
A scalar equal to their common magnitude
The zero vector
questions.answer: The zero vector
questions.explanation: Opposite equal vectors cancel component by component.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A scatter plot shows taller plants tending to have greater mass. What does a positive association establish by itself?
options: Mass cannot influence any other measurement
Higher values tend to occur together
Height alone has been proved to cause all mass differences
Every plant lies exactly on one straight line
questions.answer: Higher values tend to occur together
questions.explanation: Association describes the pattern in paired observations and alone does not establish causation.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A graph has a jump at x = a. Why is the function not continuous there?
options: Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
Its value must be negative
Its slope must be positive
Its domain must contain only integers
questions.answer: Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
questions.explanation: Continuity requires the two-sided limit to exist and equal the function value.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A differentiable function has positive derivative throughout an interval. What does this imply?
options: It is constant
It must be linear
It is increasing on the interval
Its values are all positive
questions.answer: It is increasing on the interval
questions.explanation: Positive derivative gives increasing function values, regardless of their signs.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A nonnegative rate of water inflow is graphed against time. What does area under the graph represent?
options: The elapsed time squared
Total water added over that time
The highest flow rate
The tank's initial volume alone
questions.answer: Total water added over that time
questions.explanation: Integrating a rate over time gives the accumulated quantity.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A population's growth rate is proportional to its current size with a positive constant. What qualitative behaviour follows?
options: Constant absolute growth
Linear decline
Immediate extinction
Exponential growth in the ideal model
questions.answer: Exponential growth in the ideal model
questions.explanation: The differential equation dP/dt = kP gives exponential growth for positive k.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A matrix has two rows and three columns. Why cannot it be added directly to a three-by-two matrix?
options: Every entry must be positive
Their entries must first be determinants
Matrix addition requires matching dimensions
Only square matrices can ever be added
questions.answer: Matrix addition requires matching dimensions
questions.explanation: Elementwise addition requires corresponding entries in matrices of the same shape.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two events are mutually exclusive. What is impossible in one trial?
options: Both occurring together
Either event occurring
Neither event occurring
Their probabilities adding to less than one
questions.answer: Both occurring together
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events have an empty intersection.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A bag contains red and blue counters. You learn the chosen counter is red. What happens to the relevant sample space?
options: It expands to all possible bags
Every original outcome remains equally relevant
It contains no outcomes
It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
questions.answer: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
questions.explanation: Conditioning restricts attention to outcomes satisfying the given information.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A linear model predicts steady growth from a limited observed interval. Why should far-future predictions be treated cautiously?
options: All data outside the interval are known to be false
The observed relationship may not continue outside the data range
A straight line cannot fit any real data
Extrapolation always predicts a negative value
questions.answer: The observed relationship may not continue outside the data range
questions.explanation: Extrapolation assumes the model remains suitable beyond the observations, where conditions can change.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A plot of log y against x is a straight line with positive slope. Which model for positive y is supported?
options: Exponential growth in x
A fixed additive increase in y per unit x
A constant value of y
A negative probability model
questions.answer: Exponential growth in x
questions.explanation: Taking logarithms turns an exponential relationship into a linear one; positive slope represents growth.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two machines act in sequence: the first doubles an input, the second adds three. Why can reversing them change the result?
options: Both machines must produce zero
The first machine has no output
The operations need not commute
Addition always occurs before multiplication in any real process
questions.answer: The operations need not commute
questions.explanation: Doubling after adding three also doubles the added amount, unlike adding it afterward.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A quadratic's discriminant changes from positive to negative as a parameter varies. What changes?
options: Every coefficient becomes negative
Two distinct real roots become no real roots
No real roots become two distinct real roots
Its leading coefficient must become zero
questions.answer: Two distinct real roots become no real roots
questions.explanation: The discriminant's sign determines whether the roots are real and distinct, repeated, or nonreal.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A sine equation has one solution in the first quadrant. Why can another occur in the second quadrant?
options: Sine is one-to-one over a full turn
Cosine is positive in both quadrants
Every angle has the same sine
Supplementary angles have equal sine
questions.answer: Supplementary angles have equal sine
questions.explanation: Reflection across the vertical axis preserves the unit-circle y-coordinate.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A complex number is multiplied by its conjugate. Why is the result real and nonnegative?
options: Conjugation changes its real part's sign
All complex products are nonnegative
It equals the square of its modulus
The imaginary part is always zero before multiplication
questions.answer: It equals the square of its modulus
questions.explanation: The imaginary cross terms cancel, leaving the sum of the squared real and imaginary parts.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A geometric sequence has ratio between zero and one. Why can the infinite sum be finite?
options: Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
There are only finitely many terms
Every term is zero
The terms eventually become negative
questions.answer: Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
questions.explanation: For absolute ratio below one, partial sums approach a finite limit.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two clinics are moved closer together but remain distinct. What geometric construction still separates locations equally distant from them?
options: A line parallel to that segment through one clinic
A circle whose radius must be the whole map width
The segment joining the clinics itself
The perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them
questions.answer: The perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them
questions.explanation: Equal-distance locations for two distinct planar points lie on their perpendicular bisector.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two points lie on the same line parallel to another line. How do their perpendicular distances to the other line compare?
options: Distances depend only on x-coordinate
They are equal
The point farther right is always closer
One distance must be zero
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Parallel lines remain a constant perpendicular distance apart.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A line touches a circle at one point. How does it relate to the radius through that point?
options: It is perpendicular to the radius
It is parallel to the radius
It passes through the centre
It has the same length as the radius
questions.answer: It is perpendicular to the radius
questions.explanation: The tangent at a circle point is perpendicular to the radius there.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two nonzero vectors have zero dot product. What does this imply?
options: They are equal
Their cross product must also be zero
They are perpendicular
They are parallel in the same direction
questions.answer: They are perpendicular
questions.explanation: The dot product is proportional to the cosine of the angle, which is zero at a right angle.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A network connects all towns with minimum total edge weight and contains a cycle. Why is the cycle incompatible with a minimum tree when all weights are positive?
options: Every minimum network must visit towns in alphabetical order
Removing a cycle edge preserves connectivity and lowers weight
A cycle can never connect any towns
Removing any edge from any graph preserves connectivity
questions.answer: Removing a cycle edge preserves connectivity and lowers weight
questions.explanation: A cycle provides redundant connectivity; deleting one of its edges leaves a connected graph with smaller positive total weight.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Residuals from a fitted straight line form a clear curve against the predictor. What does this suggest?
options: The linear fit must be exact
Residuals should always form a curve for a correct linear model
The dependent variable must be categorical
A straight-line model may miss systematic structure
questions.answer: A straight-line model may miss systematic structure
questions.explanation: A patterned residual plot indicates remaining structure rather than random scatter around a suitable fit.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A function is increasing but its slope is becoming smaller. Which combination can describe it?
options: Both derivatives negative necessarily
Zero first derivative throughout
Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
Negative first derivative and positive second derivative
questions.answer: Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.explanation: Increasing values require positive slope, while decreasing slope indicates concavity down.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A velocity-time graph has regions above and below the time axis. What does its signed integral represent?
options: Net displacement
Total distance in every case
Maximum speed
Final acceleration
questions.answer: Net displacement
questions.explanation: Positive and negative velocities contribute opposite signed displacements.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A chi-squared test compares observed counts in categories with expected counts under independence. What kind of departure gives evidence against independence?
options: Every category having any nonzero count
Expected counts being written as decimals
The table having more than one row
Observed counts differing substantially from the independence pattern
questions.answer: Observed counts differing substantially from the independence pattern
questions.explanation: The test aggregates discrepancies between observations and the counts predicted by independence.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Matrices A and B can be multiplied in both orders. Why need AB not equal BA?
options: All matrices represent the same transformation
Matrix multiplication generally depends on order
Only negative entries cause noncommutativity
Both products must be undefined
questions.answer: Matrix multiplication generally depends on order
questions.explanation: Composing linear transformations in different orders can give different results.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Samples are taken from a skewed population with finite variance. What can become approximately normal as sample size grows under suitable independence conditions?
options: The distribution of sample means
The original population itself
Every individual observation
The order in which data were collected
questions.answer: The distribution of sample means
questions.explanation: The central limit theorem concerns the sampling distribution of the mean, not a transformation of the underlying population into a normal one.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two counters are drawn without replacement from a mixed bag. Why can the second colour depend on the first?
options: All second draws are independent by definition
The first counter returns automatically
The bag's composition changes after the first draw
The colours physically transform
questions.answer: The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.explanation: Removing a counter changes the proportions remaining for the next selection.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Every value in a data set increases by the same constant. What happens to variance?
options: It doubles
It stays unchanged
It rises by that constant
It becomes zero
questions.answer: It stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The mean shifts by the same amount, leaving deviations from the mean unchanged.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: The sampling method and confidence level stay the same, but a much larger random sample is taken. What usually happens to the interval estimating a mean?
options: It becomes wider solely because the sample is larger
It must have zero width
It loses its stated confidence level by definition
It becomes narrower
questions.answer: It becomes narrower
questions.explanation: Larger samples generally reduce standard error, giving more precise estimates under the model assumptions.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A probability distribution is unchanged by multiplication by its transition matrix. What does this mean about later distributions if the model remains fixed?
options: All transition probabilities must be zero
The distribution must assign equal probability to all states
They remain the same even though individuals may change states
Every individual is permanently frozen in one state
questions.answer: They remain the same even though individuals may change states
questions.explanation: A stationary distribution preserves aggregate state probabilities; movement between states can still balance.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation

options: Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
Change every nearby value to zero
Remove both intervals entirely
Set the derivative to one without changing values
questions.answer: Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
questions.explanation: A removable discontinuity is fixed by matching the point value to its existing limit.

options: Outside both roots
Everywhere
Nowhere
Strictly between the roots
questions.answer: Strictly between the roots
questions.explanation: The parabola lies below the axis between its crossings and above it outside them.

questions.q: A differential equation's exact solution decays smoothly, but a coarse Euler approximation alternates and grows. What should be investigated first?
options: Numerical instability caused by the step size
Proof that the exact differential equation has no solution
A requirement that every decay be oscillatory
The impossibility of approximating derivatives
questions.answer: Numerical instability caused by the step size
questions.explanation: An unsuitable numerical step can produce behaviour absent from the continuous model; reducing it may improve stability.

They are identical lines

questions.answer: They are distinct parallel lines
questions.explanation: Matching coefficient ratios give the same direction, while incompatible constants prevent intersection.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Along an eigenvector direction, a matrix multiplies a vector by a factor between zero and one each time. What happens under repeated application?
options: Its length grows without bound
Its direction reverses every time
Its length remains constant
Its length tends toward zero without reversing direction
questions.answer: Its length tends toward zero without reversing direction
questions.explanation: Repeated multiplication by a positive factor smaller than one yields decay along the same eigenvector direction.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: The same students are measured before and after a programme. Why can analysing paired differences be preferable to treating the two samples as independent?
options: It removes all measurement error
It makes the sample size equal to the whole population
It accounts for the link between each student's measurements
It guarantees that the programme caused every change
questions.answer: It accounts for the link between each student's measurements
questions.explanation: Pairing uses within-student comparisons and can account for stable differences between students; it does not by itself prove causation.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A small study fails to reject no difference between two groups. Why is 'the groups are identical' too strong?
options: The test may lack power to detect a real difference
A nonsignificant result proves a large difference
All null hypotheses are true until rejected
Sample size cannot influence test sensitivity
questions.answer: The test may lack power to detect a real difference
questions.explanation: Nonrejection may reflect limited evidence or low power; it does not establish exact equality.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A tiny effect becomes statistically significant in an enormous sample. What additional judgement is needed?
options: Whether statistical significance guarantees a large effect
Whether the p-value equals the effect size
Whether increasing sample size invalidates all tests
Whether the effect is large enough to matter in context
questions.answer: Whether the effect is large enough to matter in context
questions.explanation: Statistical evidence and practical importance are distinct; sample size can make small effects detectable.

options: The function is constant nearby
The function keeps increasing through it
The function is discontinuous there
The derivative is undefined there

options: It immediately jumps to zero
It grows exponentially without limit at all sizes
It increases toward K
It decreases away from K

questions.explanation: For 0<P<K the growth rate is positive and becomes smaller near the stable equilibrium K.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A line predicting y from x minimises vertical residuals. Why should its algebraic inverse not automatically be used as the best line predicting x from y?
options: The original correlation becomes zero on exchanging axes
The reversed prediction problem minimises different residuals
Every regression line has slope one
Regression lines cannot be rearranged algebraically
questions.answer: The reversed prediction problem minimises different residuals
questions.explanation: Least-squares regression is directional; switching response and predictor changes which errors are minimised.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A square coefficient matrix is invertible. What follows for a linear system with that matrix and any right-hand side?
options: There are always no solutions
There are always infinitely many solutions
Only a zero right-hand side is allowed
There is exactly one solution
questions.answer: There is exactly one solution
questions.explanation: Multiplying by the inverse determines a unique solution vector.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A rare condition has a test with some false positives. Why need a positive result not make the condition highly likely?
options: A positive result proves the condition is absent
Rare conditions cannot be tested
The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
Test accuracy is irrelevant
questions.answer: The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.explanation: The posterior probability depends on both test performance and the prior prevalence.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Two random variables have finite means but are dependent. Which statement still holds?
options: The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
Their variances always add without a covariance term
Their product mean always equals the product of their means
They must have identical distributions
questions.answer: The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
questions.explanation: Linearity of expectation does not require independence.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: Every observation is multiplied by a constant c. Why is variance multiplied by c squared?
options: The mean is always unchanged
Variance counts observations without using values
Only negative constants affect variance
Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
questions.answer: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
questions.explanation: Variance averages squared deviations, so scaling values squares the scale factor.

questions.subject: Applications & Interpretation
questions.q: A binomial model has many trials but a very small success probability. Why may a symmetric normal approximation still be poor?
options: The outcomes stop being discrete when probability is small
The distribution can remain strongly skewed if expected successes are few
A large trial count always makes every distribution exactly normal
The binomial mean must be negative
questions.answer: The distribution can remain strongly skewed if expected successes are few
questions.explanation: Both expected successes and expected failures matter for a useful normal approximation; many trials alone are insufficient.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two organisms share many inherited structural features. What does this most reasonably suggest?
options: They must be the same species
They cannot differ in DNA
A relatively close evolutionary relationship
Identical habitats are required
questions.answer: A relatively close evolutionary relationship
questions.explanation: Shared inherited features can indicate common ancestry, although convergent features must be distinguished.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A cell is placed in a solution with lower water potential than its cytoplasm. What tends to happen?
options: Water leaves the cell
Water enters the cell only
The cell instantly makes more water
Solute movement must stop
questions.answer: Water leaves the cell
questions.explanation: Water moves by osmosis toward the lower water potential across a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A cell grows much larger without changing shape. Why can exchange become less efficient relative to its needs?
options: Surface area disappears
Its membrane becomes nonselective automatically
Its enzymes stop existing
Volume increases faster than surface area
questions.answer: Volume increases faster than surface area
questions.explanation: A decreasing surface-area-to-volume ratio makes exchange less sufficient for the larger internal volume.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A tissue repairs a small wound by mitosis. What should daughter cells normally retain?
options: No DNA
The parent cell's chromosome number
Half the parent cell's chromosomes
A completely new genetic code
questions.answer: The parent cell's chromosome number
questions.explanation: Mitosis normally preserves chromosome number in genetically similar daughter cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Why does meiosis reduce chromosome number before fertilisation?
options: It prevents chromosome number doubling each generation
It makes gametes have no genes
It prevents all genetic variation
It makes every offspring identical
questions.answer: It prevents chromosome number doubling each generation
questions.explanation: Fusion of two haploid gametes restores diploidy without continually increasing chromosome number.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A leaf receives light but very little carbon dioxide. Why may increasing light fail to raise photosynthesis?
options: Light never affects photosynthesis
Oxygen replaces carbon dioxide in sugar synthesis
Carbon dioxide is limiting
Chlorophyll must be absent
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide is limiting
questions.explanation: Increasing a nonlimiting factor has little effect when another required factor restricts the rate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A working muscle's ATP demand rises. Why must ATP be continually regenerated?
options: ATP contains no transferable energy
Cells hold only a limited immediately available ATP supply
ATP cannot be broken down
All ATP is stored permanently in DNA
questions.answer: Cells hold only a limited immediately available ATP supply
questions.explanation: ATP is rapidly used and resynthesized to support continuing cellular work.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A shoot bends toward light. Why does unequal growth produce bending?
options: All cells shorten equally
The root changes into a leaf
The light physically pushes the shoot
Cells on one side elongate more
questions.answer: Cells on one side elongate more
questions.explanation: Differential elongation across the shoot causes curvature toward the light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Alveoli have thin walls and a large total surface area. What does this arrangement improve?
options: Filtration of red blood cells
Production of bone tissue
Diffusion of respiratory gases
Storage of undigested food
questions.answer: Diffusion of respiratory gases
questions.explanation: A short diffusion distance and large surface support rapid oxygen and carbon-dioxide exchange.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person produces a smaller volume of concentrated urine when conserving water. What kidney change contributes?
options: More water is reabsorbed from the filtrate
All filtration stops permanently
More water is secreted into the tubule
Blood cells pass freely into urine
questions.answer: More water is reabsorbed from the filtrate
questions.explanation: Greater tubular water reabsorption reduces urine volume and concentrates remaining solutes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A reflex withdraws a hand from a painful stimulus before deliberate action. What advantage does this offer?
options: Permanent loss of brain function
A response without any neurons
Proof that muscles detect every stimulus alone
A rapid protective response
questions.answer: A rapid protective response
questions.explanation: Reflex pathways allow quick responses without waiting for conscious planning.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A muscle pulls on a bone across a joint. Why is another muscle needed for the opposite movement?
options: Muscles have no force when shortening
Muscles actively pull rather than push
Bones contract independently
A single tendon can reverse its attachment
questions.answer: Muscles actively pull rather than push
questions.explanation: Antagonistic muscles create opposing joint movements by pulling in different directions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A flower receives pollen from another plant of the same species. What may this increase compared with self-pollination?
options: Genetic variation in offspring
The number of chromosomes in every gamete
The certainty that all seeds are identical
The elimination of fertilisation
questions.answer: Genetic variation in offspring
questions.explanation: Cross-pollination can combine alleles from different individuals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A recessive trait appears in a child of two unaffected parents in a simple autosomal model. What is a possible explanation?
options: The allele must be dominant
The child has no chromosomes
Both parents carry the recessive allele
Neither parent has the allele
questions.answer: Both parents carry the recessive allele
questions.explanation: Two heterozygous parents can each transmit the recessive allele.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Before cell division, DNA is copied. Why is accurate copying important?
options: Proteins cannot exist near DNA
Each daughter cell needs inherited genetic information
DNA supplies all the cell's oxygen
Copying removes every mutation from the species
questions.answer: Each daughter cell needs inherited genetic information
questions.explanation: Replication preserves genetic instructions for transmission to daughter cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Antibiotic treatment leaves a few resistant bacteria alive. Why can resistance become more common afterward?
options: Every bacterium deliberately chooses a mutation
The antibiotic teaches all bacteria to resist
Sensitive bacteria become mammals
Resistant survivors reproduce
questions.answer: Resistant survivors reproduce
questions.explanation: Selection favours resistant variants already present or arising through mutation and gene transfer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A population grows rapidly, then slows as food becomes scarce. What explains the slowdown?
options: The disappearance of reproduction in all species
A lack of any environmental effect
Density-dependent competition
An unlimited carrying capacity
questions.answer: Density-dependent competition
questions.explanation: Competition intensifies as population density approaches resource limits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A species survives only within a narrow temperature range. As a region warms, what response is plausible if other needs can be met elsewhere?
options: Its suitable habitat shifts toward cooler locations
Every individual immediately changes its inherited tolerance
The species must gain energy without food
Temperature ceases to affect its enzymes
questions.answer: Its suitable habitat shifts toward cooler locations
questions.explanation: Environmental change can shift where conditions fall within a species' tolerance limits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A reserve protects several connected habitats instead of one tiny isolated patch. What advantage can connections provide?
options: Guaranteed extinction of predators
Elimination of all competition
Identical conditions everywhere
Movement and gene flow between populations
questions.answer: Movement and gene flow between populations
questions.explanation: Habitat connections can reduce isolation and support dispersal and genetic exchange.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A useful gene is introduced into a bacterial plasmid. Why can this help produce its protein?
options: The gene has to become a virus first
The plasmid can carry the gene into a suitable host
The plasmid directly becomes the protein
Bacteria do not require gene expression
questions.answer: The plasmid can carry the gene into a suitable host
questions.explanation: A vector can transfer a gene for expression in a compatible host system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two species look alike but their similarities evolved independently in similar environments. What should a classification study do?
options: Use additional inherited and molecular evidence
Assume identical appearance proves recent ancestry
Ignore DNA because appearance is always decisive
Treat similar environments as identical genomes
questions.answer: Use additional inherited and molecular evidence
questions.explanation: Convergence can imitate relatedness, so multiple lines of evidence are needed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A membrane protein moves ions against their concentration gradient. What additional requirement is likely?
options: Identical ion concentrations on both sides
Destruction of all membrane proteins
An energy source
A completely impermeable cell wall
questions.answer: An energy source
questions.explanation: Moving against an electrochemical gradient requires energy, directly or through coupling.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Adding more substrate reduces the effect of a reversible competitive inhibitor. Why?
options: The reaction no longer needs enzymes
Substrate competes more successfully for the active site
The inhibitor is converted into substrate
The enzyme is permanently denatured
questions.answer: Substrate competes more successfully for the active site
questions.explanation: Higher substrate concentration increases the likelihood of substrate occupying the shared binding site.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Homologous chromosomes exchange corresponding segments during meiosis. What can result?
options: A doubling of chromosome number in every gamete
Loss of all genes from both chromosomes
Identical copies of one parental chromosome only
New combinations of alleles on a chromosome
questions.answer: New combinations of alleles on a chromosome
questions.explanation: Crossing over recombines linked alleles between homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Light reactions stop supplying ATP and NADPH. Why does carbon fixation soon slow?
options: Carbon dioxide instantly disappears from the atmosphere
The chloroplast loses all membranes immediately
Carbon reduction needs their energy and reducing power
The Calvin cycle directly absorbs all required photons
questions.answer: Carbon reduction needs their energy and reducing power
questions.explanation: The Calvin cycle depends on ATP and NADPH generated by light-dependent reactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Oxygen becomes unavailable to aerobic cells. Why does the mitochondrial electron-transport chain stall?
options: Its final electron acceptor is missing
Glucose cannot contain carbon anymore
All glycolysis enzymes require oxygen directly
The Krebs cycle becomes a photosynthetic cycle
questions.answer: Its final electron acceptor is missing
questions.explanation: Without oxygen accepting electrons, electron carriers cannot be efficiently reoxidised.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Why can fermentation sustain glycolysis when oxygen is absent?
options: It produces oxygen for mitochondria
It makes ATP without any substrate
It eliminates the need for enzymes
It regenerates NAD+
questions.answer: It regenerates NAD+
questions.explanation: Regeneration of NAD+ allows the oxidation step in glycolysis to continue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Sucrose is loaded into phloem at a source. How can this promote bulk flow toward a sink?
options: Every sucrose molecule is individually pumped along the full tube
Water enters osmotically, raising pressure near the source
Sucrose evaporates and pulls sap as a gas
The sieve tube becomes impermeable to all water
questions.answer: Water enters osmotically, raising pressure near the source
questions.explanation: Solute loading draws in water and can establish a pressure difference that drives bulk flow.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Exercising tissue releases more carbon dioxide and becomes more acidic. How can this assist oxygen delivery?
options: Haemoglobin's oxygen affinity decreases locally
Haemoglobin binds oxygen irreversibly
Blood stops flowing to that tissue
Carbon dioxide replaces iron in every haem group
questions.answer: Haemoglobin's oxygen affinity decreases locally
questions.explanation: The Bohr effect promotes oxygen unloading where metabolic activity is high.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: ADH secretion rises when blood becomes more concentrated. What combined response is expected?
options: Complete cessation of filtration in all nephrons
Increased loss of water with no feedback
More collecting-duct water reabsorption and less urine
Less water reabsorption and more dilute urine
questions.answer: More collecting-duct water reabsorption and less urine
questions.explanation: ADH increases collecting-duct water permeability, helping conserve water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A chemical synapse normally transmits in one direction. Why?
options: The neurotransmitter destroys the receiving neuron
Vesicle release and postsynaptic receptors are arranged asymmetrically
Electrical charge can move only one way through all materials
Both neurons have identical release machinery at the same contact
questions.answer: Vesicle release and postsynaptic receptors are arranged asymmetrically
questions.explanation: The presynaptic terminal releases transmitter onto receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A skeletal muscle sarcomere shortens while actin and myosin filament lengths stay constant. How?
options: Both filaments are chemically dissolved
