Actin converts completely into myosin
The muscle loses all ATP
The filaments slide past each other
questions.answer: The filaments slide past each other
questions.explanation: Cross-bridge cycling increases filament overlap without shortening individual filaments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An edit alters a gene's regulatory sequence without changing its protein-coding sequence. What can still change?
options: The amino-acid sequence must always change
The number of protons in each DNA atom
When or how much of the protein is made
The genetic code used by every ribosome
questions.answer: When or how much of the protein is made
questions.explanation: Regulatory DNA influences expression, so protein abundance or timing can change without altering its amino-acid sequence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Red and white flowers produce pink heterozygotes in a simple inheritance model. What does this demonstrate?
options: The heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype
The parental alleles are permanently blended and lost
The trait has no genetic basis
Every allele is recessive
questions.answer: The heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance changes the heterozygote phenotype without erasing the separate alleles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two species differ greatly in appearance but share many homologous DNA sequences. What should this suggest when reconstructing ancestry?
options: DNA similarity proves they occupy the same habitat
Their genomes must be identical in every base
No evolutionary divergence has ever occurred
External similarity alone may underestimate their relatedness
questions.answer: External similarity alone may underestimate their relatedness
questions.explanation: Molecular evidence can reveal common ancestry despite changes in outward form.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A gene's mRNA is present but no protein is produced after ribosome function is blocked. Which stage is directly affected?
options: Chromosome segregation
Translation
DNA replication
Transcription initiation only
questions.answer: Translation
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA and assemble amino acids during translation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A population's allele frequencies shift sharply after a random disaster leaves few survivors. What process can explain this?
options: Genetic drift through a bottleneck
Directed mutation to help every survivor
Guaranteed stabilising selection
Inheritance of acquired injuries
questions.answer: Genetic drift through a bottleneck
questions.explanation: Chance sampling during a bottleneck can change allele frequencies independently of adaptive value.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A flowering plant gains pollination while an insect gains nectar. What makes this mutualism?
options: Neither species gains anything
Both must be the same species
Both species benefit
Only the insect benefits and the plant is harmed
questions.answer: Both species benefit
questions.explanation: Mutualism describes interactions with a benefit to each participating species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A pond can have less producer biomass than consumer biomass at one instant. How is this possible?
options: Biomass and productivity are identical measures
Producers reproduce and are consumed rapidly
Energy increases at every trophic transfer
Consumers perform all photosynthesis
questions.answer: Producers reproduce and are consumed rapidly
questions.explanation: Rapid producer turnover can sustain consumers despite low standing producer biomass.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A DNA sample is repeatedly heated, cooled with primers, and extended by polymerase. Why are primers needed?
options: They replace all template DNA
They cut every target molecule into amino acids
They convert RNA directly into protein
They provide starting points for DNA synthesis
questions.answer: They provide starting points for DNA synthesis
questions.explanation: DNA polymerase extends from an existing primer with a free 3-prime end.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two populations look different but interbreed and produce fertile offspring naturally. Under a biological species concept, what is strongest evidence they belong to one species?
options: Different local food sources alone
The fact that both have cells
Reproductive compatibility and gene flow
Different body colour alone
questions.answer: Reproductive compatibility and gene flow
questions.explanation: The biological species concept emphasizes reproductive connection rather than appearance alone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Plant and animal cells are placed in sufficiently dilute solutions. Why can the plant cell become turgid while the animal cell may burst?
options: The plant wall resists expansion and builds opposing pressure
Plant membranes are completely impermeable to water
Animal cells contain no solute
The plant cell has no osmotic gradient
questions.answer: The plant wall resists expansion and builds opposing pressure
questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall limits expansion, allowing pressure potential to oppose further water entry.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A reversible inhibitor binds only away from the active site and reduces active enzyme function; adding substrate does not restore maximum rate. What is supported?
options: Simple competition only for the same active site
A substrate shortage as the sole cause
An increase in enzyme concentration
Noncompetitive inhibition in the ideal model
questions.answer: Noncompetitive inhibition in the ideal model
questions.explanation: An ideal noncompetitive inhibitor lowers functional catalytic capacity that extra substrate cannot restore.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A mitochondrial membrane becomes freely permeable to protons while electron transfer can continue. What happens to ATP synthesis by ATP synthase?
options: It moves into the nucleus
It decreases as the proton gradient dissipates
It increases without limit
It becomes independent of the gradient
questions.answer: It decreases as the proton gradient dissipates
questions.explanation: ATP synthase relies on the proton-motive force; a proton leak uncouples it from electron transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A leaf's photosynthesis increases with added CO2 at one light level but barely responds in dim light. What explains the contrast?
options: The limiting factor differs between conditions
CO2 is never a photosynthetic substrate
Dim light destroys every chloroplast instantly
Light and CO2 act independently at all levels
questions.answer: The limiting factor differs between conditions
questions.explanation: CO2 may limit at adequate light, whereas insufficient light limits the response in dim conditions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A stronger stimulus causes more frequent action potentials rather than proportionately taller action potentials in one axon. Why?
options: Stimulus strength changes the genetic code each time
Stronger stimuli eliminate refractory periods
Individual action potentials are all-or-none events
Axons cannot transmit repeated signals
questions.answer: Individual action potentials are all-or-none events
questions.explanation: Stimulus intensity can be encoded by firing frequency while action-potential amplitude remains broadly fixed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: ATP becomes unavailable in a contracted muscle fibre. Why can cross-bridges remain attached?
options: Calcium immediately removes every cross-bridge
ATP binding is needed to detach myosin from actin
ATP destroys all actin filaments
Myosin is never attached during contraction
questions.answer: ATP binding is needed to detach myosin from actin
questions.explanation: ATP binding releases the myosin head from actin; depletion prevents normal detachment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A trait follows mitochondrial inheritance in the usual human model. Why can affected mothers pass it on while affected fathers generally do not?
options: Fathers have no mitochondria
Mitochondrial DNA is carried on the Y chromosome
Only sons receive egg cytoplasm
Most embryonic mitochondria come from the egg
questions.answer: Most embryonic mitochondria come from the egg
questions.explanation: The egg supplies nearly all zygotic cytoplasm and mitochondria in typical human inheritance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two genes yield parental allele combinations much more frequently than recombinants. What is most consistent with this?
options: They have no alleles
Every meiosis produces only recombinant chromosomes
They are linked on the same chromosome
They must be on different chromosomes
questions.answer: They are linked on the same chromosome
questions.explanation: Linked genes tend to be inherited together, with crossing over producing fewer recombinants when loci are close.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A human coding sequence is placed in bacteria, but no protein appears because the promoter is unsuitable. What does this illustrate?
options: A shared genetic code does not guarantee compatible expression signals
Bacteria cannot use any human coding sequence
Promoters are translated into all proteins
DNA bases have completely different chemical identities in bacteria
questions.answer: A shared genetic code does not guarantee compatible expression signals
questions.explanation: Transcription also requires host-recognised regulatory sequences, beyond codon compatibility.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A trait is heritable and improves survival but reduces reproduction enough to lower total offspring contribution. What determines its evolutionary success?
options: Survival duration alone
The organism's desire to pass it on
Body size alone
Its net contribution to reproductive fitness
questions.answer: Its net contribution to reproductive fitness
questions.explanation: Selection depends on genetic contribution to future generations, integrating survival and reproduction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A food chain lengthens while primary production is unchanged. Why does adding a top consumer limit the biomass it can support?
options: Longer chains create energy
Repeated trophic transfers reduce available energy
Energy is fully recycled at each feeding step
All producers stop photosynthesising
questions.answer: Repeated trophic transfers reduce available energy
questions.explanation: Energy transfer is inefficient, leaving progressively less available to additional consumer levels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two equal-sized reserves differ: one contains varied habitats and one is uniform. Why might the varied reserve support more species?
options: It offers more kinds of ecological niches
Area alone determines every species count
Every habitat supports identical communities
Variation eliminates resource limits
questions.answer: It offers more kinds of ecological niches
questions.explanation: Habitat heterogeneity can provide different resources and conditions supporting more species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A PCR negative control with no added template produces the target-sized band. What should be suspected first?
options: A perfectly valid negative control
A need to report every sample as negative
Contamination or another control failure
Proof that the target sequence arose by natural selection during PCR
questions.answer: Contamination or another control failure
questions.explanation: A target-like product in a no-template control undermines confidence that sample products reflect only their original DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A DNA insert and vector have compatible sticky ends but are not ligated. What is missing for stable recombinant DNA formation?
options: Removal of the vector's origin of replication
Covalent sealing of the sugar-phosphate backbone
Conversion of DNA into protein
Destruction of all complementary bases
questions.answer: Covalent sealing of the sugar-phosphate backbone
questions.explanation: Base pairing can align fragments, while ligase seals backbone nicks to stabilize the construct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two DNA samples produce bands at the same position in a standard size-separating gel. What does this establish most directly?
options: Their complete base sequences must be identical
They came from the same organism
They code for the same protein
The detected fragments have similar lengths
questions.answer: The detected fragments have similar lengths
questions.explanation: Migration in this gel primarily reflects fragment length; different sequences can share the same length.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A small isolated population grows numerically from only a few founders. Why can genetic vulnerability persist despite the larger headcount?
options: Larger population size instantly eliminates inbreeding history
Mutation recreates all lost alleles in one generation
Growth need not restore alleles lost at founding
Every new individual adds an entirely new set of alleles
questions.answer: Growth need not restore alleles lost at founding
questions.explanation: Population expansion can multiply existing genomes without restoring the original diversity lost in a bottleneck.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: At the same oxygen partial pressure, a right-shifted oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve indicates what?
options: Less oxygen bound and easier unloading
More oxygen bound and less unloading
No haemoglobin remains in the blood
Oxygen partial pressure has become zero
questions.answer: Less oxygen bound and easier unloading
questions.explanation: A right shift represents reduced haemoglobin affinity at a given oxygen partial pressure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Species richness stays constant after disturbance, but several species are replaced and energy pathways change. Why is unchanged richness insufficient to show full recovery?
options: Equal richness guarantees identical food webs
Every species performs exactly the same ecological role
Recovery can be measured only by total rainfall
Richness does not capture species identity or ecosystem functioning
questions.answer: Richness does not capture species identity or ecosystem functioning
questions.explanation: A single count of species can hide changes in composition, interactions and function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During succession on bare rock, early colonisers help later plants establish. Which mechanism explains this facilitation?
options: All nutrients disappear permanently
Weathering and organic-matter accumulation improve substrate
Early colonisers create mature soil instantly
The rock already contains a complete forest root system
questions.answer: Weathering and organic-matter accumulation improve substrate
questions.explanation: Pioneer organisms can modify the substrate and add organic matter, supporting subsequent communities.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Students regularly complain that the only lunch queue is too slow. Why could this suggest a business opportunity?
options: It guarantees that any proposed service will be profitable
It proves that students will pay any price
It removes the need to investigate demand
It identifies an unmet customer need
questions.answer: It identifies an unmet customer need
questions.explanation: A repeated customer problem can suggest an opportunity, but demand and feasibility still require investigation.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A new business sets a target to reach monthly break-even within six months. Why is this more useful than simply saying do well?
options: It makes cash planning unnecessary
It means growth no longer matters
It provides a measurable result and a time frame
It guarantees the target will be achieved
questions.answer: It provides a measurable result and a time frame
questions.explanation: A specific measurable objective supports planning and assessment of progress.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A founder estimates sales, costs, staffing and delivery arrangements before opening. What does combining these in a plan help reveal?
options: A guarantee that competitors will not respond
Whether the proposed activities and resources fit together
The exact future profit with certainty
A way to avoid all future decisions
questions.answer: Whether the proposed activities and resources fit together
questions.explanation: A plan links the idea to its operational and financial requirements while exposing assumptions.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Demand for a new product is uncertain. Why might a small pilot launch be useful?
options: It gathers evidence before a larger commitment
It eliminates every possible future loss
It proves nationwide demand from any pilot size
It replaces the need to calculate costs
questions.answer: It gathers evidence before a larger commitment
questions.explanation: A pilot tests important assumptions on a limited scale before more resources are committed.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A shop offers lightweight bags to cyclists and large bags to families. What is it responding to?
options: A requirement that every customer buy both types
A guarantee that both groups pay identical prices
A rule that markets cannot contain several segments
Different needs in different customer groups
questions.answer: Different needs in different customer groups
questions.explanation: Segmentation recognises groups with differing needs and helps tailor the offer.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A founder interviews potential customers about a proposed service. Why is this primary research?
options: The respondents have already bought the service
The information has no collection cost
The data are collected directly for the current investigation
The data must be more accurate than every published source
questions.answer: The data are collected directly for the current investigation
questions.explanation: Primary research gathers new evidence for a particular purpose, though quality depends on its design.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Two cafés charge the same price, but one promises quick collection for commuters. What is the second café highlighting?
options: A requirement that every customer travel by train
A customer benefit that can distinguish its offer
A guarantee of lower production costs
A change in legal ownership
questions.answer: A customer benefit that can distinguish its offer
questions.explanation: A value proposition explains why a target customer might choose that business.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A popular product is difficult for customers to obtain because stockists are too far away. Which part of the offer needs attention?
options: Distribution and availability
The colour of the accounting ledger
Only the product's production cost
Only the number of shareholders
questions.answer: Distribution and availability
questions.explanation: A good product still needs a convenient route to its intended customers.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: An advertisement introduces an unfamiliar product and explains its use. What is its immediate purpose?
options: Record the business's liabilities
Guarantee customer loyalty permanently
Replace the product's quality checks
Build awareness and understanding
questions.answer: Build awareness and understanding
questions.explanation: Informative promotion helps potential customers recognise an offering and understand its benefits.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A business charges less than the variable cost of making each extra unit. What happens as it sells more of those units, all else equal?
options: Fixed costs disappear automatically
The selling price becomes the unit contribution
Each extra unit increases the loss before fixed costs
Every extra sale necessarily improves profit
questions.answer: Each extra unit increases the loss before fixed costs
questions.explanation: Negative unit contribution means additional units do not cover their own variable costs.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A shop's sales revenue rises, but its costs rise by a larger amount. What can happen to profit?
options: It is unaffected by costs
It can fall
It must rise by the revenue increase
It must equal revenue
questions.answer: It can fall
questions.explanation: Profit is revenue minus costs, so faster cost growth can reduce it.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A profitable sale is made on credit, with payment due next month. Why might it not help pay today's wages?
options: The cash has not yet been received
Credit sales can never generate revenue
Profit and cash receipts are always simultaneous
Wages can be paid only from cash sales
questions.answer: The cash has not yet been received
questions.explanation: Recognising a sale and collecting its cash can happen at different times.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A business needs to pay suppliers before customers pay it. What does this create?
options: A guarantee of accounting profit
A reduction of every future expense
A reason to stop recording receivables
A need to finance day-to-day cash commitments
questions.answer: A need to finance day-to-day cash commitments
questions.explanation: The timing gap between payments and receipts creates a working-capital requirement.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: An owner uses retained profit to fund a small expansion. What is one consequence?
options: Ownership must be sold to every customer
The funding has no alternative possible use
The business avoids borrowing that amount from an external lender
The retained profit becomes a new loan
questions.answer: The business avoids borrowing that amount from an external lender
questions.explanation: Retained profit is an internal funding source, although using it still has an opportunity cost.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A manager gives a trained employee authority to handle routine refunds within a limit. What is being delegated?
options: Authority to ignore the stated limit
A defined decision-making responsibility
Ownership of the entire business
Every duty of the manager permanently
questions.answer: A defined decision-making responsibility
questions.explanation: Delegation assigns specified authority and work while overall accountability remains with management.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: New staff make errors using unfamiliar equipment. What response directly addresses the skills gap?
options: Relevant practical training
Changing the business name
Increasing sales targets without instruction
Removing every performance measure
questions.answer: Relevant practical training
questions.explanation: Training develops the knowledge and skills needed to perform the task correctly.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Employees say they do not know whether their work is useful or successful. Which response directly addresses that concern?
options: Withholding all information about results
Changing working hours at random
Increasing the number of unexplained rules
Clear goals and constructive feedback
questions.answer: Clear goals and constructive feedback
questions.explanation: Goals and feedback clarify expectations and help employees understand their contribution.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A bakery's ovens are fully used at peak time, and orders are delayed. What is the immediate operational constraint?
options: The age of its logo
The total number of products advertised elsewhere
Available oven capacity at the peak
The number of entries in its customer database
questions.answer: Available oven capacity at the peak
questions.explanation: A fully utilised limiting resource can prevent the business from meeting additional demand promptly.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A manufacturer checks finished items against specifications before dispatch. What does this help do?
options: Prove that every customer wants the product
Identify products that do not meet the standard
Guarantee that defects can never occur
Replace the need for clear specifications
questions.answer: Identify products that do not meet the standard
questions.explanation: Quality checks detect departures from requirements so defective output can be addressed.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A business reduces wasted raw material while producing the same acceptable output. What direct benefit follows?
options: Less material is required per acceptable unit
Sales revenue must double
Every fixed cost disappears
Product demand becomes unlimited
questions.answer: Less material is required per acceptable unit
questions.explanation: Reducing waste improves resource productivity and can reduce material costs and environmental impact.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Many customers like an idea, but few will pay enough to cover its costs. What does this suggest?
options: Positive opinions guarantee commercial demand at any price
Costs cease to matter when an idea is popular
The idea must have no social value
Interest alone does not establish a viable business model
questions.answer: Interest alone does not establish a viable business model
questions.explanation: Viability requires a workable relationship between willingness to pay, demand and the resources needed to deliver.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A firm extends opening hours to increase sales, but employees object to the new shifts. What must managers balance?
options: A requirement that all stakeholders have identical objectives
A rule that longer hours always increase profit
Potential customer and revenue benefits against workforce effects
Only the preferences of whichever group is larger
questions.answer: Potential customer and revenue benefits against workforce effects
questions.explanation: Business decisions can affect stakeholders differently, requiring consideration of benefits, costs and implementation.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A fast-growing firm buys more stock and offers more customer credit. Why might it need extra finance despite rising sales?
options: Offering credit immediately increases cash receipts
Growth can tie up cash before receipts arrive
Rising sales guarantee a positive cash balance at every date
Inventory purchases have no cash effect
questions.answer: Growth can tie up cash before receipts arrive
questions.explanation: Expansion can increase inventory and receivables, creating a funding need before customers pay.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A repair service moves from one-off payments to subscriptions. Which issue should it reassess?
options: Whether recurring income covers the expected service demand and costs
Only whether the company name sounds modern
Whether subscriptions eliminate all customer cancellations
Whether every subscriber will require the same work
questions.answer: Whether recurring income covers the expected service demand and costs
questions.explanation: Changing the revenue model changes both income timing and the obligations that must be funded.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A business surveys only its most loyal customers before entering a new market. What is the main limitation?
options: Loyal customers cannot express preferences
A large loyal-customer sample necessarily represents noncustomers
Primary research cannot use existing customers
Their preferences may not represent the new target customers
questions.answer: Their preferences may not represent the new target customers
questions.explanation: The usefulness of research depends on how well respondents match the population relevant to the decision.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Demand is price elastic over a proposed price reduction. What happens to revenue if the expected response occurs?
options: Quantity does not respond to price
Costs must fall by the same percentage as price
The percentage rise in quantity exceeds the percentage price fall, raising revenue
Revenue necessarily falls because the price falls
questions.answer: The percentage rise in quantity exceeds the percentage price fall, raising revenue
questions.explanation: With elastic demand, the quantity response more than offsets the lower price in revenue terms.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A premium brand cuts prices sharply and advertises only bargains. What strategic concern arises?
options: All customers value only the lowest price
The message may conflict with its quality-based position
Lower prices always strengthen a premium image
Price cannot influence how customers interpret a brand
questions.answer: The message may conflict with its quality-based position
questions.explanation: Marketing choices should form a coherent position; a price-led message can change perceived value.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Selling directly online increases the producer's margin per sale but requires delivery and support. What comparison matters?
options: The extra margin against the added costs and responsibilities
The margin alone, with all new costs ignored
Only the number of intermediaries removed
A presumption that direct sales are always cheaper overall
questions.answer: The extra margin against the added costs and responsibilities
questions.explanation: Removing intermediaries can transfer their functions and costs to the producer.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: An existing product is entering a market with different user needs. Why test an adapted version?
options: To establish that all markets have identical preferences
To avoid measuring demand
To prove the original version had no value
To check whether the changes fit the new customers' requirements
questions.answer: To check whether the changes fit the new customers' requirements
questions.explanation: Adaptation should respond to evidence about the target market rather than assuming one version fits every context.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A campaign gets many views but few enquiries from the intended customers. What should be examined?
options: Only the duration of the advertisement
Whether a larger audience always contains more suitable buyers
Whether the reach converts into the campaign's relevant outcomes
Views alone as proof of commercial success
questions.answer: Whether the reach converts into the campaign's relevant outcomes
questions.explanation: Promotional activity should be assessed against its objective and target audience, not only exposure counts.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Unit contribution rises while fixed costs stay unchanged. What happens to the break-even quantity?
options: It becomes equal to the selling price
It falls
It rises
It stays unchanged regardless of contribution
questions.answer: It falls
questions.explanation: Each unit contributes more toward the same fixed-cost total, so fewer units are needed to cover it.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A firm buys equipment expected to serve for several years. Why can relying entirely on a repayable short-term facility be risky?
options: Repayment may fall due before the equipment generates enough cash
Long-lived equipment cannot be financed externally
Short-term finance never carries a repayment obligation
The equipment's useful life guarantees immediate cash recovery
questions.answer: Repayment may fall due before the equipment generates enough cash
questions.explanation: Funding maturity should be considered alongside the timing of the asset's expected cash benefits.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A forecast shows a temporary cash deficit two months ahead. What is its practical value?
options: It proves the business is permanently unprofitable
It records cash already received in that future month
It eliminates uncertainty about every forecast input
It gives time to arrange funding or adjust cash timing
questions.answer: It gives time to arrange funding or adjust cash timing
questions.explanation: Forecasting supports advance action, while its assumptions and predicted amounts remain uncertain.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A founder raises equity from a new investor instead of taking a loan. What trade-off may result?
options: No effect on ownership under any equity agreement
The removal of all future business risk
Less contractual debt repayment but a share of ownership and control given up
Guaranteed fixed interest payments to the investor
questions.answer: Less contractual debt repayment but a share of ownership and control given up
questions.explanation: Equity funding shares ownership and residual returns rather than simply creating a conventional loan obligation.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Routine decisions must pass through many management layers. What problem can delegation help reduce?
options: The cost of every raw material
Delays in decisions that capable local staff could make
The need for any accountability
Every difference between departments
questions.answer: Delays in decisions that capable local staff could make
questions.explanation: Appropriate delegation moves decisions nearer the information and work, subject to clear limits and competence.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A business can train existing staff or recruit specialists for a new process. What should guide the choice?
options: The urgency, required skills and relative costs of each route
Only the number of current staff
A rule that recruitment is always cheaper
A rule that existing staff can master any task immediately
questions.answer: The urgency, required skills and relative costs of each route
questions.explanation: The best route depends on available time, skills gaps, resources and the business's longer-term needs.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A bonus rewards only the number of units produced. Quality falls. What explains the outcome?
options: Pay incentives cannot affect behaviour
More units always imply better customer value
The quality target was necessarily met because output rose
The measure can encourage output at the expense of unmeasured quality
questions.answer: The measure can encourage output at the expense of unmeasured quality
questions.explanation: People may focus on rewarded measures, so incentives should reflect important dimensions of performance.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Holding less stock reduces storage costs but deliveries are unreliable. What trade-off follows?
options: Storage costs and stockouts are the same cost
Supplier reliability becomes irrelevant when inventory falls
Lower holding costs may come with greater stockout risk
Lower stock always improves service reliability
questions.answer: Lower holding costs may come with greater stockout risk
questions.explanation: Lean inventories reduce buffers, making dependable replenishment more important.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A firm increases output using spare existing capacity. Why might average fixed cost fall?
options: Every additional unit is costless
The same fixed cost is spread over more units
Total fixed cost must fall to zero
Variable cost per unit must double
questions.answer: The same fixed cost is spread over more units
questions.explanation: Within the relevant capacity range, fixed costs do not rise proportionately with output.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A supplier offers a lower production price, but the task is central to the brand's quality. What else matters?
options: Quality control, reliability and dependence on the supplier
Only the quoted unit price
Whether all internal expertise can be discarded immediately
A guarantee that external suppliers always outperform internal staff
questions.answer: Quality control, reliability and dependence on the supplier
questions.explanation: An outsourcing decision includes strategic and operational consequences as well as direct purchase cost.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A pilot succeeds only because the founder provides unpaid labour that would need paid staff at scale. What should be revised before expansion?
options: Only the pilot's sales total
The assumption that unpaid work has no economic cost
The conclusion that any successful pilot guarantees scalable profit
The cost model and feasibility under realistic staffing
questions.answer: The cost model and feasibility under realistic staffing
questions.explanation: Scaling can change the resource requirements; omitted labour costs can make the apparent model misleading.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A delivery firm rewards speed alone, and damaged parcels increase. What change best addresses the problem?
options: Count only the fastest delivery each week
Treat damaged parcels as unrelated to the incentive
Use a balanced performance measure including timely, undamaged delivery
Raise the speed target further without monitoring damage
questions.answer: Use a balanced performance measure including timely, undamaged delivery
questions.explanation: A measure should reflect the intended service outcome and avoid rewarding behaviour that undermines it.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Buying a competitor expands market access quickly but joins firms with conflicting cultures. What makes the decision more complex than comparing purchase price with current profit?
options: Culture cannot affect operations or staff retention
Integration risks can change the expected future benefits
Past profit guarantees identical future profit after acquisition
Combining ownership automatically removes all duplication costs
questions.answer: Integration risks can change the expected future benefits
questions.explanation: Acquisition outcomes depend on integration, retention and coordination as well as the initial financial comparison.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A project has already spent money that cannot be recovered. Future cash benefits are now below avoidable future costs. Which reasoning is sound?
options: Assess continuation using the future costs and benefits affected by the decision
Continue solely to justify the irrecoverable spending
Count the sunk spending as a new cash payment each future month
Ignore all future costs because development has already begun
questions.answer: Assess continuation using the future costs and benefits affected by the decision
questions.explanation: Irrecoverable past expenditure is unchanged by the current choice; relevant future consequences should guide it.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Customers say they would buy a product, but actual trial purchases are low. What should the business infer?
options: The survey must have been deliberately falsified
Actual purchases are irrelevant if opinions are positive
Every trial purchaser represents every future customer
Stated intentions may differ from behaviour under real purchasing conditions
questions.answer: Stated intentions may differ from behaviour under real purchasing conditions
questions.explanation: Purchasing evidence tests willingness to commit under real price and context constraints, complementing survey responses.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A price cut raises revenue because demand is elastic. Why can profit still fall?
options: Elastic demand guarantees zero variable cost
The price reduction removes all fixed costs
Extra volume and the lower margin can increase costs enough to outweigh revenue gains
Higher revenue always means higher profit
questions.answer: Extra volume and the lower margin can increase costs enough to outweigh revenue gains
questions.explanation: Revenue effects alone do not determine profit; the contribution and total cost consequences also matter.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A product has a small market share in a rapidly growing market. Why is immediate withdrawal not automatic?
options: A portfolio label determines the decision without context
It may offer growth potential, but the investment and competitive prospects need assessment
Every low-share product must already be highly profitable
Market growth guarantees that this product will become the leader
questions.answer: It may offer growth potential, but the investment and competitive prospects need assessment
questions.explanation: Portfolio categories inform analysis but do not replace judgement about resources, differentiation and expected returns.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A producer starts direct online sales below its retailers' prices. What longer-term issue should it assess?
options: Retailers may reduce support or stop carrying the product
Direct selling guarantees that retail support is no longer useful
Retailers' responses cannot affect total sales
Every channel serves exactly the same customers at the same cost
questions.answer: Retailers may reduce support or stop carrying the product
questions.explanation: A direct channel can affect partner incentives and the wider route to customers.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A firm's advantage comes only from a feature competitors can copy cheaply next month. What is the concern?
options: Low copying cost guarantees permanent differentiation
The feature cannot create any present customer value
A copied feature automatically reduces all industry demand to zero
The advantage may be difficult to sustain
questions.answer: The advantage may be difficult to sustain
questions.explanation: An easily imitated benefit may provide limited lasting protection from competition.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Sales rise during a campaign, but a major competitor also closes temporarily. What is needed before crediting the campaign with the whole increase?
options: Only the campaign's total number of views
A rule that sales increases never have multiple causes
Evidence separating the campaign effect from other changes
An assumption that every simultaneous sale was caused by advertising
questions.answer: Evidence separating the campaign effect from other changes
questions.explanation: A before-and-after increase can reflect several influences, so attribution requires an appropriate comparison or supporting evidence.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A break-even chart assumes constant unit price and variable cost, but expansion requires discounts and overtime. What should be questioned?
options: Whether every chart must have a zero sales line
Whether the original contribution assumptions still apply at the higher output
Whether fixed costs can ever be measured
Whether break-even analysis always predicts demand
questions.answer: Whether the original contribution assumptions still apply at the higher output
questions.explanation: Changing prices or unit costs changes contribution and can make the original linear projection inappropriate.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A profitable wholesaler's receivables grow much faster than sales and customers pay increasingly late. What risk follows?
options: It may struggle to meet cash commitments despite reported profit
Receivables growth guarantees immediate cash availability
Accounting profit prevents any liquidity problem
Late collection necessarily increases every customer's demand
questions.answer: It may struggle to meet cash commitments despite reported profit
questions.explanation: Profit can be tied up in unpaid balances while cash payments still fall due.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A project is attractive only if its sales forecast is achieved exactly; a small shortfall makes it unattractive. What does this reveal?
options: The forecast has been proved accurate
The project has no risk because a calculation was completed
The sales forecast can be ignored once the initial result is positive
The decision is sensitive to the sales assumption
questions.answer: The decision is sensitive to the sales assumption
questions.explanation: Sensitivity analysis shows how conclusions change when uncertain assumptions move.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A founder rejects all outside equity to retain control, although internal funds cannot support a planned expansion. What is the real trade-off?
options: External equity must be accepted by every growing firm
Internal finance is unlimited when the founder remains sole owner
Retaining ownership may limit the speed or scale of growth
Control and funding availability are always independent
questions.answer: Retaining ownership may limit the speed or scale of growth
questions.explanation: Finance choices can affect both ownership and the resources available to pursue objectives.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A manager delegates an important task but gives neither adequate authority nor access to information. Why may delegation fail?
options: Assigning a title guarantees effective action
The employee lacks the means needed to fulfil the responsibility
Delegation requires the manager to abandon all oversight
Authority and information cannot affect task performance
questions.answer: The employee lacks the means needed to fulfil the responsibility
questions.explanation: Responsibility should be matched with suitable authority, information and support.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: New software is technically sound, but staff bypass it because the workflow is slower and training was rushed. What should management examine?
options: How implementation, training and workflow fit affect adoption
Only whether the software launches without crashing
Whether resistance proves every employee opposes improvement
Whether another announcement alone guarantees compliance
questions.answer: How implementation, training and workflow fit affect adoption
questions.explanation: Successful change requires practical integration and user capability as well as technical functionality.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Two sales teams have different territory potential but are judged only on total revenue. Why can this distort appraisal?
options: Total revenue measures effort perfectly in every context
All teams must face identical demand because they share an employer
A larger territory always has a lower sales potential
Results may reflect territory differences as well as effort and skill
questions.answer: Results may reflect territory differences as well as effort and skill
questions.explanation: Performance measures need context to distinguish controllable contribution from differing opportunities.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: Packing can handle twice the output that assembly can produce. Why might faster packing equipment add little overall output?
options: The fastest stage determines the whole process's capacity
Packing speed always doubles assembly speed
Assembly remains the limiting stage
Overall capacity is the sum of every stage's capacity
questions.answer: Assembly remains the limiting stage
questions.explanation: A sequential process is constrained by its bottleneck unless the limiting stage or flow changes.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A firm inspects more finished goods, but the same defect keeps recurring. What additional approach targets the cause?
options: Treat rework as proof that the process is reliable
Improve the process that produces the defect
Inspect only the products that look attractive
Increase output while keeping the faulty process unchanged
questions.answer: Improve the process that produces the defect
questions.explanation: Inspection detects defects; process improvement and quality assurance seek to prevent them.

questions.subject: Business Management
questions.q: A package uses less material per unit, but total sales rise enough that material use increases overall. What distinction matters?
options: Per-unit efficiency and total resource use can move in different directions
A per-unit reduction guarantees lower total use
Higher total use proves no per-unit saving occurred
Only revenue can measure environmental resource use
questions.answer: Per-unit efficiency and total resource use can move in different directions
questions.explanation: Total consumption depends on both material per unit and the number of units produced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen and oxygen react in a sealed vessel. Why is total mass unchanged despite new water forming?
options: The vessel creates replacement atoms
Atoms are rearranged rather than created or destroyed
Water has no mass
Gases lose mass when they react
questions.answer: Atoms are rearranged rather than created or destroyed
questions.explanation: Chemical reactions conserve atoms, so a closed system conserves mass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two atoms have the same proton number but different neutron numbers. Why do they have similar chemical behaviour?
options: Their nuclear masses are identical
Neutrons determine all bonding
They must have different element names
They have the same electronic arrangement when neutral
questions.answer: They have the same electronic arrangement when neutral
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number and normally similar electron configurations.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An atom loses its outermost electron. What happens to its net charge?
options: It remains neutral
Its proton number decreases
It becomes more positive
It becomes more negative
questions.answer: It becomes more positive
questions.explanation: Removing negative charge makes the remaining particle more positive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, but the melt does. Why?
options: Melting allows ions to move
Melting changes ions into free protons
The solid contains no charged particles
Only molten salt contains atoms
questions.answer: Melting allows ions to move
questions.explanation: The solid's ions are fixed in a lattice; mobile ions carry charge in the liquid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why can a covalent molecule contain shared electrons without having a net charge?
options: Sharing removes the electrons' charge
Covalent bonds contain only neutrons
The molecule has no nucleus
The total proton and electron charges can balance
questions.answer: The total proton and electron charges can balance
questions.explanation: Bonding rearranges electrons, while a neutral molecule still has balanced positive and negative charge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol mixes readily with water. Which interaction helps explain this?
options: Breaking every carbon-carbon bond
Hydrogen bonding between their molecules
Metallic bonding between all atoms
Formation of an ionic lattice
questions.answer: Hydrogen bonding between their molecules
questions.explanation: Ethanol's hydroxyl group can form hydrogen bonds with water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A sealed gas sample is compressed slowly at constant temperature. Why does its pressure rise?
options: Molecules strike the walls more frequently per unit area
Its molecules become heavier
Its average kinetic energy must rise
Its amount of gas doubles
questions.answer: Molecules strike the walls more frequently per unit area
questions.explanation: Reduced volume increases wall-collision frequency while mean kinetic energy remains temperature-dependent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why does breaking a covalent bond require energy?
options: Bond electrons have no energy
Breaking bonds always releases heat
Attractive interactions must be overcome
The atoms must always become new elements
questions.answer: Attractive interactions must be overcome
questions.explanation: Energy is required to separate atoms held together by an attractive bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Reactants and products remain at constant concentrations in a closed reacting system. What can still be happening?
options: No molecular collisions
Forward and reverse reactions at equal rates
Only the forward reaction
Only the reverse reaction
questions.answer: Forward and reverse reactions at equal rates
questions.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium has continuing reactions whose equal rates leave concentrations unchanged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An acid is diluted with pure water. What usually happens to hydrogen-ion concentration?
options: It increases
It stays fixed at every dilution
It becomes negative
It decreases
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Dilution spreads the acid over more solvent, reducing hydrogen-ion concentration in ordinary acidic solutions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrochloric acid is mixed with just enough sodium hydroxide to neutralise it. What happens to H+ and OH-?
options: They both become electrons
They remain unchanged in equal large concentrations
They form water
They form sodium metal
questions.answer: They form water
questions.explanation: The net ionic neutralisation reaction combines hydrogen and hydroxide ions into water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A galvanic cell powers a lamp. What overall energy conversion occurs?
options: Chemical energy to electrical energy
Electrical energy to nuclear energy
Light energy to chemical energy only
Thermal energy to mass
questions.answer: Chemical energy to electrical energy
questions.explanation: A spontaneous redox reaction drives electron flow through the external circuit.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An electrolytic cell deposits metal at its cathode. What happens to the metal ions there?
options: They lose protons
They gain oxygen in every case
They become more positively charged
They gain electrons
questions.answer: They gain electrons
questions.explanation: Cathodic reduction supplies electrons to metal cations to form neutral metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element's spectrum has two isotope peaks, one much larger than the other. What does the larger peak indicate?
options: That isotope has more electron shells
That isotope is more abundant in the sample
That isotope has twice as many protons
That isotope must be more radioactive
questions.answer: That isotope is more abundant in the sample
questions.explanation: Peak intensity measures relative abundance, while peak position gives mass-to-charge information.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solid reactant is powdered before reacting with a solution. Why can reaction become faster?
options: More surface is available for collisions
The solid's atoms become smaller
The reaction enthalpy must change
The powder is necessarily a catalyst
questions.answer: More surface is available for collisions
questions.explanation: Increasing surface area exposes more reacting particles to the solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two compounds have the same molecular formula but different atom connections. What does this imply?
options: Their molecular masses must differ
One cannot contain covalent bonds
They can have different properties
They must be the same substance
questions.answer: They can have different properties
questions.explanation: Structural isomers differ in connectivity, which can change physical and chemical behaviour.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethene reacts by adding atoms across its double bond. Why is addition possible?
options: Its carbon-carbon sigma bond must always vanish
The pi bond can be replaced by new sigma bonds
Carbon must gain a fifth bond
The carbon nuclei split
questions.answer: The pi bond can be replaced by new sigma bonds
questions.explanation: The pi component of the double bond can open while new sigma bonds form.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aldehyde is oxidised under suitable conditions. Which functional group is commonly formed?
options: An alkene group
An ether group only
An amine group
A carboxylic acid group
questions.answer: A carboxylic acid group
questions.explanation: Oxidation of an aldehyde normally produces the corresponding carboxylic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A carboxylic acid reacts with a carbonate and releases gas. What does this show?
options: Every carbon atom becomes gas
It is necessarily a strong mineral acid
Its acidic proton can react with carbonate
It contains no covalent bonds
questions.answer: Its acidic proton can react with carbonate
questions.explanation: Acid-carbonate reactions release carbon dioxide; a weak carboxylic acid can still produce this reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two substances move different distances on the same chromatogram. What helps explain the separation?
options: They interact differently with the mobile and stationary phases
One substance has ceased to contain atoms
The stationary phase must travel with one substance
Both substances necessarily have different colours
questions.answer: They interact differently with the mobile and stationary phases
questions.explanation: Different relative affinities lead to different migration speeds through a chromatographic system.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Equal numbers of nitrogen and hydrogen molecules react to make ammonia. Which is left over if reaction goes to the stoichiometric limit?
options: Hydrogen
Both are fully consumed
Ammonia cannot form
Nitrogen
questions.answer: Nitrogen
questions.explanation: The reaction needs three hydrogen molecules per nitrogen molecule, so hydrogen is limiting in an equal-number mixture.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why is Na+ smaller than a neutral sodium atom?
options: Its nucleus has fewer neutrons necessarily
It has lost its outer electron shell
It has gained a proton
Its remaining electrons repel more strongly than before
questions.answer: It has lost its outer electron shell
questions.explanation: Losing the outermost electron removes the occupied third shell and strengthens attraction per remaining electron.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element shows a large jump after its second ionisation energy. What does this suggest?
options: It has two relatively accessible valence electrons
It has two neutrons
It must be a noble gas
Its third electron is easier to remove
questions.answer: It has two relatively accessible valence electrons
questions.explanation: A large jump suggests that further removal enters a more strongly bound inner shell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two comparable bonds differ mainly in bond order. Which trend is generally expected for the higher-order bond?
options: Longer and stronger in all cases
Identical length and energy
Shorter and stronger
Longer and weaker
questions.answer: Shorter and stronger
questions.explanation: More shared bonding electron density generally strengthens a bond and shortens its equilibrium length.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why does water have an unusually high boiling point compared with H2S?
options: Water's O-H covalent bonds must break on boiling
Water forms a stronger extended hydrogen-bond network
Water has greater molecular mass
H2S has no electrons
questions.answer: Water forms a stronger extended hydrogen-bond network
questions.explanation: Boiling separates molecules; strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding raises the energy required.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A liquid evaporates into a much larger available gas volume. What usually happens to the substance's entropy?
options: It decreases necessarily
It is unchanged because mass is conserved
It becomes zero
It increases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: The gaseous state allows many more accessible arrangements and molecular positions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, increased pressure at fixed temperature favours which side?
options: Neither side because gases cannot equilibrate
Whichever side contains a catalyst
Ammonia
Nitrogen and hydrogen
questions.answer: Ammonia
questions.explanation: Compression favours the side with fewer gas molecules, which is the ammonia side.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Equal-concentration strong and weak monoprotic acids are compared. Why does the weak acid usually have higher pH?
options: A smaller fraction of its molecules ionises
Each molecule releases more protons
Its concentration must be zero
Its conjugate base is absent
questions.answer: A smaller fraction of its molecules ionises
questions.explanation: Partial ionisation gives a lower hydrogen-ion concentration than a fully dissociated acid of equal concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A little acid is added to a mixture of a weak acid and its conjugate base. Why does pH change only slightly?
options: The solvent loses all polarity
The weak acid becomes a strong acid
The added acid is not conserved
The conjugate base consumes much of the added H+
questions.answer: The conjugate base consumes much of the added H+
questions.explanation: The buffer's base component reacts with added hydrogen ions, limiting the concentration change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A species oxidises another reactant. What happens to that species itself?
options: It cannot change oxidation state
It is reduced
It is also oxidised necessarily
Its electrons vanish
questions.answer: It is reduced
questions.explanation: The oxidising agent accepts electrons and undergoes reduction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why is a salt bridge useful in a galvanic cell?
options: It allows ionic movement that prevents charge buildup
It sends electrons through the solution between electrodes
It replaces both electrodes
It makes the redox reaction nonspontaneous
questions.answer: It allows ionic movement that prevents charge buildup
questions.explanation: Ion migration maintains electrical neutrality as oxidation and reduction proceed in separate compartments.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A molecular-ion region has two peaks two mass units apart in approximately a three-to-one ratio. What evidence would this pattern support?
options: Two carbon atoms being removed successively
A molecule containing only hydrogen
One chlorine atom in the molecular ion
One fluorine atom with two equally common isotopes
questions.answer: One chlorine atom in the molecular ion
questions.explanation: The common chlorine isotopes differ by two mass units and occur in an approximately three-to-one abundance ratio.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A sample gives one spot in one solvent system. Why is that insufficient to prove absolute purity?
options: One spot means the sample has one atom
Different substances can coincide under those conditions
Pure substances always give two spots
Chromatography cannot separate any organic compounds
questions.answer: Different substances can coincide under those conditions
questions.explanation: Co-migration or undetected components can hide impurities, so one result provides limited rather than conclusive evidence.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Doubling a reactant concentration doubles the initial rate while other conditions are fixed. What does this support?
options: Second-order dependence on that reactant
Zero-order dependence on that reactant
A negative reaction order necessarily
First-order dependence on that reactant
questions.answer: First-order dependence on that reactant
questions.explanation: A proportional rate change is consistent with a first-power concentration dependence.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why can a small temperature increase greatly accelerate a reaction?
options: The activation energy must rise
The equilibrium constant always becomes one
The fraction of collisions above activation energy increases
Every collision becomes successful
questions.answer: The fraction of collisions above activation energy increases
questions.explanation: The high-energy tail of the molecular energy distribution grows with temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A haloalkane forms an alkene by losing a hydrogen and a halogen from adjacent carbons. Which change distinguishes this process?
options: A carbon-carbon double bond forms
The carbon chain necessarily lengthens
An oxygen atom replaces the halogen
The molecule must become an ionic solid
questions.answer: A carbon-carbon double bond forms
questions.explanation: Elimination removes groups from neighbouring atoms and forms a pi bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Under controlled oxidation, a primary alcohol forms an aldehyde. Why is further oxidation often prevented by removing the aldehyde promptly?
options: Aldehydes cannot evaporate
The alcohol changes into a ketone when distilled
Removing product stops all molecular collisions
Aldehydes can oxidise further to acids
questions.answer: Aldehydes can oxidise further to acids
questions.explanation: Separating the aldehyde limits its continued exposure to the oxidising agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A carbonyl carbon is attacked by a nucleophile. Why?
options: The carbonyl group is nonpolar
The C=O bond makes carbon partially positive
Carbon always carries a full positive charge
Oxygen donates all its electrons permanently
questions.answer: The C=O bond makes carbon partially positive
questions.explanation: Oxygen draws electron density toward itself, making carbon electrophilic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An ester is hydrolysed under acidic conditions. Which products are expected?
options: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol
Two alkenes
An amine and an alkane
Only carbon dioxide and water
questions.answer: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis reverses ester formation by restoring an acid and alcohol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A student compares rates at two temperatures using different reactant concentrations too. What weakens the conclusion about temperature?
options: A rate comparison requires identical products only
Changing two variables automatically doubles the rate
Concentration is a confounding variable
Temperature can never affect rate
questions.answer: Concentration is a confounding variable
questions.explanation: Both temperature and concentration can affect rate, so their separate effects cannot be isolated in that comparison.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A product yield is lower than the stoichiometric maximum although the limiting reactant is consumed. Which explanation is possible?
options: The balanced equation must contain fractional atoms
Some reactant formed a side product
Mass conservation failed
The limiting reactant was unlimited
questions.answer: Some reactant formed a side product
questions.explanation: Consumption need not all follow the desired pathway; side reactions can lower isolated yield.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: First ionisation energy of boron is lower than beryllium's despite higher nuclear charge. Why?
options: Boron has fewer protons
Beryllium's outer shell is farther from the nucleus
Boron loses an inner 1s electron first
Boron loses a higher-energy 2p electron
questions.answer: Boron loses a higher-energy 2p electron
questions.explanation: Beryllium's filled 2s subshell is relatively stable, while boron's first removed electron is in 2p.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two resonance structures of an ion place charge on different atoms. What is the actual ion best described as?
options: A mixture of different compounds
An ion whose atoms exchange positions
One delocalised structure
A rapid physical oscillation between complete drawings
questions.answer: One delocalised structure
questions.explanation: Resonance drawings represent contributors to one electronic structure; atoms do not switch places.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A process has positive enthalpy change and positive entropy change. Under what condition can it be spontaneous?
options: At sufficiently high temperature
Only at absolute zero
At no temperature
At all temperatures necessarily
questions.answer: At sufficiently high temperature
questions.explanation: In Gibbs energy, the favourable T delta-S term can exceed the positive enthalpy change at high temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A reversible reaction equation is multiplied by two. How does its equilibrium constant change?
options: It doubles
It halves
It stays unchanged
It is squared
questions.answer: It is squared
questions.explanation: Multiplying all stoichiometric coefficients doubles the exponents in the equilibrium expression.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An inert gas is added to a reacting ideal-gas mixture at constant volume and temperature. What happens to equilibrium composition?
options: All reactants are consumed
It is unchanged
It always shifts toward fewer gas molecules
It always shifts toward more gas molecules
questions.answer: It is unchanged
questions.explanation: Reactant and product partial pressures stay unchanged at fixed volume and temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two buffers have the same acid-to-base ratio but different total concentrations. What differs most directly?
options: The more concentrated buffer resists added acid or base better
Only the dilute buffer has a definable pH
The concentrated buffer must have a radically different initial pH
Both can absorb unlimited acid
questions.answer: The more concentrated buffer resists added acid or base better
questions.explanation: Similar ratios give similar pH, but more buffer components provide greater capacity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A catalyst shortens the time needed to reach equilibrium but leaves final composition unchanged at fixed temperature. Which claim is ruled out by the final result?
options: The catalyst affects both reaction directions
The uncatalysed reaction can reach the same equilibrium
The catalyst changed the equilibrium constant
The catalyst provides a faster pathway
questions.answer: The catalyst changed the equilibrium constant
questions.explanation: A changed equilibrium constant would change the equilibrium relation at that temperature; a catalyst changes kinetics instead.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A cell reaction has positive standard cell potential. What follows about standard Gibbs-energy change?
options: It is independent of electron transfer
It is negative
It is positive
It must be zero
questions.answer: It is negative
questions.explanation: The relation delta-G-standard = -nFE-standard gives a negative Gibbs-energy change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aqueous salt electrolysis is compared with molten-salt electrolysis. Why may the cathode products differ?
options: Ions have no charge in water
Molten salts contain no cations
Electrode reactions never depend on the medium
Water can compete for reduction in the aqueous cell
questions.answer: Water can compete for reduction in the aqueous cell
questions.explanation: Aqueous solutions introduce water as a possible reactant, changing which reduction occurs.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A sample containing equal amounts of two enantiomers gives no net optical rotation. Which conclusion is justified?
options: The two enantiomers have become one structural isomer
No light interacts with the sample
Opposite rotations cancel; the molecules can still be chiral
Every molecule in the mixture must be achiral
questions.answer: Opposite rotations cancel; the molecules can still be chiral
questions.explanation: A racemic mixture can be optically inactive overall even though its individual molecules are chiral.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An observed rate law differs from the coefficients in the overall balanced equation. What is the best inference?
options: The overall equation need not represent one elementary step
The equation violates conservation of mass
The measured concentrations must be zero
All reactions have zero order
questions.answer: The overall equation need not represent one elementary step
questions.explanation: Overall stoichiometry does not determine rate-law exponents unless it describes an appropriate elementary step.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reactant starts at two different concentrations under identical conditions. How do its half-lives compare?
options: The more concentrated sample has twice the half-life
The less concentrated sample has twice the half-life
Half-life cannot be defined for a chemical reaction
They are equal
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: A first-order half-life depends on the rate constant, not the initial concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Excess ligand L shifts a reversible metal-ligand exchange toward the L-complex. Why does this not show the reverse reaction has become impossible?
options: Ligand exchange is never reversible
The new equilibrium favours the product but remains dynamic
Equilibrium requires equal concentrations of every complex
Excess ligand changes the metal's proton number
questions.answer: The new equilibrium favours the product but remains dynamic
questions.explanation: Changing ligand concentration shifts equilibrium composition while forward and reverse processes can still occur.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A molecule has one tetrahedral carbon bonded to four different groups. What is possible?
options: A pair of nonsuperimposable mirror-image forms
Only one spatial arrangement under all conditions
A required carbon-carbon triple bond
A mandatory ionic lattice
questions.answer: A pair of nonsuperimposable mirror-image forms
questions.explanation: A tetrahedral stereogenic centre can give two enantiomeric arrangements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aniline is brominated readily compared with benzene under comparable conditions. Why?
options: Aniline is a saturated hydrocarbon
The benzene ring in aniline has no resonance
The amino group donates electron density into the ring
Nitrogen removes every pi electron
questions.answer: The amino group donates electron density into the ring
questions.explanation: The amino group's resonance donation activates the ring toward electrophilic substitution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A tertiary haloalkane reacts by an SN1 pathway in a suitable polar protic solvent. What most directly favours its first step?
options: Formation of a carbon atom with five permanent bonds
Stabilisation of the tertiary carbocation
Unhindered backside attack at the tertiary carbon
A required free radical
questions.answer: Stabilisation of the tertiary carbocation
questions.explanation: SN1 ionisation is favoured when the resulting carbocation is relatively stabilised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aniline is less basic than a comparable aliphatic amine in the usual aqueous comparison. Why?
options: Its nitrogen has no lone pair
All aromatic compounds are strong acids
Its nitrogen nucleus has fewer protons
Its nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the aromatic ring
questions.answer: Its nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the aromatic ring
questions.explanation: Delocalisation reduces the lone pair's availability for bonding to a proton.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two comparable metal carbonates differ in cation polarising power. Why can the more polarising cation lower thermal stability?
options: It changes carbon into another element
It makes carbon dioxide unable to form
It distorts the carbonate electron cloud and facilitates decomposition
It prevents any distortion of the anion
questions.answer: It distorts the carbonate electron cloud and facilitates decomposition
questions.explanation: Stronger cation polarisation weakens stability of the carbonate anion relative to decomposition products.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two proposed isomers have the same formula. One predicts fewer distinct proton environments through symmetry. How can NMR help choose between them?
options: Compare the observed number and pattern of signals with each prediction
Select the isomer with the larger molecular mass
Count each hydrogen as a separate signal automatically
Ignore symmetry because all protons have identical shifts
questions.answer: Compare the observed number and pattern of signals with each prediction
questions.explanation: Structural symmetry can make hydrogens equivalent; their predicted signal patterns can distinguish isomers of equal mass.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A program must read marks, calculate averages and print reports. Why split these into separate tasks?
options: Each part can be developed and checked more clearly
Splitting guarantees that no errors remain
Each task must run on a different computer
Separate tasks remove the need to pass data
questions.answer: Each part can be developed and checked more clearly
questions.explanation: Decomposition breaks a problem into manageable components with identifiable responsibilities.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A variable total is 5. The program assigns total=total+2. What value does total then hold?
questions.explanation: The right-hand expression uses the previous value before assigning the new result.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Entry is allowed only when a ticket is valid AND the visitor meets the age requirement. A valid ticket alone is presented. What must still be checked?
options: Whether the ticket has the larger numerical value
Whether the two conditions have identical names
Whether the age requirement is met
Whether at least one condition is false
questions.answer: Whether the age requirement is met
questions.explanation: AND requires both conditions to be true.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A program must inspect every item in a known list once. Which approach directly fits?
options: Sort the list without inspecting its values
Loop through the list's items
Inspect only its first item
Repeat until an unrelated password changes
questions.answer: Loop through the list's items
questions.explanation: Traversal applies the required operation to each element of the collection.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A postcode begins with zero and is not used in arithmetic. Why store it as text?
options: To preserve its characters, including the leading zero
To make numerical addition faster
To force every postcode to have the same value
To prevent all invalid input automatically
questions.answer: To preserve its characters, including the leading zero
questions.explanation: An identifier's character representation matters; numeric conversion can discard leading zeros.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: The same calculation is needed in five places. What is an advantage of placing it in a function?
options: The function makes every caller's input valid automatically
It must run five times faster
The function cannot return different results for different inputs
Its logic can be maintained in one place
