The improvement must move production inside the old frontier
Opportunity cost disappears for both goods
The maximum output of one good rises while the other intercept need not change
questions.answer: The maximum output of one good rises while the other intercept need not change
questions.explanation: A sector-specific productivity gain affects production possibilities asymmetrically.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A firm must decide whether to produce one more unit. A past setup cost cannot be recovered or changed. Why exclude that cost from this marginal decision?
options: Past costs always increase future marginal revenue
The extra unit must be produced regardless of its variable cost
It is unchanged by producing the extra unit
All fixed costs are zero in accounting
questions.answer: It is unchanged by producing the extra unit
questions.explanation: Relevant marginal decisions compare costs and benefits altered by the additional action.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Demand is perfectly inelastic and supply is upward sloping. In the standard model, how does a per-unit tax affect traded quantity?
options: It necessarily falls by the tax amount
It stays unchanged while the buyer price rises
It falls to zero
It rises because the tax raises revenue
questions.answer: It stays unchanged while the buyer price rises
questions.explanation: Vertical demand fixes quantity; buyers bear the tax through a higher price under the stated assumptions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A straight downward-sloping demand curve has constant slope. Why does its price elasticity still vary along the curve?
options: Elasticity also depends on the price-to-quantity ratio
Slope and elasticity are always numerically identical
Quantity is constant along every straight line
Elasticity depends only on the currency symbol
questions.answer: Elasticity also depends on the price-to-quantity ratio
questions.explanation: Point elasticity combines the curve's slope with the local price and quantity values.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A law requires sellers rather than buyers to remit a tax. Why does this alone not determine who bears its economic burden?
options: The legal payer must bear every unit of the burden
Buyers cannot bear a tax unless they transfer it directly
Tax incidence is unrelated to market prices
Prices adjust according to demand and supply responsiveness
questions.answer: Prices adjust according to demand and supply responsiveness
questions.explanation: Economic incidence reflects the resulting price wedge and market responses, not merely the collection rule.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A competitive firm's fixed cost rises while its marginal-cost schedule and price are unchanged. What happens to its short-run profit-maximising positive output, if it still operates?
options: It must fall to zero regardless of variable costs
Marginal cost rises by the same amount at every unit
It is unchanged, although profit falls
It must rise by the fixed-cost increase
questions.answer: It is unchanged, although profit falls
questions.explanation: An unchanged marginal comparison leaves the optimal operating output unchanged, while higher fixed cost reduces profit.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A single-price monopolist restricts output below the point where demand equals marginal cost. What is the welfare concern?
options: Marginal cost necessarily exceeds price at the chosen output
Some units valued above their marginal cost are not produced
Every unit produced must have negative value
The monopolist's entire revenue is deadweight loss
questions.answer: Some units valued above their marginal cost are not produced
questions.explanation: Foregone trades with benefit above cost create a loss of potential total surplus.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Two firms would jointly earn more by keeping prices high, but each can gain by cutting while the other stays high. What makes cooperation fragile?
options: Each has an individual incentive to deviate
Joint benefit guarantees individual compliance
The firms must have identical costs for any strategic problem
A profitable deviation cannot exist in an oligopoly
questions.answer: Each has an individual incentive to deviate
questions.explanation: A collectively preferable outcome may be unstable when unilateral deviation is attractive.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In a simple monopsony model, why can a suitably set minimum wage increase employment?
options: Every minimum wage increases employment in every labour market
A wage floor removes all labour supply constraints
It forces every firm to hire unlimited workers
It can alter the employer's marginal hiring-cost schedule and reduce wage-setting power
questions.answer: It can alter the employer's marginal hiring-cost schedule and reduce wage-setting power
questions.explanation: The outcome depends on market structure and the level of the wage floor, unlike a universal claim about all labour markets.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A public good is valuable, but people can benefit without paying. Why does observing little voluntary payment not prove low social value?
options: A public good must have zero production cost
Every valuable good is easily sold separately to each user
Individual incentives to free ride can conceal willingness to benefit
Nonpayers necessarily receive no benefit
questions.answer: Individual incentives to free ride can conceal willingness to benefit
questions.explanation: Nonexcludability can weaken payment incentives even when combined benefits justify provision.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A country has positive gross investment but depreciation is larger. What follows for its produced capital stock, other changes excluded?
options: It becomes identical to current consumption
It declines because net investment is negative
It rises because gross investment is positive
It stays fixed because depreciation is only a price index
questions.answer: It declines because net investment is negative
questions.explanation: Net investment subtracts depreciation from gross investment; a negative amount means capital is not fully replaced.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A firm produces goods this year but sells them next year. How should the production be treated in expenditure-based GDP?
options: This year's unsold output enters inventory investment
It enters GDP only next year as new production
It enters neither year's GDP because no immediate sale occurred
Its full value is counted as new output in both years
questions.answer: This year's unsold output enters inventory investment
questions.explanation: Inventory investment accounts for current production not yet sold, preventing omission and later double counting.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Inflation expectations rise while supply conditions otherwise stay unchanged. In the expectations-augmented model, what happens?
options: The long-run unemployment-inflation trade-off becomes permanently exploitable
The short-run Phillips curve must shift downward
The natural unemployment rate must fall to zero
The short-run Phillips curve shifts upward
questions.answer: The short-run Phillips curve shifts upward
questions.explanation: At a given unemployment rate, higher expected inflation feeds into wage and price setting.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Demand expands beyond potential output with no lasting productivity gain. In the standard long-run AD–AS adjustment, what remains after wages and prices adjust?
options: A lower price level and lower natural unemployment
An outward production frontier caused only by spending
A higher price level with output returning to potential
Permanently higher real output solely from demand
questions.answer: A higher price level with output returning to potential
questions.explanation: Rising input prices shift short-run supply until output returns to unchanged productive capacity.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: An adverse supply shock causes inflation and an output loss. Why is demand expansion a difficult response?
options: It removes the original input-cost increase directly
It may support output while adding further price pressure
It shifts productive capacity right immediately
It necessarily lowers both inflation and unemployment without trade-offs
questions.answer: It may support output while adding further price pressure
questions.explanation: Demand management can cushion the output fall but can worsen inflation caused by constrained supply.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In the simple closed-economy model with lump-sum taxes and idle resources, government raises purchases and taxes equally. Why can equilibrium output rise?
options: Purchases enter demand fully while households reduce consumption by only part of the tax rise
The equal changes necessarily cancel every spending round
The tax rise is recorded as an equal increase in private consumption
The result requires a marginal propensity to consume greater than one
questions.answer: Purchases enter demand fully while households reduce consumption by only part of the tax rise
questions.explanation: With a marginal propensity to consume between zero and one, the initial net demand effect is positive.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Reserves are already ample and the overnight rate is anchored by administered rates. Why may another small reserve injection have little rate effect?
options: Every reserve injection must lower rates proportionally
Banks lose all access to central-bank accounts
The injection directly fixes every long-term bond yield
It need not change the administered return or create new scarcity conditions
questions.answer: It need not change the administered return or create new scarcity conditions
questions.explanation: Once reserves are ample, reserve quantity changes can have less influence than changes in the rates governing reserve returns.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: An economy keeps adding physical capital per worker with unchanged technology. Why can growth from this source slow?
options: Depreciation must fall to zero
Technology automatically deteriorates as investment rises
Diminishing returns can reduce the extra output from each additional unit of capital
More capital necessarily makes every worker less productive
questions.answer: Diminishing returns can reduce the extra output from each additional unit of capital
questions.explanation: With other factors fixed, capital deepening commonly delivers diminishing additions to output per worker.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A currency depreciates, but foreign sellers cut their own-currency prices to protect sales. What follows?
options: The currency cannot have depreciated
Domestic import prices may rise by less than the currency depreciation
Domestic import prices must rise by exactly the depreciation rate
Domestic import prices must be unchanged in every case
questions.answer: Domestic import prices may rise by less than the currency depreciation
questions.explanation: Exporters' pricing responses can partially absorb exchange-rate changes, so pass-through need not be complete.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: After a currency depreciation, import spending rises before trade quantities adjust. Why can the trade balance initially worsen?
options: Higher import prices can act before buyers change quantities sufficiently
Depreciation immediately makes all imports free
Export volumes must drop permanently by definition
Accounting requires a trade surplus after every depreciation
questions.answer: Higher import prices can act before buyers change quantities sufficiently
questions.explanation: Short-run contracts and adjustment lags can delay quantity responses while import costs change sooner.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A monic cubic has no x² term. What does this imply about the sum of its three roots, counting multiplicity?
options: All three roots are positive
Two roots must be equal
The sum is zero
The product is zero
questions.answer: The sum is zero
questions.explanation: The coefficient of x² is the negative of the sum of the roots.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A rational function can be written x+1+1/(x-2). Which line does its graph approach as x becomes very large?
options: y=x+1
y=x-2
questions.answer: y=x+1
questions.explanation: The reciprocal remainder tends to zero, leaving the oblique asymptote y=x+1.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: At an input where f(x) is negative, what happens to the real graph y=√f(x)?
options: The output equals -√(-f(x))
The output is zero
The output equals f(x)²
There is no real point at that input
questions.answer: There is no real point at that input
questions.explanation: A real square root requires a nonnegative argument.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: For column vectors, transformation B is applied first and A second. Which matrix represents the result?
options: A-B
AB
BA
A+B
questions.answer: AB
questions.explanation: The output is A(Bv), so the composite matrix is AB.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A plane transformation has determinant -3. How does it change an area?
options: It multiplies area by 3
It multiplies area by -3
It divides area by 3
It preserves area because the determinant is negative
questions.answer: It multiplies area by 3
questions.explanation: Area scales by the absolute determinant; the negative sign concerns orientation.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: In polar coordinates with r≥0, what locus is described by r=3?
options: A ray at angle 3 radians
A circle of diameter 3 centred at the pole
A circle of radius 3 centred at the pole
A horizontal line 3 units above the pole
questions.answer: A circle of radius 3 centred at the pole
questions.explanation: Every point remains at the fixed distance 3 from the pole.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A polar region is enlarged by replacing every radius r with 2r while keeping its angular limits. What happens to its area?
options: It is divided by 2
It is multiplied by 4
It is multiplied by 2
It stays the same
questions.answer: It is multiplied by 4
questions.explanation: Polar sector area involves r², so doubling radii quadruples area.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Nonparallel vectors a and b lie in a plane. Why can a×b be used as a normal to that plane?
options: It is parallel to a+b
It always has unit length
It is the same as a scalar dot product
It is perpendicular to both spanning vectors
questions.answer: It is perpendicular to both spanning vectors
questions.explanation: The cross product is perpendicular to each factor and is nonzero when the factors are nonparallel.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: An argument shows P(k) implies P(k+1) for every k≥1. Why must P(1) still be established?
options: A base case proves every later case without the implication
The starting statement must be false for induction to work
The implication needs a true starting statement
The implication already proves every statement without a starting case
questions.answer: The implication needs a true starting statement
questions.explanation: Induction combines a valid starting case with a step that propagates truth to later integers.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A smooth function has f(0)=2 and f′(0)=3. What are the constant and linear terms of its Maclaurin expansion?
options: 2+3x²
2x+3x²
questions.explanation: The constant term is the function value at zero and the linear coefficient is the first derivative at zero.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A positive increasing function is integrated over an interval using equal-width rectangles. Which endpoint choice gives a lower estimate?
options: Right endpoints
Whichever endpoint has the larger function value
Both endpoint choices give identical estimates
Left endpoints
questions.answer: Left endpoints
questions.explanation: On each subinterval, the left endpoint gives the smallest height for an increasing function.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: The solutions of y′=2y include y=Ce²ˣ. What does specifying y(0)=5 do?
options: Leaves every value of C possible
Selects C=5
Makes C vary with x
Requires C=0
questions.answer: Selects C=5
questions.explanation: At x=0 the exponential equals one, so the initial value fixes the integration constant.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.topic: Mechanics: Work by a perpendicular force
questions.q: A force remains perpendicular to an object's instantaneous displacement. What work does that force do over that displacement?
options: Zero
Positive work equal to force magnitude
Negative work in every case
Work that depends only on the object's mass
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Work involves the force component along displacement; a perpendicular force has no such component.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Two marks lie on the same rigid rotating disc at different distances from its axis. Which has greater linear speed?
options: Both always have identical linear speeds
Neither can move while the disc rotates
The mark farther from the axis
The mark nearer the axis
questions.answer: The mark farther from the axis
questions.explanation: All marks share angular speed, while tangential speed is angular speed multiplied by radius.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Two forces turn a wheel in opposite senses about a fixed axis. How do their torque contributions combine?
options: They must cancel regardless of size
With opposite signs
By adding only their positive magnitudes
By ignoring both torques
questions.answer: With opposite signs
questions.explanation: Clockwise and anticlockwise moments oppose; the net torque depends on their signed magnitudes.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A stone moves at constant speed in a circle. Why is it accelerating?
options: Its mass changes continuously
Its speed must be increasing
Its kinetic energy must increase
Its velocity changes direction
questions.answer: Its velocity changes direction
questions.explanation: Velocity includes direction, which changes throughout circular motion.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: For a count X with PGF G(t)=0.2+0.8t, what does the coefficient 0.8 represent?
options: The variance of X
The probability that X=2
The probability that X=1
The probability that X=0
questions.answer: The probability that X=1
questions.explanation: In a probability generating function, the coefficient of t to the power k is P(X=k).

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A school records each sampled student's journey time in minutes. Which population quantity would a one-sample mean interval estimate?
options: The population average journey time
The population proportion who travel by bus
Every student's exact journey time
The largest journey time in the school
questions.answer: The population average journey time
questions.explanation: A mean procedure estimates the centre of a quantitative variable such as elapsed time.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: The same students take a concentration test before and after a break. Why analyse their individual changes?
options: The before and after samples are independent groups
The two sets of scores must have equal means
Pairing makes measurement error impossible
Each student's two scores are linked
questions.answer: Each student's two scores are linked
questions.explanation: Analysing within-student differences respects the pairing and accounts for differences between students.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Under independence, 40% of students choose art. In a year group of 50 students, what expected art count follows?
questions.explanation: Independence applies the same 40% art proportion within that year group, giving 0.4 times 50.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Two roots have a known sum S and product P. How can their sum of squares be found without solving for each root?
options: Use S²-2P
Use S²+2P
Use 2S-P
Use P²-2S
questions.answer: Use S²-2P
questions.explanation: Expanding the square of the sum gives the two squares plus twice the product.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: If f(x) approaches zero through positive values, what happens to 1/f(x)?
options: It approaches one
It approaches the same finite zero as f(x)
It increases without bound
It approaches zero through negative values
questions.answer: It increases without bound
questions.explanation: Reciprocals of increasingly small positive numbers become increasingly large.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Writing y=f(x) leads to a quadratic in x. Why can its discriminant restrict the possible values of y?
options: The range is always every real number for a rational function
An attainable y must allow at least one real admissible x
The discriminant must equal zero for every attainable y
A negative discriminant gives two real inputs
questions.answer: An attainable y must allow at least one real admissible x
questions.explanation: Real inputs require a nonnegative discriminant, followed by checks for excluded inputs or degenerate cases.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A reversible transformation applies A followed by B to column vectors. Which composite undoes both steps?
options: B⁻¹A⁻¹
AB
A⁻¹+B⁻¹
A⁻¹B⁻¹
questions.answer: A⁻¹B⁻¹
questions.explanation: Undoing the last step first gives B⁻¹ followed by A⁻¹, represented by A⁻¹B⁻¹.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A matrix maps each vector on a line through the origin to twice itself. Is the line invariant even though its nonzero points move?
options: No; doubling always rotates a line
Yes, but only if every vector on it is zero
Yes; the image remains the same line
No; an invariant line requires every point to stay fixed
questions.answer: Yes; the image remains the same line
questions.explanation: Setwise invariance preserves the line as a set, whereas pointwise invariance would require eigenvalue 1.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A polar curve's equation is unchanged when θ is replaced by -θ. What symmetry does this indicate?
options: Reflection symmetry about the initial line
Reflection symmetry about every line through the pole
Translation symmetry parallel to the initial line
A fixed radius at every angle
questions.answer: Reflection symmetry about the initial line
questions.explanation: Changing θ to -θ reflects a point across the polar initial line while retaining its radius.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Two nonnegative polar radii describe an outer and inner boundary over the same angular interval. What gives the area between them?
options: One half the integral of the difference of radii squared
The integral of outer radius minus inner radius without squaring
The product of the two sector areas
One half the integral of outer radius squared minus inner radius squared
questions.answer: One half the integral of outer radius squared minus inner radius squared
questions.explanation: Subtracting sector areas subtracts their squared-radius integrands, not the square of their difference.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Why use the component of a point's displacement along a plane's unit normal to find perpendicular distance?
options: The full displacement to any point on the plane is always the shortest distance
Tangential components do not change distance from the plane
All displacement components have equal influence on distance
The plane's normal must point toward the origin
questions.answer: Tangential components do not change distance from the plane
questions.explanation: Projection onto the normal isolates the component perpendicular to the plane.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: To prove a sum formula by induction, why may its truth for n=k be assumed within the induction step?
options: The task is to prove the implication from that assumption to the k+1 case
The assumption alone proves the formula for all integers
Checking k=2 substitutes for proving the implication
Assuming a false formula makes the conclusion valid automatically
questions.answer: The task is to prove the implication from that assumption to the k+1 case
questions.explanation: The induction step is conditional; together with a verified base case it establishes all later cases.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: An analytic even function is expanded at zero. Which pattern should its expansion have?
options: All coefficients must be positive
The constant term must be zero
Only even powers can have nonzero coefficients
Only odd powers can have nonzero coefficients
questions.answer: Only even powers can have nonzero coefficients
questions.explanation: Even symmetry makes the odd derivatives at zero vanish, eliminating odd-power terms.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A reduction formula relates Iₙ to Iₙ₋₂. Why might both I₀ and I₁ be needed to evaluate all nonnegative-index cases?
options: Knowing either base value makes the other unnecessary for all cases
Even and odd indices reduce along separate chains
The formula always changes even indices into odd ones
Every integral must have exactly two numerical values
questions.answer: Even and odd indices reduce along separate chains
questions.explanation: Repeated reductions preserve parity, so the two parity chains need their respective starting values.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Multiplying y′+p(x)y=q(x) by a suitable integrating factor μ makes the left side what?
options: The derivative of y/μ in every case
A constant independent of x
The square of y′
The derivative of μy
questions.answer: The derivative of μy
questions.explanation: Choosing μ′=pμ turns μy′+μpy into the product derivative (μy)′.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Two balls are released from the same height, one dropped and one projected horizontally. With no air resistance, why do they land together?
options: Horizontal motion removes gravity
Their horizontal distances are equal
Their vertical motions have the same initial conditions and acceleration
Their total speeds are equal at every instant
questions.answer: Their vertical motions have the same initial conditions and acceleration
questions.explanation: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent in this ideal model, so equal vertical conditions give equal falling times.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Two springs store equal elastic energy. One is stiffer. Which is stretched less from equilibrium?
options: The stiffer spring
The softer spring
Both must have equal extension
Neither can store energy without permanent damage
questions.answer: The stiffer spring
questions.explanation: Elastic energy is one half stiffness times extension squared, so greater stiffness needs less extension for equal energy.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Equal opposite parallel forces act on different lines of action on a rigid body. What can result?
options: Zero net force and zero torque in every arrangement
A net force equal to either individual force
A torque only if the forces have different magnitudes
Zero net force but nonzero net torque
questions.answer: Zero net force but nonzero net torque
questions.explanation: Separated equal opposite forces form a couple that can rotate without accelerating the centre of mass.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: An internal explosion separates a moving object into fragments with negligible external force. How does its centre of mass move?
options: It accelerates because internal forces are large
With its original constant velocity
Toward the fastest fragment necessarily
It immediately stops
questions.answer: With its original constant velocity
questions.explanation: Internal forces cannot change the total momentum or centre-of-mass velocity of an isolated system.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A proposed probability generating function gives G(1)=1.3. Why can it not represent a probability distribution?
options: Its coefficients do not sum to one
Every PGF must satisfy G(1)=0
Its expected value must be negative
All PGFs must be linear functions
questions.answer: Its coefficients do not sum to one
questions.explanation: At t=1 all powers equal one, so the PGF returns the sum of the probabilities.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Twelve students provide before-and-after scores. When checking a paired t procedure's normality condition, which distribution matters?
options: Only the after scores
The pooled scores treated as 24 independent observations
The distribution of within-student score differences
Only the before scores
questions.answer: The distribution of within-student score differences
questions.explanation: A paired analysis is a one-sample analysis of the differences, so its distributional checks concern those differences.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A school tests whether a new schedule reduces average waiting time below 10 minutes. Which parameter statement fits the alternative?
options: The population mean waiting time differs from 10 in either direction
The population mean waiting time is below 10 minutes
The observed sample mean equals 10 minutes
The population standard deviation is below 10 minutes
questions.answer: The population mean waiting time is below 10 minutes
questions.explanation: The question specifies a decrease in a population mean, so the alternative is directional.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: One random sample records each student's year group and preferred elective. Which procedure can test whether the variables are associated?
options: A one-sample t test of mean year group
A paired t test of elective labels
A test of whether the two sample means are equal
A chi-square test of independence
questions.answer: A chi-square test of independence
questions.explanation: Both variables are categorical, and the observations form one two-way table from a single sample.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A real monic cubic has zero x² coefficient and three strictly positive real roots. Why is this impossible?
options: A real cubic cannot have three real roots
A zero x² coefficient requires a zero constant term
Positive roots cannot have the required zero sum
Positive roots must always have zero product
questions.answer: Positive roots cannot have the required zero sum
questions.explanation: The missing quadratic coefficient forces the root sum to be zero, contradicting three positive roots.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A discriminant calculation suggests an output y is attainable, but its only candidate input makes the original denominator zero. What follows?
options: That output must be excluded unless another valid input exists
The discriminant restores the excluded input to the domain
Every nonnegative discriminant guarantees a valid original input
The denominator restriction applies only to negative inputs
questions.answer: That output must be excluded unless another valid input exists
questions.explanation: Algebraic candidate solutions must satisfy the domain of the original rational function.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: On an interval where f(x)>0, the equation y²=f(x) has two branches. What is wrong with plotting only y=√f(x)?
options: It includes points with negative f(x)
It changes every x-coordinate to -x
It adds a branch that never satisfies the equation
It omits the negative branch y=-√f(x)
questions.answer: It omits the negative branch y=-√f(x)
questions.explanation: Both signs square to the same positive output, so both branches belong to the relation.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A plane transformation maps two distinct points to the same point. Why can it not have an inverse on the whole plane?
options: Every transformation with a repeated output is a rotation
Different inputs cannot be recovered uniquely from that common output
Its determinant must be negative rather than zero
Its matrix must contain a negative entry
questions.answer: Different inputs cannot be recovered uniquely from that common output
questions.explanation: The map is not one-to-one, so the inverse cannot assign a unique original input.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: If A=QDQ⁻¹, why is Aⁿ=QDⁿQ⁻¹ useful for large integer n?
options: Intermediate Q⁻¹Q factors cancel and diagonal entries are easy to raise to powers
Q and D can always be multiplied in any order
Aⁿ equals QⁿDⁿQ⁻ⁿ without any conditions
The eigenvectors must change after each application
questions.answer: Intermediate Q⁻¹Q factors cancel and diagonal entries are easy to raise to powers
questions.explanation: Repeated multiplication cancels adjacent inverse factors, leaving only powers of the diagonal matrix.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A polar parametrisation traces the same region twice over the chosen angular interval. What issue arises in applying one half the integral of r²?
options: Repeated tracing makes the geometric area zero
The radius must be negative on the second trace
The integral can count the region's area twice
The formula automatically counts each spatial point only once
questions.answer: The integral can count the region's area twice
questions.explanation: Polar integration counts swept sectors over the parameter interval, so repeated coverage must be accounted for.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A formula produces r<0 for some angles, but a sketch is required under the convention r≥0. What should be checked?
options: Whether the whole curve must be discarded
Which angular intervals are admissible or need an equivalent positive-radius representation
Whether negative radii can simply be plotted without adjusting the angle
Whether every negative output can be changed to zero
questions.answer: Which angular intervals are admissible or need an equivalent positive-radius representation
questions.explanation: The same point can be represented by reversing the radial direction and adding π to the angle; conventions affect the parameter description.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.topic: Pure 1: shortest distance between skew lines
questions.q: A proposed connecting segment meets one skew line at a right angle but not the other. Why is it not the shortest connecting segment?
options: Being perpendicular to either line is sufficient
The shortest segment must instead be parallel to both lines
Skew lines have no finite shortest distance
A shortest segment must be perpendicular to both line directions
questions.answer: A shortest segment must be perpendicular to both line directions
questions.explanation: If a component remains along either line, moving the endpoint along that line can shorten the connection.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A proof establishes P(1) and P(k) implies P(k+2) for every k≥1. What has it established without another base case?
options: Only P(1) and P(3), with no later cases
Only the positive even-indexed cases
Only the positive odd-indexed cases
Every positive integer case
questions.answer: Only the positive odd-indexed cases
questions.explanation: Starting at 1 and advancing by 2 reaches odd integers; P(2) would start the separate even chain.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Two analytic functions share their first four Maclaurin coefficients. What is justified?
options: Their expansions agree through those terms, but higher-order behaviour can differ
They must be identical everywhere
They must have identical fifth derivatives at zero
Their difference must be a nonzero constant
questions.answer: Their expansions agree through those terms, but higher-order behaviour can differ
questions.explanation: Finite matching local information does not determine all later coefficients or the entire function.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A curve y=f(x)>0 is rotated about the x-axis. Why is 2πy multiplied by arc-length element ds for surface area?
options: Each strip is a solid disc of area πy²
The sloping length always equals dx
The circumference should be multiplied by y again regardless of slope
A small curve segment sweeps a narrow surface strip with that circumference
questions.answer: A small curve segment sweeps a narrow surface strip with that circumference
questions.explanation: The surface strip has circumference 2πy and slant width ds; volume uses a different element.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: For y″-y=eˣ, why does a trial particular solution Aeˣ fail for every constant A?
options: The coefficient A must equal eˣ
It lies in the complementary solution, so the left side becomes zero
The forcing term is a polynomial
The equation has no solutions at all
questions.answer: It lies in the complementary solution, so the left side becomes zero
questions.explanation: The differential operator annihilates eˣ; a modified trial such as Axeˣ is needed.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A stationary isolated object separates into two pieces. One piece has twice the mass of the other. How do their velocity vectors compare afterward?
options: They are opposite, and the heavier piece has half the speed
They are equal and point in the same direction
The heavier piece has twice the speed in the opposite direction
Only the lighter piece can move
questions.answer: They are opposite, and the heavier piece has half the speed
questions.explanation: Zero initial momentum requires equal opposite final momenta, so speed is inversely related to mass for the two pieces.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A mass is added to a vertical spring and allowed to settle, then undergoes small oscillations. Why does gravity shift equilibrium without appearing explicitly in the ideal period formula?
options: The mass's weight changes sign during every oscillation
The spring stops storing potential energy
About the new equilibrium, net restoring force is still proportional to displacement with the same stiffness
Gravity becomes physically absent
questions.answer: About the new equilibrium, net restoring force is still proportional to displacement with the same stiffness
questions.explanation: Gravity changes the equilibrium extension, while deviations around it obey the same linear restoring-force law.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A light and a heavy cart collide. Why can their acceleration magnitudes differ despite equal contact force magnitudes?
options: Equal forces require equal changes in velocity regardless of mass
Acceleration also depends on mass
Newton's third law fails during short collisions
The light cart's force is actually always larger
questions.answer: Acceleration also depends on mass
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives different accelerations when equal force magnitudes act on unequal masses.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Two isolated carts stick together after colliding. Which statement is generally correct?
options: Both momentum and kinetic energy must decrease
Kinetic energy is conserved but momentum is not
Neither quantity can be tracked
Momentum is conserved but kinetic energy may decrease
questions.answer: Momentum is conserved but kinetic energy may decrease
questions.explanation: Sticking is inelastic: internal deformation can reduce kinetic energy while total momentum is conserved.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: Independent counts X and Y have PGFs G and H. Why is GH the PGF of X+Y?
options: The counts must have identical distributions
The product rule applies only if one count is always zero
Independence factors the expectation of tˣtʸ into two expectations
The probabilities of equal counts must be added before multiplying
questions.answer: Independence factors the expectation of tˣtʸ into two expectations
questions.explanation: Since t^(X+Y)=tˣtʸ, independence permits factorisation of the expectation.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A paired t analysis defines change as after minus before. If all differences are instead before minus after, what happens to the two-sided p-value?
options: It stays the same while the test statistic changes sign
It doubles because the direction was reversed
It becomes one minus the original p-value
It becomes zero whenever the original mean change was positive
questions.answer: It stays the same while the test statistic changes sign
questions.explanation: Reversing differences negates their mean and t statistic but preserves the statistic's magnitude and the two-sided tail area.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.q: A sample of eight independent observations contains severe right skew and one extreme outlier. Why question a conventional t interval for the mean?
options: The t distribution requires the population standard deviation to be known
Any sample size below 30 makes every t procedure invalid
An outlier can be ignored whenever the sample was random
The small sample offers little protection against strong nonnormality
questions.answer: The small sample offers little protection against strong nonnormality
questions.explanation: With a small sample, strong skewness or outliers can make the t approximation unreliable; random selection alone does not resolve that issue.

questions.subject: Further Mathematics
questions.topic: Statistics: expected counts and test validity
questions.q: A large contingency table has a large total sample but several very small expected cell counts. Why still check the chi-square approximation?
options: More categories always improve the approximation without additional data
Its adequacy depends on expected cell counts, not just the grand total
A large grand total automatically guarantees adequate expected counts in every cell
Observed counts can replace expected counts in every approximation condition
questions.answer: Its adequacy depends on expected cell counts, not just the grand total
questions.explanation: A large sample can still be thinly spread across categories, leaving the chi-square approximation unreliable in sparse cells.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every member of set A is also in B, but B has extra members. Which statement follows?
options: A and B are disjoint
B is a proper subset of A
A equals B
A is a proper subset of B
questions.answer: A is a proper subset of B
questions.explanation: A is contained in B without being equal to it.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A real-valued rule contains the term 1/(x-3). Which input must be excluded?
questions.explanation: At x = 3 the denominator is zero, so the expression is undefined.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The graph of y = f(x) is changed to y = f(x)+4. What changes?
options: Every point moves upward by four units
Every point moves right by four units
All slopes double
The domain necessarily shrinks
questions.answer: Every point moves upward by four units
questions.explanation: Adding a constant to the output produces a vertical translation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An inequality is multiplied on both sides by a negative number. What must change?
options: The inequality becomes an equality
Only the larger side is multiplied
The inequality direction reverses
Both sides become zero
questions.answer: The inequality direction reverses
questions.explanation: Multiplication by a negative number reverses order on the number line.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An angle is increased by one full turn. What happens to its sine and cosine?
options: Both become zero
Both stay the same
Both change sign
Sine doubles while cosine stays fixed
questions.answer: Both stay the same
questions.explanation: Sine and cosine are periodic with a full-turn period.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A sequence increases by the same amount at every step. What feature does its term-number graph have?
options: A continuously doubling slope
A vertical line
A repeating circle
A constant slope
questions.answer: A constant slope
questions.explanation: A constant difference makes the term a linear function of its index.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A positive quantity grows by the same percentage each year. Which model is appropriate?
options: A fixed value with no change
A sequence with constant second difference necessarily
Geometric growth
A constant additive increase
questions.answer: Geometric growth
questions.explanation: Repeated multiplication by a fixed factor produces a geometric sequence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In expanding (1+x)^n for a positive integer n, why is the constant term 1?
options: It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
Every term contains x
The exponents must all be zero
All coefficients are equal to one
questions.answer: It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
questions.explanation: Only the product of all constant choices contributes to the x-to-the-zero term.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two distinct nonvertical lines have the same slope. What follows?
options: They are perpendicular
They meet exactly once
They must pass through the origin
They are parallel
questions.answer: They are parallel
questions.explanation: Equal slopes give the same direction; distinct intercepts keep the lines separate.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two circles subtend the same central angle. Why is the intercepted arc longer on the larger circle?
options: The arc becomes a diameter in every larger circle
Arc length is proportional to radius for a fixed angle
The angle necessarily becomes larger on the larger circle
Arc length is independent of radius
questions.answer: Arc length is proportional to radius for a fixed angle
questions.explanation: The relation between arc length, radius and angle makes arc length scale with radius when angle is fixed.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two vectors have equal magnitudes and opposite directions. What is their sum?
options: The zero vector
A vector twice as long
A unit vector
A scalar equal to their common magnitude
questions.answer: The zero vector
questions.explanation: Opposite equal vectors cancel component by component.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Values of f(x) approach 5 as x approaches 2, but f(2) is defined as 9. What is the limit at 2?
options: It must not exist
questions.explanation: A limit concerns nearby values, not the separately assigned value at the point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A graph has a jump at x = a. Why is the function not continuous there?
options: Its domain must contain only integers
Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
Its value must be negative
Its slope must be positive
questions.answer: Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
questions.explanation: Continuity requires the two-sided limit to exist and equal the function value.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A differentiable function has positive derivative throughout an interval. What does this imply?
options: Its values are all positive
It is constant
It must be linear
It is increasing on the interval
questions.answer: It is increasing on the interval
questions.explanation: Positive derivative gives increasing function values, regardless of their signs.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A nonnegative rate of water inflow is graphed against time. What does area under the graph represent?
options: The tank's initial volume alone
The elapsed time squared
Total water added over that time
The highest flow rate
questions.answer: Total water added over that time
questions.explanation: Integrating a rate over time gives the accumulated quantity.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A population's growth rate is proportional to its current size with a positive constant. What qualitative behaviour follows?
options: Exponential growth in the ideal model
Constant absolute growth
Linear decline
Immediate extinction
questions.answer: Exponential growth in the ideal model
questions.explanation: The differential equation dP/dt = kP gives exponential growth for positive k.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A continuous normal distribution is symmetric about its mean. What proportion lies above the mean?
options: All of it
None of it
A proportion determined only by its standard deviation
One half
questions.answer: One half
questions.explanation: Symmetry divides the total probability equally on either side, with zero probability at one exact value.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two events are mutually exclusive. What is impossible in one trial?
options: Their probabilities adding to less than one
Both occurring together
Either event occurring
Neither event occurring
questions.answer: Both occurring together
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events have an empty intersection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A bag contains red and blue counters. You learn the chosen counter is red. What happens to the relevant sample space?
options: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
It expands to all possible bags
Every original outcome remains equally relevant
It contains no outcomes
questions.answer: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
questions.explanation: Conditioning restricts attention to outcomes satisfying the given information.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For a continuous random variable, probability over an interval is represented by what feature of its density graph?
options: The curve's total length
The number of turning points
Area over that interval
The value at just the left endpoint
questions.answer: Area over that interval
questions.explanation: Density accumulates into probability through area, rather than a single graph height.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A student belongs to A or B, but not both. Which membership condition describes this?
options: Membership in the universal set only
Membership in their symmetric difference
Membership in their intersection
Membership in neither set
questions.answer: Membership in their symmetric difference
questions.explanation: The symmetric difference contains elements belonging to exactly one of the two sets.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two machines act in sequence: the first doubles an input, the second adds three. Why can reversing them change the result?
options: Addition always occurs before multiplication in any real process
Both machines must produce zero
The first machine has no output
The operations need not commute
questions.answer: The operations need not commute
questions.explanation: Doubling after adding three also doubles the added amount, unlike adding it afterward.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A quadratic's discriminant changes from positive to negative as a parameter varies. What changes?
options: Its leading coefficient must become zero
Every coefficient becomes negative
Two distinct real roots become no real roots
No real roots become two distinct real roots
questions.answer: Two distinct real roots become no real roots
questions.explanation: The discriminant's sign determines whether the roots are real and distinct, repeated, or nonreal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A sine equation has one solution in the first quadrant. Why can another occur in the second quadrant?
options: Supplementary angles have equal sine
Sine is one-to-one over a full turn
Cosine is positive in both quadrants
Every angle has the same sine
questions.answer: Supplementary angles have equal sine
questions.explanation: Reflection across the vertical axis preserves the unit-circle y-coordinate.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A complex number is multiplied by its conjugate. Why is the result real and nonnegative?
options: The imaginary part is always zero before multiplication
Conjugation changes its real part's sign
All complex products are nonnegative
It equals the square of its modulus
questions.answer: It equals the square of its modulus
questions.explanation: The imaginary cross terms cancel, leaving the sum of the squared real and imaginary parts.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A geometric sequence has ratio between zero and one. Why can the infinite sum be finite?
options: The terms eventually become negative
Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
There are only finitely many terms
Every term is zero
questions.answer: Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
questions.explanation: For absolute ratio below one, partial sums approach a finite limit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two committee roles are distinct. Why does assigning the same two people in exchanged roles create a different outcome?
options: The role assignment is part of the outcome
The membership becomes a different size
One person disappears
All arrangements are unordered
questions.answer: The role assignment is part of the outcome
questions.explanation: When positions or roles matter, permutations distinguish assignments with the same members.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two points lie on the same line parallel to another line. How do their perpendicular distances to the other line compare?
options: One distance must be zero
Distances depend only on x-coordinate
They are equal
The point farther right is always closer
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Parallel lines remain a constant perpendicular distance apart.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A line touches a circle at one point. How does it relate to the radius through that point?
options: It has the same length as the radius
It is perpendicular to the radius
It is parallel to the radius
It passes through the centre
questions.answer: It is perpendicular to the radius
questions.explanation: The tangent at a circle point is perpendicular to the radius there.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two nonzero vectors have zero dot product. What does this imply?
options: They are parallel in the same direction
They are equal
Their cross product must also be zero
They are perpendicular
questions.answer: They are perpendicular
questions.explanation: The dot product is proportional to the cosine of the angle, which is zero at a right angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two lines in three-dimensional space do not meet and are not parallel. What is possible?
options: They are the same line
Their direction vectors are zero
They are skew
They must lie in one plane
questions.answer: They are skew
questions.explanation: Skew lines are nonparallel, nonintersecting lines in different planes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The graph of absolute value of x has a sharp corner at zero. What is true there?
options: It is continuous but not differentiable
It is differentiable but not continuous
It has an infinite function value
It has the same tangent slope from both sides
questions.answer: It is continuous but not differentiable
questions.explanation: The left and right slopes differ although the function has no discontinuity.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function is increasing but its slope is becoming smaller. Which combination can describe it?
options: Negative first derivative and positive second derivative
Both derivatives negative necessarily
Zero first derivative throughout
Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.answer: Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.explanation: Increasing values require positive slope, while decreasing slope indicates concavity down.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A velocity-time graph has regions above and below the time axis. What does its signed integral represent?
options: Final acceleration
Net displacement
Total distance in every case
Maximum speed
questions.answer: Net displacement
questions.explanation: Positive and negative velocities contribute opposite signed displacements.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: F(x) is the area accumulated under a continuous function f from a fixed starting point to x. What does F'(x) measure?
options: The current value f(x)
The total area squared
Only the starting value of f
Always zero
questions.answer: The current value f(x)
questions.explanation: The derivative of accumulated area recovers the instantaneous integrand.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Events follow a constant-rate Poisson process. An observation interval doubles. What changes about the expected event count?
options: It stays constant
It becomes a negative number
It doubles
It halves
questions.answer: It doubles
questions.explanation: For a constant-rate process, the mean count is proportional to interval length.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two linear equations describe the same line. What is their solution set?
options: One point chosen by the larger coefficient
Infinitely many points on that line
No points
Exactly two points
questions.answer: Infinitely many points on that line
questions.explanation: Dependent equations impose the same condition rather than two independent constraints.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two counters are drawn without replacement from a mixed bag. Why can the second colour depend on the first?
options: The colours physically transform
All second draws are independent by definition
The first counter returns automatically
The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.answer: The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.explanation: Removing a counter changes the proportions remaining for the next selection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every value in a data set increases by the same constant. What happens to variance?
options: It becomes zero
It doubles
It stays unchanged
It rises by that constant
questions.answer: It stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The mean shifts by the same amount, leaving deviations from the mean unchanged.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The sampling method and confidence level stay the same, but a much larger random sample is taken. What usually happens to the interval estimating a mean?
options: It becomes narrower
It becomes wider solely because the sample is larger
It must have zero width
It loses its stated confidence level by definition
questions.answer: It becomes narrower
questions.explanation: Larger samples generally reduce standard error, giving more precise estimates under the model assumptions.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: To disprove the statement 'Every positive integer has property P', what is sufficient?
options: Many integers having P
One negative integer lacking P
No tested counterexample
One positive integer lacking P
questions.answer: One positive integer lacking P
questions.explanation: A single counterexample within the stated domain disproves a universal claim.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A piecewise function has equal left and right limits at a joining point, but its assigned value differs. What repairs continuity there?
options: Set the derivative to one without changing values
Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
Change every nearby value to zero
Remove both intervals entirely
questions.answer: Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
questions.explanation: A removable discontinuity is fixed by matching the point value to its existing limit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An upward-opening quadratic has two distinct real roots. Where is it negative?
options: Strictly between the roots
Outside both roots
Everywhere
Nowhere
questions.answer: Strictly between the roots
questions.explanation: The parabola lies below the axis between its crossings and above it outside them.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Multiplying a nonzero complex number by i changes its plane representation how?
options: Reflection only across the real axis
A quarter-turn clockwise with doubled modulus
A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
A doubling of modulus without rotation
questions.answer: A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
questions.explanation: Multiplication by i adds an angle of pi over two and has modulus one.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A series has terms that approach zero. Why does that alone not prove convergence?
options: A zero term forces every later term to vanish
The partial sums may still grow without bound
Every such series is finite
Terms approaching zero must alternate
questions.answer: The partial sums may still grow without bound
questions.explanation: Vanishing terms are necessary but not sufficient; the harmonic series is a standard counterexample.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair coin has produced several heads in independent tosses. Why is tails not made more likely on the next toss?
options: Tails becomes impossible after enough heads
The coin remembers its previous states
A balancing sequence is guaranteed immediately
The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
questions.answer: The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
questions.explanation: Independent trials retain the same probability regardless of previous outcomes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two lines have proportional x and y coefficients but nonproportional constants in their equations. What follows?
options: They intersect at the origin necessarily
They are perpendicular
They are distinct parallel lines
They are identical lines
questions.answer: They are distinct parallel lines
questions.explanation: Matching coefficient ratios give the same direction, while incompatible constants prevent intersection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A small study fails to reject no difference between two groups. Why is 'the groups are identical' too strong?
options: The test may lack power to detect a real difference
A nonsignificant result proves a large difference
All null hypotheses are true until rejected
Sample size cannot influence test sensitivity
questions.answer: The test may lack power to detect a real difference
questions.explanation: Nonrejection may reflect limited evidence or low power; it does not establish exact equality.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A binomial model has many trials but a very small success probability. Why may a symmetric normal approximation still be poor?
options: A large trial count always makes every distribution exactly normal
The binomial mean must be negative
The outcomes stop being discrete when probability is small
The distribution can remain strongly skewed if expected successes are few
questions.answer: The distribution can remain strongly skewed if expected successes are few
questions.explanation: Both expected successes and expected failures matter for a useful normal approximation; many trials alone are insufficient.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function oscillates between values near -1 and 1 arbitrarily close to a point without narrowing its range. What happens to its limit there?
options: The limit equals the point's assigned value
No single limit exists
The limit must be zero by averaging
The limit must be one
questions.answer: No single limit exists
questions.explanation: Persistent full-amplitude oscillation prevents values from approaching one number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function is differentiable at an interior point. Which conclusion is guaranteed?
options: It is continuous there
Its derivative is positive there
It is locally linear exactly
It has a local extremum there
questions.answer: It is continuous there
questions.explanation: Differentiability implies continuity, but does not determine slope sign or the presence of an extremum.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For f(x)=x cubed, the derivative is zero at zero. Why is zero not a local maximum or minimum?
options: The derivative is undefined there
The function is constant nearby
The function keeps increasing through it
The function is discontinuous there
questions.answer: The function keeps increasing through it
questions.explanation: A zero derivative alone is insufficient; the function increases on both sides of the stationary point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A continuous odd function is integrated from -a to a. Why is the integral zero?
options: Every antiderivative is constant
Opposite signed contributions cancel
The function must be zero everywhere
The interval has zero length
questions.answer: Opposite signed contributions cancel
questions.explanation: Odd symmetry gives equal-magnitude contributions of opposite sign on symmetric intervals.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In dP/dt = kP(1-P/K), with k and K positive, a population is slightly below K. What does the model predict?
options: It decreases away from K
It immediately jumps to zero
It grows exponentially without limit at all sizes
It increases toward K
questions.answer: It increases toward K
questions.explanation: For 0<P<K the growth rate is positive and becomes smaller near the stable equilibrium K.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function changes sign across a vertical asymptote. Why does this not guarantee a root between the endpoints?
options: The intermediate value theorem requires differentiability everywhere
An asymptote must itself be a zero
Continuity on the whole interval is missing
A sign change never gives any information
questions.answer: Continuity on the whole interval is missing
questions.explanation: The intermediate value theorem requires continuity; a discontinuity can separate opposite signs without a zero.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two successive iterates are close together. Why does that alone not prove an accurate root has been found?
options: An iteration can stagnate away from a root
Nearby iterates always prove a root
Every root has a derivative of zero
Iteration values must be integers
questions.answer: An iteration can stagnate away from a root
questions.explanation: Checking the residual and method behaviour is needed; a small step alone can reflect stagnation or numerical limitations.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rare condition has a test with some false positives. Why need a positive result not make the condition highly likely?
options: Test accuracy is irrelevant
A positive result proves the condition is absent
Rare conditions cannot be tested
The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.answer: The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.explanation: The posterior probability depends on both test performance and the prior prevalence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two random variables have finite means but are dependent. Which statement still holds?
options: They must have identical distributions
The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
Their variances always add without a covariance term
Their product mean always equals the product of their means
questions.answer: The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
questions.explanation: Linearity of expectation does not require independence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every observation is multiplied by a constant c. Why is variance multiplied by c squared?
options: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
The mean is always unchanged
Variance counts observations without using values
Only negative constants affect variance
questions.answer: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
questions.explanation: Variance averages squared deviations, so scaling values squares the scale factor.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rate rule is positive just below an equilibrium and negative just above it. What behaviour does this indicate for nearby solutions?
options: They remain at their starting values regardless of the rate
The rule has no equilibrium
They move toward the equilibrium
They move away from the equilibrium
questions.answer: They move toward the equilibrium
questions.explanation: The signs direct motion upward from below and downward from above, indicating local stability.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A trolley moves forward while its velocity-time graph slopes downward. What is happening?
options: It is slowing down
It is moving backward
Its acceleration is zero
Its distance travelled is decreasing
questions.answer: It is slowing down
questions.explanation: A downward slope means negative acceleration; with positive velocity this reduces speed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A passenger leans forward when a bus brakes. Why?
options: The seat increases the passenger's speed
The passenger loses mass
The passenger's body tends to keep moving
A forward force from gravity appears
questions.answer: The passenger's body tends to keep moving
questions.explanation: Inertia resists the change from the body's original forward motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A box remains stationary while you push it gently on a rough floor. What balances your push?
options: An upward force from the floor
Static friction
Kinetic friction
The box's weight alone
questions.answer: Static friction
questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to oppose the push until its limiting value is reached.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two carts initially at rest push apart on a frictionless track. What must their momenta do?
options: Have equal velocities
Point in the same direction
Increase the total momentum
Add to zero
questions.answer: Add to zero
questions.explanation: With no external horizontal force, total momentum remains its initial value of zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone moves at constant speed in a circle. Why is it accelerating?
options: Its speed must be increasing
Its kinetic energy must increase
Its velocity changes direction
Its mass changes continuously
questions.answer: Its velocity changes direction
questions.explanation: Velocity includes direction, which changes throughout circular motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical springs support equal loads, one singly and two in parallel. Which arrangement stretches less?
options: The parallel pair
The single spring
Both stretch equally
Neither arrangement can stretch
questions.answer: The parallel pair
questions.explanation: The parallel springs share the load, increasing the effective stiffness.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two points are at equal depth in connected water at rest. One is in a wide region and one in a narrow region. How do their pressures compare?
options: The narrow region must have higher pressure
The wide region must have higher pressure
Pressure depends only on the container's total volume
They are equal
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure depends on depth, density and surface pressure, not container width.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ice is melting at its melting point under constant pressure. Why can heat enter without raising temperature?
options: All added energy becomes light
Energy changes the phase
The ice has stopped absorbing energy
Its specific heat becomes zero
questions.answer: Energy changes the phase
questions.explanation: Latent heat changes intermolecular arrangement rather than increasing temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Gas expands and pushes a piston. What energy transfer occurs through the moving piston?
options: The gas does work on its surroundings
The surroundings always do positive work on the gas
The gas necessarily gains internal energy
No energy crosses the boundary
questions.answer: The gas does work on its surroundings
questions.explanation: An outward force acting through the piston's displacement transfers energy as work.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At the extreme position of a mass on an ideal spring, which quantity is zero?
options: Its acceleration magnitude
Its elastic potential energy
Its instantaneous speed
Its restoring force
questions.answer: Its instantaneous speed
questions.explanation: The mass reverses direction at the extreme, where its instantaneous velocity is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cork bobs as a water wave passes. What does this illustrate?
options: The cork must move permanently forward
Energy can travel without the cork travelling with the wave
All water travels at the wave speed
The wave carries no energy
questions.answer: Energy can travel without the cork travelling with the wave
questions.explanation: The disturbance propagates while material particles oscillate about local positions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two initially neutral objects become oppositely charged by rubbing. What was transferred between them?
options: Protons between nuclei
Whole positive nuclei only
Gravitational mass
Electrons
questions.answer: Electrons
questions.explanation: Charge separation in ordinary rubbing results from electron transfer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A positive test charge is released in a uniform electric field, with no other force. Which way does it initially accelerate?
options: Perpendicular to the field
It cannot accelerate
Along the field
Against the field
questions.answer: Along the field
questions.explanation: The electric force on a positive charge points along the electric field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One branch of two resistors in parallel is removed from an ideal battery. What happens to current in the remaining branch?
options: It stays the same
It doubles automatically
It falls to zero
It reverses direction
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: The remaining branch still has the same battery voltage across the same resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metal wire is made longer without changing material, temperature or cross-sectional area. Why does resistance increase?
options: The wire gains a larger cross-section
Its resistivity must decrease
Electrons stop carrying charge
Charge carriers encounter a longer conducting path
questions.answer: Charge carriers encounter a longer conducting path
questions.explanation: For fixed resistivity and area, resistance is proportional to length.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnet is held stationary inside a stationary coil. What induced emf results from this unchanged arrangement?
options: An emf that alternates automatically
Zero
A steady emf set only by magnet strength
An emf that grows with time
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Induction requires changing magnetic flux, not merely the presence of a magnetic field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Why does an ordinary transformer need changing current in its primary coil?
options: It needs changing magnetic flux
Its core must rotate
Direct current has no charge carriers
The secondary must touch the primary
questions.answer: It needs changing magnetic flux
questions.explanation: A changing primary current produces flux changes that induce an emf in the secondary.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens forms an image of a very distant object. Where is the image approximately formed?
options: At the lens centre
On the object's side as a virtual image
At the focal plane
At twice the focal length always
questions.answer: At the focal plane
questions.explanation: Nearly parallel incident rays converge near the principal focal plane.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two coherent light waves meet with crest aligned to crest. What happens locally?
options: Their wavelengths halve
Their amplitudes reinforce
Their frequencies cancel
Their speeds double
questions.answer: Their amplitudes reinforce
questions.explanation: The displacements add constructively when the waves are in phase.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radioactive sample contains fewer undecayed nuclei after one half-life. What happens to its activity?
options: It increases
It stays fixed until the last nucleus decays
It becomes independent of the number of nuclei
It decreases
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Activity is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei for a fixed decay constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A velocity-time graph crosses from positive to negative values. What occurs at the crossing?
options: Its distance travelled returns to zero
Its mass changes sign
The object reverses direction
Its acceleration must be zero
questions.answer: The object reverses direction
questions.explanation: The velocity changes sign, indicating reversal; acceleration is determined by the graph's slope.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two balls are launched horizontally from the same height with different speeds. Ignoring air resistance, which lands first?
options: They land together
The faster ball
The slower ball
The heavier ball regardless of speed
questions.answer: They land together
questions.explanation: Their initial vertical velocities and vertical accelerations are identical.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two touching blocks accelerate together on a smooth floor when one is pushed. Why are their net forces unequal if their masses differ?
options: Contact forces violate Newton's third law
The lighter block has no net force
Their velocities must be different
They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
questions.answer: They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives different net forces for different masses at the same acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball moves upward after being thrown, ignoring air resistance. Which description is correct?
options: Gravity does positive work during ascent
Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
Both energies increase
Mechanical energy decreases because speed decreases
questions.answer: Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
questions.explanation: Gravity converts kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy while total mechanical energy stays constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ultrasound pulse gives a later returning echo from interface B than from A in the same tissue. What does that imply?
options: B is farther from the probe
B must reflect more energy
B must be moving toward the probe
The transmitted pulse has a different frequency for each echo
questions.answer: B is farther from the probe
questions.explanation: With the same wave speed, greater round-trip travel time indicates a greater distance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two satellites have circular orbits around Earth. Why is the lower satellite faster?
options: The higher satellite is beyond gravity
The lower satellite must have greater mass
A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
