The lower satellite has no gravitational potential energy
questions.answer: A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
questions.explanation: For a circular orbit, speed is proportional to the inverse square root of orbital radius.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two stars known to have equal luminosity appear with different brightnesses, with negligible absorption. What explains the fainter one?
options: It has lost its intrinsic luminosity by travelling
It is farther away
It necessarily has a lower surface temperature
It emits photons that slow down more
questions.answer: It is farther away
questions.explanation: Flux from a source of fixed luminosity falls with the square of distance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vacuum flask reduces heat transfer through its evacuated gap. Which process can still cross that gap?
options: Conduction through air
Convection of trapped gas
Bulk flow of liquid
Thermal radiation
questions.answer: Thermal radiation
questions.explanation: Radiation does not require matter, whereas gas conduction and convection are suppressed by the vacuum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal gas expands adiabatically while doing work. Why does its temperature decrease?
options: Its number of molecules decreases necessarily
Adiabatic expansion means constant temperature
The work comes from its internal energy
Heat flows into it faster than work leaves
questions.answer: The work comes from its internal energy
questions.explanation: With no heat input, work done by the gas reduces its internal energy and temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal spring oscillator's amplitude doubles while its mass and spring constant stay fixed. What happens to its period?
options: It stays the same
It doubles
It halves
It becomes four times larger
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: The ideal spring period depends on mass and stiffness, not amplitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in its second harmonic. What appears in addition to the end nodes?
options: An antinode at its midpoint
No internal nodes
A travelling crest fixed at one end
A node at its midpoint
questions.answer: A node at its midpoint
questions.explanation: The second harmonic contains two loops separated by a central node.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charge moves along an equipotential surface. What work does the electric field do?
options: Work equal to charge times field strength
Zero
Positive for every charge
Negative for every charge
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Electric work depends on the potential difference, which is zero along an equipotential.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An isolated conductor reaches electrostatic equilibrium. Why is its interior electric field zero?
options: Free charges redistribute until the internal field cancels
The conductor contains no electrons
The conductor's potential must be zero
All external electric fields disappear everywhere
questions.answer: Free charges redistribute until the internal field cancels
questions.explanation: A nonzero internal field would keep free charges moving, contradicting electrostatic equilibrium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A real battery supplies a larger current. Why can its terminal voltage fall?
options: External resistance creates charge
The battery's internal current becomes zero
More voltage is lost across its internal resistance
Its emf must instantly become zero
questions.answer: More voltage is lost across its internal resistance
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage during discharge equals emf minus the internal voltage drop.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At a junction, one entering current becomes two outgoing currents. Why must their sum equal the entering current in steady state?
options: Both outgoing currents must be equal
Charge does not accumulate at the junction
Energy is created at the junction
Resistance is always equal in both branches
questions.answer: Charge does not accumulate at the junction
questions.explanation: Current conservation follows from charge conservation when there is no accumulating charge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnet approaching a conducting loop experiences resistance to its motion. What explains this?
options: The loop creates energy from nothing
The loop always attracts every magnetic pole
Induced current cancels the magnet's mass
The induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux
questions.answer: The induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux
questions.explanation: Lenz's law makes the induced effect oppose the flux change, requiring mechanical work.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal transformer raises the output voltage while transferring the same power. What happens to the output current relative to input current?
options: It is unchanged
It changes direction permanently to DC
It is lower
It is higher
questions.answer: It is lower
questions.explanation: Equal input and output power means current falls when voltage rises.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnifying glass is used with an object inside its focal length. What image does the eye view?
options: An upright magnified virtual image
An inverted reduced real image
A real image at the lens centre
An upright image on a screen behind the lens
questions.answer: An upright magnified virtual image
questions.explanation: A converging lens used inside its focal distance produces an upright enlarged virtual image.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a double-slit experiment, the screen moves farther away while wavelength and slit spacing stay fixed. What happens to fringe spacing?
options: It decreases
It stays fixed
All bright fringes vanish
It increases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Fringe spacing is proportional to the screen distance under the small-angle approximation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A p-n diode is forward biased. How does this promote conduction?
options: It turns both regions into insulators
It reduces the junction barrier
It removes all charge carriers
It widens the depletion region indefinitely
questions.answer: It reduces the junction barrier
questions.explanation: Forward bias lowers the potential barrier, allowing more majority carriers to cross the junction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ruler has a fixed positive zero error. Repeating a length measurement many times gives closely grouped results. What remains unresolved?
options: The systematic offset
Random scatter only
Whether the ruler has markings
The object's physical length changes
questions.answer: The systematic offset
questions.explanation: Repeated readings can improve precision without removing a fixed systematic error.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person stands on a scale in a lift moving upward but slowing down. How does the reading compare with their weight?
options: It equals weight because motion is upward
It is zero in every slowing lift
It is smaller
It is larger
questions.answer: It is smaller
questions.explanation: Upward motion with decreasing speed means downward acceleration, so the normal force is below weight.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two ideal stars have the same luminosity. One has a higher surface temperature. What must be true about its radius?
options: Its radius follows distance from Earth only
It is smaller
It is larger
It must be identical
questions.answer: It is smaller
questions.explanation: A hotter surface emits more power per unit area, so equal total luminosity requires a smaller emitting area.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A star's absorption lines are all shifted to longer wavelengths by the same fractional amount. Which explanation is supported more directly than a change in chemical composition?
options: Every element in the star has changed its electron charge
The star emits no continuum radiation
The star's surface contains no atoms
Recession of the star relative to the observer
questions.answer: Recession of the star relative to the observer
questions.explanation: A common fractional shift of known spectral features is consistent with Doppler recession, while composition changes which features are present.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A satellite is moved into a larger circular orbit. Which combination describes its new state?
options: Lower speed and lower total mechanical energy
Unchanged speed and unchanged total mechanical energy
Lower speed and greater total mechanical energy
Higher speed and greater total mechanical energy
questions.answer: Lower speed and greater total mechanical energy
questions.explanation: Larger circular orbits have lower orbital speed but less negative total mechanical energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metal plate with a circular hole is heated uniformly. Which prediction is consistent with uniform expansion?
options: The hole enlarges as though the missing metal also expanded
The hole shrinks because metal expands inward only
The hole area stays fixed
The hole closes if the plate is thick
questions.answer: The hole enlarges as though the missing metal also expanded
questions.explanation: All linear dimensions scale upward under unconstrained uniform expansion, including the hole diameter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal gas completes a full cycle and performs positive net work. What must be true of net heat transfer?
options: Net heat leaves the gas
Net heat is zero
Internal energy increases each cycle
Net heat enters the gas
questions.answer: Net heat enters the gas
questions.explanation: The internal-energy change over a complete cycle is zero, so net heat input equals net work output.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In ideal spring motion, when is acceleration magnitude greatest while kinetic energy is least?
options: At every position equally
At either extreme displacement
At equilibrium only
Halfway in time between equilibrium and an extreme always
questions.answer: At either extreme displacement
questions.explanation: Restoring acceleration is proportional to displacement, while speed is zero at the extremes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A driven oscillator has modest damping. Increasing damping near resonance most directly does what to its response curve?
options: Lowers and broadens the resonance peak
Raises and narrows the resonance peak
Removes all forcing frequencies
Makes amplitude independent of the drive
questions.answer: Lowers and broadens the resonance peak
questions.explanation: Damping dissipates energy, reducing resonant amplitude and making the response less sharply selective.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At the midpoint between equal positive charges, electric field is zero. What about electric potential, taking zero at infinity?
options: It is negative
It is undefined because fields cancel
It is positive
It is zero because field is zero
questions.answer: It is positive
questions.explanation: Vector fields cancel at the midpoint, but the two positive scalar potentials add.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectified supply uses a capacitor across its load. The load draws more current, all else unchanged. Why does the ripple generally increase?
options: The capacitor remains at peak voltage regardless of load
The capacitor loses more charge between charging peaks
The capacitor's capacitance necessarily increases
Rectification changes the mains frequency to zero
questions.answer: The capacitor loses more charge between charging peaks
questions.explanation: Greater load current discharges the capacitor farther between peaks, increasing voltage variation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical resistors are first in series and then in parallel across the same ideal voltage source. Which arrangement uses greater total power?
options: Series
Both use equal power
Neither can dissipate power
Parallel
questions.answer: Parallel
questions.explanation: Parallel connection has lower equivalent resistance, so total power V squared divided by resistance is greater.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A loop rotates in a uniform magnetic field at constant angular speed. At maximum flux, what is its instantaneous induced emf?
options: Equal to the flux
Infinite
Zero
Maximum magnitude
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Emf depends on the rate of change of flux, which is zero at a smooth flux maximum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A telescope's aperture is increased with the wavelength unchanged. Why can it resolve closer angular details?
options: The diffraction pattern becomes narrower
The incoming wavelength increases
The stars move farther apart
The focal length must become zero
questions.answer: The diffraction pattern becomes narrower
questions.explanation: A larger aperture reduces the diffraction-limited angular spread.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sample is chemically combined into a new compound. In the standard school model, what happens to its nuclear half-life?
options: It halves because bonds form
It doubles because electrons are shared
It follows the compound's boiling point
It remains essentially unchanged
questions.answer: It remains essentially unchanged
questions.explanation: Ordinary chemical changes affect electronic bonding, not the nuclear decay constant in this model.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A positive charge is released from rest where electric potential decreases toward the right. What initially happens?
options: It accelerates right and potential energy increases
It accelerates right and electric potential energy decreases
It accelerates left and electric potential energy decreases
It stays still because potential is a scalar
questions.answer: It accelerates right and electric potential energy decreases
questions.explanation: Electric field points toward decreasing potential, and a positive charge lowers its potential energy as it accelerates that way.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A resistance is inferred from voltage divided by current. Both measurements have small independent uncertainties. Why can the inferred resistance be less precise than either reading alone?
options: Uncertainty from both quantities contributes to the result
Division cancels all measurement uncertainty
Only the quantity in the numerator can affect uncertainty
The answer has no uncertainty if many decimal places are retained
questions.answer: Uncertainty from both quantities contributes to the result
questions.explanation: The ratio depends on both measured values; their fractional uncertainties contribute rather than disappearing through calculation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A glass converging lens is immersed in a liquid whose refractive index is closer to that of glass than air's is. What happens to its converging power?
options: It is fixed by shape alone
It becomes infinite
It decreases
It increases
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Reduced relative refractive index weakens refraction at the lens surfaces.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A proton and an alpha particle enter the same uniform magnetic field perpendicularly with equal speeds. Which has the larger circular radius?
options: Neither follows a curved path
The alpha particle
The proton
Their radii are equal
questions.answer: The alpha particle
questions.explanation: Radius is proportional to mass divided by charge at fixed speed and field; an alpha particle has about twice the proton's mass-to-charge ratio.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron and a proton have equal nonrelativistic kinetic energies. Which has the longer de Broglie wavelength?
options: The proton
They have equal wavelengths
Wavelength depends only on charge
The electron
questions.answer: The electron
questions.explanation: At fixed kinetic energy, the lighter particle has smaller momentum and therefore larger wavelength.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A flood-warning system benefits residents even when individual users cannot easily be charged. Why might collective provision be considered?
options: Individual charges may not capture the shared benefit
Every resident must value it identically
It has no production cost
Only its operator can benefit
questions.answer: Individual charges may not capture the shared benefit
questions.explanation: Some services have shared benefits and are difficult to provide solely through individual purchase.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Two groups accept parts of each other's proposals to reach an agreement. What does this illustrate?
options: Complete agreement on every original demand
The absence of conflicting interests
A decision made without participation
A negotiated compromise
questions.answer: A negotiated compromise
questions.explanation: Compromise can reconcile competing aims through concessions rather than identical preferences.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A constitution allocates authority to national and regional governments. What feature does this illustrate?
options: The absence of national institutions
A requirement that every policy be identical everywhere
A constitutional division of governing powers
All authority belonging to one local official
questions.answer: A constitutional division of governing powers
questions.explanation: Federal arrangements divide authority between levels of government under constitutional rules.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A constitution protects expression even when officials dislike criticism. What purpose does the protection serve?
options: Giving officials unlimited control over opinions
Limiting how public power may be used against individuals
Guaranteeing that every statement is accurate
Making all political disagreement disappear
questions.answer: Limiting how public power may be used against individuals
questions.explanation: Rights protections can constrain government action and preserve space for criticism and participation.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A campaign uses petitions, public meetings and lobbying to seek a reform. What do these activities show?
options: Participation can extend beyond voting
Elections are the only means of expressing political demands
Public opinion cannot influence representatives
Every campaign automatically achieves its goals
questions.answer: Participation can extend beyond voting
questions.explanation: Citizens and organised groups can pursue political change through several forms of engagement.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: An article openly states the political position from which it argues. What can readers do with that disclosure?
options: Assume every statement is false
Treat disclosure as proof of complete neutrality
Stop checking factual claims
Consider how the stated perspective shapes its selection and interpretation of evidence
questions.answer: Consider how the stated perspective shapes its selection and interpretation of evidence
questions.explanation: Identifying a perspective helps readers evaluate framing while still examining the evidence.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A poll asks whether respondents support a proposal described as obviously sensible. What is the concern?
options: The phrase makes every answer more accurate
A leading phrase affects only the survey's length
The wording may lead respondents toward a preferred answer
The wording guarantees a representative sample
questions.answer: The wording may lead respondents toward a preferred answer
questions.explanation: Evaluative wording can introduce response bias rather than neutrally measuring opinions.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Voters are asked to approve or reject a specific policy proposition directly. What distinguishes this from electing a representative?
options: It guarantees that the proposal protects all rights
The vote concerns a policy decision rather than selecting a person to decide
It removes every role for public institutions
It means every voter agrees on the proposal's meaning
questions.answer: The vote concerns a policy decision rather than selecting a person to decide
questions.explanation: A referendum puts a proposition to voters, whereas representative elections choose officeholders.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Several apparently separate news outlets have the same parent owner. What should an analysis of media diversity consider?
options: Common ownership may affect how independent their editorial choices are
Different outlet names prove complete independence
One owner guarantees identical reporting on every issue
Ownership makes the content impossible to examine
questions.answer: Common ownership may affect how independent their editorial choices are
questions.explanation: Ownership structure is relevant to potential influence and diversity, though actual editorial practice also matters.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Reporters examine documents to investigate the misuse of public funds. What democratic function can this support?
options: Automatic proof of every accusation
Replacement of all courts by newspapers
Removal of the need for evidence
Public scrutiny of those exercising power
questions.answer: Public scrutiny of those exercising power
questions.explanation: Investigative reporting can reveal information that helps people hold public authorities accountable.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: In a party-list proportional system, seats are distributed broadly according to parties' vote shares. What is the intended relationship?
options: The largest party must win every seat
Votes are irrelevant once parties submit lists
Representation should reflect the distribution of votes more proportionately
Every party must receive the same seats
questions.answer: Representation should reflect the distribution of votes more proportionately
questions.explanation: Proportional allocation aims to connect the share of seats to electoral support, subject to the system's rules.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: An organisation presents evidence to lawmakers in support of its members' interests. What activity is illustrated?
options: A referendum of all citizens
Lobbying
A judicial verdict
A constitutional amendment by itself
questions.answer: Lobbying
questions.explanation: Lobbying seeks to influence public decisions through communication with decision-makers.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A volunteer joins a campaign because they care about its cause, without expecting personal material reward. What motivates participation here?
options: Commitment to the policy aim
A guaranteed financial payment
An absence of political preferences
A requirement to obtain public office
questions.answer: Commitment to the policy aim
questions.explanation: People can participate because they value a collective or policy objective.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: District boundaries are deliberately drawn to favour one party's chances. What is the main representational concern?
options: Boundaries automatically reveal every voter's preference
Every district must then have identical turnout
Population geography has no connection to representation
Boundary choices can distort how votes translate into seats
questions.answer: Boundary choices can distort how votes translate into seats
questions.explanation: Partisan boundary design can give one side an advantage beyond its overall vote share.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A representative prioritises an area's transport problems after hearing from residents. What relationship is illustrated?
options: Complete independence from constituent interests
A transfer of all legislative power to one resident
Responsiveness to constituency concerns
A guarantee that every resident has identical priorities
questions.answer: Responsiveness to constituency concerns
questions.explanation: Constituency representation involves responding to the interests and concerns of the people represented.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A legislature increasingly includes people from backgrounds previously excluded. Which change is directly described?
options: A necessary change to every constitutional rule
Greater descriptive representation
Proof that every group's policy aims are achieved
The end of all political disagreement
questions.answer: Greater descriptive representation
questions.explanation: Descriptive representation concerns who representatives are, which differs from what policies they pursue.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: In a system authorising judicial review, a court examines whether a law conflicts with the constitution. What role is it exercising?
options: Checking legislation against higher constitutional rules
Writing every future law on its own
Conducting a public opinion poll
Choosing the next election's winner
questions.answer: Checking legislation against higher constitutional rules
questions.explanation: Judicial review assesses the compatibility of public acts with constitutional requirements in systems that provide it.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: One institution makes laws while another implements them under the constitutional arrangement. What distinction is illustrated?
options: Public and private speech only
National and foreign currency
Two identical tasks with different names
Legislative and executive functions
questions.answer: Legislative and executive functions
questions.explanation: Making general rules and administering or enforcing them are distinct governing functions.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A policy is described as successful. Which evidence is most relevant to evaluating that claim?
options: The size of the report's cover image
The number of times officials repeat the claim
Reliable outcomes compared with the policy's stated objectives
Only the popularity of its name
questions.answer: Reliable outcomes compared with the policy's stated objectives
questions.explanation: Evaluation requires evidence about whether intended results were achieved and what other effects occurred.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A government's spending exceeds its revenue in a particular year. What does this describe?
options: A guarantee that every public service has expanded
A budget deficit for that period
The entire accumulated public debt
A budget surplus
questions.answer: A budget deficit for that period
questions.explanation: The annual deficit is a flow, distinct from the stock of debt accumulated over time.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Many groups are allowed to participate, but a small wealthy group has consistently greater access to decision-makers. What should political analysis distinguish?
options: Formal opportunities to participate from unequal practical influence
Legal participation from the complete absence of power
Wealth from influence as necessarily unrelated
The number of group names from all actual outcomes
questions.answer: Formal opportunities to participate from unequal practical influence
questions.explanation: Equal formal access does not establish equal resources, attention or influence in practice.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A respondent gives an immediate answer about an unfamiliar issue, then changes it after learning more. What should a poll analyst consider?
options: Every changed answer is deliberate dishonesty
The first answer must be the only genuine preference
All opinions are fixed before people encounter information
Some expressed preferences may be weakly formed or sensitive to information
questions.answer: Some expressed preferences may be weakly formed or sensitive to information
questions.explanation: Opinions vary in strength and familiarity, so a response need not represent a settled position.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: One chamber represents population while another gives regions equal representation. What tension can this design address?
options: The elimination of every legislative disagreement
A requirement that both chambers always have identical members
Representation of people alongside representation of constituent regions
The need to give every region the same population
questions.answer: Representation of people alongside representation of constituent regions
questions.explanation: Different representation rules can balance population-based and territorial interests.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A higher government requires a new regional service but supplies no additional funding. What issue arises?
options: The requirement guarantees uniform local capacity
Responsibility can increase without matching financial resources
The service is necessarily cost-free
Regional budgets automatically rise by the required amount
questions.answer: Responsibility can increase without matching financial resources
questions.explanation: A mandate can impose costs that the implementing authority must find resources to meet.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Regional governments choose different policies and have unequal revenue bases. What consequence is possible?
options: Service provision may vary across regions
Every resident must receive identical provision
Regional choice guarantees equal economic resources
A constitution makes all implementation differences impossible
questions.answer: Service provision may vary across regions
questions.explanation: Decentralised choices and unequal capacity can produce variation in public services.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A right binds national authorities but is not effectively protected against equivalent regional action. What gap remains?
options: The right is necessarily protected equally everywhere
Regional authority can have no effect on individuals
Written national rights automatically resolve every enforcement issue
Protection depends on which level exercises the power
questions.answer: Protection depends on which level exercises the power
questions.explanation: Effective rights protection requires attention to the authorities bound by the rules and the means of enforcement.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A rule is written identically for everyone but creates severe barriers for one group. What must an equality analysis examine?
options: Whether every rule must have identical effects in all circumstances
Whether unequal effects make evidence unnecessary
Its practical effects as well as its formally equal wording
Only whether the same font is used
questions.answer: Its practical effects as well as its formally equal wording
questions.explanation: Formal uniformity does not settle whether a policy creates unjustified or discriminatory disadvantages.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A policy protects one group's interests while restricting another group's liberty. What should a reasoned assessment consider?
options: An assumption that interests can never conflict
The justification, effects and proportionality of the competing claims
Only which group is larger
A rule that every restriction is justified by popularity
questions.answer: The justification, effects and proportionality of the competing claims
questions.explanation: Political judgement often requires weighing rights and interests rather than treating one benefit as decisive by itself.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A popular top-level candidate attracts voters who also support other candidates from the same party. What effect is illustrated?
options: A coattail effect across linked contests
Proof that every candidate has identical personal popularity
A change in the legal voting age
An absence of party influence
questions.answer: A coattail effect across linked contests
questions.explanation: Support for one prominent candidate can benefit other candidates sharing the party label.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: An officeholder has greater name recognition and a record of constituency service than a new challenger. Why can this matter electorally?
options: Holding office guarantees re-election
Challengers cannot communicate with voters
Voters are legally required to support incumbents
Existing office can provide advantages separate from the merits of a new proposal
questions.answer: Existing office can provide advantages separate from the merits of a new proposal
questions.explanation: Visibility, established networks and service records can contribute to incumbency advantages.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Two reports use the same statistics, but one foregrounds individual stories and the other institutions and long-term trends. What differs?
options: The existence of the event being reported
The legal status of both publishers
The framing of the issue
Necessarily the arithmetic of every statistic
questions.answer: The framing of the issue
questions.explanation: Framing selects which aspects and explanations receive attention, even when some underlying facts are shared.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A small party has substantial national support spread thinly across many single-member plurality districts. Why might it win few seats?
options: The system counts only the opinions of party leaders
It may rarely finish first in any district
National vote share automatically guarantees equal seat share
Every district must reserve it a seat
questions.answer: It may rarely finish first in any district
questions.explanation: Geographically dispersed support can translate poorly into seats where winning each district is decisive.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A campaign's success would benefit supporters and non-contributors alike. Why may it struggle to recruit contributions?
options: People may hope to benefit from others' effort without contributing
The benefit cannot be shared by definition
Non-contributors must receive no benefit
A shared aim guarantees equal contributions
questions.answer: People may hope to benefit from others' effort without contributing
questions.explanation: Free-rider incentives can make collective organisation difficult even when the outcome has broad value.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A system requires both chambers to approve the same bill, but they pass different versions. What must happen before enactment under that rule?
options: Either version automatically becomes law without further action
The larger chamber's version always prevails regardless of the rule
The two texts can be treated as identical because their titles match
The disagreement must be resolved so both approve a common text
questions.answer: The disagreement must be resolved so both approve a common text
questions.explanation: Requiring concurrence gives both chambers a role in agreeing the legislation's actual content.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A proposed constitution makes the executive entirely dependent on a single legislature for appointment and removal. What concern might critics raise?
options: The disappearance of all legislative authority
A necessary increase in judicial power in every case
Insufficient institutional independence to check that legislature
A guarantee that the executive cannot be influenced
questions.answer: Insufficient institutional independence to check that legislature
questions.explanation: The arrangement may concentrate effective control unless other checks and accountability mechanisms operate.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: An executive appeals directly to the public to build support for a policy that legislators resist. What resource is being used?
options: The right to cancel every future election
The visibility and persuasive platform of executive office
A judicial power to invalidate legislation
A guarantee of automatic legislative approval
questions.answer: The visibility and persuasive platform of executive office
questions.explanation: Public communication can create political pressure even when it does not supply a formal power to legislate.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: An executive nominates an official, but another institution must approve the appointment. What is the intended check?
options: More than one institution participates in selecting the official
The nominee automatically chooses all approvers
Approval is unnecessary once a nomination exists
The public has no possible interest in appointments
questions.answer: More than one institution participates in selecting the official
questions.explanation: Shared appointment powers can limit unilateral control, while also creating opportunities for disagreement or delay.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A judge gives weight to the choices of elected institutions when the legal framework permits discretion. What approach does this illustrate?
options: A claim that courts never interpret law
A power to replace every elected decision automatically
The abolition of constitutional rules
Judicial restraint
questions.answer: Judicial restraint
questions.explanation: Judicial restraint emphasises limits on judicial intervention and respect for other institutions' legitimate roles.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A national grant is available only if a regional government adopts specified practices. How can it influence regional policy?
options: Funding conditions have no influence on incentives
The grant removes all need for regional administration
Financial conditions can encourage choices beyond an unconditional transfer
The region receives the funds regardless of every condition
questions.answer: Financial conditions can encourage choices beyond an unconditional transfer
questions.explanation: Conditional grants can shape decisions by linking resources to compliance with policy requirements.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Public employees are selected through job-related qualifications rather than personal party connections. What principle is emphasised?
options: Selection by the largest private donation
Merit-based recruitment
Political patronage as the only criterion
Inheritance of every public position
questions.answer: Merit-based recruitment
questions.explanation: Merit systems aim to connect recruitment with competence rather than personal or partisan favour.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Everyone values a shared benefit, yet voluntary contributions remain low because people expect others to pay. What explains the gap?
options: Individual incentives can obstruct a collectively desired outcome
Low contributions prove nobody values the outcome
Shared benefits automatically produce full cooperation
The outcome cannot have any public-good characteristics
questions.answer: Individual incentives can obstruct a collectively desired outcome
questions.explanation: Collective value does not remove incentives to free ride when benefits cannot easily be withheld from non-contributors.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Two powerful groups reach a compromise that imposes substantial costs on people excluded from negotiation. What remains to assess?
options: Only whether the negotiating groups are satisfied
Whether compromise automatically guarantees justice
Whether excluded people can have legitimate interests
Whether the agreement fairly considers affected non-participants
questions.answer: Whether the agreement fairly considers affected non-participants
questions.explanation: Agreement among participants does not establish legitimacy or fairness for everyone affected.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A constitution makes amendment much harder than ordinary lawmaking. What trade-off does this create?
options: The ability to change every rule without consent
An absence of any future constitutional dispute
Stability and protection against sudden change versus adaptability
A guarantee that all existing provisions are just
questions.answer: Stability and protection against sudden change versus adaptability
questions.explanation: Entrenchment can protect foundational rules but can also make needed reform more difficult.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Two states give regions similar practical powers, but only one constitution protects those powers against ordinary national revocation. Why is the distinction important?
options: The number of regions alone determines their legal security
Similar current arrangements can rest on different guarantees of regional autonomy
Practical delegation is always constitutionally identical to federalism
A written guarantee proves that no disputes will occur
questions.answer: Similar current arrangements can rest on different guarantees of regional autonomy
questions.explanation: The source and protection of regional authority matter alongside the powers currently exercised.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Regional policy experiments reveal useful results, but some effects cross regional borders. What must an evaluation include?
options: Learning benefits alongside spillovers affecting other jurisdictions
Only outcomes inside the experimenting region
An assumption that regional boundaries stop all effects
A rule that variation prevents any useful comparison
questions.answer: Learning benefits alongside spillovers affecting other jurisdictions
questions.explanation: Decentralised experimentation can generate information while creating external effects requiring coordination.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A large voluntary poll has many responses but attracts mainly highly motivated supporters. Why is size alone insufficient?
options: A large poll must represent every group equally
More responses necessarily remove every wording effect
A narrow numerical margin proves random recruitment
Selection bias can persist despite a large sample
questions.answer: Selection bias can persist despite a large sample
questions.explanation: Precision from many observations does not repair systematic differences between respondents and the target population.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A clear majority supports a measure restricting a minority's protected rights. Why does the vote alone not settle legitimacy?
options: Minority rights require unanimous agreement on every policy
Popularity automatically eliminates constitutional limits
Democratic decisions must also be assessed against rights and constitutional constraints
A majority can never make any legitimate decision
questions.answer: Democratic decisions must also be assessed against rights and constitutional constraints
questions.explanation: Majority rule is one democratic principle and operates alongside protections against misuse of public power.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Incumbents win often, but stronger candidates also tend to become incumbents. Why is the win rate alone not the causal effect of holding office?
options: A causal conclusion requires no comparison
Candidate selection and office advantages may both contribute
The win rate proves office has no possible effect
All incumbents and challengers must be equally strong
questions.answer: Candidate selection and office advantages may both contribute
questions.explanation: Separating incumbency's effect requires considering differences that existed before the office was held.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A market has many outlet brands but concentrated ownership and similar source dependence. What would best assess viewpoint diversity?
options: Examine ownership, editorial practice and the actual range of coverage
Count brand names and assume each is independent
Assume one owner forces identical coverage in every article
Treat audience size as the only measure of diversity
questions.answer: Examine ownership, editorial practice and the actual range of coverage
questions.explanation: The number of labels alone does not reveal independence or variation in the information supplied.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Readers see the same event framed either as individual failure or as a result of institutional conditions. Why might their preferred responses differ?
options: Framing must change every underlying fact
Readers' preferences cannot respond to interpretation
Only the article's publication date can matter
Different causal emphases can make different remedies seem appropriate
questions.answer: Different causal emphases can make different remedies seem appropriate
questions.explanation: Explanations of why a problem occurs influence which policy responses appear relevant or justified.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: Two electoral systems produce different seat shares from the same distribution of votes. What follows?
options: One numerical outcome proves every other system undemocratic
Electoral rules have no substantive political consequences
Rules translating votes into seats affect representation
The voters must secretly have cast different ballots
questions.answer: Rules translating votes into seats affect representation
questions.explanation: District structures, thresholds and allocation rules can produce different representative outcomes from similar support.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: An oddly shaped district benefits one party, but settlement patterns are also geographically uneven. What is needed before attributing the result solely to manipulation?
options: Only the colour used to draw the map
Evidence about boundary choices and plausible alternatives given population geography
A rule that every unusual shape proves partisan intent
An assumption that population geography explains every boundary
questions.answer: Evidence about boundary choices and plausible alternatives given population geography
questions.explanation: Assessing gerrymandering requires more than shape alone and should consider the design process and relevant alternatives.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A legislature becomes more socially diverse, but policy outcomes for excluded groups barely change. What distinction matters?
options: Who holds office and whose interests policy serves are related but distinct
Social diversity has no possible political relevance
Diverse membership guarantees every desired policy
Policy outcomes can be inferred from appearance alone
questions.answer: Who holds office and whose interests policy serves are related but distinct
questions.explanation: Descriptive representation does not automatically establish substantive representation in decisions and outcomes.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A proposal has broad support but must pass several independent approval stages. Why can it still fail?
options: Popular support automatically overrides all procedures
Multiple stages guarantee faster agreement
Only the proposal's title determines its passage
Each stage can create a veto point or bargaining obstacle
questions.answer: Each stage can create a veto point or bargaining obstacle
questions.explanation: Institutional procedures shape which preferences become policy and can block measures despite substantial support.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A court can invalidate an elected legislature's law under constitutional rules. What tension must an analysis consider?
options: Proof that elections have no value
A guarantee that courts never make contested interpretations
Protecting constitutional limits while respecting democratic accountability
A choice between having any law and having no law
questions.answer: Protecting constitutional limits while respecting democratic accountability
questions.explanation: Constitutional review can constrain majorities, raising questions about both rights protection and the legitimate scope of judicial power.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A commentator praises judicial restraint only when it helps their preferred policy and demands intervention otherwise. What weakens the argument?
options: A preferred outcome makes consistency irrelevant
The stated institutional principle is being applied selectively
Every change of opinion is necessarily dishonest
No judicial decision can be evaluated
questions.answer: The stated institutional principle is being applied selectively
questions.explanation: A principled institutional argument needs reasons for different treatment beyond whether the outcome is personally favoured.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: An agency is judged only by the number of cases processed and begins prioritising easy cases over urgent complex ones. What problem is illustrated?
options: A performance measure can redirect effort away from the underlying public purpose
Higher counts prove better service for every group
Measurement removes every need for judgement
Complex cases must be outside the agency's responsibility
questions.answer: A performance measure can redirect effort away from the underlying public purpose
questions.explanation: Narrow targets can create incentives that improve the metric while weakening the outcome it was meant to represent.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A public service is contracted to a private provider, but government remains responsible for access and standards. What follows?
options: Private delivery automatically ends all public responsibility
A contract guarantees quality without monitoring
Ownership alone resolves every access concern
Contracting changes delivery without removing the need for public oversight
questions.answer: Contracting changes delivery without removing the need for public oversight
questions.explanation: Accountability requires arrangements for standards, monitoring and remedy even when a different organisation delivers the service.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: An outcome improves after a reform while several other relevant conditions change. What is the strongest evaluation approach?
options: Reject all evidence because circumstances are complex
Use only supporters' descriptions of success
Compare credible alternatives and account for the other changes before attributing the effect
Assign the full improvement to the reform because it came first
questions.answer: Compare credible alternatives and account for the other changes before attributing the effect
questions.explanation: Temporal sequence alone cannot isolate a reform's causal contribution when other influences are changing.

questions.subject: Politics
questions.q: A deficit grows during a downturn even though tax rules and spending programmes are unchanged. Why not assume a new discretionary stimulus?
options: The public budget is independent of economic conditions
Automatic changes in receipts and some payments can widen the deficit
An unchanged programme guarantees an unchanged budget balance
Every deficit increase proves a new law was passed
questions.answer: Automatic changes in receipts and some payments can widen the deficit
questions.explanation: The fiscal balance can respond to the cycle without a deliberate change in policy settings.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Two organisms share many inherited structural features. What does this most reasonably suggest?
options: They cannot differ in DNA
A relatively close evolutionary relationship
Identical habitats are required
They must be the same species
questions.answer: A relatively close evolutionary relationship
questions.explanation: Shared inherited features can indicate common ancestry, although convergent features must be distinguished.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A cell is placed in a solution with lower water potential than its cytoplasm. What tends to happen?
options: Water enters the cell only
The cell instantly makes more water
Solute movement must stop
Water leaves the cell
questions.answer: Water leaves the cell
questions.explanation: Water moves by osmosis toward the lower water potential across a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A cell grows much larger without changing shape. Why can exchange become less efficient relative to its needs?
options: Its membrane becomes nonselective automatically
Its enzymes stop existing
Volume increases faster than surface area
Surface area disappears
questions.answer: Volume increases faster than surface area
questions.explanation: A decreasing surface-area-to-volume ratio makes exchange less sufficient for the larger internal volume.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A tissue repairs a small wound by mitosis. What should daughter cells normally retain?
options: The parent cell's chromosome number
Half the parent cell's chromosomes
A completely new genetic code
No DNA
questions.answer: The parent cell's chromosome number
questions.explanation: Mitosis normally preserves chromosome number in genetically similar daughter cells.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Why does meiosis reduce chromosome number before fertilisation?
options: It makes gametes have no genes
It prevents all genetic variation
It makes every offspring identical
It prevents chromosome number doubling each generation
questions.answer: It prevents chromosome number doubling each generation
questions.explanation: Fusion of two haploid gametes restores diploidy without continually increasing chromosome number.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A leaf receives light but very little carbon dioxide. Why may increasing light fail to raise photosynthesis?
options: Oxygen replaces carbon dioxide in sugar synthesis
Carbon dioxide is limiting
Chlorophyll must be absent
Light never affects photosynthesis
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide is limiting
questions.explanation: Increasing a nonlimiting factor has little effect when another required factor restricts the rate.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A working muscle's ATP demand rises. Why must ATP be continually regenerated?
options: Cells hold only a limited immediately available ATP supply
ATP cannot be broken down
All ATP is stored permanently in DNA
ATP contains no transferable energy
questions.answer: Cells hold only a limited immediately available ATP supply
questions.explanation: ATP is rapidly used and resynthesized to support continuing cellular work.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A recessive trait appears in a child of two unaffected parents in a simple autosomal model. What is a possible explanation?
options: The allele must be dominant
The child has no chromosomes
Both parents carry the recessive allele
Neither parent has the allele
questions.answer: Both parents carry the recessive allele
questions.explanation: Two heterozygous parents can each transmit the recessive allele.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Before cell division, DNA is copied. Why is accurate copying important?
options: Proteins cannot exist near DNA
Each daughter cell needs inherited genetic information
DNA supplies all the cell's oxygen
Copying removes every mutation from the species
questions.answer: Each daughter cell needs inherited genetic information
questions.explanation: Replication preserves genetic instructions for transmission to daughter cells.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Antibiotic treatment leaves a few resistant bacteria alive. Why can resistance become more common afterward?
options: Every bacterium deliberately chooses a mutation
The antibiotic teaches all bacteria to resist
Sensitive bacteria become mammals
Resistant survivors reproduce
questions.answer: Resistant survivors reproduce
questions.explanation: Selection favours resistant variants already present or arising through mutation and gene transfer.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A population grows rapidly, then slows as food becomes scarce. What explains the slowdown?
options: The disappearance of reproduction in all species
A lack of any environmental effect
Density-dependent competition
An unlimited carrying capacity
questions.answer: Density-dependent competition
questions.explanation: Competition intensifies as population density approaches resource limits.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Dead leaves decay and mineral nutrients return to soil. What ecological link is illustrated?
options: Decomposers recycle matter
Decomposers create sunlight
Energy cycles without any loss
Plants do not need nutrients
questions.answer: Decomposers recycle matter
questions.explanation: Decomposition releases nutrients from organic matter for reuse in ecosystems.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A reserve protects several connected habitats instead of one tiny isolated patch. What advantage can connections provide?
options: Guaranteed extinction of predators
Elimination of all competition
Identical conditions everywhere
Movement and gene flow between populations
questions.answer: Movement and gene flow between populations
questions.explanation: Habitat connections can reduce isolation and support dispersal and genetic exchange.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A large amount of heat causes only a modest temperature rise in water. How can hydrogen bonding help explain this?
options: Water cannot absorb energy at all
Some energy disrupts intermolecular attractions before substantially increasing molecular motion
Water molecules contain no kinetic energy
Hydrogen bonds turn heat into new oxygen atoms
questions.answer: Some energy disrupts intermolecular attractions before substantially increasing molecular motion
questions.explanation: Intermolecular hydrogen bonding contributes to water's high specific heat capacity.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Phospholipids placed in water form a bilayer. Which arrangement minimises unfavourable contact?
options: Hydrophobic tails face inward away from water
Hydrophilic heads face inward away from water
All tails remain individually exposed to water
Every phospholipid breaks into separate atoms
questions.answer: Hydrophobic tails face inward away from water
questions.explanation: Amphipathic phospholipids arrange polar heads toward water and nonpolar tails toward each other.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A signalling molecule is present around two cell types, but only one responds. What can account for this?
options: All cells must respond identically to any signal
Nonresponsive cells necessarily have no DNA
Only the responsive cells have the appropriate receptor and pathway
The molecule has a different chemical identity beside each cell
questions.answer: Only the responsive cells have the appropriate receptor and pathway
questions.explanation: Cellular response depends on compatible receptors and downstream machinery, not just signal presence.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A cell uses ATP hydrolysis to drive an otherwise unfavourable reaction. What must coupling accomplish?
options: Convert the reaction into an equilibrium with no net change
Make the combined process energetically favourable
Remove the need for conservation of energy
Ensure every individual step releases more energy than the last
questions.answer: Make the combined process energetically favourable
questions.explanation: An energetically favourable coupled process can drive a component reaction that would not proceed favourably on its own.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A damaged cell fails to respond to a signal that normally stops division. What risk increases?
options: Immediate repair of all mutations
Permanent prevention of any further division
Loss of every chromosome before DNA replication
Proliferation of cells carrying the damage
questions.answer: Proliferation of cells carrying the damage
questions.explanation: Checkpoint failures can allow damaged genetic material to be replicated and passed to descendant cells.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Genetically similar plants grow to different heights under different light conditions. What does this show?
options: The plants must belong to unrelated species
Light directly dictates the same DNA mutation in every plant
Environment can affect phenotype
Height cannot have any genetic contribution
questions.answer: Environment can affect phenotype
questions.explanation: Phenotype reflects interactions between inherited information and environmental conditions.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A botanist wants to estimate grass cover across a large field. Why sample several randomly placed quadrats?
options: To reduce location bias and represent variation
To guarantee every quadrat has identical cover
To count only the largest plants
To avoid using observations in the estimate
questions.answer: To reduce location bias and represent variation
questions.explanation: Random placement reduces selection bias, and multiple samples better capture spatial variation.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Two species look alike but their similarities evolved independently in similar environments. What should a classification study do?
options: Assume identical appearance proves recent ancestry
Ignore DNA because appearance is always decisive
Treat similar environments as identical genomes
Use additional inherited and molecular evidence
questions.answer: Use additional inherited and molecular evidence
questions.explanation: Convergence can imitate relatedness, so multiple lines of evidence are needed.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A membrane protein moves ions against their concentration gradient. What additional requirement is likely?
options: Destruction of all membrane proteins
An energy source
A completely impermeable cell wall
Identical ion concentrations on both sides
questions.answer: An energy source
questions.explanation: Moving against an electrochemical gradient requires energy, directly or through coupling.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Adding more substrate reduces the effect of a reversible competitive inhibitor. Why?
options: Substrate competes more successfully for the active site
The inhibitor is converted into substrate
The enzyme is permanently denatured
The reaction no longer needs enzymes
questions.answer: Substrate competes more successfully for the active site
questions.explanation: Higher substrate concentration increases the likelihood of substrate occupying the shared binding site.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Homologous chromosomes exchange corresponding segments during meiosis. What can result?
options: Loss of all genes from both chromosomes
Identical copies of one parental chromosome only
New combinations of alleles on a chromosome
A doubling of chromosome number in every gamete
questions.answer: New combinations of alleles on a chromosome
questions.explanation: Crossing over recombines linked alleles between homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Light reactions stop supplying ATP and NADPH. Why does carbon fixation soon slow?
options: The chloroplast loses all membranes immediately
Carbon reduction needs their energy and reducing power
The Calvin cycle directly absorbs all required photons
Carbon dioxide instantly disappears from the atmosphere
questions.answer: Carbon reduction needs their energy and reducing power
questions.explanation: The Calvin cycle depends on ATP and NADPH generated by light-dependent reactions.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Why can fermentation sustain glycolysis when oxygen is absent?
options: It produces oxygen for mitochondria
It makes ATP without any substrate
It eliminates the need for enzymes
It regenerates NAD+
questions.answer: It regenerates NAD+
questions.explanation: Regeneration of NAD+ allows the oxidation step in glycolysis to continue.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A hormone raises a variable, and the rise then reduces that hormone's secretion. What does this feedback do?
options: Prevents any response to change
Makes secretion independent of conditions
Stabilises the variable
Amplifies the change indefinitely
questions.answer: Stabilises the variable
questions.explanation: Negative feedback opposes deviations and helps maintain a regulated range.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A DNA base changes but the encoded amino acid stays the same. What explains this?
options: Different codons can specify the same amino acid
Every mutation deletes a chromosome
Ribosomes ignore all RNA
Amino acids determine DNA bases in reverse
questions.answer: Different codons can specify the same amino acid
questions.explanation: The genetic code is degenerate, allowing some substitutions to be synonymous.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A gene's mRNA is present but no protein is produced after ribosome function is blocked. Which stage is directly affected?
options: DNA replication
Transcription initiation only
Chromosome segregation
Translation
questions.answer: Translation
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA and assemble amino acids during translation.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Two species use nearly identical limited resources in the same habitat. What reduces direct competition?
options: Having identical resource requirements forever
Partitioning resources or feeding times
Increasing their niche overlap
Eliminating all environmental variation
questions.answer: Partitioning resources or feeding times
questions.explanation: Niche differentiation allows species to use different parts of available resources.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A flowering plant gains pollination while an insect gains nectar. What makes this mutualism?
options: Both species benefit
Only the insect benefits and the plant is harmed
Neither species gains anything
Both must be the same species
questions.answer: Both species benefit
questions.explanation: Mutualism describes interactions with a benefit to each participating species.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A DNA sample is repeatedly heated, cooled with primers, and extended by polymerase. Why are primers needed?
options: They cut every target molecule into amino acids
They convert RNA directly into protein
They provide starting points for DNA synthesis
They replace all template DNA
questions.answer: They provide starting points for DNA synthesis
questions.explanation: DNA polymerase extends from an existing primer with a free 3-prime end.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: One activated receptor triggers several enzymes, each activating many further molecules. What property of the pathway is illustrated?
options: Production of new atoms from the signal
Signal amplification
A requirement that every step use one molecule only
Loss of information because receptors cannot bind signals
questions.answer: Signal amplification
questions.explanation: A cascade can turn a small initial signal into a larger intracellular response through successive activation.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: One gene gives rise to different mature mRNAs in two tissues. How can this expand protein diversity?
options: Every tissue must use a different genetic code
RNA splicing adds new chromosomes to the nucleus
All variants must contain the same amino-acid sequence
Different exon combinations can produce different protein variants
questions.answer: Different exon combinations can produce different protein variants
questions.explanation: Different processing of one transcript can retain different coding segments and generate multiple products.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: At a lower temperature, a cell's membrane contains more unsaturated fatty-acid tails. How can this help maintain fluidity?
options: Unsaturated lipids eliminate the bilayer
The tails become fully water-soluble
Kinks hinder tight packing of the tails
Double bonds make tails pack more tightly in every case
questions.answer: Kinks hinder tight packing of the tails
questions.explanation: Cis double bonds introduce kinks that reduce tight packing, helping membranes remain fluid.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Pollen from another population fertilises local plants. How can this alter local genetic variation?
options: It can introduce alleles carried by the other population
It guarantees that local mutation stops
It changes all offspring to haploid adults
It necessarily removes every local allele immediately
questions.answer: It can introduce alleles carried by the other population
questions.explanation: Migration of genetic material between populations can change allele frequencies and introduce variants.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A population becomes crowded and disease transmission rises because contacts are more frequent. What kind of regulation is illustrated?
options: A factor independent of population density by definition
An increase in carrying capacity with no other change
The absence of interactions between organisms
Density-dependent limitation
questions.answer: Density-dependent limitation
questions.explanation: The effect intensifies with crowding, linking population density to survival or reproduction.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Observed offspring counts differ slightly from a Mendelian expected ratio. Why is a statistical test useful?
options: The test identifies the full DNA sequence
It helps assess whether the discrepancy exceeds plausible sampling variation
Any difference automatically disproves inheritance
Expected ratios require exactly equal counts in every small sample
questions.answer: It helps assess whether the discrepancy exceeds plausible sampling variation
questions.explanation: Chance affects finite samples; statistical comparison evaluates the strength of evidence against the expected pattern.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A solute's uptake rate levels off as external concentration rises, despite an increasing gradient. What can explain the plateau?
options: A limited number of transport proteins are saturated
Diffusion gradients have become irrelevant to all membranes
The solute must be converted into water
The membrane has acquired unlimited carriers
questions.answer: A limited number of transport proteins are saturated
questions.explanation: Carrier-mediated transport has a finite capacity when the available proteins are fully occupied.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Two random samples from the same habitat give somewhat different species estimates. What is the best initial interpretation?
options: The habitat necessarily changed completely between samples
Random sampling guarantees identical results
Sampling variation can occur even with a sound method
One sample must have been fabricated
questions.answer: Sampling variation can occur even with a sound method
questions.explanation: Random samples differ; replication helps quantify variation and improves the estimate.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Two populations look different but interbreed and produce fertile offspring naturally. Under a biological species concept, what is strongest evidence they belong to one species?
options: The fact that both have cells
Reproductive compatibility and gene flow
Different body colour alone
Different local food sources alone
questions.answer: Reproductive compatibility and gene flow
questions.explanation: The biological species concept emphasizes reproductive connection rather than appearance alone.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Plant and animal cells are placed in sufficiently dilute solutions. Why can the plant cell become turgid while the animal cell may burst?
options: Plant membranes are completely impermeable to water
Animal cells contain no solute
The plant cell has no osmotic gradient
The plant wall resists expansion and builds opposing pressure
questions.answer: The plant wall resists expansion and builds opposing pressure
questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall limits expansion, allowing pressure potential to oppose further water entry.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A reversible inhibitor binds only away from the active site and reduces active enzyme function; adding substrate does not restore maximum rate. What is supported?
options: A substrate shortage as the sole cause
An increase in enzyme concentration
Noncompetitive inhibition in the ideal model
Simple competition only for the same active site
questions.answer: Noncompetitive inhibition in the ideal model
questions.explanation: An ideal noncompetitive inhibitor lowers functional catalytic capacity that extra substrate cannot restore.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A mitochondrial membrane becomes freely permeable to protons while electron transfer can continue. What happens to ATP synthesis by ATP synthase?
options: It decreases as the proton gradient dissipates
It increases without limit
It becomes independent of the gradient
It moves into the nucleus
questions.answer: It decreases as the proton gradient dissipates
questions.explanation: ATP synthase relies on the proton-motive force; a proton leak uncouples it from electron transport.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A leaf's photosynthesis increases with added CO2 at one light level but barely responds in dim light. What explains the contrast?
options: CO2 is never a photosynthetic substrate
Dim light destroys every chloroplast instantly
Light and CO2 act independently at all levels
The limiting factor differs between conditions
questions.answer: The limiting factor differs between conditions
questions.explanation: CO2 may limit at adequate light, whereas insufficient light limits the response in dim conditions.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A trait follows mitochondrial inheritance in the usual human model. Why can affected mothers pass it on while affected fathers generally do not?
options: Only sons receive egg cytoplasm
Most embryonic mitochondria come from the egg
Fathers have no mitochondria
Mitochondrial DNA is carried on the Y chromosome
questions.answer: Most embryonic mitochondria come from the egg
questions.explanation: The egg supplies nearly all zygotic cytoplasm and mitochondria in typical human inheritance.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Two genes yield parental allele combinations much more frequently than recombinants. What is most consistent with this?
options: They are linked on the same chromosome
They must be on different chromosomes
They have no alleles
Every meiosis produces only recombinant chromosomes
questions.answer: They are linked on the same chromosome
questions.explanation: Linked genes tend to be inherited together, with crossing over producing fewer recombinants when loci are close.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A human coding sequence is placed in bacteria, but no protein appears because the promoter is unsuitable. What does this illustrate?
options: Promoters are translated into all proteins
DNA bases have completely different chemical identities in bacteria
A shared genetic code does not guarantee compatible expression signals
Bacteria cannot use any human coding sequence
questions.answer: A shared genetic code does not guarantee compatible expression signals
questions.explanation: Transcription also requires host-recognised regulatory sequences, beyond codon compatibility.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A trait is heritable and improves survival but reduces reproduction enough to lower total offspring contribution. What determines its evolutionary success?
options: Body size alone
Its net contribution to reproductive fitness
Survival duration alone
The organism's desire to pass it on
questions.answer: Its net contribution to reproductive fitness
questions.explanation: Selection depends on genetic contribution to future generations, integrating survival and reproduction.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A food chain lengthens while primary production is unchanged. Why does adding a top consumer limit the biomass it can support?
options: Energy is fully recycled at each feeding step
All producers stop photosynthesising
Longer chains create energy
Repeated trophic transfers reduce available energy
questions.answer: Repeated trophic transfers reduce available energy
questions.explanation: Energy transfer is inefficient, leaving progressively less available to additional consumer levels.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Two equal-sized reserves differ: one contains varied habitats and one is uniform. Why might the varied reserve support more species?
options: Every habitat supports identical communities
Variation eliminates resource limits
It offers more kinds of ecological niches
Area alone determines every species count
questions.answer: It offers more kinds of ecological niches
questions.explanation: Habitat heterogeneity can provide different resources and conditions supporting more species.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A DNA insert and vector have compatible sticky ends but are not ligated. What is missing for stable recombinant DNA formation?
options: Covalent sealing of the sugar-phosphate backbone
Conversion of DNA into protein
Destruction of all complementary bases
Removal of the vector's origin of replication
questions.answer: Covalent sealing of the sugar-phosphate backbone
questions.explanation: Base pairing can align fragments, while ligase seals backbone nicks to stabilize the construct.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A tall pea plant crossed with a homozygous recessive dwarf produces both tall and dwarf offspring. What follows under a single-gene dominant model?
options: The tall parent is homozygous dominant
Dwarfism is caused only by the environment
Every offspring must be heterozygous
The tall parent is heterozygous
questions.answer: The tall parent is heterozygous
questions.explanation: Producing recessive offspring means the tall parent can supply the recessive allele.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A replication fork has leading and lagging strands. Why is lagging-strand synthesis discontinuous?
options: Ligase prevents every continuous strand
Polymerase extends only 5-prime to 3-prime on antiparallel templates
DNA polymerase synthesises only RNA
The two templates run in the same direction
questions.answer: Polymerase extends only 5-prime to 3-prime on antiparallel templates
questions.explanation: The fixed synthesis direction on antiparallel templates requires short fragments on one side of the moving fork.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: A receptor fails to activate its first relay, but directly activating a later relay restores the response. What does this result support?
options: Downstream response machinery can function despite the earlier defect
The receptor is unnecessary in every normal cell
The signalling molecule must directly change every gene
All relay steps are permanently inactive
questions.answer: Downstream response machinery can function despite the earlier defect
questions.explanation: Bypassing the early block and recovering a response indicates that at least the tested downstream machinery remains functional.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: One nucleotide is inserted near the start of a coding sequence rather than three together. Why is the first change often more disruptive?
options: It necessarily changes only the final stop codon
It leaves all downstream codon groupings unchanged
It can shift the reading frame for downstream codons
It always adds exactly one harmless amino acid
questions.answer: It can shift the reading frame for downstream codons
questions.explanation: An insertion not divisible by three can change the downstream grouping of bases into codons.

questions.subject: AP Biology
