questions.q: An allele becomes common in a very small population, but no reproductive advantage is measured. Why is selection not the only explanation?
options: Mutation must have made all individuals identical
Random genetic drift can cause large frequency changes
Only beneficial alleles can increase in frequency
Small populations have no sampling variation
questions.answer: Random genetic drift can cause large frequency changes
questions.explanation: Chance differences in reproduction can substantially change frequencies, especially in small populations.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Two species have similar streamlined bodies but distant common ancestry. Why is body shape alone weak evidence of close relatedness?
options: Evolution cannot change body shape
Every structural similarity must be homologous
Distant relatives cannot live in similar environments
Similar selection pressures can produce analogous adaptations
questions.answer: Similar selection pressures can produce analogous adaptations
questions.explanation: Convergence can produce functional similarity independently, so multiple inherited and molecular features strengthen ancestry inference.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Removing species A increases species B only when resource R is scarce. What is the best-supported interpretation?
options: The two species cannot share any resources
Resource abundance is irrelevant to the interaction
Competition may depend on the availability of R
A always preys on B under every condition
questions.answer: Competition may depend on the availability of R
questions.explanation: A conditional removal response is consistent with competition becoming important when a shared resource is limiting.

questions.subject: AP Biology
questions.q: Two DNA samples produce bands at the same position in a standard size-separating gel. What does this establish most directly?
options: The detected fragments have similar lengths
Their complete base sequences must be identical
They came from the same organism
They code for the same protein
questions.answer: The detected fragments have similar lengths
questions.explanation: Migration in this gel primarily reflects fragment length; different sequences can share the same length.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: As x approaches 3, f(x) approaches 7, but f(3)=2. Which value describes the limit?
options: The limit cannot exist
questions.explanation: A limit depends on nearby function values, not the separately assigned value at the point.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A graph has a hole at (4,6), and nearby values approach 6 from both sides. How can the hole be removed?
options: Set the derivative at 4 to zero without defining f(4)
Define f(4)=6
Define f(4)=4
Delete every value near 4
questions.answer: Define f(4)=6
questions.explanation: Continuity is restored by setting the point value equal to the common limit.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: As x approaches 1 from the right, f(x) increases without bound. What does this indicate?
options: A vertical asymptote at x=1
A horizontal asymptote at y=1
A finite maximum at x=1
A limit equal to zero
questions.answer: A vertical asymptote at x=1
questions.explanation: Unbounded behaviour as x approaches a fixed input indicates a vertical asymptote.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: C(t) measures concentration in grams per litre and t is in minutes. What are the units of C'(t)?
options: Minutes per gram per litre
Grams per litre only
Grams per litre per minute
Grams times litres per minute
questions.answer: Grams per litre per minute
questions.explanation: A derivative has units of the output quantity divided by the input quantity.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A secant through (a,f(a)) and (a+h,f(a+h)) approaches a unique tangent as h approaches zero. What does its limiting slope represent?
options: The average value of f on its domain
f'(a)
f(a)
The area under f near a
questions.answer: f'(a)
questions.explanation: The derivative is the limit of average rates of change over shrinking intervals.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: For f(x)=x², how does the tangent slope change when x increases from 1 to 2?
options: It stays the same
It halves
It changes from positive to negative
It doubles
questions.answer: It doubles
questions.explanation: The slope is f'(x)=2x, so doubling this positive x-value doubles the slope.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A quantity is f(3t). Compared with f'(3t), what extra factor is needed when differentiating with respect to t?
options: t
f(3t)
questions.explanation: The chain rule multiplies the outer derivative by the derivative of the inner function 3t.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A differentiable function has a local inverse and nonzero slope 4 at a point. What is the inverse's slope at the corresponding point?
questions.explanation: Corresponding nonzero slopes of differentiable inverse functions are reciprocals.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A particle's position graph has a horizontal tangent at t=5. What is zero at that instant?
options: Its position necessarily
Its acceleration necessarily
Its total distance travelled necessarily
Its velocity
questions.answer: Its velocity
questions.explanation: Velocity is the derivative of position, represented by tangent slope.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A tangent-line approximation is intended to estimate f(x) near x=a. Why is it usually used near a?
options: It requires the function to be constant
It matches the function's value and slope at a
It exactly matches every point of the curve
It ignores the value of f(a)
questions.answer: It matches the function's value and slope at a
questions.explanation: Local linearity uses agreement at the point to approximate nearby behaviour.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A differentiable function has f'(x)>0 throughout an interval. What follows?
options: The function is increasing there
The function's values are all positive
The function is necessarily linear
Its second derivative is necessarily positive
questions.answer: The function is increasing there
questions.explanation: Positive derivative describes increasing values, not the sign or curvature of the function.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: Why must endpoints be checked when finding an absolute maximum on a closed interval?
options: Interior values cannot be compared
A closed interval has no interior points
The greatest value may occur at an endpoint
Every endpoint is a stationary point
questions.answer: The greatest value may occur at an endpoint
questions.explanation: An absolute extremum can occur at an endpoint even when its derivative is not zero.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A continuous graph has a sharp corner at an interior point. Why might that point need checking for an extremum?
options: Only points with positive coordinates can be critical
The function is defined there but its derivative does not exist
The function must be discontinuous there
Every corner is an absolute maximum
questions.answer: The function is defined there but its derivative does not exist
questions.explanation: An interior point where the derivative is undefined can be a critical point.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A(x)=integral from 0 to x of a continuous function f(t) dt. What is A'(x)?
options: A(x)
f(x)
questions.answer: f(x)
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus links the derivative of accumulation to the integrand.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: If the integral of f from a to b equals 9, what is the integral from b to a?
questions.explanation: Reversing the bounds reverses the sign of a definite integral.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: In an integral containing 2x times a function of x², why can u=x² be useful?
options: du=2x dx matches the remaining factor
du=x² dx removes all variables automatically
Every factor of 2x can be ignored
The bounds must always stay unchanged
questions.answer: du=2x dx matches the remaining factor
questions.explanation: Substitution is effective when the derivative of the inner expression is also present.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: For y'=y-2, what do slope-field segments on the line y=2 look like?
options: Vertical
All with slope 2
All with slope -2
Horizontal
questions.answer: Horizontal
questions.explanation: Substituting y=2 into the differential equation gives slope zero.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: How can a proposed y(x) be checked against a differential equation y'=F(x,y)?
options: Compare only the largest values on a graph
Differentiate it and compare with F(x,y(x))
Check only that y(0) is positive
Integrate the equation's title
questions.answer: Differentiate it and compare with F(x,y(x))
questions.explanation: A solution must satisfy the rate equation when both the function and its derivative are substituted.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A tank starts with 50 litres, and the integral of its net inflow rate over an hour is 12 litres. What is its final volume?
options: 62 litres
12 litres
38 litres
600 litres
questions.answer: 62 litres
questions.explanation: Final quantity equals the initial quantity plus accumulated net change.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A solid has cross-sectional area A(x) perpendicular to the x-axis. What does integrating A(x) over its length give?
options: The largest cross-sectional area
The average perimeter
Volume
Surface area necessarily
questions.answer: Volume
questions.explanation: Area times a thin length gives a volume element, and integration accumulates those elements.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: Near zero, -x² ≤ f(x) ≤ x². What can be concluded about the limit of f at zero?
options: It cannot exist because f is bounded
It is zero
It is 1
It depends only on f(0)
questions.answer: It is zero
questions.explanation: Both bounding functions approach zero, forcing the function between them to approach zero.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: The Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a root of a continuous function between opposite-sign endpoint values. Why does it not guarantee exactly one?
options: Continuity forces exactly two roots
A root must occur at the midpoint
The theorem requires the derivative to be positive
The function may cross zero several times
questions.answer: The function may cross zero several times
questions.explanation: The theorem establishes existence without controlling how often the intermediate value occurs.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A rational function has a nonzero denominator at x=a. Why can its limit there be found by direct substitution?
options: A nonzero denominator forces a zero numerator
Substitution always works at vertical asymptotes
It is continuous wherever its denominator is nonzero
Every rational function is continuous everywhere
questions.answer: It is continuous wherever its denominator is nonzero
questions.explanation: Polynomials are continuous, and their quotient is continuous where division is defined.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: The numerator of a positive ratio stays constant while its positive denominator increases. What happens to the ratio?
options: It decreases
It increases
It remains constant
It must become negative
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Increasing the positive denominator with a fixed positive numerator reduces the quotient.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: Cost depends on quantity, and quantity depends on time. What combines cost per extra unit with units added per hour?
options: Addition gives cost change per hour
Division always gives total cost
Their difference gives accumulated cost
Multiplication gives cost change per hour
questions.answer: Multiplication gives cost change per hour
questions.explanation: The chain rule multiplies the linked rates, with the intermediate units cancelling.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: On x²+y²=1, the point (0,1) has dy/dx=-x/y. What is the tangent direction there?
options: Slope -1
Horizontal
Vertical
Slope 1
questions.answer: Horizontal
questions.explanation: At that point the numerator is zero and the denominator is nonzero, giving slope zero.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A particle has negative velocity and positive acceleration. What happens to its speed at that instant?
options: It is decreasing
It is increasing
It equals its acceleration
It must be zero
questions.answer: It is decreasing
questions.explanation: Opposite signs of velocity and acceleration reduce the magnitude of velocity.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A twice-differentiable function has f''>0 throughout a neighbourhood of a. How does its tangent line at a estimate nearby values?
options: It is exact throughout the neighbourhood
Its error depends only on whether f(a) is positive
It underestimates them except at the point of tangency
It overestimates them everywhere
questions.answer: It underestimates them except at the point of tangency
questions.explanation: A concave-up graph lies above its tangent line locally.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: Direct substitution into a quotient gives 0/0. What does this indicate before using L'Hospital's Rule?
options: The quotient must have no limit
An indeterminate form for which the rule's other conditions must be checked
The limit is automatically zero
The limit is automatically one
questions.answer: An indeterminate form for which the rule's other conditions must be checked
questions.explanation: The form does not determine the limit and does not replace the rule's hypotheses.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A derivative changes from positive to negative through a critical point. What does this indicate for the function?
options: A local minimum
An unavoidable discontinuity
A stationary point with no extremum
A local maximum
questions.answer: A local maximum
questions.explanation: The function increases into the point and decreases after it.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: At a stationary point, f''=0. What follows from the second derivative test alone?
options: There must be a local maximum
There must be an inflection point
The test is inconclusive
There must be a local minimum
questions.answer: The test is inconclusive
questions.explanation: A zero second derivative does not classify the stationary point without further analysis.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A continuous function is defined on the closed interval [a,b]. What is guaranteed?
options: Both an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum are attained
Both extrema occur in the interior
The extrema have derivative zero
The maximum is positive
questions.answer: Both an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum are attained
questions.explanation: Continuity on a closed bounded interval guarantees attainment of extrema, including possibly at endpoints.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: For an increasing continuous function, left and right sums use the same partition. How is the integral positioned?
options: Above both sums
Below both sums
Equal to their product
Between the left and right sums
questions.answer: Between the left and right sums
questions.explanation: On each subinterval, the function lies between its endpoint heights.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.topic: Unit 6: accumulation with a changing upper bound
questions.q: For continuous f, G(x)=integral from 0 to x² of f(t) dt. What is G'(x)?
options: The integral from 0 to 2x of f(t) dt
2x f(x²)
f(x²)
2x f(x)
questions.answer: 2x f(x²)
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem gives f at the upper bound, and the chain rule supplies 2x.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: Why can an integral from a to c be split at an intermediate point b?
options: Accumulations over adjacent intervals add
Each subinterval must have the same length
The integrand must be positive
The function must vanish at b
questions.answer: Accumulations over adjacent intervals add
questions.explanation: Additivity of definite integrals combines signed accumulation across adjacent intervals.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: Water enters a tank at I(t) and leaves at O(t). Which rate must be integrated to find the volume change?
options: I(t)O(t)
I(t)/O(t)
I(t)-O(t)
I(t)+O(t)
questions.answer: I(t)-O(t)
questions.explanation: Net change subtracts the outgoing rate from the incoming rate.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A proposed curve passes through a slope-field point but has a different tangent slope there. Can it be a solution through that point?
options: Only if the point's coordinates are positive
No; it fails the differential equation's local rate condition
Yes; passing through the point is sufficient
Yes; any smooth curve fits every slope field
questions.answer: No; it fails the differential equation's local rate condition
questions.explanation: A solution must match the prescribed slope as well as the point.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A positive solution of y'=ky has constant k. What is constant over equal time intervals?
options: The absolute increase in y
The tangent slope
The second derivative's value
The multiplicative growth factor
questions.answer: The multiplicative growth factor
questions.explanation: Exponential change gives equal proportional changes over equal time steps.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A continuous function has average value M on [a,b]. Why must it equal M somewhere on that interval?
options: Its derivative must equal M everywhere
Its integral must be zero
Its average lies between its minimum and maximum, and continuity fills intermediate values
Its midpoint value always equals M
questions.answer: Its average lies between its minimum and maximum, and continuity fills intermediate values
questions.explanation: Continuity and the bounds on the average guarantee at least one point attaining the average value.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A region rotated about an axis has outer radius R and inner radius r. Why is the cross-sectional area π(R²-r²)?
options: The inner disk's area is removed from the outer disk's area
The radii are first subtracted and then squared
The two disk areas are added
Only the larger circumference matters
questions.answer: The inner disk's area is removed from the outer disk's area
questions.explanation: A washer is an outer disk with its inner disk removed.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A finite table shows f(x) close to 4 near x=2. Why does the table alone not prove the limit is 4?
options: Finite tables cannot provide any useful evidence
A limit must equal a sampled value exactly
Only a negative input can disprove a limit
Unexamined inputs arbitrarily near 2 may behave differently
questions.answer: Unexamined inputs arbitrarily near 2 may behave differently
questions.explanation: A limit concerns all sufficiently nearby inputs, beyond a finite set of samples.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: g(x) approaches L as x approaches a. What condition on f guarantees f(g(x)) approaches f(L)?
options: g(a) equals zero
f is continuous at L
f is continuous only at a
f(L) is positive
questions.answer: f is continuous at L
questions.explanation: Continuity of the outer function at the approached input allows the limit to pass through the composition.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: For f(x)=absolute value of x on [-1,1], the secant slope is zero but no derivative inside equals zero. Why is there no contradiction?
options: The function is not differentiable at the interior point zero
The interval is not closed
The endpoint values differ
The function is not continuous at zero
questions.answer: The function is not differentiable at the interior point zero
questions.explanation: The Mean Value Theorem requires differentiability throughout the open interval, which fails at the corner.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: For h(x)=f(g(x)), suppose g is differentiable at a and f'(g(a))=0. What follows?
options: f(g(a))=0 necessarily
h has a local maximum at a necessarily
g'(a)=0 necessarily
questions.explanation: The chain-rule product is zero, but a stationary derivative alone does not classify an extremum.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: The function f(x)=x³ is invertible, but f'(0)=0. What happens to the inverse's ordinary finite derivative at zero?
options: The inverse function itself does not exist
It does not exist as a finite number
It equals zero
It equals one
questions.answer: It does not exist as a finite number
questions.explanation: The cube-root inverse has an unbounded difference quotient at zero; invertibility alone does not ensure a finite inverse derivative.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.topic: Unit 4: motion at a turning point
questions.q: At t=a, a particle has velocity zero and positive acceleration that remains positive nearby. What is the local behaviour of position?
options: A local maximum
A constant position throughout the neighbourhood
A discontinuous jump
A local minimum
questions.answer: A local minimum
questions.explanation: Velocity increases through zero from negative to positive, so position decreases then increases.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A circle's area grows at a constant positive rate. As its positive radius becomes larger, what happens to the radius's growth rate?
options: It increases proportionally to radius
It becomes negative
It decreases
It stays constant
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: From dA/dt=2πr dr/dt, the same area rate requires a smaller radius rate at a larger radius.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A continuous function on [a,b] is differentiable inside, with f'(x)>2 throughout. What follows?
options: f(b)>2 regardless of f(a)
The average rate is less than 2
questions.explanation: The Mean Value Theorem makes the average rate equal to an interior derivative, which exceeds 2.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.topic: Unit 5: zero derivative and a missing point
questions.q: A function has derivative zero for x<0 and for x>0, but jumps at zero. Why need it not be constant on the whole real line?
options: A zero derivative always permits arbitrary variation within an interval
The function is differentiable at the jump
The jump's value determines every other value
The zero-derivative conclusion applies separately to the two intervals
questions.answer: The zero-derivative conclusion applies separately to the two intervals
questions.explanation: The theorem requiring zero derivative throughout an interval cannot be applied across the nondifferentiable jump.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A function's only interior local maximum has value 5, but an endpoint has value 8. What can be concluded?
options: The function violates continuity necessarily
The interior local maximum is not the absolute maximum
The endpoint cannot be considered
The absolute maximum must have value 5
questions.answer: The interior local maximum is not the absolute maximum
questions.explanation: A local comparison does not override a larger value elsewhere in the domain.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: An algebraic stationary point lies outside the physically permitted interval of an optimisation problem. What should be done?
options: Exclude it as infeasible and compare valid candidates
Accept it because its derivative is zero
Expand the physical domain without justification
Ignore all endpoints
questions.answer: Exclude it as infeasible and compare valid candidates
questions.explanation: Optimisation is over the stated feasible domain, not every algebraic solution.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: A step function equals 1 to the left of a and 3 to the right. Its accumulated integral is continuous at a. Why is that accumulation not differentiable there?
options: Its integral is undefined on every interval
Continuity guarantees differentiability, so it is differentiable
Its one-sided slopes are 1 and 3
Its values must jump by 2
questions.answer: Its one-sided slopes are 1 and 3
questions.explanation: Accumulation remains continuous, but unequal one-sided rate values produce a corner.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: For continuous f, H(x)=integral from x to 2x of f(t) dt. What is H'(x)?
options: The integral from 1 to 2 of f(t) dt
f(2x)-f(x)
2f(x)
questions.explanation: The upper-bound contribution includes its derivative 2, and the lower-bound contribution is subtracted.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.topic: Unit 6: zero integral of a nonnegative function
questions.q: A continuous nonnegative function has integral zero on [a,b], with a<b. What follows?
options: It can be positive on an open subinterval
It must be negative somewhere
Its endpoint values alone must sum to zero
It is zero throughout the interval
questions.answer: It is zero throughout the interval
questions.explanation: A positive value would, by continuity, create a positive contribution over a nearby interval.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: Two continuous functions have average values A and B on the same interval. What is the average of 2f-g?
options: A²-B
The average cannot be determined
2A-B
questions.answer: 2A-B
questions.explanation: Linearity of integration carries through division by the common interval length.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.topic: Unit 6: improper use of the Fundamental Theorem
questions.q: A student evaluates the integral of 1/x from -1 to 1 by substituting endpoints into ln absolute value of x. What invalidates this direct calculation?
options: The integrand is undefined at an interior point, so the ordinary theorem does not apply across the whole interval
The derivative of ln absolute value of x is never 1/x
Negative bounds are forbidden for every integral
The interval has zero length
questions.answer: The integrand is undefined at an interior point, so the ordinary theorem does not apply across the whole interval
questions.explanation: The singularity at zero breaks the hypotheses for applying the usual endpoint evaluation over the full interval.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.topic: Unit 7: initial conditions and excluded solutions
questions.q: A student divides y'=y²-1 by y²-1 and later says no constant solutions exist. Which check reveals the error?
options: Check only the separated expression
Assume division never removes solutions
Replace the initial condition by any convenient value
Substitute y=-1 and y=1 into the original equation
questions.answer: Substitute y=-1 and y=1 into the original equation
questions.explanation: Both excluded factors correspond to equilibrium solutions of the original differential equation.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.topic: Unit 7: exponential change with negative initial value
questions.q: A solution satisfies y'=ky, k>0, with y(0)<0. What happens to y as time increases?
options: It remains constant
It becomes more negative
It increases toward zero
It becomes positive immediately
questions.answer: It becomes more negative
questions.explanation: The solution is the negative initial value multiplied by an increasing positive exponential factor.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: For P'=k(100-P), k>0, what does the rate depend on?
options: The gap between P and the equilibrium value 100
P alone in direct positive proportion
A constant rate independent of P
The square of elapsed time
questions.answer: The gap between P and the equilibrium value 100
questions.explanation: The model moves P toward 100 at a rate proportional to its remaining difference from that value.

questions.subject: AP Calculus AB
questions.q: Two continuous curves exchange which one is above the other. Why must an area calculation account for the crossing?
options: Crossing makes every area infinite
Only the endpoint order matters
The vertical strip height is the absolute difference, not one fixed signed order
Area is found by integrating the product
questions.answer: The vertical strip height is the absolute difference, not one fixed signed order
questions.explanation: The upper-minus-lower expression changes when the curves cross, preventing cancellation of geometric area.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: As x approaches 3, f(x) approaches 7, but f(3)=2. Which value describes the limit?
options: The limit cannot exist
questions.explanation: A limit depends on nearby function values, not the separately assigned value at the point.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A continuous function has f(0)=-1 and f(2)=3. What must occur between 0 and 2?
options: Its derivative is always positive
Its graph is a straight line
The function takes the value zero at least once
It takes zero exactly once
questions.answer: The function takes the value zero at least once
questions.explanation: Continuity forces the function to pass through every intermediate output value.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: C(t) measures concentration in grams per litre and t is in minutes. What are the units of C'(t)?
options: Grams per litre only
Grams per litre per minute
Grams times litres per minute
Minutes per gram per litre
questions.answer: Grams per litre per minute
questions.explanation: A derivative has units of the output quantity divided by the input quantity.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A quantity is f(3t). Compared with f'(3t), what extra factor is needed when differentiating with respect to t?
options: t
f(3t)
questions.explanation: The chain rule multiplies the outer derivative by the derivative of the inner function 3t.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: On x²+y²=25, y depends on x. Why does differentiating y² produce 2y times dy/dx?
options: Every derivative of y equals 1
The equation must first be divided by 25
The chain rule accounts for y changing with x
y is held constant while x changes
questions.answer: The chain rule accounts for y changing with x
questions.explanation: Implicit differentiation treats y as a function of x, so its rate of change is included.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A tangent-line approximation is intended to estimate f(x) near x=a. Why is it usually used near a?
options: It matches the function's value and slope at a
It exactly matches every point of the curve
It ignores the value of f(a)
It requires the function to be constant
questions.answer: It matches the function's value and slope at a
questions.explanation: Local linearity uses agreement at the point to approximate nearby behaviour.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A differentiable function has f'(x)>0 throughout an interval. What follows?
options: The function's values are all positive
The function is necessarily linear
Its second derivative is necessarily positive
The function is increasing there
questions.answer: The function is increasing there
questions.explanation: Positive derivative describes increasing values, not the sign or curvature of the function.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: For a positive increasing function on an interval, how does a left-endpoint rectangle sum compare with the integral?
options: Its sign must be negative
It underestimates the integral
It overestimates the integral
It is always exact
questions.answer: It underestimates the integral
questions.explanation: On each subinterval, the left endpoint gives the smallest height for an increasing function.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A(x)=integral from 0 to x of a continuous function f(t) dt. What is A'(x)?
options: f(x)
A(x)
questions.answer: f(x)
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus links the derivative of accumulation to the integrand.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A tank starts with 50 litres, and the integral of its net inflow rate over an hour is 12 litres. What is its final volume?
options: 38 litres
600 litres
62 litres
12 litres
questions.answer: 62 litres
questions.explanation: Final quantity equals the initial quantity plus accumulated net change.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.topic: Unit 10: terms of a convergent series
questions.q: An infinite series has terms that approach 2 rather than zero. What follows?
options: Its sum equals its first term
The series diverges
The series converges to 2
The series converges to zero
questions.answer: The series diverges
questions.explanation: Terms of a convergent series must approach zero, so a nonzero term limit proves divergence.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: The harmonic series has terms 1/n approaching zero but diverges. What does it demonstrate?
options: Terms approaching zero guarantee convergence
Every decreasing series converges
A divergent series must have terms increasing
Terms approaching zero do not by themselves guarantee convergence
questions.answer: Terms approaching zero do not by themselves guarantee convergence
questions.explanation: A zero term limit is necessary, not sufficient, for convergence of a series.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: Why does the series with terms 1/n² converge while the harmonic series does not?
options: Squaring n makes only finitely many terms nonzero
The first term determines convergence
Its positive terms decrease sufficiently faster for a finite sum
Every smaller positive term sequence must converge
questions.answer: Its positive terms decrease sufficiently faster for a finite sum
questions.explanation: The p-series criterion gives convergence for exponent p>1, including p=2.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A Taylor polynomial centred at a matches f and its first several derivatives at a. What is its intended role?
options: Approximate f near a
Match f exactly at every input
Replace the domain of f
Find only the zeros of f
questions.answer: Approximate f near a
questions.explanation: Matching local derivative information creates a polynomial approximation near the centre.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.topic: Unit 10: centre of a power series
questions.q: In a power series in powers of x-a, what happens when x=a?
options: Every term becomes 1
The series necessarily diverges
Every coefficient must be zero
Every positive-power term vanishes
questions.answer: Every positive-power term vanishes
questions.explanation: At the centre, x-a=0, leaving only the constant term.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: For x(t) and y(t), x'(t) is nonzero. Why is dy/dx equal to y'(t)/x'(t)?
options: It ignores the change in x
It compares their changes with the common parameter cancelled
It is the product of the coordinate velocities
It equals y(t)/x(t) in every case
questions.answer: It compares their changes with the common parameter cancelled
questions.explanation: The chain-rule relationship dy/dt=(dy/dx)(dx/dt) gives the quotient.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A particle has velocity vector (3,4). What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Speed is the magnitude of velocity, found here from a 3-4-5 right triangle.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: For the integral of x e^x, why is choosing u=x useful in integration by parts?
options: The exponential factor has no antiderivative
A product is integrated by multiplying antiderivatives
Differentiating x simplifies that factor
Differentiating x reproduces x²
questions.answer: Differentiating x simplifies that factor
questions.explanation: The choice reduces the polynomial factor while e^x remains easy to integrate.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: An integral extends to infinity. What replaces direct substitution of infinity into an antiderivative?
options: Differentiating the lower bound
A limit as the finite upper bound increases without bound
Setting infinity equal to a large fixed integer
Ignoring the upper bound
questions.answer: A limit as the finite upper bound increases without bound
questions.explanation: An improper integral is defined through a limit of finite-interval integrals.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: In P'=kP(1-P/K), with k,K>0, what happens when 0<P<K?
options: P decreases
P is constant at every such value
P immediately equals K
P increases
questions.answer: P increases
questions.explanation: Both factors P and 1-P/K are positive, so the model's rate is positive.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: Near zero, -x² ≤ f(x) ≤ x². What can be concluded about the limit of f at zero?
options: It depends only on f(0)
It cannot exist because f is bounded
It is zero
It is 1
questions.answer: It is zero
questions.explanation: Both bounding functions approach zero, forcing the function between them to approach zero.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: Both f and g vary with x. Why is the derivative of fg generally not just f'g'?
options: Each factor's change contributes while the other factor is retained
Products cannot be differentiated
Only the larger factor can change
A product's derivative is always the sum f'+g'
questions.answer: Each factor's change contributes while the other factor is retained
questions.explanation: The product rule is f'g+fg', accounting for both sources of change.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: Cost depends on quantity, and quantity depends on time. What combines cost per extra unit with units added per hour?
options: Addition gives cost change per hour
Division always gives total cost
Their difference gives accumulated cost
Multiplication gives cost change per hour
questions.answer: Multiplication gives cost change per hour
questions.explanation: The chain rule multiplies the linked rates, with the intermediate units cancelling.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A particle has negative velocity and positive acceleration. What happens to its speed at that instant?
options: It must be zero
It is decreasing
It is increasing
It equals its acceleration
questions.answer: It is decreasing
questions.explanation: Opposite signs of velocity and acceleration reduce the magnitude of velocity.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A twice-differentiable function has f''>0 throughout a neighbourhood of a. How does its tangent line at a estimate nearby values?
options: It underestimates them except at the point of tangency
It overestimates them everywhere
It is exact throughout the neighbourhood
Its error depends only on whether f(a) is positive
questions.answer: It underestimates them except at the point of tangency
questions.explanation: A concave-up graph lies above its tangent line locally.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A derivative changes from positive to negative through a critical point. What does this indicate for the function?
options: An unavoidable discontinuity
A stationary point with no extremum
A local maximum
A local minimum
questions.answer: A local maximum
questions.explanation: The function increases into the point and decreases after it.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A continuous function is defined on the closed interval [a,b]. What is guaranteed?
options: The maximum is positive
Both an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum are attained
Both extrema occur in the interior
The extrema have derivative zero
questions.answer: Both an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum are attained
questions.explanation: Continuity on a closed bounded interval guarantees attainment of extrema, including possibly at endpoints.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A definite integral uses u=x² over x from 1 to 3. If everything is rewritten in u, what bounds are needed?
options: 1 to 3
0 to 2
2 to 6
1 to 9
questions.answer: 1 to 9
questions.explanation: Bounds must be transformed through the same substitution as the integrand.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A proposed curve passes through a slope-field point but has a different tangent slope there. Can it be a solution through that point?
options: Yes; any smooth curve fits every slope field
Only if the point's coordinates are positive
No; it fails the differential equation's local rate condition
Yes; passing through the point is sufficient
questions.answer: No; it fails the differential equation's local rate condition
questions.explanation: A solution must match the prescribed slope as well as the point.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A region rotated about an axis has outer radius R and inner radius r. Why is the cross-sectional area π(R²-r²)?
options: The inner disk's area is removed from the outer disk's area
The radii are first subtracted and then squared
The two disk areas are added
Only the larger circumference matters
questions.answer: The inner disk's area is removed from the outer disk's area
questions.explanation: A washer is an outer disk with its inner disk removed.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: The alternating harmonic series converges, while the series of its absolute term values diverges. How is its convergence classified?
options: Absolute
Geometric
No convergence of any kind
Conditional
questions.answer: Conditional
questions.explanation: Conditional convergence means convergence of the signed series without convergence of its absolute-value series.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: The Ratio Test gives a limit of 1. What should be concluded?
options: The sum must equal 1
Another method is needed
The series must converge
The series must diverge
questions.answer: Another method is needed
questions.explanation: A ratio limit of 1 can occur for both convergent and divergent series.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.topic: Unit 10: symmetry of a Maclaurin series
questions.q: A function analytic near zero is even. Which feature should its Maclaurin series have?
options: Zero coefficients for odd powers
Zero coefficients for all even powers
Only a nonzero linear term
A necessarily zero constant term
questions.answer: Zero coefficients for odd powers
questions.explanation: Even symmetry is preserved by even powers; the odd derivatives at zero vanish.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: For all sufficiently large n, 0≤a_n≤1/n². What follows for the sum of a_n?
options: Its sum equals the sum of 1/n²
Its terms must eventually be zero
It converges
It diverges like the harmonic series
questions.answer: It converges
questions.explanation: A nonnegative series bounded above by a convergent positive series converges.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: Why check that an interpolating function is positive, continuous and decreasing before applying the Integral Test?
options: They determine the series sum exactly
These conditions support comparison between the series and its associated area
They guarantee that every improper integral converges
They force the function to be a polynomial
questions.answer: These conditions support comparison between the series and its associated area
questions.explanation: The test relates convergence through area comparisons under its stated hypotheses.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: After finding dy/dx as a function of t, how is d²y/dx² obtained when x'(t)≠0?
options: Differentiate dy/dx with respect to t only
Divide y''(t) by x''(t) in every case
Square dy/dx
Differentiate dy/dx with respect to t, then divide by x'(t)
questions.answer: Differentiate dy/dx with respect to t, then divide by x'(t)
questions.explanation: A second derivative is a rate with respect to x, so another chain-rule conversion is needed.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A particle moves at constant speed around a circle. How can its acceleration be nonzero?
options: Constant speed requires a straight path
The position vector must stay constant
Velocity changes direction even though its magnitude is constant
Acceleration measures only changes in speed
questions.answer: Velocity changes direction even though its magnitude is constant
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector, so changing direction produces acceleration without a change in speed.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A proper rational function has denominator (x-a)(x-b), with a≠b. What decomposition form is appropriate?
options: A/(x-a)+B/(x-b)
A/(x-a)² only
A(x-a)+B(x-b) only
A/(x-a)(x-b) with no separation
questions.answer: A/(x-a)+B/(x-b)
questions.explanation: Distinct linear factors permit separate constant-numerator fractions for integration.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: An integrand is unbounded at a point inside the interval. What is required for the improper integral to converge?
options: Only the endpoint antiderivative values must cancel
The singular point must be assigned zero
Only the longer side needs checking
Both one-sided improper integrals must converge separately
questions.answer: Both one-sided improper integrals must converge separately
questions.explanation: Convergence across an interior singularity requires convergence on both sides independently.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: For P'=kP(1-P/K), with k,K>0, at which population is the absolute growth rate greatest within 0≤P≤K?
options: P=2K
P=K/2
P=K
questions.answer: P=K/2
questions.explanation: The rate is a downward-opening quadratic in P with its vertex halfway between its zeros 0 and K.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A finite table shows f(x) close to 4 near x=2. Why does the table alone not prove the limit is 4?
options: Unexamined inputs arbitrarily near 2 may behave differently
Finite tables cannot provide any useful evidence
A limit must equal a sampled value exactly
Only a negative input can disprove a limit
questions.answer: Unexamined inputs arbitrarily near 2 may behave differently
questions.explanation: A limit concerns all sufficiently nearby inputs, beyond a finite set of samples.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: For f(x)=absolute value of x on [-1,1], the secant slope is zero but no derivative inside equals zero. Why is there no contradiction?
options: The endpoint values differ
The function is not continuous at zero
The function is not differentiable at the interior point zero
The interval is not closed
questions.answer: The function is not differentiable at the interior point zero
questions.explanation: The Mean Value Theorem requires differentiability throughout the open interval, which fails at the corner.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: Differentiable functions satisfy f(a)=g(a)=0. What must be true of the derivative of their product at a?
options: It equals f'(a)+g'(a)
It equals zero
It equals f'(a)g'(a)
It is undefined
questions.answer: It equals zero
questions.explanation: Both terms f'(a)g(a) and f(a)g'(a) vanish, regardless of the individual slopes.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: The function f(x)=x³ is invertible, but f'(0)=0. What happens to the inverse's ordinary finite derivative at zero?
options: It equals zero
It equals one
The inverse function itself does not exist
It does not exist as a finite number
questions.answer: It does not exist as a finite number
questions.explanation: The cube-root inverse has an unbounded difference quotient at zero; invertibility alone does not ensure a finite inverse derivative.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.topic: Unit 4: motion at a turning point
questions.q: At t=a, a particle has velocity zero and positive acceleration that remains positive nearby. What is the local behaviour of position?
options: A constant position throughout the neighbourhood
A discontinuous jump
A local minimum
A local maximum
questions.answer: A local minimum
questions.explanation: Velocity increases through zero from negative to positive, so position decreases then increases.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: For f(x)=x⁴, f''(0)=0. Why is zero not an inflection point?
options: Concavity does not change across zero
The first derivative is nonzero there
The function is discontinuous there
The function has no local extremum there
questions.answer: Concavity does not change across zero
questions.explanation: The second derivative is nonnegative on both sides, so the graph stays concave up.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: An algebraic stationary point lies outside the physically permitted interval of an optimisation problem. What should be done?
options: Accept it because its derivative is zero
Expand the physical domain without justification
Ignore all endpoints
Exclude it as infeasible and compare valid candidates
questions.answer: Exclude it as infeasible and compare valid candidates
questions.explanation: Optimisation is over the stated feasible domain, not every algebraic solution.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.topic: Unit 6: zero integral of a nonnegative function
questions.q: A continuous nonnegative function has integral zero on [a,b], with a<b. What follows?
options: Its endpoint values alone must sum to zero
It is zero throughout the interval
It can be positive on an open subinterval
It must be negative somewhere
questions.answer: It is zero throughout the interval
questions.explanation: A positive value would, by continuity, create a positive contribution over a nearby interval.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: For continuous f and differentiable g with continuous derivative, g(a)=g(b). What is the integral of f(g(x))g'(x) from a to b?
options: Zero
The length b-a
f(g(a))
It is undefined unless g is increasing
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: An antiderivative F(g(x)) has identical endpoint values even if g changes direction inside.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: Two continuous curves exchange which one is above the other. Why must an area calculation account for the crossing?
options: Crossing makes every area infinite
Only the endpoint order matters
The vertical strip height is the absolute difference, not one fixed signed order
Area is found by integrating the product
questions.answer: The vertical strip height is the absolute difference, not one fixed signed order
questions.explanation: The upper-minus-lower expression changes when the curves cross, preventing cancellation of geometric area.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: Positive sequences satisfy a_n/b_n approaching a finite positive constant, and the sum of b_n diverges. What follows?
options: The sum of a_n converges only if the constant is below 1
The sum of a_n also diverges
The sum of a_n must converge
The two sums are equal term by term
questions.answer: The sum of a_n also diverges
questions.explanation: A finite nonzero ratio means the terms have comparable tail size, so the series share convergence behaviour.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A series alternates signs, but its term magnitudes approach a positive number. Why is the Alternating Series Test insufficient to show convergence?
options: Alternation alone guarantees convergence
A positive magnitude limit makes absolute convergence likely
The first two signs determine the sum
The required zero term limit fails, and the series diverges
questions.answer: The required zero term limit fails, and the series diverges
questions.explanation: The terms do not approach zero, violating a necessary condition for any convergent series.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A Taylor error estimate uses a bound on the next derivative only at the centre. Why may that be inadequate?
options: Only the function value at the centre matters
A polynomial approximation never has an error bound
The derivative must be bounded over the interval between the centre and evaluation point
The derivative's sign must always be negative
questions.answer: The derivative must be bounded over the interval between the centre and evaluation point
questions.explanation: The Lagrange remainder involves a derivative value at an intermediate point, requiring an interval-wide bound.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A power series has finite positive radius R. What happens to the radius after termwise differentiation?
options: It remains R, though endpoint convergence may change
It always halves
It becomes infinite
It becomes zero
questions.answer: It remains R, though endpoint convergence may change
questions.explanation: Differentiation preserves the radius of convergence but may alter boundary behaviour.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: The geometric series in x diverges at x=1. Its termwise integral from 0 to x has terms x^(n+1)/(n+1). What happens at x=-1?
options: It diverges because the original series diverges there
It converges absolutely
It terminates after one term
It converges conditionally
questions.answer: It converges conditionally
questions.explanation: At x=-1 the integrated series is an alternating harmonic series; termwise integration can change endpoint convergence.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: At a parameter value, both x' and y' are zero. What follows about the tangent from those two values alone?
options: The curve must have no tangent
Further analysis is needed
The tangent must be vertical
The tangent must be horizontal
questions.answer: Further analysis is needed
questions.explanation: The quotient y'/x' is indeterminate, and nearby behaviour can lead to different tangent outcomes.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: A smooth path is traversed once more quickly under a different parameter schedule. What happens to its geometric arc length?
options: It stays the same
It increases with speed
It decreases with elapsed time
It equals the final speed
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: Arc length accumulates speed over the traversal; a different schedule does not change the path's length.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: An integral contains a product of a polynomial and a logarithm with no matching inner derivative. Why may integration by parts help more than direct substitution?
options: Logarithms have no derivatives
Integration by parts removes the need to check the resulting integral
Differentiating the logarithm can simplify one factor while the polynomial is integrable
Every product requires only substitution
questions.answer: Differentiating the logarithm can simplify one factor while the polynomial is integrable
questions.explanation: The method transfers differentiation to one factor and integration to the other, often simplifying the product.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: Symmetric cut-offs around an interior singularity give a finite limiting cancellation, but the two one-sided integrals diverge. What is true of the usual improper integral?
options: It converges whenever the interval is symmetric
It diverges despite the symmetric cancellation
It converges to the cancellation value
It becomes a proper integral
questions.answer: It diverges despite the symmetric cancellation
questions.explanation: A symmetric principal-value cancellation is not the definition of ordinary improper-integral convergence.

questions.subject: AP Calculus BC
questions.q: For P'=kP(1-P/K), with k,K>0 and initial P>K, what does the model predict?
options: P increases without bound
P jumps instantly to K
P passes through K and continues toward zero
P decreases toward K
questions.answer: P decreases toward K
questions.explanation: The rate is negative above K, and the equilibrium solution at K prevents crossing for this unique solution family.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen and oxygen react in a sealed vessel. Why is total mass unchanged despite new water forming?
options: Gases lose mass when they react
The vessel creates replacement atoms
Atoms are rearranged rather than created or destroyed
Water has no mass
questions.answer: Atoms are rearranged rather than created or destroyed
questions.explanation: Chemical reactions conserve atoms, so a closed system conserves mass.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Two atoms have the same proton number but different neutron numbers. Why do they have similar chemical behaviour?
options: They have the same electronic arrangement when neutral
Their nuclear masses are identical
Neutrons determine all bonding
They must have different element names
questions.answer: They have the same electronic arrangement when neutral
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number and normally similar electron configurations.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: An atom loses its outermost electron. What happens to its net charge?
options: It becomes more negative
It remains neutral
Its proton number decreases
It becomes more positive
questions.answer: It becomes more positive
questions.explanation: Removing negative charge makes the remaining particle more positive.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, but the melt does. Why?
options: Only molten salt contains atoms
Melting allows ions to move
Melting changes ions into free protons
The solid contains no charged particles
questions.answer: Melting allows ions to move
questions.explanation: The solid's ions are fixed in a lattice; mobile ions carry charge in the liquid.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Why can a covalent molecule contain shared electrons without having a net charge?
options: The total proton and electron charges can balance
Sharing removes the electrons' charge
Covalent bonds contain only neutrons
The molecule has no nucleus
questions.answer: The total proton and electron charges can balance
questions.explanation: Bonding rearranges electrons, while a neutral molecule still has balanced positive and negative charge.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol mixes readily with water. Which interaction helps explain this?
options: Formation of an ionic lattice
Breaking every carbon-carbon bond
Hydrogen bonding between their molecules
Metallic bonding between all atoms
questions.answer: Hydrogen bonding between their molecules
questions.explanation: Ethanol's hydroxyl group can form hydrogen bonds with water.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A sealed gas sample is compressed slowly at constant temperature. Why does its pressure rise?
options: Its amount of gas doubles
Molecules strike the walls more frequently per unit area
Its molecules become heavier
Its average kinetic energy must rise
questions.answer: Molecules strike the walls more frequently per unit area
questions.explanation: Reduced volume increases wall-collision frequency while mean kinetic energy remains temperature-dependent.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Why does breaking a covalent bond require energy?
options: The atoms must always become new elements
Bond electrons have no energy
Breaking bonds always releases heat
Attractive interactions must be overcome
questions.answer: Attractive interactions must be overcome
questions.explanation: Energy is required to separate atoms held together by an attractive bond.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Reactants and products remain at constant concentrations in a closed reacting system. What can still be happening?
options: Only the reverse reaction
No molecular collisions
Forward and reverse reactions at equal rates
Only the forward reaction
questions.answer: Forward and reverse reactions at equal rates
questions.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium has continuing reactions whose equal rates leave concentrations unchanged.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: An acid is diluted with pure water. What usually happens to hydrogen-ion concentration?
options: It decreases
It increases
It stays fixed at every dilution
It becomes negative
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Dilution spreads the acid over more solvent, reducing hydrogen-ion concentration in ordinary acidic solutions.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrochloric acid is mixed with just enough sodium hydroxide to neutralise it. What happens to H+ and OH-?
options: They form sodium metal
They both become electrons
They remain unchanged in equal large concentrations
They form water
questions.answer: They form water
questions.explanation: The net ionic neutralisation reaction combines hydrogen and hydroxide ions into water.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A galvanic cell powers a lamp. What overall energy conversion occurs?
options: Thermal energy to mass
Chemical energy to electrical energy
Electrical energy to nuclear energy
Light energy to chemical energy only
questions.answer: Chemical energy to electrical energy
questions.explanation: A spontaneous redox reaction drives electron flow through the external circuit.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: An electrolytic cell deposits metal at its cathode. What happens to the metal ions there?
options: They gain electrons
They lose protons
They gain oxygen in every case
They become more positively charged
questions.answer: They gain electrons
questions.explanation: Cathodic reduction supplies electrons to metal cations to form neutral metal.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A solid reactant is powdered before reacting with a solution. Why can reaction become faster?
options: The reaction enthalpy must change
The powder is necessarily a catalyst
More surface is available for collisions
The solid's atoms become smaller
questions.answer: More surface is available for collisions
questions.explanation: Increasing surface area exposes more reacting particles to the solution.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A catalyst speeds up a reaction. How?
options: It permanently increases the equilibrium constant
It provides a pathway with lower activation energy
It makes the products have no energy
It changes the element identities
questions.answer: It provides a pathway with lower activation energy
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation barrier without altering the reaction's overall thermodynamic change.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Two dilute solutions of the same coloured solute are measured at the same wavelength in identical cells. Why does the more concentrated solution usually absorb more light?
options: Its photons have a different speed in vacuum
Each solute particle must become a new element
The cell becomes longer automatically
More absorbing particles lie along the light path
questions.answer: More absorbing particles lie along the light path
questions.explanation: Within the Beer-Lambert range, absorbance increases with concentration at fixed path length and wavelength.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Sodium and nitrate ions remain unchanged when two solutions form an insoluble silver salt. Why can they be omitted from the net ionic equation?
options: They have left the beaker permanently
Their atoms have been destroyed
They are spectator ions in that reaction
They no longer have electric charge
questions.answer: They are spectator ions in that reaction
questions.explanation: A net ionic equation retains species involved in the net chemical change and omits unchanged spectators.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A nonreacting gas is added to a rigid container at fixed temperature. What happens to the original gas's partial pressure in the ideal model?
options: It stays unchanged
It rises solely because another gas is present
It falls to zero
It becomes equal to the added gas's pressure automatically
questions.answer: It stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The original gas keeps the same amount, temperature and volume, so its partial pressure is unchanged.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Two otherwise comparable ionic solids have ions of the same charges, but one has smaller ion separations. Which attraction is stronger?
options: The attraction in the solid with larger separations
Both attractions must vanish
Separation cannot affect electrostatic attraction
The attraction in the solid with smaller separations
questions.answer: The attraction in the solid with smaller separations
questions.explanation: Coulombic attraction increases as opposite charges approach one another.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Different-sized atoms are mixed into a metal lattice. Why can the alloy be harder to deform than the pure metal?
options: The alloy necessarily contains no electrons
The added atoms can hinder layers from sliding easily
All metallic bonding must disappear
Every atom becomes a negative ion
questions.answer: The added atoms can hinder layers from sliding easily
questions.explanation: Distortions and obstacles to dislocation motion can make plastic deformation more difficult.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Equal numbers of nitrogen and hydrogen molecules react to make ammonia. Which is left over if reaction goes to the stoichiometric limit?
options: Nitrogen
Hydrogen
Both are fully consumed
Ammonia cannot form
questions.answer: Nitrogen
questions.explanation: The reaction needs three hydrogen molecules per nitrogen molecule, so hydrogen is limiting in an equal-number mixture.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Why is Na+ smaller than a neutral sodium atom?
options: Its remaining electrons repel more strongly than before
Its nucleus has fewer neutrons necessarily
It has lost its outer electron shell
It has gained a proton
questions.answer: It has lost its outer electron shell
questions.explanation: Losing the outermost electron removes the occupied third shell and strengthens attraction per remaining electron.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: An element shows a large jump after its second ionisation energy. What does this suggest?
options: Its third electron is easier to remove
It has two relatively accessible valence electrons
It has two neutrons
It must be a noble gas
questions.answer: It has two relatively accessible valence electrons
questions.explanation: A large jump suggests that further removal enters a more strongly bound inner shell.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Two comparable bonds differ mainly in bond order. Which trend is generally expected for the higher-order bond?
options: Longer and weaker
Longer and stronger in all cases
Identical length and energy
Shorter and stronger
questions.answer: Shorter and stronger
questions.explanation: More shared bonding electron density generally strengthens a bond and shortens its equilibrium length.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Why does water have an unusually high boiling point compared with H2S?
options: H2S has no electrons
Water's O-H covalent bonds must break on boiling
Water forms a stronger extended hydrogen-bond network
Water has greater molecular mass
questions.answer: Water forms a stronger extended hydrogen-bond network
questions.explanation: Boiling separates molecules; strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding raises the energy required.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A liquid evaporates into a much larger available gas volume. What usually happens to the substance's entropy?
options: It increases
It decreases necessarily
It is unchanged because mass is conserved
It becomes zero
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: The gaseous state allows many more accessible arrangements and molecular positions.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: For N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, increased pressure at fixed temperature favours which side?
options: Nitrogen and hydrogen
Neither side because gases cannot equilibrate
Whichever side contains a catalyst
Ammonia
questions.answer: Ammonia
questions.explanation: Compression favours the side with fewer gas molecules, which is the ammonia side.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Equal-concentration strong and weak monoprotic acids are compared. Why does the weak acid usually have higher pH?
options: Its conjugate base is absent
A smaller fraction of its molecules ionises
Each molecule releases more protons
Its concentration must be zero
questions.answer: A smaller fraction of its molecules ionises
questions.explanation: Partial ionisation gives a lower hydrogen-ion concentration than a fully dissociated acid of equal concentration.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A little acid is added to a mixture of a weak acid and its conjugate base. Why does pH change only slightly?
options: The conjugate base consumes much of the added H+
The solvent loses all polarity
The weak acid becomes a strong acid
The added acid is not conserved
questions.answer: The conjugate base consumes much of the added H+
questions.explanation: The buffer's base component reacts with added hydrogen ions, limiting the concentration change.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A species oxidises another reactant. What happens to that species itself?
options: Its electrons vanish
It cannot change oxidation state
It is reduced
It is also oxidised necessarily
questions.answer: It is reduced
questions.explanation: The oxidising agent accepts electrons and undergoes reduction.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Why is a salt bridge useful in a galvanic cell?
options: It makes the redox reaction nonspontaneous
It allows ionic movement that prevents charge buildup
It sends electrons through the solution between electrodes
It replaces both electrodes
questions.answer: It allows ionic movement that prevents charge buildup
questions.explanation: Ion migration maintains electrical neutrality as oxidation and reduction proceed in separate compartments.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Doubling a reactant concentration doubles the initial rate while other conditions are fixed. What does this support?
options: Second-order dependence on that reactant
Zero-order dependence on that reactant
A negative reaction order necessarily
First-order dependence on that reactant
questions.answer: First-order dependence on that reactant
questions.explanation: A proportional rate change is consistent with a first-power concentration dependence.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Why can a small temperature increase greatly accelerate a reaction?
options: The activation energy must rise
The equilibrium constant always becomes one
The fraction of collisions above activation energy increases
Every collision becomes successful
questions.answer: The fraction of collisions above activation energy increases
questions.explanation: The high-energy tail of the molecular energy distribution grows with temperature.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: An acid-base titration has a steep pH change around its equivalence point. What makes an indicator suitable?
options: Its transition range lies within that steep change
Its colour is darkest before any titrant is added
Its transition must occur exactly at pH 7 in every titration
It must react with all of the analyte first
questions.answer: Its transition range lies within that steep change
questions.explanation: An indicator whose transition lies within the steep region can signal a volume close to equivalence.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A photoelectron spectrum has two peaks with different areas under comparable detection conditions. What does the area comparison help infer?
options: The number of neutrons in each electron
The colour of each individual orbital
The sample's molecular shape by itself
Relative numbers of electrons in the represented subshells
questions.answer: Relative numbers of electrons in the represented subshells
questions.explanation: Peak binding energies identify how tightly electrons are held, while relative areas reflect electron populations.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: At low temperature, an attractive real gas can exert less pressure than an ideal prediction at the same amount and volume. Why?
options: Attractions necessarily increase every wall impact
Attractions reduce the momentum transferred outward at the walls
Gas molecules have no mass at low temperature
The particles turn into an ideal vacuum
questions.answer: Attractions reduce the momentum transferred outward at the walls
questions.explanation: Intermolecular attractions can reduce the force exerted on the container relative to the ideal noninteracting model.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Water boils at a lower temperature on a high mountain. What change helps explain this?
options: Lower external pressure lets vapour pressure match it sooner
Water molecules have lost their covalent bonds
Gravity removes all intermolecular attraction
Lower pressure requires a higher vapour pressure to boil
questions.answer: Lower external pressure lets vapour pressure match it sooner
questions.explanation: Boiling occurs when liquid vapour pressure matches external pressure; a lower external pressure is reached at a lower temperature.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: An exothermic experiment loses some heat to the room but calculates heat using only the solution's rise. How is the released heat magnitude likely biased?
options: Unaffected by heat loss
Forced to be exactly zero
Underestimated
Overestimated in every case
questions.answer: Underestimated
questions.explanation: Unmeasured heat leaving to the room makes the observed solution warming smaller than the total reaction heat release.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A dilute strong acid and a concentrated weak acid are compared. Why is acid strength alone insufficient to rank their pH values?
options: Concentration affects only the solution colour
pH depends on both dissociation and analytical concentration
A strong acid always has lower pH at every possible concentration
Weak acids cannot supply hydrogen ions
questions.answer: pH depends on both dissociation and analytical concentration
questions.explanation: Hydrogen-ion concentration depends on how much acid is present as well as how far it dissociates.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A proposed elementary step involves one A and one B colliding. Which rate dependence is expected for that elementary step?
options: Independent of both concentrations in every case
Proportional only to the final product concentration
Always third order regardless of participants
Proportional to the product of their concentrations
questions.answer: Proportional to the product of their concentrations
questions.explanation: For a simple bimolecular elementary event, encounter rate depends on both reactant concentrations.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A product yield is lower than the stoichiometric maximum although the limiting reactant is consumed. Which explanation is possible?
options: The limiting reactant was unlimited
The balanced equation must contain fractional atoms
Some reactant formed a side product
Mass conservation failed
questions.answer: Some reactant formed a side product
questions.explanation: Consumption need not all follow the desired pathway; side reactions can lower isolated yield.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: First ionisation energy of boron is lower than beryllium's despite higher nuclear charge. Why?
options: Boron loses a higher-energy 2p electron
Boron has fewer protons
Beryllium's outer shell is farther from the nucleus
Boron loses an inner 1s electron first
questions.answer: Boron loses a higher-energy 2p electron
questions.explanation: Beryllium's filled 2s subshell is relatively stable, while boron's first removed electron is in 2p.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Two resonance structures of an ion place charge on different atoms. What is the actual ion best described as?
options: A rapid physical oscillation between complete drawings
A mixture of different compounds
An ion whose atoms exchange positions
One delocalised structure
questions.answer: One delocalised structure
questions.explanation: Resonance drawings represent contributors to one electronic structure; atoms do not switch places.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A reversible reaction equation is multiplied by two. How does its equilibrium constant change?
options: It stays unchanged
It is squared
It doubles
It halves
questions.answer: It is squared
questions.explanation: Multiplying all stoichiometric coefficients doubles the exponents in the equilibrium expression.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: For a reaction written forward, Q is smaller than K at the current temperature. What net change is favoured?
options: Formation of more products
Formation of more reactants
No change because Q and K are unrelated
A decrease of K until it equals Q
questions.answer: Formation of more products
questions.explanation: The mixture moves forward until the reaction quotient reaches its equilibrium value.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Two buffers have the same acid-to-base ratio but different total concentrations. What differs most directly?
options: The concentrated buffer must have a radically different initial pH
Both can absorb unlimited acid
The more concentrated buffer resists added acid or base better
Only the dilute buffer has a definable pH
questions.answer: The more concentrated buffer resists added acid or base better
questions.explanation: Similar ratios give similar pH, but more buffer components provide greater capacity.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A weak acid is titrated to equivalence with a strong base. Why is the equivalence solution usually basic?
options: All weak-acid titrations end at pH 7
The conjugate base reacts with water to form OH-
Excess strong base is required by definition at equivalence
The acid has no hydrogen
questions.answer: The conjugate base reacts with water to form OH-
questions.explanation: At equivalence the salt's conjugate base undergoes hydrolysis and raises pH.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A cell reaction has positive standard cell potential. What follows about standard Gibbs-energy change?
options: It is positive
It must be zero
It is independent of electron transfer
It is negative
questions.answer: It is negative
questions.explanation: The relation delta-G-standard = -nFE-standard gives a negative Gibbs-energy change.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: Aqueous salt electrolysis is compared with molten-salt electrolysis. Why may the cathode products differ?
options: Molten salts contain no cations
Electrode reactions never depend on the medium
Water can compete for reduction in the aqueous cell
Ions have no charge in water
questions.answer: Water can compete for reduction in the aqueous cell
questions.explanation: Aqueous solutions introduce water as a possible reactant, changing which reduction occurs.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reactant starts at two different concentrations under identical conditions. How do its half-lives compare?
options: They are equal
The more concentrated sample has twice the half-life
The less concentrated sample has twice the half-life
Half-life cannot be defined for a chemical reaction
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: A first-order half-life depends on the rate constant, not the initial concentration.

questions.subject: AP Chemistry
