The unemployment rate by arithmetic identity
A consumer price index that includes those imports
questions.answer: A consumer price index that includes those imports
questions.explanation: Consumer price measures can include imports, whereas the GDP deflator concerns domestically produced output.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Some unemployed people stop actively seeking work and leave the labour force. What can happen without new jobs being created?
options: The labour force must grow
Every remaining job seeker becomes employed
The measured unemployment rate can fall
The employed population must rise
questions.answer: The measured unemployment rate can fall
questions.explanation: Removing unemployed people from both numerator and denominator can lower the rate while employment is unchanged.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A fixed nominal loan was agreed before unexpectedly high inflation. Who tends to benefit in real repayment terms?
options: Neither because inflation cannot affect real debts
The borrower
The lender
Both because the nominal debt doubles
questions.answer: The borrower
questions.explanation: Unexpected inflation reduces the purchasing power of the fixed nominal repayment.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Short-run equilibrium output is below potential because demand is weak. With sticky wages, what is a likely consequence?
options: Cyclical unemployment
An immediate disappearance of all unemployment
Output permanently exceeding capacity
A necessary rise in the natural unemployment rate by the entire gap
questions.answer: Cyclical unemployment
questions.explanation: Weak demand leaves resources underused before wages and prices fully adjust.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: An adverse supply shock raises production costs. What short-run combination can result in the AD–AS model?
options: Lower prices and higher real output
Higher real output with no price effect
Unchanged output because demand exists
Higher prices and lower real output
questions.answer: Higher prices and lower real output
questions.explanation: A leftward short-run aggregate-supply shift can produce inflation alongside reduced output.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Government cuts household taxes while purchases stay unchanged. Why is the first increase in consumption typically smaller than the tax cut?
options: Every household must repay the full cut immediately
A tax cut cannot change disposable income
Households save part of the extra disposable income
Taxes are counted directly as private investment
questions.answer: Households save part of the extra disposable income
questions.explanation: With a marginal propensity to consume below one, only part of additional disposable income is initially spent.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Two otherwise identical economies receive the same spending injection. One has a higher marginal propensity to save. Which has the smaller simple expenditure multiplier?
options: The economy with higher initial government spending regardless of saving
The economy with the higher propensity to save
The economy with the lower propensity to save
Both necessarily have the same multiplier
questions.answer: The economy with the higher propensity to save
questions.explanation: More saving from each income increase means less spending passed to the next round.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Unemployment-benefit payments rise during a downturn under existing rules. Why is this an automatic stabiliser?
options: Transfers support disposable income without a fresh policy vote
Transfers directly count as government production in GDP
Every recipient stops being unemployed when paid
Benefits necessarily eliminate the output gap
questions.answer: Transfers support disposable income without a fresh policy vote
questions.explanation: The existing system offsets part of the fall in private income and spending.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: People want to hold more liquid balances at every interest rate while money supply is fixed in the simple money-market model. What pressure arises?
options: The equilibrium interest rate falls
Money demand must shift back immediately
The price of every bond must rise
The equilibrium interest rate rises
questions.answer: The equilibrium interest rate rises
questions.explanation: Excess demand for money encourages asset sales, lowering bond prices and raising interest rates in this model.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A bank has abundant reserves but faces weak creditworthy loan demand. Why might lending remain subdued?
options: Deposits cannot coexist with reserves
Bank lending is independent of expected repayment
Reserves alone do not ensure willing, suitable borrowers
Every reserve balance legally has to be lent out immediately
questions.answer: Reserves alone do not ensure willing, suitable borrowers
questions.explanation: Credit demand, borrower risk and other bank constraints matter alongside liquidity.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: The nominal interest rate stays fixed while expected inflation rises. What happens to the approximate expected real rate?
options: It becomes equal to expected inflation
It falls
It rises
It stays fixed because the nominal rate is fixed
questions.answer: It falls
questions.explanation: The approximate expected real rate is the nominal rate minus expected inflation.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: In an ample-reserves system, a central bank raises interest paid on reserve balances. Why can this push overnight market rates upward?
options: Banks have a more attractive return from holding reserve balances
Banks are forced to lend at a lower return than before
The change directly increases every household's income-tax rate
Reserve balances cease to be central-bank liabilities
questions.answer: Banks have a more attractive return from holding reserve balances
questions.explanation: A higher administered return strengthens banks' incentive to require comparable returns on short-term lending.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Government borrowing increases demand for loanable funds when saving supply is unchanged. What can partly offset the fiscal demand stimulus?
options: Lower real interest rates eliminating all saving
A necessary equal increase in private investment
A fall in government purchases by definition
Higher real interest rates reducing private investment
questions.answer: Higher real interest rates reducing private investment
questions.explanation: Greater borrowing can raise financing costs and displace some interest-sensitive private spending.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: An improvement in technology raises output possible from the same inputs. How is it represented in an AD–AS model?
options: Aggregate demand must shift left by the same amount
Potential output remains unchanged by definition
Long-run aggregate supply shifts right
Only a movement along an unchanged long-run supply curve
questions.answer: Long-run aggregate supply shifts right
questions.explanation: Better technology expands the economy's sustainable productive capacity.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A currency depreciates and domestic import prices rise. Why might domestic inflation increase?
options: Imported goods stop entering the consumption basket
Imported final goods and imported inputs can become more expensive
Depreciation necessarily lowers every domestic production cost
The exchange-rate change directly reduces every tax rate
questions.answer: Imported final goods and imported inputs can become more expensive
questions.explanation: Higher import costs can affect both consumer prices and firms' production costs.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A country buys more abroad than it earns in current-account receipts. How can it finance the gap?
options: By net borrowing, selling assets or reducing external assets
Only by recording the imports as exports
Only by increasing current receipts on paper
By making all financial transactions disappear
questions.answer: By net borrowing, selling assets or reducing external assets
questions.explanation: A current-account deficit is matched by financing transactions, subject to the accounting convention and statistical discrepancy.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Domestic real returns rise relative to foreign returns with risk and expectations unchanged. What can follow under flexible exchange rates?
options: Capital outflows and depreciation pressure necessarily
No possible change in asset demand
A required legal devaluation
Capital inflows and appreciation pressure
questions.answer: Capital inflows and appreciation pressure
questions.explanation: More attractive relative returns can draw investors and increase demand for the domestic currency.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: An economy raises investment by cutting current consumption. Why is faster future growth not guaranteed merely by a larger investment total?
options: Consumption and investment use unrelated resources
The total guarantees equal benefits to every resident
The productivity and effective use of the investment also matter
Any investment automatically reduces future capacity
questions.answer: The productivity and effective use of the investment also matter
questions.explanation: Wasteful or poorly used investment may deliver little additional productive capacity despite its current resource cost.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Trade raises total potential gains, but workers in an import-competing industry lose jobs. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Total gains guarantee automatic compensation to every loser
Aggregate gains can coexist with concentrated adjustment costs
Those job losses prove that no consumer can gain
Comparative advantage guarantees no worker ever changes jobs
questions.answer: Aggregate gains can coexist with concentrated adjustment costs
questions.explanation: Efficiency gains do not determine how benefits and costs are distributed or whether compensation occurs.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A country has positive gross investment but depreciation is larger. What follows for its produced capital stock, other changes excluded?
options: It declines because net investment is negative
It rises because gross investment is positive
It stays fixed because depreciation is only a price index
It becomes identical to current consumption
questions.answer: It declines because net investment is negative
questions.explanation: Net investment subtracts depreciation from gross investment; a negative amount means capital is not fully replaced.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A firm produces goods this year but sells them next year. How should the production be treated in expenditure-based GDP?
options: It enters GDP only next year as new production
It enters neither year's GDP because no immediate sale occurred
Its full value is counted as new output in both years
This year's unsold output enters inventory investment
questions.answer: This year's unsold output enters inventory investment
questions.explanation: Inventory investment accounts for current production not yet sold, preventing omission and later double counting.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: An economy operates at potential output but workers are still changing jobs or lack required skills. What does this imply?
options: All unemployment must be cyclical
Potential output is defined as zero labour-force participation
Full employment can coexist with frictional and structural unemployment
Potential output requires every adult to hold a job
questions.answer: Full employment can coexist with frictional and structural unemployment
questions.explanation: Full employment excludes cyclical unemployment, not all search and skill-mismatch unemployment.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Inflation expectations rise while supply conditions otherwise stay unchanged. In the expectations-augmented model, what happens?
options: The natural unemployment rate must fall to zero
The short-run Phillips curve shifts upward
The long-run unemployment-inflation trade-off becomes permanently exploitable
The short-run Phillips curve must shift downward
questions.answer: The short-run Phillips curve shifts upward
questions.explanation: At a given unemployment rate, higher expected inflation feeds into wage and price setting.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Demand expands beyond potential output with no lasting productivity gain. In the standard long-run AD–AS adjustment, what remains after wages and prices adjust?
options: A higher price level with output returning to potential
Permanently higher real output solely from demand
A lower price level and lower natural unemployment
An outward production frontier caused only by spending
questions.answer: A higher price level with output returning to potential
questions.explanation: Rising input prices shift short-run supply until output returns to unchanged productive capacity.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: An adverse supply shock causes inflation and an output loss. Why is demand expansion a difficult response?
options: It shifts productive capacity right immediately
It necessarily lowers both inflation and unemployment without trade-offs
It removes the original input-cost increase directly
It may support output while adding further price pressure
questions.answer: It may support output while adding further price pressure
questions.explanation: Demand management can cushion the output fall but can worsen inflation caused by constrained supply.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: In the simple closed-economy model with lump-sum taxes and idle resources, government raises purchases and taxes equally. Why can equilibrium output rise?
options: The tax rise is recorded as an equal increase in private consumption
The result requires a marginal propensity to consume greater than one
Purchases enter demand fully while households reduce consumption by only part of the tax rise
The equal changes necessarily cancel every spending round
questions.answer: Purchases enter demand fully while households reduce consumption by only part of the tax rise
questions.explanation: With a marginal propensity to consume between zero and one, the initial net demand effect is positive.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A textbook multiplier predicts a large output gain, but the economy is already near capacity. Why might the real output gain be smaller?
options: Potential output must equal nominal spending at all prices
Additional demand may raise prices and crowd out other spending
The marginal propensity to save must become negative
Every household must stop consuming
questions.answer: Additional demand may raise prices and crowd out other spending
questions.explanation: Fixed-price spare-capacity assumptions become less appropriate as resource constraints tighten.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A budget deficit widens during recession without any new spending programme or tax-rate change. What should be checked before calling policy more expansionary by design?
options: The effect of falling receipts and automatic benefit payments
Whether the public debt is measured in years
Whether all imports were banned
Whether nominal interest rates are positive
questions.answer: The effect of falling receipts and automatic benefit payments
questions.explanation: The cyclical deficit can change automatically, so the headline balance alone does not reveal discretionary policy changes.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Policy reduces interest rates, yet firms expect poor sales and cut investment. What best explains this outcome?
options: Interest rates and expected returns cannot jointly affect investment
Every rate cut must increase investment by a fixed amount
The central bank directly sets every firm's sales
Lower financing costs may be outweighed by weak expected returns
questions.answer: Lower financing costs may be outweighed by weak expected returns
questions.explanation: Investment depends on expected profitability as well as borrowing costs, so rate cuts do not guarantee expansion.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A simple deposit multiplier assumes no cash leakage and no excess reserves. What happens to realised deposit expansion if households retain more cash from loans?
options: It becomes independent of redepositing
The retained cash automatically becomes a new bank deposit elsewhere
It can be smaller than the simple maximum
It must exceed the simple maximum
questions.answer: It can be smaller than the simple maximum
questions.explanation: Cash leakage leaves less funding circulating through repeated bank deposit and loan expansion in the simple model.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Nominal rates rise by less than expected inflation. Why can borrowing become cheaper in expected real terms?
options: Expected inflation is added twice to nominal rates
The expected real interest rate falls despite a higher nominal rate
Real rates must rise whenever nominal rates rise
The principal automatically shrinks in nominal terms
questions.answer: The expected real interest rate falls despite a higher nominal rate
questions.explanation: The real-rate change depends on both nominal rates and expected inflation, not the nominal change alone.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: Reserves are already ample and the overnight rate is anchored by administered rates. Why may another small reserve injection have little rate effect?
options: It need not change the administered return or create new scarcity conditions
Every reserve injection must lower rates proportionally
Banks lose all access to central-bank accounts
The injection directly fixes every long-term bond yield
questions.answer: It need not change the administered return or create new scarcity conditions
questions.explanation: Once reserves are ample, reserve quantity changes can have less influence than changes in the rates governing reserve returns.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.topic: Policy mix in an open economy
questions.q: Fiscal expansion raises domestic interest rates and attracts capital under a floating exchange rate. What can reduce its boost to demand?
options: Currency appreciation must increase export competitiveness
Capital inflows automatically eliminate all imports
The fiscal multiplier becomes infinite
Currency appreciation can weaken net exports
questions.answer: Currency appreciation can weaken net exports
questions.explanation: Appreciation makes exports relatively dearer and imports relatively cheaper, potentially offsetting some domestic demand expansion.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: An economy keeps adding physical capital per worker with unchanged technology. Why can growth from this source slow?
options: Depreciation must fall to zero
Technology automatically deteriorates as investment rises
Diminishing returns can reduce the extra output from each additional unit of capital
More capital necessarily makes every worker less productive
questions.answer: Diminishing returns can reduce the extra output from each additional unit of capital
questions.explanation: With other factors fixed, capital deepening commonly delivers diminishing additions to output per worker.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A currency depreciates, but foreign sellers cut their own-currency prices to protect sales. What follows?
options: The currency cannot have depreciated
Domestic import prices may rise by less than the currency depreciation
Domestic import prices must rise by exactly the depreciation rate
Domestic import prices must be unchanged in every case
questions.answer: Domestic import prices may rise by less than the currency depreciation
questions.explanation: Exporters' pricing responses can partially absorb exchange-rate changes, so pass-through need not be complete.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: After a currency depreciation, import spending rises before trade quantities adjust. Why can the trade balance initially worsen?
options: Higher import prices can act before buyers change quantities sufficiently
Depreciation immediately makes all imports free
Export volumes must drop permanently by definition
Accounting requires a trade surplus after every depreciation
questions.answer: Higher import prices can act before buyers change quantities sufficiently
questions.explanation: Short-run contracts and adjustment lags can delay quantity responses while import costs change sooner.

questions.subject: AP Macroeconomics
questions.q: A central bank defends a currency facing downward pressure by selling foreign reserves and buying domestic currency. What constraint can eventually bind?
options: Its purchases create unlimited foreign reserves automatically
The exchange rate no longer needs any supporting transactions
A fixed rate guarantees investors cannot sell domestic assets
Its available foreign reserves can be depleted
questions.answer: Its available foreign reserves can be depleted
questions.explanation: Defending the rate in this direction uses foreign assets, so persistent pressure can exhaust the reserve buffer.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A student uses a free hour for paid work instead of their next-best option, study. What is the opportunity cost?
options: Only the bus fare, even if no bus is used
The wage earned from working
The value of the study opportunity forgone
Every activity the student could imagine
questions.answer: The value of the study opportunity forgone
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative sacrificed.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: An economy moves from an inefficient point inside its production frontier to the frontier. What can explain this?
options: A change in the units used on the graph only
Better use of existing resources
A necessary reduction in every output
A guarantee that new resources were discovered
questions.answer: Better use of existing resources
questions.explanation: Reducing unemployment or inefficiency can increase output without shifting productive capacity.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: One producer gives up fewer units of cloth to make a unit of food than another. In which good does it have comparative advantage?
options: Food
Cloth automatically
Both goods automatically
Neither because absolute output is unknown
questions.answer: Food
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage depends on lower opportunity cost.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: An extra hour of tutoring brings a benefit greater than its additional cost. What does marginal analysis support, other things equal?
options: Rejecting it because a cost exists
Ignoring the additional benefit
Taking unlimited hours regardless of later costs
Taking that extra hour
questions.answer: Taking that extra hour
questions.explanation: An additional activity is worthwhile while its marginal benefit exceeds its marginal cost.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Consumers' incomes rise and a good is normal. With other factors unchanged, what happens to demand?
options: There is only movement along an unchanged demand curve
Supply must shift left
It shifts right
It shifts left
questions.answer: It shifts right
questions.explanation: A normal good is demanded more at each price when income rises.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A production method reduces unit costs. What happens to supply, other things equal?
options: Quantity supplied is fixed at every price
It shifts right
It shifts left
Demand necessarily falls
questions.answer: It shifts right
questions.explanation: Lower production costs make more output worth supplying at a given price.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: At the current price, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied. What pressure normally arises in an unregulated market?
options: Upward pressure on price
Downward pressure on price
A guarantee that demand becomes zero
A surplus of unsold goods
questions.answer: Upward pressure on price
questions.explanation: Competition among buyers for scarce available output tends to raise price.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A small percentage price rise causes a much larger percentage fall in quantity demanded. What does this indicate?
options: Perfectly inelastic demand
No relationship between price and quantity
A shift in supply by definition
Price-elastic demand
questions.answer: Price-elastic demand
questions.explanation: Elastic demand has a quantity response proportionately larger than the price change.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: The price of tea rises while other factors stay fixed. If tea and coffee are substitutes, what happens to coffee demand?
options: It cannot change
It becomes coffee supply
It tends to rise
It must fall
questions.answer: It tends to rise
questions.explanation: Some buyers switch toward the relatively more attractive substitute.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A maximum legal price is set below the market-clearing price. What is the standard competitive-market prediction?
options: An automatic increase in supply
A shortage
A surplus
No effect because every ceiling is nonbinding
questions.answer: A shortage
questions.explanation: At a binding ceiling, consumers demand more than producers are willing to supply.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A per-unit tax raises the cost of supplying a product. In the standard model, what happens to the supply curve as seen by buyers?
options: It shifts upward by the tax amount
It shifts downward by the tax amount
It becomes the demand curve
It disappears because taxes stop all trade
questions.answer: It shifts upward by the tax amount
questions.explanation: The tax creates a wedge between the buyer's price and the amount retained by the seller.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A factory pays the same monthly rent whether it produces 100 or 200 units within its capacity. What does this illustrate?
options: A cost that must be zero at positive output
A variable cost proportional to units
A marginal revenue receipt
A fixed cost over that output range
questions.answer: A fixed cost over that output range
questions.explanation: Fixed costs do not change with output within the relevant short-run range.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Producing one extra unit adds 8 to total cost. What is the marginal cost of that unit?
options: The selling price in every case
The average of all past prices
The entire previous total cost
questions.explanation: Marginal cost measures the additional cost of extra output.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A business owner forgoes a salary elsewhere to run the business. Why count that forgone salary in economic cost?
options: It has no relevance because no invoice exists
It is an opportunity cost of the owner's labour
It is always a cash payment to an employee
It is extra sales revenue
questions.answer: It is an opportunity cost of the owner's labour
questions.explanation: Economic cost includes implicit opportunity costs as well as explicit payments.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A small firm sells an identical product in a perfectly competitive market. Why can it not profitably charge much above the market price?
options: Buyers can obtain the same product from other sellers
It controls the whole market supply
Its own costs determine every other firm's price
Every buyer is required to buy from it
questions.answer: Buyers can obtain the same product from other sellers
questions.explanation: A competitive firm faces readily available substitutes and is a price taker.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A sole seller raises its price. Why is it not guaranteed higher profit?
options: A monopoly can sell any quantity at any price
Revenue must rise whenever price rises
A monopolist never faces a demand curve
Customers may reduce purchases, and costs also matter
questions.answer: Customers may reduce purchases, and costs also matter
questions.explanation: Market power does not remove the relationship between price, quantity demanded and costs.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A firm in a market with a few major sellers considers cutting price. Why consider rivals' responses?
options: Each firm operates in a completely separate market
A price cut guarantees permanent market leadership
Their actions can affect the cut's effect on sales and profit
Rivals must leave their prices unchanged
questions.answer: Their actions can affect the cut's effect on sales and profit
questions.explanation: Strategic interdependence means one firm's outcome depends partly on competitors' choices.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Demand for a factory's product rises. Why might its demand for workers increase?
options: Product demand is unrelated to production resources
Labour helps produce the more-demanded output
Workers' preferences automatically become product demand
Every wage must fall to zero
questions.answer: Labour helps produce the more-demanded output
questions.explanation: Demand for a factor is derived partly from demand for the output it helps produce.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A factory's emissions impose costs on nearby residents that the factory does not pay. What is missing from its private production cost?
options: An external cost
The factory's sales revenue
Every wage paid by the factory
Only the residents' private purchases
questions.answer: An external cost
questions.explanation: A negative externality imposes costs on third parties outside the market transaction.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A warning signal can benefit additional residents without reducing others' benefit, and nonpayers are difficult to exclude. What problem may hinder private provision?
options: A requirement that each user's benefit must reduce everyone else's
A guarantee that all users voluntarily pay the full cost
An absence of any social benefit
Free riding
questions.answer: Free riding
questions.explanation: Nonexcludability makes it difficult to collect payment from everyone who benefits.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A bowed-out production frontier shows that making more of one good requires giving up increasing amounts of another. Why?
options: Opportunity cost is always zero
The economy must be operating inside the frontier
Resources are not equally suited to both activities
All resources have identical productivity in both activities
questions.answer: Resources are not equally suited to both activities
questions.explanation: Shifting progressively less suitable resources raises the opportunity cost of additional output.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A producer is more productive in both goods. Why can trade still benefit both producers?
options: Trade requires identical production ratios
Their relative opportunity costs can differ
Absolute advantage eliminates every possible trade gain
Only the less productive producer has any opportunity cost
questions.answer: Their relative opportunity costs can differ
questions.explanation: Specialisation can be based on comparative rather than absolute advantage.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A consumer can move spending toward a good that gives more marginal utility per unit of currency. Why can this improve total utility?
options: The same spending can obtain a larger marginal benefit
Every purchase must have the same total utility
Price has no role in comparing purchases
Marginal utility increases forever for every good
questions.answer: The same spending can obtain a larger marginal benefit
questions.explanation: Allocating a limited budget compares additional benefit per unit of expenditure.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Demand for a good falls when income rises, with other factors fixed. What does this imply?
options: The good must be physically defective
Its price elasticity must be zero
It is necessarily a luxury good
The good is inferior over that income range
questions.answer: The good is inferior over that income range
questions.explanation: Inferior goods have negative income elasticity over the specified range.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A good's own price falls, with demand determinants unchanged. Which description is correct?
options: Supply becomes demand
Income must have risen
Quantity demanded rises along the existing demand curve
The demand curve necessarily shifts right
questions.answer: Quantity demanded rises along the existing demand curve
questions.explanation: A change in the good's own price causes movement along its demand curve.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Producers have more time to adjust equipment and enter an industry. Why may supply become more price elastic?
options: Supply elasticity is determined only by today's price
More production adjustments become possible
Longer time makes all resources fixed
A longer period forces demand to disappear
questions.answer: More production adjustments become possible
questions.explanation: Adjustment opportunities generally expand over longer time horizons.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Demand increases while supply stays unchanged in a standard upward-sloping supply model. What happens to equilibrium?
options: Price and quantity both rise
Price falls and quantity rises
Price rises and quantity falls
Both price and quantity fall
questions.answer: Price and quantity both rise
questions.explanation: The demand increase moves the market to a higher price and larger quantity on the existing supply curve.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Demand is inelastic over a price rise. What happens to total revenue if the expected response occurs?
options: It necessarily falls
It stays constant by definition
It becomes equal to production cost
It rises
questions.answer: It rises
questions.explanation: The percentage fall in quantity is smaller than the percentage increase in price.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A buyer is willing to pay 30 for a unit but pays 22. What does the difference represent?
options: Tax revenue automatically
The seller's entire profit
Consumer surplus
Producer marginal cost
questions.answer: Consumer surplus
questions.explanation: Consumer surplus is willingness to pay minus the actual price for the unit.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A minimum price is imposed above equilibrium. What occurs in the standard competitive model without government purchase of excess output?
options: Every unit offered is guaranteed a buyer
Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied
The floor has no effect at any level
questions.answer: Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded
questions.explanation: A binding floor raises the price above market clearing and creates excess supply.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Demand is much less elastic than supply. Who generally bears more of a per-unit tax burden?
options: Buyers
Sellers regardless of elasticity
Only the government
Whichever side formally sends the payment, regardless of market responses
questions.answer: Buyers
questions.explanation: The less price-responsive side has fewer adjustment options and bears more of the burden.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: More workers are added to a fixed amount of equipment. Why might the extra output per added worker eventually fall?
options: Each new worker necessarily has less ability
Total output must fall as soon as a second worker is hired
The equipment becomes a variable input automatically
Workers increasingly share the fixed input
questions.answer: Workers increasingly share the fixed input
questions.explanation: With some inputs fixed, successive additions of a variable input can yield diminishing marginal product.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Marginal cost is below average total cost at the current output. What does one more unit tend to do to average total cost?
options: Leave it unchanged necessarily
Make total cost negative
Reduce it
Increase it
questions.answer: Reduce it
questions.explanation: An additional unit costing less than the existing average pulls that average down.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: At the current output, marginal revenue exceeds marginal cost. What does increasing output slightly do to profit under the usual smooth model?
options: Make fixed costs disappear
Increase it
Decrease it
Leave it unchanged by definition
questions.answer: Increase it
questions.explanation: The added unit contributes more revenue than cost while marginal revenue exceeds marginal cost.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A competitive firm can cover variable costs but not all fixed costs at its best positive output. Why may it keep operating in the short run?
options: Operating contributes toward unavoidable fixed costs
Every accounting loss requires immediate shutdown
Fixed costs are avoided only by producing more
Revenue below total cost proves variable costs are uncovered
questions.answer: Operating contributes toward unavoidable fixed costs
questions.explanation: If shutting down would leave fixed costs payable, a positive contribution can reduce the loss.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A single-price monopolist cuts price to sell an extra unit. Why can marginal revenue be below the new price?
options: The extra unit produces no revenue at all
The monopolist's marginal cost is always zero
All demand curves are horizontal
The lower price also applies to units it would otherwise have sold
questions.answer: The lower price also applies to units it would otherwise have sold
questions.explanation: Additional revenue is offset partly by reduced receipts on existing sales.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Firms earn economic profit in a market with differentiated products and low entry barriers. What pressure does entry create over time?
options: It makes all products identical immediately
It removes all fixed costs
It reduces each incumbent's demand and profit opportunities
It guarantees every incumbent's sales increase
questions.answer: It reduces each incumbent's demand and profit opportunities
questions.explanation: New alternatives compete for customers, tending to erode abnormal profit.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A worker's marginal product rises while output price stays fixed in a competitive product market. What happens to that worker's marginal revenue product?
options: It becomes the worker's total wage income
It rises
It falls
It stays unchanged regardless of productivity
questions.answer: It rises
questions.explanation: Marginal revenue product equals the added output times the marginal revenue per unit.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Education can benefit people beyond the individual student. In a model where those benefits are ignored by buyers, what can result?
options: Consumption below the socially efficient level
Consumption necessarily above the social optimum
Private benefit exceeding social benefit by definition
Zero benefit to the student
questions.answer: Consumption below the socially efficient level
questions.explanation: Unpriced external benefits can make private demand lower than the social marginal-benefit schedule.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Fish in an open-access fishery are difficult to exclude others from catching, but one person's catch leaves fewer fish. What pressure can arise?
options: The same free availability as a nonrival public good without depletion
Guaranteed optimal conservation by every user
A permanent increase in fish stock after every catch
Overuse of a rival common resource
questions.answer: Overuse of a rival common resource
questions.explanation: Users may not account for the depletion cost imposed on others and future users.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: An allocation maximises total surplus but leaves one group with very little income. What follows?
options: An unequal allocation can never be efficient under any definition
Distribution is measured only by total surplus
Efficiency alone does not establish an equitable distribution
Maximum surplus guarantees equal income for everyone
questions.answer: Efficiency alone does not establish an equitable distribution
questions.explanation: Efficiency concerns total gains or resource use; equity concerns how benefits and resources are distributed.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Technology improves only in the production of one of two goods. Why might the frontier rotate outward rather than shift equally everywhere?
options: Opportunity cost disappears for both goods
The maximum output of one good rises while the other intercept need not change
Every technological improvement must expand both intercepts equally
The improvement must move production inside the old frontier
questions.answer: The maximum output of one good rises while the other intercept need not change
questions.explanation: A sector-specific productivity gain affects production possibilities asymmetrically.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Two producers have different opportunity costs for a good. Where must a mutually beneficial exchange ratio normally lie?
options: Between their opportunity-cost ratios
Above both ratios for both to gain
Below both ratios for both to gain
Exactly at the larger producer's absolute output
questions.answer: Between their opportunity-cost ratios
questions.explanation: A ratio between their internal trade-offs lets each obtain the imported good more cheaply than by producing it alone.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A firm must decide whether to produce one more unit. A past setup cost cannot be recovered or changed. Why exclude that cost from this marginal decision?
options: All fixed costs are zero in accounting
Past costs always increase future marginal revenue
The extra unit must be produced regardless of its variable cost
It is unchanged by producing the extra unit
questions.answer: It is unchanged by producing the extra unit
questions.explanation: Relevant marginal decisions compare costs and benefits altered by the additional action.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Demand and supply both increase in a competitive market. Without knowing their relative sizes, what can be concluded?
options: Price necessarily falls and quantity is ambiguous
Both price and quantity must remain unchanged
Equilibrium quantity rises, but the price change is ambiguous
Price necessarily rises and quantity is ambiguous
questions.answer: Equilibrium quantity rises, but the price change is ambiguous
questions.explanation: Both shifts increase quantity, while their effects on price oppose each other.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Demand is perfectly inelastic and supply is upward sloping. In the standard model, how does a per-unit tax affect traded quantity?
options: It necessarily falls by the tax amount
It stays unchanged while the buyer price rises
It falls to zero
It rises because the tax raises revenue
questions.answer: It stays unchanged while the buyer price rises
questions.explanation: Vertical demand fixes quantity; buyers bear the tax through a higher price under the stated assumptions.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A price ceiling is set above the unregulated equilibrium price. Why does it not change the standard market outcome?
options: The market-clearing price already satisfies the ceiling
Every price ceiling creates a shortage regardless of level
The ceiling increases supply by definition
Buyers must pay the ceiling even when sellers offer less
questions.answer: The market-clearing price already satisfies the ceiling
questions.explanation: A control has no direct effect when the unconstrained equilibrium is permitted.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A straight downward-sloping demand curve has constant slope. Why does its price elasticity still vary along the curve?
options: Slope and elasticity are always numerically identical
Quantity is constant along every straight line
Elasticity depends only on the currency symbol
Elasticity also depends on the price-to-quantity ratio
questions.answer: Elasticity also depends on the price-to-quantity ratio
questions.explanation: Point elasticity combines the curve's slope with the local price and quantity values.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A tax payment transfers money to government. Why is the tax revenue itself not the same as deadweight loss?
options: Tax revenue measures all consumer surplus before tax
Deadweight loss must equal tax revenue in every market
Deadweight loss is lost total surplus from foregone mutually beneficial trades
Every transferred unit of money is destroyed
questions.answer: Deadweight loss is lost total surplus from foregone mutually beneficial trades
questions.explanation: Transfers redistribute purchasing power; deadweight loss measures gains from trade that are no longer realised.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A law requires sellers rather than buyers to remit a tax. Why does this alone not determine who bears its economic burden?
options: Tax incidence is unrelated to market prices
Prices adjust according to demand and supply responsiveness
The legal payer must bear every unit of the burden
Buyers cannot bear a tax unless they transfer it directly
questions.answer: Prices adjust according to demand and supply responsiveness
questions.explanation: Economic incidence reflects the resulting price wedge and market responses, not merely the collection rule.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A subsidy is intended to correct an external benefit. Why should its size relate to the marginal external benefit at the efficient quantity?
options: That aligns private incentives with the unpriced social gain
Any positive subsidy guarantees efficiency
The subsidy should equal total industry revenue
A subsidy removes the need to consider production costs
questions.answer: That aligns private incentives with the unpriced social gain
questions.explanation: A corrective subsidy targets the gap between private and social marginal benefit at the desired allocation.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A competitive firm's fixed cost rises while its marginal-cost schedule and price are unchanged. What happens to its short-run profit-maximising positive output, if it still operates?
options: It must rise by the fixed-cost increase
It must fall to zero regardless of variable costs
Marginal cost rises by the same amount at every unit
It is unchanged, although profit falls
questions.answer: It is unchanged, although profit falls
questions.explanation: An unchanged marginal comparison leaves the optimal operating output unchanged, while higher fixed cost reduces profit.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A competitive firm earns zero economic profit in long-run equilibrium. Does this mean its owner receives no return?
options: Yes; accounting revenue must be zero
No; economic profit excludes every implicit cost
No; normal opportunity-cost returns are included in economic costs
Yes; the owner must receive no income of any kind
questions.answer: No; normal opportunity-cost returns are included in economic costs
questions.explanation: Zero economic profit means revenue covers explicit costs and the normal returns included as implicit costs.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A single-price monopolist restricts output below the point where demand equals marginal cost. What is the welfare concern?
options: Marginal cost necessarily exceeds price at the chosen output
Some units valued above their marginal cost are not produced
Every unit produced must have negative value
The monopolist's entire revenue is deadweight loss
questions.answer: Some units valued above their marginal cost are not produced
questions.explanation: Foregone trades with benefit above cost create a loss of potential total surplus.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A firm charges different customer groups different prices for the same product. Why is preventing resale between groups important?
options: Resale could undermine the price differences
Resale makes demand perfectly inelastic automatically
Different prices require identical willingness to pay
Price discrimination depends only on different production costs
questions.answer: Resale could undermine the price differences
questions.explanation: Arbitrage allows low-price buyers to resell to high-price buyers, weakening market separation.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: Two firms would jointly earn more by keeping prices high, but each can gain by cutting while the other stays high. What makes cooperation fragile?
options: Joint benefit guarantees individual compliance
The firms must have identical costs for any strategic problem
A profitable deviation cannot exist in an oligopoly
Each has an individual incentive to deviate
questions.answer: Each has an individual incentive to deviate
questions.explanation: A collectively preferable outcome may be unstable when unilateral deviation is attractive.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A single major employer must raise the wage for all workers to attract one more worker. Why does marginal factor cost exceed that worker's wage?
options: All labour supply curves are horizontal
The employer pays no wages to existing workers
The wage increase also raises pay for existing workers
The extra worker produces no output by definition
questions.answer: The wage increase also raises pay for existing workers
questions.explanation: Hiring another worker adds both the new wage and the cost of higher wages for current workers.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: In a simple monopsony model, why can a suitably set minimum wage increase employment?
options: It forces every firm to hire unlimited workers
It can alter the employer's marginal hiring-cost schedule and reduce wage-setting power
Every minimum wage increases employment in every labour market
A wage floor removes all labour supply constraints
questions.answer: It can alter the employer's marginal hiring-cost schedule and reduce wage-setting power
questions.explanation: The outcome depends on market structure and the level of the wage floor, unlike a universal claim about all labour markets.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A pollution tax is set without reliable information about marginal damage. What remains uncertain?
options: Whether it leads to the socially efficient pollution level
Whether pollution can ever impose external costs
Whether any tax can change incentives
Whether tax payments can be collected in principle
questions.answer: Whether it leads to the socially efficient pollution level
questions.explanation: Corrective policy needs a suitable estimate of the external-cost gap; an arbitrary rate need not be optimal.

questions.subject: AP Microeconomics
questions.q: A public good is valuable, but people can benefit without paying. Why does observing little voluntary payment not prove low social value?
options: Nonpayers necessarily receive no benefit
A public good must have zero production cost
Every valuable good is easily sold separately to each user
Individual incentives to free ride can conceal willingness to benefit
questions.answer: Individual incentives to free ride can conceal willingness to benefit
questions.explanation: Nonexcludability can weaken payment incentives even when combined benefits justify provision.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A trolley moves forward while its velocity-time graph slopes downward. What is happening?
options: It is slowing down
It is moving backward
Its acceleration is zero
Its distance travelled is decreasing
questions.answer: It is slowing down
questions.explanation: A downward slope means negative acceleration; with positive velocity this reduces speed.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A passenger leans forward when a bus brakes. Why?
options: The seat increases the passenger's speed
The passenger loses mass
The passenger's body tends to keep moving
A forward force from gravity appears
questions.answer: The passenger's body tends to keep moving
questions.explanation: Inertia resists the change from the body's original forward motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A box remains stationary while you push it gently on a rough floor. What balances your push?
options: An upward force from the floor
Static friction
Kinetic friction
The box's weight alone
questions.answer: Static friction
questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to oppose the push until its limiting value is reached.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two carts initially at rest push apart on a frictionless track. What must their momenta do?
options: Have equal velocities
Point in the same direction
Increase the total momentum
Add to zero
questions.answer: Add to zero
questions.explanation: With no external horizontal force, total momentum remains its initial value of zero.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A stone moves at constant speed in a circle. Why is it accelerating?
options: Its speed must be increasing
Its kinetic energy must increase
Its velocity changes direction
Its mass changes continuously
questions.answer: Its velocity changes direction
questions.explanation: Velocity includes direction, which changes throughout circular motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two identical springs support equal loads, one singly and two in parallel. Which arrangement stretches less?
options: The parallel pair
The single spring
Both stretch equally
Neither arrangement can stretch
questions.answer: The parallel pair
questions.explanation: The parallel springs share the load, increasing the effective stiffness.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A sealed hydraulic system has connected pistons of different areas. Why can the larger piston exert more force?
options: Pressure must be larger at the larger piston
The fluid creates extra energy
The smaller piston has no displacement
The same pressure acts over a larger area
questions.answer: The same pressure acts over a larger area
questions.explanation: Transmitted pressure is the same at equal depth, while force equals pressure times area.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two points are at equal depth in connected water at rest. One is in a wide region and one in a narrow region. How do their pressures compare?
options: Pressure depends only on the container's total volume
They are equal
The narrow region must have higher pressure
The wide region must have higher pressure
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure depends on depth, density and surface pressure, not container width.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A force is applied farther from a hinge, at right angles to a door. Why is the door easier to turn?
options: The same force produces a larger moment
The door's weight disappears
The force becomes larger by definition
The hinge stops exerting a force
questions.answer: The same force produces a larger moment
questions.explanation: Turning effect increases with perpendicular distance from the pivot.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A runner completes one lap and returns to the starting point. How do distance and displacement compare?
options: Both equal the track circumference as vectors
Displacement is positive and distance is zero
Distance is positive and displacement is zero
Both are zero
questions.answer: Distance is positive and displacement is zero
questions.explanation: Distance counts the path travelled, while displacement compares final and initial positions.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A small cart pushes a large cart during contact. How do their forces on each other compare?
options: The forces are equal only if their masses match
Equal magnitude and opposite direction
The large cart always exerts the larger force
The small cart exerts no force
questions.answer: Equal magnitude and opposite direction
questions.explanation: Newton's third law gives equal opposite interaction forces, though different masses can have different accelerations.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A book rests on a table. Which two forces on the book balance vertically?
options: Its weight and its force on Earth
The table's weight and the book's force on the table
The book's weight and an extra upward gravity force
Its weight and the table's normal force
questions.answer: Its weight and the table's normal force
questions.explanation: The book has downward gravitational force and upward contact force from the table; balanced forces act on the same object.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A box slides across a rough stationary floor. In what direction does kinetic friction on the box act?
options: Always toward geographic north
Perpendicular to the floor only
Opposite its sliding relative to the floor
Always in the direction of its acceleration
questions.answer: Opposite its sliding relative to the floor
questions.explanation: Kinetic friction opposes the relative sliding at the contacting surfaces.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: The zero of gravitational potential energy is shifted while the physical motion stays the same. What remains unchanged?
options: Potential-energy differences
Every numerical potential-energy value
The object's mass becomes zero
The direction of gravity reverses
questions.answer: Potential-energy differences
questions.explanation: Changing the reference adds a constant without altering differences or predicted forces and motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two marks lie on the same rigid rotating disc at different distances from its axis. Which has greater linear speed?
options: The mark nearer the axis
Both always have identical linear speeds
Neither can move while the disc rotates
The mark farther from the axis
questions.answer: The mark farther from the axis
questions.explanation: All marks share angular speed, while tangential speed is angular speed multiplied by radius.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A mass is moved farther from a rotation axis. What happens to its contribution to rotational inertia?
options: It becomes negative
It increases
It decreases
It stays fixed because mass is fixed
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Contribution to rotational inertia grows with the square of perpendicular distance from the axis.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A wheel rolls without slipping on a stationary surface. What is the instantaneous velocity of its contact point relative to the surface?
options: Zero
Twice the centre's speed forward
Equal to the centre's speed forward
Equal to the centre's speed backward
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Translation and rotation cancel at the contact point during ideal rolling without slipping.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two small-angle pendulums have equal lengths but different bob masses. How do their ideal periods compare?
options: The lighter bob always has a longer period
The period is proportional to bob mass
They are equal
The heavier bob always has a longer period
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: For small oscillations in the same gravitational field, the ideal pendulum period depends on length, not mass.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A fully submerged rigid object is moved deeper into a uniform-density incompressible liquid. How does its buoyant force change in the usual model?
options: It reverses direction
It stays the same
It grows in proportion to depth
It becomes zero below the surface
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: Buoyant force depends on the displaced volume and fluid density, which remain unchanged here.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A mass on an ideal Hooke's-law spring is released from a greater displacement without changing mass or spring constant. What happens to its period?
options: It doubles whenever amplitude doubles
It falls to zero
It is determined only by the new maximum speed
It stays unchanged
questions.answer: It stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The ideal mass-spring period depends on mass and stiffness, not amplitude within the linear regime.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A velocity-time graph crosses from positive to negative values. What occurs at the crossing?
options: Its distance travelled returns to zero
Its mass changes sign
The object reverses direction
Its acceleration must be zero
questions.answer: The object reverses direction
questions.explanation: The velocity changes sign, indicating reversal; acceleration is determined by the graph's slope.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two balls are launched horizontally from the same height with different speeds. Ignoring air resistance, which lands first?
options: They land together
The faster ball
The slower ball
The heavier ball regardless of speed
questions.answer: They land together
questions.explanation: Their initial vertical velocities and vertical accelerations are identical.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two touching blocks accelerate together on a smooth floor when one is pushed. Why are their net forces unequal if their masses differ?
options: Contact forces violate Newton's third law
The lighter block has no net force
Their velocities must be different
They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
questions.answer: They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives different net forces for different masses at the same acceleration.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A ball moves upward after being thrown, ignoring air resistance. Which description is correct?
options: Gravity does positive work during ascent
Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
Both energies increase
Mechanical energy decreases because speed decreases
questions.answer: Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
questions.explanation: Gravity converts kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy while total mechanical energy stays constant.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A skater pulls in their arms while experiencing negligible external torque. Why do they spin faster?
options: Their moment of inertia decreases while angular momentum stays constant
Their angular momentum increases spontaneously
Their mass decreases
Their rotational kinetic energy must remain constant
questions.answer: Their moment of inertia decreases while angular momentum stays constant
questions.explanation: Conservation of angular momentum links smaller moment of inertia to greater angular speed.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two satellites have circular orbits around Earth. Why is the lower satellite faster?
options: The higher satellite is beyond gravity
The lower satellite must have greater mass
A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
The lower satellite has no gravitational potential energy
questions.answer: A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
questions.explanation: For a circular orbit, speed is proportional to the inverse square root of orbital radius.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Steady incompressible flow enters a narrower section of a pipe. What happens to average flow speed?
options: It must become zero
It increases
It decreases
It stays constant while volume flow increases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Conservation of volume flow requires area times average speed to remain constant.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: An ideal spring oscillator's amplitude doubles while its mass and spring constant stay fixed. What happens to its period?
options: It doubles
It halves
It becomes four times larger
It stays the same
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: The ideal spring period depends on mass and stiffness, not amplitude.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A spring remains within its proportional range. Why does doubling its extension require more than twice the stored energy?
options: Extension is unrelated to work
The spring's mass must increase
The stretching force also grows during extension
The spring constant necessarily doubles
questions.answer: The stretching force also grows during extension
questions.explanation: Elastic energy is the area under the force-extension graph, so it grows with extension squared.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A box moves with an accelerating conveyor belt without slipping. What horizontal force can accelerate the box?
options: Static friction in the belt's acceleration direction
Kinetic friction necessarily opposite the belt's motion
Weight acting horizontally
No horizontal force because there is no slipping
questions.answer: Static friction in the belt's acceleration direction
questions.explanation: Static friction can act forward to prevent relative slip and accelerate an object with the surface.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two force-time pulses have equal signed areas but different peak heights. What do they produce on the same isolated object's momentum?
options: Equal peak accelerations necessarily
Different impulses because peaks differ
No momentum change unless the pulses are rectangular
Equal changes in momentum
questions.answer: Equal changes in momentum
questions.explanation: Impulse is the signed area under the force-time curve, regardless of the pulse's detailed shape.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A load is raised between the same two heights along two different frictionless paths. What is the gravitational work comparison?
options: It depends only on the time taken
It is the same on both paths
It is larger on the longer path
It is larger on the path with more turns
questions.answer: It is the same on both paths
questions.explanation: Gravity is conservative, so its work depends on the endpoints rather than the route.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two springs store equal elastic energy. One is stiffer. Which is stretched less from equilibrium?
options: The stiffer spring
The softer spring
Both must have equal extension
Neither can store energy without permanent damage
questions.answer: The stiffer spring
questions.explanation: Elastic energy is one half stiffness times extension squared, so greater stiffness needs less extension for equal energy.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Equal opposite parallel forces act on different lines of action on a rigid body. What can result?
options: A net force equal to either individual force
A torque only if the forces have different magnitudes
Zero net force but nonzero net torque
Zero net force and zero torque in every arrangement
questions.answer: Zero net force but nonzero net torque
questions.explanation: Separated equal opposite forces form a couple that can rotate without accelerating the centre of mass.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A spinning disc experiences a brief braking torque. What feature determines the change in angular momentum?
options: The total angle alone regardless of torque
Signed area under the torque-time graph
The disc's colour
Only the maximum angular speed before braking
questions.answer: Signed area under the torque-time graph
questions.explanation: Angular impulse is the integral of torque over time and equals angular momentum change.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two identical spring oscillators have the same amplitude but opposite displacements and opposite velocities at an instant. How do their total energies compare?
options: One must have negative energy
They differ because displacement signs differ
The oscillator moving right always has more energy
They are equal
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Energy depends on squared displacement and squared speed, so reversing both signs does not change it.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: The same small-angle pendulum operates where gravitational acceleration is smaller. Why does its period increase?
options: The bob's mass necessarily increases
Gravity no longer affects oscillation
The restoring acceleration for a given angle is weaker
The string becomes longer by definition
questions.answer: The restoring acceleration for a given angle is weaker
questions.explanation: A weaker restoring effect takes more time to complete an oscillation for unchanged pendulum length.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: An ideal hydraulic lift multiplies force at its larger piston. Why does this not multiply the input energy?
options: The larger piston moves through a smaller distance
The smaller piston experiences no force
Pressure produces energy from nothing
The output piston must move farther as well
questions.answer: The larger piston moves through a smaller distance
questions.explanation: Incompressible volume transfer trades distance for force, preserving work in the ideal system.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Steady ideal flow rises to a higher level with the same speed. What happens to its static pressure?
options: It increases
It is unchanged because speed matches
It must become atmospheric pressure
It decreases
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: At unchanged kinetic energy per unit volume, increased gravitational energy is balanced by lower pressure in Bernoulli's relation.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A student times one very short oscillation using a stopwatch with noticeable reaction delay. Why can timing many oscillations improve the period estimate?
options: It makes the reaction delay exactly zero
The start-stop timing uncertainty is spread over more cycles
It removes all systematic clock errors automatically
The true period changes after many oscillations
questions.answer: The start-stop timing uncertainty is spread over more cycles
questions.explanation: Measuring a longer total interval can reduce the fractional effect of approximately fixed start-stop timing uncertainty.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A ruler has a fixed positive zero error. Repeating a length measurement many times gives closely grouped results. What remains unresolved?
options: The systematic offset
Random scatter only
Whether the ruler has markings
The object's physical length changes
questions.answer: The systematic offset
questions.explanation: Repeated readings can improve precision without removing a fixed systematic error.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A person stands on a scale in a lift moving upward but slowing down. How does the reading compare with their weight?
options: It equals weight because motion is upward
It is zero in every slowing lift
It is smaller
It is larger
questions.answer: It is smaller
questions.explanation: Upward motion with decreasing speed means downward acceleration, so the normal force is below weight.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A rigid wheel rolls without slipping at constant speed on a level surface with no resistive losses or applied horizontal forces. What static friction is required?
options: A force that continually increases its speed
Zero
A force equal to its weight
The maximum possible static friction
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Static friction supplies only the force needed by the dynamics; ideal steady rolling needs none here.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A solid sphere and a hoop roll without slipping down the same incline from rest. Why does the sphere arrive first in the ideal model?
options: It experiences no gravitational force
Its centre of mass loses more height
The hoop must slide rather than roll
A smaller fraction of its energy goes into rotation
questions.answer: A smaller fraction of its energy goes into rotation
questions.explanation: The sphere has a smaller moment-of-inertia-to-mass-radius-squared ratio, giving greater translational acceleration.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A satellite is moved into a larger circular orbit. Which combination describes its new state?
options: Lower speed and lower total mechanical energy
Unchanged speed and unchanged total mechanical energy
Lower speed and greater total mechanical energy
Higher speed and greater total mechanical energy
questions.answer: Lower speed and greater total mechanical energy
questions.explanation: Larger circular orbits have lower orbital speed but less negative total mechanical energy.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: In ideal spring motion, when is acceleration magnitude greatest while kinetic energy is least?
options: At either extreme displacement
At equilibrium only
Halfway in time between equilibrium and an extreme always
At every position equally
questions.answer: At either extreme displacement
questions.explanation: Restoring acceleration is proportional to displacement, while speed is zero at the extremes.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A pendulum bob is at the bottom of its swing. Which comparison is correct?
options: Tension equals weight because the path is momentarily horizontal
Tension is less than weight
Tension is zero because tangential acceleration is zero
Tension exceeds weight
questions.answer: Tension exceeds weight
questions.explanation: The inward centripetal acceleration requires an upward resultant, so tension must exceed weight.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two wheels have equal mass and radius, but one places more mass near its rim. Equal constant torques act from rest. Which wheel gains angular speed more slowly?
options: Neither can accelerate without a changing torque
The wheel with more mass near the rim
The wheel with more mass near its axis
Both must accelerate equally because their masses match
questions.answer: The wheel with more mass near the rim
questions.explanation: Mass farther from the axis increases moment of inertia, reducing angular acceleration for a given torque.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A car turns at constant speed on a level circular track. Why can it accelerate while its kinetic energy stays constant?
options: Acceleration changes velocity direction while the resultant is perpendicular to motion
Acceleration always requires increasing speed
Kinetic energy depends on velocity direction alone
The net force is zero because speed is constant
questions.answer: Acceleration changes velocity direction while the resultant is perpendicular to motion
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector, so direction change is acceleration; perpendicular force does no work on the car's translational motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A stationary isolated object separates into two pieces. One piece has twice the mass of the other. How do their velocity vectors compare afterward?
options: The heavier piece has twice the speed in the opposite direction
Only the lighter piece can move
They are opposite, and the heavier piece has half the speed
They are equal and point in the same direction
questions.answer: They are opposite, and the heavier piece has half the speed
questions.explanation: Zero initial momentum requires equal opposite final momenta, so speed is inversely related to mass for the two pieces.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A light and a heavy cart collide. Why can their acceleration magnitudes differ despite equal contact force magnitudes?
options: Equal forces require equal changes in velocity regardless of mass
Acceleration also depends on mass
Newton's third law fails during short collisions
The light cart's force is actually always larger
questions.answer: Acceleration also depends on mass
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives different accelerations when equal force magnitudes act on unequal masses.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A stationary box is accelerated by a moving belt without relative slipping. Can static friction do positive work on the box in the ground frame?
options: No, because static friction always does zero work in every frame
No, because the box has zero acceleration when it does not slip
Yes, only if the coefficient of friction is negative
Yes, because the box's contact region moves forward while friction acts forward
questions.answer: Yes, because the box's contact region moves forward while friction acts forward
questions.explanation: No relative slip does not mean zero ground-frame displacement; static friction can transfer energy from the driven belt to the box.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: Two identical hanging masses systems differ only because one pulley has appreciable rotational inertia. With unequal hanging masses and no axle loss, why is acceleration smaller there?
options: The pulley must dissipate all energy as heat
The string tensions must remain equal on both sides of the massive pulley
Some driving torque accelerates the pulley's rotation
The masses' weights have become equal
questions.answer: Some driving torque accelerates the pulley's rotation
questions.explanation: Accelerating the pulley requires a net torque and rotational energy, reducing the masses' translational acceleration.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A skater reduces rotational inertia while conserving angular momentum. Why can rotational energy rise?
options: Internal work is done while pulling the body inward
Conservation of angular momentum requires conservation of rotational energy
The skater gains angular momentum from empty space
The final inertia must actually be larger
questions.answer: Internal work is done while pulling the body inward
questions.explanation: At fixed angular momentum, lower inertia corresponds to higher rotational energy, supplied through the skater's internal work.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A rigid object has zero net force but a nonzero net torque. What motion is possible from rest?
options: Pure translation with no rotation
Complete equilibrium
A change in mass without motion
Rotation with no initial acceleration of its centre of mass
questions.answer: Rotation with no initial acceleration of its centre of mass
questions.explanation: Zero resultant force fixes centre-of-mass acceleration, while nonzero torque can still produce angular acceleration.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
