questions.q: A mass is added to a vertical spring and allowed to settle, then undergoes small oscillations. Why does gravity shift equilibrium without appearing explicitly in the ideal period formula?
options: The spring stops storing potential energy
About the new equilibrium, net restoring force is still proportional to displacement with the same stiffness
Gravity becomes physically absent
The mass's weight changes sign during every oscillation
questions.answer: About the new equilibrium, net restoring force is still proportional to displacement with the same stiffness
questions.explanation: Gravity changes the equilibrium extension, while deviations around it obey the same linear restoring-force law.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A small-angle pendulum's length is increased while local gravitational acceleration is increased by the same factor. What happens to its period?
options: It stays the same
It increases by that factor
It decreases by that factor
It depends only on bob mass now
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: The period depends on the square root of length divided by gravitational acceleration, so equal scaling leaves that ratio unchanged.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A floating ice block contains a dense object that sinks after the ice melts. Compared with its earlier contribution while floating, why does the object's water displacement then decrease?
options: Its mass disappears during melting
A denser object always displaces more water when submerged than when supported by floating ice
It displaces its volume rather than water of equal weight
A sinking object displaces no water at all
questions.answer: It displaces its volume rather than water of equal weight
questions.explanation: While floating with the ice, its added weight requires equal-weight water displacement; a denser-than-water object displaces less volume when submerged alone.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A pipe narrows sharply and significant viscous losses occur. Why may a simple lossless Bernoulli prediction be inaccurate?
options: Pressure can no longer exert forces
Mechanical energy is dissipated along the flow
Mass conservation must also fail
The liquid necessarily becomes compressible
questions.answer: Mechanical energy is dissipated along the flow
questions.explanation: Continuity can still hold while viscous dissipation requires an energy-loss term beyond the ideal Bernoulli model.

questions.subject: AP Physics 1
questions.q: A particle rests where the force is zero. Why is this insufficient to establish stable equilibrium?
options: Zero force always means a minimum
Stable equilibrium requires nonzero constant force
Potential energy cannot describe equilibrium
The point could be a potential-energy maximum rather than a minimum
questions.answer: The point could be a potential-energy maximum rather than a minimum
questions.explanation: Both maxima and minima can have zero gradient, but nearby forces restore toward a minimum and drive away from a maximum.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A metal lid loosens when warmed more than the jar neck. Which change helps?
options: Its mass decreases
Its thickness becomes zero
Its atoms become smaller
Its opening expands
questions.answer: Its opening expands
questions.explanation: Thermal expansion increases the dimensions of the lid, including its opening.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Gas expands and pushes a piston. What energy transfer occurs through the moving piston?
options: No energy crosses the boundary
The gas does work on its surroundings
The surroundings always do positive work on the gas
The gas necessarily gains internal energy
questions.answer: The gas does work on its surroundings
questions.explanation: An outward force acting through the piston's displacement transfers energy as work.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: An ideal gas is heated in a rigid sealed container. Why does pressure rise?
options: Molecules transfer more momentum to the walls per unit time
The molecules become larger
More molecules are created
The container's volume must increase
questions.answer: Molecules transfer more momentum to the walls per unit time
questions.explanation: Higher temperature increases average molecular kinetic energy and wall momentum transfer.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Sound enters a medium where its speed is greater. Its source is unchanged. What happens to wavelength?
options: It becomes zero
It stays fixed because frequency changes
It increases
It decreases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: The source fixes frequency, and wavelength equals wave speed divided by frequency.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Two initially neutral objects become oppositely charged by rubbing. What was transferred between them?
options: Gravitational mass
Electrons
Protons between nuclei
Whole positive nuclei only
questions.answer: Electrons
questions.explanation: Charge separation in ordinary rubbing results from electron transfer.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A capacitor is connected to a fixed-voltage supply. What happens to stored charge if capacitance increases?
options: It decreases
It remains fixed
It becomes negative regardless of polarity
It increases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: The relation Q = CV gives more stored charge at the same potential difference.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: One branch of two resistors in parallel is removed from an ideal battery. What happens to current in the remaining branch?
options: It falls to zero
It reverses direction
It stays the same
It doubles automatically
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: The remaining branch still has the same battery voltage across the same resistance.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A charged particle moves exactly parallel to a uniform magnetic field. What magnetic force acts on it?
options: Zero
A force along its velocity
A force against its velocity
The maximum possible sideways force
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Magnetic force has magnitude qvB sin(theta), which vanishes for parallel motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A magnet is held stationary inside a stationary coil. What induced emf results from this unchanged arrangement?
options: A steady emf set only by magnet strength
An emf that grows with time
An emf that alternates automatically
Zero
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Induction requires changing magnetic flux, not merely the presence of a magnetic field.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A converging lens forms an image of a very distant object. Where is the image approximately formed?
options: On the object's side as a virtual image
At the focal plane
At twice the focal length always
At the lens centre
questions.answer: At the focal plane
questions.explanation: Nearly parallel incident rays converge near the principal focal plane.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Two coherent light waves meet with crest aligned to crest. What happens locally?
options: Their amplitudes reinforce
Their frequencies cancel
Their speeds double
Their wavelengths halve
questions.answer: Their amplitudes reinforce
questions.explanation: The displacements add constructively when the waves are in phase.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A radioactive sample contains fewer undecayed nuclei after one half-life. What happens to its activity?
options: It stays fixed until the last nucleus decays
It becomes independent of the number of nuclei
It decreases
It increases
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Activity is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei for a fixed decay constant.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A star's thermal spectrum peaks at a shorter wavelength than another star's. What can be inferred about its surface temperature?
options: Its temperature cannot affect the spectrum
It is hotter
It is cooler
It must have the same temperature
questions.answer: It is hotter
questions.explanation: Wien's displacement relation associates shorter peak wavelengths with higher absolute temperatures.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Two samples of the same isotope contain different numbers of undecayed nuclei. Which has greater expected activity?
options: The sample with fewer undecayed nuclei
Both must have identical activity
The sample in the darker container
The sample with more undecayed nuclei
questions.answer: The sample with more undecayed nuclei
questions.explanation: For one isotope, activity is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A radio wave and visible light travel through a vacuum. Which comparison is correct?
options: The radio wave is faster because its wavelength is longer
Visible light is faster because photons have more energy
Equal speeds but different frequencies
Equal frequencies but different speeds
questions.answer: Equal speeds but different frequencies
questions.explanation: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same vacuum speed; wavelength and frequency vary inversely.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A string supports a standing wave. Why does a node remain still?
options: The opposing waves cancel displacement there at all times
No waves reach that position
The string is cut at every node
The wave frequency becomes zero there
questions.answer: The opposing waves cancel displacement there at all times
questions.explanation: At a node, equal opposing displacements cancel continuously even though waves travel through the string.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Ice melts while its temperature remains steady. Where does the supplied energy principally go?
options: Into increasing average molecular kinetic energy only
Into increasing the mass of every molecule
Into reducing the amount of energy in the sample
Into changing the intermolecular arrangement
questions.answer: Into changing the intermolecular arrangement
questions.explanation: During a phase change, supplied energy changes the arrangement and potential energy without a temperature rise.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field parallel to the field. What magnetic deflection occurs?
options: An immediate reversal along its path
None
A circle perpendicular to the field
A steadily increasing sideways acceleration
questions.answer: None
questions.explanation: The magnetic force depends on the velocity component perpendicular to the field, which is zero here.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Field lines are closer together in region A than region B on the same consistently drawn diagram. What does this indicate?
options: A stronger field in A
A higher charge on every particle in A
A lower force per unit charge in A
A necessarily higher potential in A
questions.answer: A stronger field in A
questions.explanation: Line density represents field magnitude; potential also depends on reference and position along the field.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Light crosses from air into glass. Why can its wavelength change while frequency stays the same?
options: The source oscillation rate changes when the light arrives
The glass creates a new source with arbitrary timing
Its propagation speed changes at the boundary
Each photon splits into two lower-frequency photons
questions.answer: Its propagation speed changes at the boundary
questions.explanation: The boundary preserves wave frequency, while changed speed changes wavelength through the wave relation.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A vacuum flask reduces heat transfer through its evacuated gap. Which process can still cross that gap?
options: Bulk flow of liquid
Thermal radiation
Conduction through air
Convection of trapped gas
questions.answer: Thermal radiation
questions.explanation: Radiation does not require matter, whereas gas conduction and convection are suppressed by the vacuum.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Two ideal gases have the same temperature but different molecular masses. What is equal?
options: Their root-mean-square speeds
Their momentum per molecule
Their molecular masses
Their mean translational kinetic energy
questions.answer: Their mean translational kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Mean translational kinetic energy depends only on absolute temperature; lighter molecules move faster on average.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in its second harmonic. What appears in addition to the end nodes?
options: No internal nodes
A travelling crest fixed at one end
A node at its midpoint
An antinode at its midpoint
questions.answer: A node at its midpoint
questions.explanation: The second harmonic contains two loops separated by a central node.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A charge moves along an equipotential surface. What work does the electric field do?
options: Zero
Positive for every charge
Negative for every charge
Work equal to charge times field strength
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Electric work depends on the potential difference, which is zero along an equipotential.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: An isolated conductor reaches electrostatic equilibrium. Why is its interior electric field zero?
options: The conductor contains no electrons
The conductor's potential must be zero
All external electric fields disappear everywhere
Free charges redistribute until the internal field cancels
questions.answer: Free charges redistribute until the internal field cancels
questions.explanation: A nonzero internal field would keep free charges moving, contradicting electrostatic equilibrium.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A real battery supplies a larger current. Why can its terminal voltage fall?
options: The battery's internal current becomes zero
More voltage is lost across its internal resistance
Its emf must instantly become zero
External resistance creates charge
questions.answer: More voltage is lost across its internal resistance
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage during discharge equals emf minus the internal voltage drop.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: At a junction, one entering current becomes two outgoing currents. Why must their sum equal the entering current in steady state?
options: Charge does not accumulate at the junction
Energy is created at the junction
Resistance is always equal in both branches
Both outgoing currents must be equal
questions.answer: Charge does not accumulate at the junction
questions.explanation: Current conservation follows from charge conservation when there is no accumulating charge.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A magnet approaching a conducting loop experiences resistance to its motion. What explains this?
options: The loop always attracts every magnetic pole
Induced current cancels the magnet's mass
The induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux
The loop creates energy from nothing
questions.answer: The induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux
questions.explanation: Lenz's law makes the induced effect oppose the flux change, requiring mechanical work.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Light in glass strikes a glass-air boundary above the critical angle. What occurs?
options: It is completely absorbed at the surface
It is totally internally reflected
It refracts along the normal
Its frequency doubles
questions.answer: It is totally internally reflected
questions.explanation: Above the critical angle, no propagating refracted ray enters the lower-index medium in the ideal model.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: In a double-slit experiment, the screen moves farther away while wavelength and slit spacing stay fixed. What happens to fringe spacing?
options: It decreases
It stays fixed
All bright fringes vanish
It increases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Fringe spacing is proportional to the screen distance under the small-angle approximation.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: An excited atom emits a higher-frequency photon than another transition in the same atom. What follows?
options: The electron's charge is larger
The atom's proton number changes
The energy-level gap is larger
The atom loses less energy
questions.answer: The energy-level gap is larger
questions.explanation: Photon energy equals the transition energy and is proportional to frequency.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A charged capacitor discharges through a larger resistance than before, with capacitance unchanged. What happens to the discharge timescale?
options: It becomes longer
It becomes shorter
It stays fixed because initial charge is unchanged
It becomes independent of capacitance
questions.answer: It becomes longer
questions.explanation: The time constant is the product of resistance and capacitance, so larger resistance slows discharge.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Most alpha particles cross a thin foil almost undeflected, but a few turn sharply. Which combined inference fits both observations?
options: Positive charge is spread uniformly through solid atoms
All atomic mass lies in orbiting electrons
Alpha particles cannot interact electrically
Atoms are mostly empty space with concentrated positive charge
questions.answer: Atoms are mostly empty space with concentrated positive charge
questions.explanation: Rare large deflections imply a small dense charged region, while frequent passage implies mostly empty volume.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A reaction produces less total rest mass but more kinetic energy, with all products counted. Which conclusion is justified?
options: All lost mass must become electric charge
Rest energy has been converted while total energy is conserved
Energy conservation has failed
Mass loss requires total momentum to increase
questions.answer: Rest energy has been converted while total energy is conserved
questions.explanation: Rest mass is one form of energy; kinetic energy can increase as rest energy decreases without changing total energy.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Electrons accelerated through a greater potential difference produce a narrower diffraction pattern for the same crystal. Which explanation fits?
options: Their momentum rises and wavelength falls
Their charge decreases and wavelength rises
Their speed falls and wavelength rises
The crystal spacing must increase
questions.answer: Their momentum rises and wavelength falls
questions.explanation: Higher kinetic energy gives higher momentum and therefore a shorter de Broglie wavelength, reducing diffraction angles.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A concave mirror forms a real image of a distant object. What changes if the mirror is replaced by a convex one in the same arrangement?
options: Reflection stops occurring
The focal length of every mirror becomes zero
The image becomes virtual and reduced
The convex mirror forms a larger real image on a screen
questions.answer: The image becomes virtual and reduced
questions.explanation: A convex mirror diverges reflected rays, forming an upright reduced virtual image behind the mirror.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: An initially uncharged capacitor is connected to an ideal battery through a resistor. Why does charging current decline with time?
options: Charge disappears as soon as it enters the capacitor
The rising capacitor voltage leaves less voltage across the resistor
The battery's voltage must decrease to zero
The resistor must acquire infinite resistance
questions.answer: The rising capacitor voltage leaves less voltage across the resistor
questions.explanation: The battery voltage is shared; as capacitor voltage rises, resistor voltage and hence current fall.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A stationary loop experiences an increasing magnetic flux. Why can an emf arise even though the loop does not move?
options: Only moving wires can ever have induced emf
The loop's resistance becomes negative
Magnetic flux itself is the same quantity as electric charge
Changing magnetic flux produces a circulating electric field
questions.answer: Changing magnetic flux produces a circulating electric field
questions.explanation: Faraday's law permits induction from a time-varying field as well as motion of conductors.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A thin transparent film shows changing colours as its thickness changes. What is the main wave explanation?
options: Light frequency changes solely because the film is thicker
All wavelengths are always reinforced equally
The relative phase of reflected waves changes with optical path length
The film creates new chemical elements at each thickness
questions.answer: The relative phase of reflected waves changes with optical path length
questions.explanation: Different optical path differences alter which wavelengths interfere constructively or destructively, including reflection phase effects.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: An ideal thermal emitter is heated. Which combination is expected?
options: Greater total emitted power per area and a shorter peak wavelength
Lower emitted power per area and a shorter peak wavelength
Greater emitted power per area and an unchanged peak wavelength
Only a change in visible colour with no change in total radiation
questions.answer: Greater total emitted power per area and a shorter peak wavelength
questions.explanation: Stefan-Boltzmann and Wien relations predict increased emission and a shift toward shorter peak wavelengths with higher temperature.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A metal plate with a circular hole is heated uniformly. Which prediction is consistent with uniform expansion?
options: The hole shrinks because metal expands inward only
The hole area stays fixed
The hole closes if the plate is thick
The hole enlarges as though the missing metal also expanded
questions.answer: The hole enlarges as though the missing metal also expanded
questions.explanation: All linear dimensions scale upward under unconstrained uniform expansion, including the hole diameter.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Two reservoirs remain at different fixed temperatures. Why can an engine between them not convert all absorbed heat into work in a cycle?
options: The hot reservoir must have zero internal energy
Some heat must be rejected to satisfy the second law
Energy conservation alone requires all heat to be wasted
A gas cannot return to its initial state
questions.answer: Some heat must be rejected to satisfy the second law
questions.explanation: A cyclic engine cannot take heat from a single reservoir and convert it entirely to work; heat rejection is required.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A driven oscillator has modest damping. Increasing damping near resonance most directly does what to its response curve?
options: Lowers and broadens the resonance peak
Raises and narrows the resonance peak
Removes all forcing frequencies
Makes amplitude independent of the drive
questions.answer: Lowers and broadens the resonance peak
questions.explanation: Damping dissipates energy, reducing resonant amplitude and making the response less sharply selective.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: At the midpoint between equal positive charges, electric field is zero. What about electric potential, taking zero at infinity?
options: It is negative
It is undefined because fields cancel
It is positive
It is zero because field is zero
questions.answer: It is positive
questions.explanation: Vector fields cancel at the midpoint, but the two positive scalar potentials add.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A dielectric is inserted fully into a capacitor while its battery remains connected. Which combination follows?
options: Both charge and capacitance remain fixed
Charge increases while voltage stays fixed
Charge stays fixed while voltage decreases
Charge decreases while voltage stays fixed
questions.answer: Charge increases while voltage stays fixed
questions.explanation: The dielectric raises capacitance, and the battery maintains voltage by supplying additional charge.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A loop rotates in a uniform magnetic field at constant angular speed. At maximum flux, what is its instantaneous induced emf?
options: Maximum magnitude
Equal to the flux
Infinite
Zero
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Emf depends on the rate of change of flux, which is zero at a smooth flux maximum.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A telescope's aperture is increased with the wavelength unchanged. Why can it resolve closer angular details?
options: The stars move farther apart
The focal length must become zero
The diffraction pattern becomes narrower
The incoming wavelength increases
questions.answer: The diffraction pattern becomes narrower
questions.explanation: A larger aperture reduces the diffraction-limited angular spread.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A positive charge is released from rest where electric potential decreases toward the right. What initially happens?
options: It accelerates right and electric potential energy decreases
It accelerates left and electric potential energy decreases
It stays still because potential is a scalar
It accelerates right and potential energy increases
questions.answer: It accelerates right and electric potential energy decreases
questions.explanation: Electric field points toward decreasing potential, and a positive charge lowers its potential energy as it accelerates that way.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A charged parallel-plate capacitor is isolated, then a dielectric is inserted. Which pair decreases?
options: Charge and capacitance
Capacitance and voltage
Charge and stored electrical energy
Voltage and stored electrical energy
questions.answer: Voltage and stored electrical energy
questions.explanation: With charge fixed, increased capacitance lowers both Q/C and Q squared divided by twice the capacitance.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A glass converging lens is immersed in a liquid whose refractive index is closer to that of glass than air's is. What happens to its converging power?
options: It becomes infinite
It decreases
It increases
It is fixed by shape alone
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Reduced relative refractive index weakens refraction at the lens surfaces.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A proton and an alpha particle enter the same uniform magnetic field perpendicularly with equal speeds. Which has the larger circular radius?
options: The alpha particle
The proton
Their radii are equal
Neither follows a curved path
questions.answer: The alpha particle
questions.explanation: Radius is proportional to mass divided by charge at fixed speed and field; an alpha particle has about twice the proton's mass-to-charge ratio.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: An electron and a proton have equal nonrelativistic kinetic energies. Which has the longer de Broglie wavelength?
options: They have equal wavelengths
Wavelength depends only on charge
The electron
The proton
questions.answer: The electron
questions.explanation: At fixed kinetic energy, the lighter particle has smaller momentum and therefore larger wavelength.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Both fusion of suitable light nuclei and fission of suitable heavy nuclei can release energy. What common comparison explains this?
options: Products must have larger individual mass numbers in both cases
Products have greater binding energy per nucleon overall
Both processes always increase total rest mass
Both processes convert every proton into a neutron
questions.answer: Products have greater binding energy per nucleon overall
questions.explanation: Moving toward more tightly bound products lowers total rest energy; the difference can appear as released energy.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A fixed resistor is above a thermistor in a potential divider, and the output is measured across the thermistor. Its resistance falls on warming. What happens to output voltage?
options: It rises because total current rises
It stays fixed because supply voltage is fixed
It reverses sign because resistance falls
It falls because the thermistor receives a smaller voltage fraction
questions.answer: It falls because the thermistor receives a smaller voltage fraction
questions.explanation: The output fraction is the thermistor resistance divided by total resistance; that fraction falls as the thermistor resistance falls.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Two independent lamps have the same average wavelength but no stable relative phase. Why is a steady two-source interference pattern not usually seen?
options: The waves cannot superpose
Light from each lamp has zero amplitude
Rapid phase variation averages the fringes away
Equal wavelengths prevent interference
questions.answer: Rapid phase variation averages the fringes away
questions.explanation: A stable visible fringe pattern needs a sustained phase relationship; randomly changing phase moves fringes during observation.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A charge follows a closed path in a static electric field and returns to its starting point. Why is the net electric work zero?
options: The field is conservative and the potential-energy change is zero
The electric force must vanish along the whole path
Every segment has zero potential difference
The charge loses its electric charge during the trip
questions.answer: The field is conservative and the potential-energy change is zero
questions.explanation: A static electrostatic field does path-independent work, so a closed trip has no net change in potential energy.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: Current through an inductor starts increasing. What direction of induced emf is consistent with energy storage in its field?
options: It always reinforces any current change
It is unrelated to the rate of current change
It must point in the current direction for both increase and decrease
It opposes the increase in current
questions.answer: It opposes the increase in current
questions.explanation: Self-induced emf opposes changes in current, while supplied work can be stored in the magnetic field.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: An ideal gas reaches the same final temperature by two different paths. Why can work differ while internal-energy change agrees?
options: The first law applies only to straight paths
Internal energy is a state function, but work depends on the path
Both work and internal energy depend only on elapsed time
Equal final temperature guarantees equal work in all cases
questions.answer: Internal energy is a state function, but work depends on the path
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas internal energy depends on temperature; the pressure-volume path determines work.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A refrigerator cools its interior while warming the room. Why does the cooled region's entropy decrease not alone violate the second law?
options: Entropy increases elsewhere can exceed that local decrease
The second law forbids considering the room
Electric work automatically destroys total entropy
Every part of a system must increase temperature simultaneously
questions.answer: Entropy increases elsewhere can exceed that local decrease
questions.explanation: The second law constrains total entropy change for the appropriate overall system, allowing local decreases with compensating increases.

questions.subject: AP Physics 2
questions.q: A photon transfers momentum to an electron during scattering. Why does this not require the photon to have nonzero rest mass?
options: Scattering destroys conservation of momentum
Every scattered photon becomes an electron
A photon can carry energy and momentum with zero rest mass
Momentum is defined only for massive objects
questions.answer: A photon can carry energy and momentum with zero rest mass
questions.explanation: Relativistic energy-momentum relations permit massless photons to carry momentum, which is exchanged in interactions.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.topic: Mechanics: Motion in a straight line
questions.q: A trolley moves forward while its velocity-time graph slopes downward. What is happening?
options: Its distance travelled is decreasing
It is slowing down
It is moving backward
Its acceleration is zero
questions.answer: It is slowing down
questions.explanation: A downward slope means negative acceleration; with positive velocity this reduces speed.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A passenger leans forward when a bus brakes. Why?
options: A forward force from gravity appears
The seat increases the passenger's speed
The passenger loses mass
The passenger's body tends to keep moving
questions.answer: The passenger's body tends to keep moving
questions.explanation: Inertia resists the change from the body's original forward motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A box remains stationary while you push it gently on a rough floor. What balances your push?
options: The box's weight alone
An upward force from the floor
Static friction
Kinetic friction
questions.answer: Static friction
questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to oppose the push until its limiting value is reached.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two carts initially at rest push apart on a frictionless track. What must their momenta do?
options: Add to zero
Have equal velocities
Point in the same direction
Increase the total momentum
questions.answer: Add to zero
questions.explanation: With no external horizontal force, total momentum remains its initial value of zero.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A stone moves at constant speed in a circle. Why is it accelerating?
options: Its mass changes continuously
Its speed must be increasing
Its kinetic energy must increase
Its velocity changes direction
questions.answer: Its velocity changes direction
questions.explanation: Velocity includes direction, which changes throughout circular motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two identical springs support equal loads, one singly and two in parallel. Which arrangement stretches less?
options: Neither arrangement can stretch
The parallel pair
The single spring
Both stretch equally
questions.answer: The parallel pair
questions.explanation: The parallel springs share the load, increasing the effective stiffness.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A runner completes one lap and returns to the starting point. How do distance and displacement compare?
options: Distance is positive and displacement is zero
Both are zero
Both equal the track circumference as vectors
Displacement is positive and distance is zero
questions.answer: Distance is positive and displacement is zero
questions.explanation: Distance counts the path travelled, while displacement compares final and initial positions.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two students on low-friction carts push apart. For the combined student-cart system, how are the push forces classified?
options: Forces supplied only by gravity
Forces acting on neither member
Internal forces
An unbalanced external force pair
questions.answer: Internal forces
questions.explanation: Both interacting objects are included in the chosen system, so their mutual push forces are internal.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A book rests on a table. Which two forces on the book balance vertically?
options: The book's weight and an extra upward gravity force
Its weight and the table's normal force
Its weight and its force on Earth
The table's weight and the book's force on the table
questions.answer: Its weight and the table's normal force
questions.explanation: The book has downward gravitational force and upward contact force from the table; balanced forces act on the same object.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two motors lift identical loads through the same height, but one finishes sooner. Which has greater average useful power?
options: The slower motor
Both necessarily have equal power
Neither performs work because the final speed can be zero
The faster motor
questions.answer: The faster motor
questions.explanation: Equal useful work completed in less time means greater average power.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: The zero of gravitational potential energy is shifted while the physical motion stays the same. What remains unchanged?
options: The object's mass becomes zero
The direction of gravity reverses
Potential-energy differences
Every numerical potential-energy value
questions.answer: Potential-energy differences
questions.explanation: Changing the reference adds a constant without altering differences or predicted forces and motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A mass is moved farther from a rotation axis. What happens to its contribution to rotational inertia?
options: It increases
It decreases
It stays fixed because mass is fixed
It becomes negative
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Contribution to rotational inertia grows with the square of perpendicular distance from the axis.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two initially neutral objects become oppositely charged by rubbing. What was transferred between them?
options: Protons between nuclei
Whole positive nuclei only
Gravitational mass
Electrons
questions.answer: Electrons
questions.explanation: Charge separation in ordinary rubbing results from electron transfer.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A capacitor is connected to a fixed-voltage supply. What happens to stored charge if capacitance increases?
options: It becomes negative regardless of polarity
It increases
It decreases
It remains fixed
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: The relation Q = CV gives more stored charge at the same potential difference.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: One branch of two resistors in parallel is removed from an ideal battery. What happens to current in the remaining branch?
options: It stays the same
It doubles automatically
It falls to zero
It reverses direction
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: The remaining branch still has the same battery voltage across the same resistance.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A charged particle moves exactly parallel to a uniform magnetic field. What magnetic force acts on it?
options: A force against its velocity
The maximum possible sideways force
Zero
A force along its velocity
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Magnetic force has magnitude qvB sin(theta), which vanishes for parallel motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A magnet is held stationary inside a stationary coil. What induced emf results from this unchanged arrangement?
options: An emf that alternates automatically
Zero
A steady emf set only by magnet strength
An emf that grows with time
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Induction requires changing magnetic flux, not merely the presence of a magnetic field.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Field lines are closer together in region A than region B on the same consistently drawn diagram. What does this indicate?
options: A higher charge on every particle in A
A lower force per unit charge in A
A necessarily higher potential in A
A stronger field in A
questions.answer: A stronger field in A
questions.explanation: Line density represents field magnitude; potential also depends on reference and position along the field.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.topic: Electricity & Magnetism: Potential difference and energy
questions.q: A charge moves between two points with zero potential difference. What is the change in its electric potential energy?
options: Necessarily negative
Equal to its charge alone
Zero
Necessarily positive
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Electric potential-energy change equals charge multiplied by potential difference.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A steady current reaches a junction and divides into two branches. How do branch currents compare with the incoming current?
options: Their sum equals it
Each must equal the full incoming current
Their difference always equals it
Both must be zero at a junction
questions.answer: Their sum equals it
questions.explanation: Steady charge conservation prevents net charge accumulation at the junction.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A velocity-time graph crosses from positive to negative values. What occurs at the crossing?
options: Its acceleration must be zero
Its distance travelled returns to zero
Its mass changes sign
The object reverses direction
questions.answer: The object reverses direction
questions.explanation: The velocity changes sign, indicating reversal; acceleration is determined by the graph's slope.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two balls are launched horizontally from the same height with different speeds. Ignoring air resistance, which lands first?
options: The heavier ball regardless of speed
They land together
The faster ball
The slower ball
questions.answer: They land together
questions.explanation: Their initial vertical velocities and vertical accelerations are identical.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two touching blocks accelerate together on a smooth floor when one is pushed. Why are their net forces unequal if their masses differ?
options: They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
Contact forces violate Newton's third law
The lighter block has no net force
Their velocities must be different
questions.answer: They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives different net forces for different masses at the same acceleration.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A ball moves upward after being thrown, ignoring air resistance. Which description is correct?
options: Mechanical energy decreases because speed decreases
Gravity does positive work during ascent
Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
Both energies increase
questions.answer: Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
questions.explanation: Gravity converts kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy while total mechanical energy stays constant.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A skater pulls in their arms while experiencing negligible external torque. Why do they spin faster?
options: Their rotational kinetic energy must remain constant
Their moment of inertia decreases while angular momentum stays constant
Their angular momentum increases spontaneously
Their mass decreases
questions.answer: Their moment of inertia decreases while angular momentum stays constant
questions.explanation: Conservation of angular momentum links smaller moment of inertia to greater angular speed.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two satellites have circular orbits around Earth. Why is the lower satellite faster?
options: The lower satellite has no gravitational potential energy
The higher satellite is beyond gravity
The lower satellite must have greater mass
A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
questions.answer: A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
questions.explanation: For a circular orbit, speed is proportional to the inverse square root of orbital radius.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: An object's velocity is negative but its velocity-time graph slopes upward. What is happening to its speed?
options: It must be zero throughout the interval
It cannot have positive acceleration
It is decreasing while velocity remains negative
It is increasing because the slope is positive
questions.answer: It is decreasing while velocity remains negative
questions.explanation: Acceleration toward positive velocity reduces the magnitude of a still-negative velocity.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two force-time pulses have equal signed areas but different peak heights. What do they produce on the same isolated object's momentum?
options: Equal changes in momentum
Equal peak accelerations necessarily
Different impulses because peaks differ
No momentum change unless the pulses are rectangular
questions.answer: Equal changes in momentum
questions.explanation: Impulse is the signed area under the force-time curve, regardless of the pulse's detailed shape.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: The same positive net work is done on two equal-mass carts initially at rest. What final comparison follows?
options: Their final momenta must point in the same direction
The cart with a longer path must be faster
The faster-applied work produces more kinetic energy
Their final speeds are equal
questions.answer: Their final speeds are equal
questions.explanation: Equal net work gives equal final kinetic energy; equal masses then have equal speed magnitudes.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two springs store equal elastic energy. One is stiffer. Which is stretched less from equilibrium?
options: Neither can store energy without permanent damage
The stiffer spring
The softer spring
Both must have equal extension
questions.answer: The stiffer spring
questions.explanation: Elastic energy is one half stiffness times extension squared, so greater stiffness needs less extension for equal energy.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A rigid disc starts from rest with a constant nonzero net torque and fixed inertia. How does angular speed change?
options: At a constant rate
It remains zero
It jumps immediately to a fixed maximum
It increases only if inertia increases
questions.answer: At a constant rate
questions.explanation: Constant net torque and inertia give constant angular acceleration.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A spinning disc experiences a brief braking torque. What feature determines the change in angular momentum?
options: Only the maximum angular speed before braking
The total angle alone regardless of torque
Signed area under the torque-time graph
The disc's colour
questions.answer: Signed area under the torque-time graph
questions.explanation: Angular impulse is the integral of torque over time and equals angular momentum change.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A charge moves along an equipotential surface. What work does the electric field do?
options: Work equal to charge times field strength
Zero
Positive for every charge
Negative for every charge
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Electric work depends on the potential difference, which is zero along an equipotential.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A charged capacitor is disconnected from its battery and its plate separation increases. What happens to its voltage?
options: It decreases
It remains fixed by the disconnected battery
It must reverse polarity
It increases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Charge remains fixed while capacitance falls, so V = Q/C increases.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A real battery supplies a larger current. Why can its terminal voltage fall?
options: External resistance creates charge
The battery's internal current becomes zero
More voltage is lost across its internal resistance
Its emf must instantly become zero
questions.answer: More voltage is lost across its internal resistance
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage during discharge equals emf minus the internal voltage drop.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A particle enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity. Why can its path curve without its speed changing?
options: The magnetic force remains perpendicular to its velocity
The force increases its kinetic energy continuously
The magnetic field reduces its mass
Its acceleration is zero
questions.answer: The magnetic force remains perpendicular to its velocity
questions.explanation: A perpendicular force changes direction but does no work on the particle.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A magnet approaching a conducting loop experiences resistance to its motion. What explains this?
options: The loop creates energy from nothing
The loop always attracts every magnetic pole
Induced current cancels the magnet's mass
The induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux
questions.answer: The induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux
questions.explanation: Lenz's law makes the induced effect oppose the flux change, requiring mechanical work.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: An initially uncharged capacitor is connected to an ideal battery through a resistor. Why does charging current decline with time?
options: Charge disappears as soon as it enters the capacitor
The rising capacitor voltage leaves less voltage across the resistor
The battery's voltage must decrease to zero
The resistor must acquire infinite resistance
questions.answer: The rising capacitor voltage leaves less voltage across the resistor
questions.explanation: The battery voltage is shared; as capacitor voltage rises, resistor voltage and hence current fall.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A new resistor branch is added across an ideal constant-voltage supply. What happens to the current through an existing unchanged branch?
options: It stays the same
It falls because all branches must share a fixed total current
It becomes zero
It doubles regardless of the new resistance
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: Each parallel branch remains across the same supply voltage, so its own unchanged resistance carries the same current.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.topic: Electricity & Magnetism: Induced field from changing flux
questions.q: A stationary loop experiences an increasing magnetic flux. Why can an emf arise even though the loop does not move?
options: The loop's resistance becomes negative
Magnetic flux itself is the same quantity as electric charge
Changing magnetic flux produces a circulating electric field
Only moving wires can ever have induced emf
questions.answer: Changing magnetic flux produces a circulating electric field
questions.explanation: Faraday's law permits induction from a time-varying field as well as motion of conductors.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A ruler has a fixed positive zero error. Repeating a length measurement many times gives closely grouped results. What remains unresolved?
options: The object's physical length changes
The systematic offset
Random scatter only
Whether the ruler has markings
questions.answer: The systematic offset
questions.explanation: Repeated readings can improve precision without removing a fixed systematic error.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A person stands on a scale in a lift moving upward but slowing down. How does the reading compare with their weight?
options: It is larger
It equals weight because motion is upward
It is zero in every slowing lift
It is smaller
questions.answer: It is smaller
questions.explanation: Upward motion with decreasing speed means downward acceleration, so the normal force is below weight.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A rigid wheel rolls without slipping at constant speed on a level surface with no resistive losses or applied horizontal forces. What static friction is required?
options: The maximum possible static friction
A force that continually increases its speed
Zero
A force equal to its weight
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Static friction supplies only the force needed by the dynamics; ideal steady rolling needs none here.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A solid sphere and a hoop roll without slipping down the same incline from rest. Why does the sphere arrive first in the ideal model?
options: A smaller fraction of its energy goes into rotation
It experiences no gravitational force
Its centre of mass loses more height
The hoop must slide rather than roll
questions.answer: A smaller fraction of its energy goes into rotation
questions.explanation: The sphere has a smaller moment-of-inertia-to-mass-radius-squared ratio, giving greater translational acceleration.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A satellite is moved into a larger circular orbit. Which combination describes its new state?
options: Higher speed and greater total mechanical energy
Lower speed and lower total mechanical energy
Unchanged speed and unchanged total mechanical energy
Lower speed and greater total mechanical energy
questions.answer: Lower speed and greater total mechanical energy
questions.explanation: Larger circular orbits have lower orbital speed but less negative total mechanical energy.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A pendulum bob is at the bottom of its swing. Which comparison is correct?
options: Tension is zero because tangential acceleration is zero
Tension exceeds weight
Tension equals weight because the path is momentarily horizontal
Tension is less than weight
questions.answer: Tension exceeds weight
questions.explanation: The inward centripetal acceleration requires an upward resultant, so tension must exceed weight.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A car turns at constant speed on a level circular track. Why can it accelerate while its kinetic energy stays constant?
options: Acceleration changes velocity direction while the resultant is perpendicular to motion
Acceleration always requires increasing speed
Kinetic energy depends on velocity direction alone
The net force is zero because speed is constant
questions.answer: Acceleration changes velocity direction while the resultant is perpendicular to motion
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector, so direction change is acceleration; perpendicular force does no work on the car's translational motion.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A stationary isolated object separates into two pieces. One piece has twice the mass of the other. How do their velocity vectors compare afterward?
options: The heavier piece has twice the speed in the opposite direction
Only the lighter piece can move
They are opposite, and the heavier piece has half the speed
They are equal and point in the same direction
questions.answer: They are opposite, and the heavier piece has half the speed
questions.explanation: Zero initial momentum requires equal opposite final momenta, so speed is inversely related to mass for the two pieces.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A light and a heavy cart collide. Why can their acceleration magnitudes differ despite equal contact force magnitudes?
options: Equal forces require equal changes in velocity regardless of mass
Acceleration also depends on mass
Newton's third law fails during short collisions
The light cart's force is actually always larger
questions.answer: Acceleration also depends on mass
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives different accelerations when equal force magnitudes act on unequal masses.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two identical hanging masses systems differ only because one pulley has appreciable rotational inertia. With unequal hanging masses and no axle loss, why is acceleration smaller there?
options: The masses' weights have become equal
The pulley must dissipate all energy as heat
The string tensions must remain equal on both sides of the massive pulley
Some driving torque accelerates the pulley's rotation
questions.answer: Some driving torque accelerates the pulley's rotation
questions.explanation: Accelerating the pulley requires a net torque and rotational energy, reducing the masses' translational acceleration.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A moving puck strikes and sticks to the edge of a freely rotating disc on a frictionless fixed axle. About the axle, which quantity can be conserved during the impact?
options: The puck's linear momentum alone
The disc's angular speed
Angular momentum
Rotational kinetic energy necessarily
questions.answer: Angular momentum
questions.explanation: If the axle exerts no torque about itself, angular momentum is conserved even though sticking dissipates kinetic energy.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A rigid object has zero net force but a nonzero net torque. What motion is possible from rest?
options: Rotation with no initial acceleration of its centre of mass
Pure translation with no rotation
Complete equilibrium
A change in mass without motion
questions.answer: Rotation with no initial acceleration of its centre of mass
questions.explanation: Zero resultant force fixes centre-of-mass acceleration, while nonzero torque can still produce angular acceleration.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: At the midpoint between equal positive charges, electric field is zero. What about electric potential, taking zero at infinity?
options: It is zero because field is zero
It is negative
It is undefined because fields cancel
It is positive
questions.answer: It is positive
questions.explanation: Vector fields cancel at the midpoint, but the two positive scalar potentials add.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A dielectric is inserted fully into a capacitor while its battery remains connected. Which combination follows?
options: Both charge and capacitance remain fixed
Charge increases while voltage stays fixed
Charge stays fixed while voltage decreases
Charge decreases while voltage stays fixed
questions.answer: Charge increases while voltage stays fixed
questions.explanation: The dielectric raises capacitance, and the battery maintains voltage by supplying additional charge.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: Two identical resistors are first in series and then in parallel across the same ideal voltage source. Which arrangement uses greater total power?
options: Parallel
Series
Both use equal power
Neither can dissipate power
questions.answer: Parallel
questions.explanation: Parallel connection has lower equivalent resistance, so total power V squared divided by resistance is greater.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A positive charge is released from rest where electric potential decreases toward the right. What initially happens?
options: It stays still because potential is a scalar
It accelerates right and potential energy increases
It accelerates right and electric potential energy decreases
It accelerates left and electric potential energy decreases
questions.answer: It accelerates right and electric potential energy decreases
questions.explanation: Electric field points toward decreasing potential, and a positive charge lowers its potential energy as it accelerates that way.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A charged parallel-plate capacitor is isolated, then a dielectric is inserted. Which pair decreases?
options: Charge and stored electrical energy
Voltage and stored electrical energy
Charge and capacitance
Capacitance and voltage
questions.answer: Voltage and stored electrical energy
questions.explanation: With charge fixed, increased capacitance lowers both Q/C and Q squared divided by twice the capacitance.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.q: A fixed resistor is above a thermistor in a potential divider, and the output is measured across the thermistor. Its resistance falls on warming. What happens to output voltage?
options: It rises because total current rises
It stays fixed because supply voltage is fixed
It reverses sign because resistance falls
It falls because the thermistor receives a smaller voltage fraction
questions.answer: It falls because the thermistor receives a smaller voltage fraction
questions.explanation: The output fraction is the thermistor resistance divided by total resistance; that fraction falls as the thermistor resistance falls.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.topic: Electricity & Magnetism: Electrostatic work around a loop
questions.q: A charge follows a closed path in a static electric field and returns to its starting point. Why is the net electric work zero?
options: Every segment has zero potential difference
The charge loses its electric charge during the trip
The field is conservative and the potential-energy change is zero
The electric force must vanish along the whole path
questions.answer: The field is conservative and the potential-energy change is zero
questions.explanation: A static electrostatic field does path-independent work, so a closed trip has no net change in potential energy.

questions.subject: AP Physics C
questions.topic: Electricity & Magnetism: Flux versus field strength
questions.q: A closed conducting loop translates entirely within a large uniform steady magnetic field without changing area or orientation. Why is there no net induced emf around it?
options: The magnetic flux through it remains constant
Magnetic field is absent inside any moving loop
A conductor cannot move through magnetic fields
A uniform field must have zero magnitude
questions.answer: The magnetic flux through it remains constant
questions.explanation: Faraday's law concerns changing flux; uniform translation with unchanged geometry leaves the loop's flux constant.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A function's output increases by 12 while its input increases by 4. What is its average rate of change over that interval?
options: 1/3 output unit per input unit
3 output units per input unit
48 output units per input unit
8 output units per input unit
questions.answer: 3 output units per input unit
questions.explanation: Average rate compares the change in output with the corresponding change in input.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A polynomial's leading term is -x⁴. What happens at both far ends of its graph?
options: Both ends rise
The left falls and the right rises
The left rises and the right falls
Both ends fall
questions.answer: Both ends fall
questions.explanation: An even power is positive at both large positive and large negative inputs; the negative coefficient reverses the sign.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: Near x=2, f(x)=(x-2)² is nonnegative on both sides. How does its graph meet the x-axis?
options: It has a vertical asymptote
It has no point at x=2
It touches without crossing
It crosses from negative to positive
questions.answer: It touches without crossing
questions.explanation: The squared factor preserves the sign on either side of its zero.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: Why is x=5 excluded from the domain of 1/(x-5)?
options: It makes the denominator zero
It makes the numerator negative
It makes the function value zero
Every positive input is excluded
questions.answer: It makes the denominator zero
questions.explanation: Division by zero is undefined, so that input cannot be used.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: The expression (x²-1)/(x-1) simplifies to x+1 for x≠1. What remains true of the original function?
options: It has value 2 at every input
Its domain becomes all real numbers automatically
It has a zero at x=1
It is undefined at x=1
questions.answer: It is undefined at x=1
questions.explanation: Algebraic cancellation does not restore a point excluded by the original denominator.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A model uses t for hours since an event began. Why might negative t be excluded in that application?
options: A model's domain must be all real numbers
It lies outside the model's stated time context
No algebraic function can accept negative numbers
Every negative time gives a negative output
questions.answer: It lies outside the model's stated time context
questions.explanation: A contextual domain can be narrower than the expression's algebraic domain.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A quantity triples over each equal time interval. Which type of model fits this pattern?
options: Exponential
Linear with constant positive slope
Constant
Quadratic with constant second differences
questions.answer: Exponential
questions.explanation: A fixed multiplicative change over equal intervals is exponential.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: The statement log base 2 of 8 equals 3 expresses which relationship?
options: 2 times 3=8
questions.explanation: A logarithm identifies the exponent needed to produce a number from its base.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: For real-valued log(x-4), what inputs are allowed?
options: All real x
questions.explanation: A real logarithm requires a strictly positive argument.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A temperature conversion is one-to-one. What should applying its inverse after the conversion do?
options: Double the converted temperature
Always produce zero
Repeat the same conversion
Recover the original temperature
questions.answer: Recover the original temperature
questions.explanation: An inverse undoes the original mapping on its appropriate domain.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A quantity is multiplied by 0.8 each hour. What happens to its absolute hourly loss as the quantity shrinks?
options: The loss becomes larger
The quantity becomes negative after five hours
The loss becomes smaller
The loss stays constant
questions.answer: The loss becomes smaller
questions.explanation: The same fractional loss acts on a progressively smaller amount.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: What does replacing a positive exponent n by -n do to b^n, for b>0?
options: Takes its reciprocal
Changes its sign
Subtracts n from b
Makes it zero
questions.answer: Takes its reciprocal
questions.explanation: The exponent rule gives b^(-n)=1/b^n.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A model repeats the same complete pattern every 6 hours. What does a period of 6 describe?
options: The maximum output
The vertical distance from minimum to maximum
The initial output
The horizontal length of one cycle
questions.answer: The horizontal length of one cycle
questions.explanation: Period measures the input interval over which a full pattern repeats.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A sine model is shifted upward by 5 without other changes. What stays unchanged?
options: Its minimum value
Its amplitude and period
Its midline
Its maximum value
questions.answer: Its amplitude and period
questions.explanation: A vertical translation moves all values together without changing the cycle's size or duration.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: The model sin(2x) is compared with sin(x). What happens to the period?
options: It halves
It doubles
It stays the same
It becomes zero
questions.answer: It halves
questions.explanation: The doubled input completes the sine cycle in half the horizontal interval.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: Why is the domain of sine restricted when defining its inverse as a function?
options: Every input must be positive
An inverse requires a constant function
Sine must become one-to-one on the chosen interval
Sine has no real outputs otherwise
questions.answer: Sine must become one-to-one on the chosen interval
questions.explanation: A one-to-one restriction ensures each output identifies only one selected input.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: Why is tan θ undefined when cos θ=0?
options: Sine and cosine are identical there
Its expression sin θ/cos θ has a zero denominator
Its numerator is always zero there
Angles cannot exceed a right angle
questions.answer: Its expression sin θ/cos θ has a zero denominator
questions.explanation: The quotient defining tangent cannot divide by zero.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: What does the polar equation r=3 represent?
options: A line with slope 3
A circle of diameter 3 centred at (3,0)
A point 3 units above the origin
A circle of radius 3 centred at the origin
questions.answer: A circle of radius 3 centred at the origin
questions.explanation: Every angle is allowed while distance from the origin remains 3.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.topic: Unit 4 optional, not AP-exam assessed: parametric functions
questions.q: A path is given by x(t)=t and y(t)=2t. What does eliminating t show?
options: The path is a circle
The path is independent of x
The path lies on y=2x
The path lies on x=2y
questions.answer: The path lies on y=2x
questions.explanation: Substituting t=x into y=2t gives the relation between the coordinates.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.topic: Unit 4 optional, not AP-exam assessed: matrix transformations
questions.q: A matrix reflects points across the x-axis. What does applying that same reflection twice do?
options: Returns every point to its original position
Rotates every point by a right angle
Doubles every distance
Reflects every point across the y-axis
questions.answer: Returns every point to its original position
questions.explanation: The first reflection changes the sign of the y-coordinate, and the second restores it.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A rational function has numerator degree 1 and denominator degree 3. What happens to its value as x grows positively without bound?
options: It grows without bound necessarily
It approaches the ratio of the constant terms
It approaches 1 necessarily
It approaches zero
questions.answer: It approaches zero
questions.explanation: The higher-degree denominator dominates the numerator for large inputs.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A real-coefficient quadratic has one nonreal zero. What can be concluded about the other?
options: It can be any unrelated complex number
It is the conjugate of the first
It must be a positive real number
It must equal zero
questions.answer: It is the conjugate of the first
questions.explanation: A degree-two real polynomial must pair its nonreal zeros as conjugates.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: For equally spaced inputs, observed first differences increase by a fixed nonzero amount. Which simple polynomial model is suggested?
options: Quadratic
Linear
Constant
No polynomial can fit such a pattern
questions.answer: Quadratic
questions.explanation: Constant nonzero second differences suggest quadratic change; finite observations alone do not prove a unique global model.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A rational graph crosses its horizontal asymptote at a finite input. Is that possible?
options: Only if the graph is discontinuous at the crossing
Only when the asymptote is vertical
Yes; the asymptote describes end behaviour
No; no asymptote can ever be crossed
questions.answer: Yes; the asymptote describes end behaviour
questions.explanation: A horizontal asymptote constrains behaviour at large inputs, not every finite point.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: In g(x)=f(2x), why do the graph's horizontal features occur at half their original x-coordinates?
options: The graph moves two units upward
The input to f reaches each old value twice as quickly
Every output is halved
Every output is doubled
questions.answer: The input to f reaches each old value twice as quickly
questions.explanation: Input scaling changes where a given original input is reached.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A fitted model has residuals that follow a clear curved pattern. What does this suggest?
options: The fit must be perfect
The data must have no measurement variation
Every model would have the same pattern
The model may miss a systematic feature of the relationship
questions.answer: The model may miss a systematic feature of the relationship
questions.explanation: Systematic residual structure indicates that the model has not captured all relevant shape in the data.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: For x>0 and c>0, how does ln(cx) compare with ln(x)?
options: It equals ln(x)+c
It equals ln(x/c)
It differs by the constant ln(c)
It equals c ln(x)
questions.answer: It differs by the constant ln(c)
questions.explanation: The product rule for logarithms turns positive input multiplication into an additive constant.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A price receives a fixed discount and then a percentage tax. Why can reversing the order change the result?
options: The percentage would apply to a different base amount
Addition and multiplication always commute in a sequence
The tax rate must change when the order changes
A fixed discount is always a percentage
questions.answer: The percentage would apply to a different base amount
questions.explanation: Subtracting a fixed amount before multiplication differs from subtracting it afterward.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A point (2,7) lies on a one-to-one function's graph. Which point lies on the inverse graph?
questions.explanation: Inversion exchanges input and output coordinates.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: An exponential quantity doubles every hour. What is its multiplicative factor over half an hour?
options: The positive square root of 2
questions.answer: The positive square root of 2
questions.explanation: Two identical half-hour factors must multiply to the hourly factor 2.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: Why cannot base 1 define an ordinary logarithmic inverse?
options: 1 raised to any exponent is always 1 and is not one-to-one
Base 1 produces only negative outputs
Its powers alternate in sign
A logarithm's base must exceed 10
questions.answer: 1 raised to any exponent is always 1 and is not one-to-one
questions.explanation: A constant exponential mapping cannot be inverted to identify a unique exponent.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A model is A times b^(t+2), with A,b>0. How can the time shift be represented as an output factor?
options: Replace b by b+2
Replace t by 2t
Replace A by A times b²
Replace A by A+2
questions.answer: Replace A by A times b²
questions.explanation: The exponent rule separates b^(t+2) into b^t times b².

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A measured periodic quantity has maximum 14 and minimum 6. What is its midline?
questions.explanation: The midline is halfway between the maximum and minimum values.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: Why can sin x=1/2 have several solutions on a sufficiently long interval?
options: Sine is one-to-one on the whole real line
Each output has only one possible angle
Only negative angles can repeat
Sine repeats and can take the same value at different positions within a cycle
questions.answer: Sine repeats and can take the same value at different positions within a cycle
questions.explanation: Both symmetry within a cycle and periodic repetition create multiple solutions.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: Two unit-circle points reflect across the vertical axis. Which trigonometric coordinate do they share?
options: Their tangent value in every case
Their angle measure
Their sine value
Their cosine value in every case
questions.answer: Their sine value
questions.explanation: Vertical-axis reflection preserves the vertical coordinate while reversing the horizontal coordinate.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: At angles where cosine is close to zero but nonzero, what can happen to secant?
options: Its magnitude becomes large
Its magnitude must approach zero
It always equals cosine
It becomes exactly 1
questions.answer: Its magnitude becomes large
questions.explanation: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine, so small nonzero cosine magnitudes produce large secant magnitudes.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: Which polar pair represents the same point as (r,θ)?
options: (r,θ+π) in every case
(-r,θ) in every case
(2r,θ/2) in every case
questions.explanation: A half-turn in angle and a reversal of radial direction cancel each other.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A sinusoidal model fits a short interval of seasonal observations. What should be checked before extrapolating many cycles?
options: Whether the model's coefficients are integers
Whether period, amplitude and underlying conditions remain reasonably stable
Whether the first fit used a calculator
Whether every observation equals the midline
questions.answer: Whether period, amplitude and underlying conditions remain reasonably stable
questions.explanation: Long-range use depends on the continued suitability of the periodic assumptions.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.topic: Unit 4 optional, not AP-exam assessed: parametrised circles
questions.q: Replacing t by -t in (cos t,sin t) does what to a full-circle traversal?
options: Reverses direction while preserving the circle
Doubles the radius
Changes the circle into a line
Moves its centre upward
questions.answer: Reverses direction while preserving the circle
questions.explanation: The same set of circle points is traversed in the opposite angular direction.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.topic: Unit 4 optional, not AP-exam assessed: singular transformations
questions.q: A plane transformation collapses every point onto a line. Why can it not have an inverse on the entire plane?
options: The line has infinite length
The transformation is not representable by a matrix
Different inputs can have the same output
Every output has a negative coordinate
questions.answer: Different inputs can have the same output
questions.explanation: Loss of one-to-one information prevents recovery of every original point.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.topic: Unit 1: finite data and global claims
questions.q: Several polynomials agree at every input in a finite dataset. What is needed to justify selecting one for prediction?
options: Ignoring the intended prediction range
Assumptions, context and validation beyond agreement at those points
Only choosing the highest degree
Assuming finite agreement proves global equality
questions.answer: Assumptions, context and validation beyond agreement at those points
questions.explanation: Finite data may support multiple models, so selection needs more than interpolation alone.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A real-coefficient cubic has a nonreal conjugate pair of zeros. What can be concluded about its remaining zero?
options: It is a third unpaired nonreal zero
It must equal zero
It must equal the real part of the pair
It is real
questions.answer: It is real
questions.explanation: A remaining nonreal zero would require another conjugate, exceeding the cubic's degree.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A polynomial graph has four distinct turning points. What minimum degree is possible?
questions.explanation: A degree-n polynomial has at most n-1 turning points, so four require degree at least five.

questions.subject: AP Precalculus
questions.q: A denominator vanishes at a, but the numerator also vanishes there. What must be checked before declaring a vertical asymptote?
options: The factors' multiplicities after cancellation
Only whether a is positive
Only the constant terms
Whether the graph has any horizontal asymptote
questions.answer: The factors' multiplicities after cancellation
