questions.explanation: Consumption need not all follow the desired pathway; side reactions can lower isolated yield.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: First ionisation energy of boron is lower than beryllium's despite higher nuclear charge. Why?
options: Boron has fewer protons
Beryllium's outer shell is farther from the nucleus
Boron loses an inner 1s electron first
Boron loses a higher-energy 2p electron
questions.answer: Boron loses a higher-energy 2p electron
questions.explanation: Beryllium's filled 2s subshell is relatively stable, while boron's first removed electron is in 2p.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two resonance structures of an ion place charge on different atoms. What is the actual ion best described as?
options: A mixture of different compounds
An ion whose atoms exchange positions
One delocalised structure
A rapid physical oscillation between complete drawings
questions.answer: One delocalised structure
questions.explanation: Resonance drawings represent contributors to one electronic structure; atoms do not switch places.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A process has positive enthalpy change and positive entropy change. Under what condition can it be spontaneous?
options: At sufficiently high temperature
Only at absolute zero
At no temperature
At all temperatures necessarily
questions.answer: At sufficiently high temperature
questions.explanation: In Gibbs energy, the favourable T delta-S term can exceed the positive enthalpy change at high temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A reversible reaction equation is multiplied by two. How does its equilibrium constant change?
options: It doubles
It halves
It stays unchanged
It is squared
questions.answer: It is squared
questions.explanation: Multiplying all stoichiometric coefficients doubles the exponents in the equilibrium expression.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An inert gas is added to a reacting ideal-gas mixture at constant volume and temperature. What happens to equilibrium composition?
options: All reactants are consumed
It is unchanged
It always shifts toward fewer gas molecules
It always shifts toward more gas molecules
questions.answer: It is unchanged
questions.explanation: Reactant and product partial pressures stay unchanged at fixed volume and temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two buffers have the same acid-to-base ratio but different total concentrations. What differs most directly?
options: The more concentrated buffer resists added acid or base better
Only the dilute buffer has a definable pH
The concentrated buffer must have a radically different initial pH
Both can absorb unlimited acid
questions.answer: The more concentrated buffer resists added acid or base better
questions.explanation: Similar ratios give similar pH, but more buffer components provide greater capacity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two metal ions are present, and one reaches its precipitation threshold at a lower added anion concentration. What can careful addition achieve?
options: A change in both metals' atomic numbers
Removal of all anions without solids
Precipitation of one ion before the other
Equal precipitation of both at every concentration
questions.answer: Precipitation of one ion before the other
questions.explanation: Different solubility equilibria can allow selective precipitation before the second salt becomes saturated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A cell reaction has positive standard cell potential. What follows about standard Gibbs-energy change?
options: It is independent of electron transfer
It is negative
It is positive
It must be zero
questions.answer: It is negative
questions.explanation: The relation delta-G-standard = -nFE-standard gives a negative Gibbs-energy change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aqueous salt electrolysis is compared with molten-salt electrolysis. Why may the cathode products differ?
options: Ions have no charge in water
Molten salts contain no cations
Electrode reactions never depend on the medium
Water can compete for reduction in the aqueous cell
questions.answer: Water can compete for reduction in the aqueous cell
questions.explanation: Aqueous solutions introduce water as a possible reactant, changing which reduction occurs.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two proposed isomers have the same formula. One predicts fewer distinct proton environments through symmetry. How can NMR help choose between them?
options: Count each hydrogen as a separate signal automatically
Ignore symmetry because all protons have identical shifts
Compare the observed number and pattern of signals with each prediction
Select the isomer with the larger molecular mass
questions.answer: Compare the observed number and pattern of signals with each prediction
questions.explanation: Structural symmetry can make hydrogens equivalent; their predicted signal patterns can distinguish isomers of equal mass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An observed rate law differs from the coefficients in the overall balanced equation. What is the best inference?
options: The overall equation need not represent one elementary step
The equation violates conservation of mass
The measured concentrations must be zero
All reactions have zero order
questions.answer: The overall equation need not represent one elementary step
questions.explanation: Overall stoichiometry does not determine rate-law exponents unless it describes an appropriate elementary step.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reactant starts at two different concentrations under identical conditions. How do its half-lives compare?
options: The more concentrated sample has twice the half-life
The less concentrated sample has twice the half-life
Half-life cannot be defined for a chemical reaction
They are equal
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: A first-order half-life depends on the rate constant, not the initial concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A square-planar complex has two identical ligands adjacent in one form and opposite in another. What differs?
options: Its empirical formula necessarily
Its spatial arrangement despite the same connectivity to the metal
Its metal's atomic number
Its total number of ligands
questions.answer: Its spatial arrangement despite the same connectivity to the metal
questions.explanation: Cis and trans arrangements are geometrical isomers of the same coordination composition.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A molecule has one tetrahedral carbon bonded to four different groups. What is possible?
options: A pair of nonsuperimposable mirror-image forms
Only one spatial arrangement under all conditions
A required carbon-carbon triple bond
A mandatory ionic lattice
questions.answer: A pair of nonsuperimposable mirror-image forms
questions.explanation: A tetrahedral stereogenic centre can give two enantiomeric arrangements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aniline is brominated readily compared with benzene under comparable conditions. Why?
options: Aniline is a saturated hydrocarbon
The benzene ring in aniline has no resonance
The amino group donates electron density into the ring
Nitrogen removes every pi electron
questions.answer: The amino group donates electron density into the ring
questions.explanation: The amino group's resonance donation activates the ring toward electrophilic substitution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A tertiary haloalkane reacts by an SN1 pathway in a suitable polar protic solvent. What most directly favours its first step?
options: Formation of a carbon atom with five permanent bonds
Stabilisation of the tertiary carbocation
Unhindered backside attack at the tertiary carbon
A required free radical
questions.answer: Stabilisation of the tertiary carbocation
questions.explanation: SN1 ionisation is favoured when the resulting carbocation is relatively stabilised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aniline is less basic than a comparable aliphatic amine in the usual aqueous comparison. Why?
options: Its nitrogen has no lone pair
All aromatic compounds are strong acids
Its nitrogen nucleus has fewer protons
Its nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the aromatic ring
questions.answer: Its nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the aromatic ring
questions.explanation: Delocalisation reduces the lone pair's availability for bonding to a proton.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A catalyst is added to a system already at equilibrium. Which combined statement is correct?
options: The equilibrium constant increases while temperature stays fixed
The reverse reaction stops
Both reaction rates increase but equilibrium composition is unchanged
Only the forward rate increases and yield rises
questions.answer: Both reaction rates increase but equilibrium composition is unchanged
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds both directions and does not change the equilibrium constant or equilibrium composition.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two polymers have similar repeating units, but one is extensively cross-linked. Why is it less able to soften and flow on heating below decomposition?
options: Links restrict movement of chains relative to one another
Cross-links remove all intermolecular forces
Its chains become shorter whenever temperature rises
Every cross-link melts independently like a small molecule
questions.answer: Links restrict movement of chains relative to one another
questions.explanation: A covalent network constrains chain motion, giving behaviour different from freely sliding linear chains.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A program must read marks, calculate averages and print reports. Why split these into separate tasks?
options: Each part can be developed and checked more clearly
Splitting guarantees that no errors remain
Each task must run on a different computer
Separate tasks remove the need to pass data
questions.answer: Each part can be developed and checked more clearly
questions.explanation: Decomposition breaks a problem into manageable components with identifiable responsibilities.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A variable total is 5. The program assigns total=total+2. What value does total then hold?
questions.explanation: The right-hand expression uses the previous value before assigning the new result.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Entry is allowed only when a ticket is valid AND the visitor meets the age requirement. A valid ticket alone is presented. What must still be checked?
options: Whether the ticket has the larger numerical value
Whether the two conditions have identical names
Whether the age requirement is met
Whether at least one condition is false
questions.answer: Whether the age requirement is met
questions.explanation: AND requires both conditions to be true.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A program must inspect every item in a known list once. Which approach directly fits?
options: Sort the list without inspecting its values
Loop through the list's items
Inspect only its first item
Repeat until an unrelated password changes
questions.answer: Loop through the list's items
questions.explanation: Traversal applies the required operation to each element of the collection.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A postcode begins with zero and is not used in arithmetic. Why store it as text?
options: To preserve its characters, including the leading zero
To make numerical addition faster
To force every postcode to have the same value
To prevent all invalid input automatically
questions.answer: To preserve its characters, including the leading zero
questions.explanation: An identifier's character representation matters; numeric conversion can discard leading zeros.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: The same calculation is needed in five places. What is an advantage of placing it in a function?
options: The function makes every caller's input valid automatically
It must run five times faster
The function cannot return different results for different inputs
Its logic can be maintained in one place
questions.answer: Its logic can be maintained in one place
questions.explanation: A reusable function reduces duplicated logic and centralises changes.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A list uses indices starting at zero and contains five items. Which index identifies its last item?
questions.explanation: Five positions beginning at zero are numbered zero through four.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: An age field permits values from 16 to 20 inclusive. Which pair best tests its permitted endpoints?
options: 0 and 100
16 and 20
17 and 19
15 and 21
questions.answer: 16 and 20
questions.explanation: The boundary values of the allowed interval are 16 and 20; adjacent invalid values are also useful in additional tests.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Two students have the same name. Why use a unique student ID as the primary key?
options: The ID distinguishes their records reliably
The ID makes every name unique
The ID removes the need to store any other field
Names cannot be stored in a database
questions.answer: The ID distinguishes their records reliably
questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies a row even when descriptive attributes repeat.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A table contains many classes, but a report needs only class 12A. What should a query's WHERE condition do?
options: Rename every row as class 12A
Delete other classes from the stored table
Sort all names without filtering
Keep rows whose class equals 12A
questions.answer: Keep rows whose class equals 12A
questions.explanation: A WHERE condition selects qualifying rows for the result without itself deleting the others.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A report should show the highest marks first. Which ordering is appropriate?
options: Alphabetical order of student names
Insertion order regardless of marks
Descending order of marks
Ascending order of marks
questions.answer: Descending order of marks
questions.explanation: Descending numerical order places larger values before smaller ones.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: An enrolment row stores a course ID that refers to a course table. What does this link allow?
options: The course table to be replaced by one large text field
Related course details to be retrieved without repeating them in every enrolment
Every course to have only one student
The enrolment's student ID to become its course name
questions.answer: Related course details to be retrieved without repeating them in every enrolment
questions.explanation: A reference connects related records while allowing shared details to be maintained separately.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A message must reach a particular device on an IP network. Why does it need destination addressing information?
options: Network equipment uses it to direct the message toward the destination
It determines the font used in the message
It guarantees that the message contains no errors
It proves that the sender is trustworthy
questions.answer: Network equipment uses it to direct the message toward the destination
questions.explanation: Destination addresses support delivery; addressing alone does not establish integrity or trust.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A user types a website name instead of its IP address. What does name resolution help provide?
options: A guarantee that the site's claims are true
A copy of the user's password
Extra storage space on the user's device
The network address associated with the name
questions.answer: The network address associated with the name
questions.explanation: DNS resolves domain names to relevant network addressing information.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Two otherwise comparable links carry the same large file. Why can the higher-bandwidth link finish sooner?
options: It eliminates every propagation delay
It changes the file's meaning
It can transfer more data per unit time
It must reduce the number of bits in the file
questions.answer: It can transfer more data per unit time
questions.explanation: Higher available throughput can reduce transmission time for the same amount of data.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A message urgently asks a student to enter a password on an unfamiliar sign-in page. What is the sound response?
options: Forward the password in a reply instead
Verify the request through a trusted route before entering credentials
Trust it because the message is urgent
Use the same password but change its capitalisation
questions.answer: Verify the request through a trusted route before entering credentials
questions.explanation: Urgency and a sign-in request can be used to steal credentials; independent verification checks the destination and request.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A document exists only in working memory when power is lost. Why might unsaved changes disappear?
options: Working memory is volatile
The processor deletes all saved files when it stops
Secondary storage requires continuous power to retain every file
The keyboard stores the document permanently
questions.answer: Working memory is volatile
questions.explanation: Volatile memory does not retain its contents without power; saving to persistent storage protects the work.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A school must store names from several writing systems. Why use a suitable Unicode encoding?
options: It makes all characters occupy exactly one byte in every encoding
It translates every name into English
It encrypts the names automatically
It supports characters beyond a narrow single-language character set
questions.answer: It supports characters beyond a narrow single-language character set
questions.explanation: Unicode provides a broad character repertoire, while the chosen encoding determines how characters are represented as bytes.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: An archive must recover a program's original bytes exactly. Which compression property is essential?
options: A fixed reduction to half the size
Replacement of text with an approximate image
Lossless reconstruction
Removal of less noticeable instructions
questions.answer: Lossless reconstruction
questions.explanation: Program files generally require exact recovery; lossy changes can alter their behaviour or make them unusable.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Students should read a timetable but only staff should edit it. Which design fits?
options: Use a longer timetable title as the only protection
Give students read access and authorised staff edit access
Give every user full edit access
Hide the filename while allowing all writes
questions.answer: Give students read access and authorised staff edit access
questions.explanation: Permissions should match each role's required operations.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A program sums a list but starts its total at 1 instead of 0. What error results?
options: The final sum is one too high
The final sum is multiplied by one
Only the last item is counted
The result is correct whenever the list has more than one item
questions.answer: The final sum is one too high
questions.explanation: The initial value is included in the accumulation, creating a constant extra one.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A value must be at least 10 and at most 20. Why is x>=10 OR x<=20 an incorrect validation condition?
options: It rejects every real x
It accepts only 10 and 20
It checks exactly the same condition as AND
It accepts every real x rather than only the intended interval
questions.answer: It accepts every real x rather than only the intended interval
questions.explanation: For any real number, at least one of those two inequalities holds; the interval requires both.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A loop runs while count<10, but count never changes inside it. If count starts at 0, what is the main problem?
options: The condition becomes false automatically after one pass
The loop must skip its body
The loop does not reach a terminating condition
The loop necessarily executes exactly ten times
questions.answer: The loop does not reach a terminating condition
questions.explanation: Without a change to the controlling state or another exit, the true condition remains true.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A function displays a calculated value but returns no usable result. Why can a caller struggle to use that value in another calculation?
options: A displayed value is always converted into a database row
Displaying output is different from returning a value to the caller
Printed values automatically become the caller's variables
Functions cannot both display and return values
questions.answer: Displaying output is different from returning a value to the caller
questions.explanation: A return communicates data through the function interface; displaying it serves a different purpose.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: An unsorted list may contain a target anywhere. Why may a linear search need to inspect every item before reporting absence?
options: Any uninspected item could still be the target
Absence can be proved by checking only the middle item
The first nonmatching item proves absence
Unsorted lists cannot be searched at all
questions.answer: Any uninspected item could still be the target
questions.explanation: Without ordering information, unchecked positions cannot generally be ruled out.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A search should treat School and school as equivalent. What preparation helps?
options: Convert only one string to uppercase regardless of the other
Compare their first characters only
Compare their lengths as proof of equality
Apply the same case normalisation to both strings
questions.answer: Apply the same case normalisation to both strings
questions.explanation: A consistent normalisation removes the intended case distinction while retaining the rest of the text.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Two variables refer to the same mutable list. One variable is used to change an element. Why does the other show the change?
options: Assignment necessarily copied every element into a new list
The other variable has become a number
Both names refer to the same underlying object
Every list in the program shares all elements
questions.answer: Both names refer to the same underlying object
questions.explanation: Aliasing means different references can access one mutable collection.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A user enters letters where a number is required. Why catch the specific conversion error?
options: The handler makes all later calculations error-free
The program can explain the invalid input and request a correction
The handler converts every word into the intended number
Catching an error proves the original input was valid
questions.answer: The program can explain the invalid input and request a correction
questions.explanation: Handling the expected failure allows a controlled recovery rather than an abrupt termination.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A school wants the average mark for each class. What does grouping by class achieve?
options: A separate aggregate is computed for each class
The table becomes sorted by every student's mark automatically
Only one student from each class is retained in storage
Each student's mark becomes the whole-school average
questions.answer: A separate aggregate is computed for each class
questions.explanation: GROUP BY partitions rows into groups for aggregate calculations.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: In SQL, some email fields are NULL. Why can COUNT(email) be smaller than COUNT(*)?
options: COUNT(*) counts only rows with missing emails
COUNT(email) removes duplicates automatically
COUNT(*) counts columns rather than rows
COUNT(email) excludes NULL email values
questions.answer: COUNT(email) excludes NULL email values
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts rows, while counting an expression excludes rows where that expression is NULL.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: One course has several enrolments. Why can joining courses to enrolments return the course details several times?
options: Every join must return exactly one row per course
The database has physically duplicated the course table
The join produces one result row for each matching enrolment
The course's primary key has necessarily become invalid
questions.answer: The join produces one result row for each matching enrolment
questions.explanation: A one-to-many relationship can repeat parent details in a query result without duplicating the stored parent record.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A teacher's phone number is copied into every class record. What problem can arise when it changes?
options: Repeated storage guarantees consistent updates
Some copies may be updated while others remain stale
Every copy must change automatically without a relationship
The number can no longer be queried
questions.answer: Some copies may be updated while others remain stale
questions.explanation: Duplicated facts require coordinated changes; separating shared details helps maintain consistency.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Packets from one message arrive out of order. What information helps reconstruct their intended order?
options: Sequence information
Only the display colour of each packet
Only the message's total storage cost
The alphabetic order of router names
questions.answer: Sequence information
questions.explanation: A receiving protocol can use sequence information to place data in the intended order.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A link's bandwidth rises, but a small request still waits on a long round-trip delay. What distinction explains this?
options: Greater bandwidth guarantees zero latency
Latency is determined only by file size
Small messages require no network travel
Transfer capacity and travel delay are different properties
questions.answer: Transfer capacity and travel delay are different properties
questions.explanation: Higher bandwidth can speed bulk transmission while propagation and response delays remain.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Data are encrypted in transit to a correctly authenticated server. What does this primarily protect against?
options: All malicious actions by an authorised recipient
Every false claim on the website
An eavesdropper reading the transmitted content
Every mistake made by the receiving application
questions.answer: An eavesdropper reading the transmitted content
questions.explanation: Transport encryption protects data on the connection, not every aspect of endpoint behaviour or content quality.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Two computers on the same local network exchange a shared file successfully while the internet connection is down. Why is this possible?
options: The internet and the local network are necessarily the same connection
Local communication need not pass through the external internet link
Every local file transfer is stored on a public website
The computers must be using identical IP addresses
questions.answer: Local communication need not pass through the external internet link
questions.explanation: Devices can communicate within a functioning LAN independently of internet access.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: An unsigned fixed-width binary field gains one extra bit. How does the number of representable patterns change?
options: It doubles
It increases by one
It stays unchanged
It is squared
questions.answer: It doubles
questions.explanation: Each old pattern can be paired with either value of the extra bit.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Several applications appear to progress on a processor executing one instruction stream at a time. What can explain this?
options: Every application owns a separate physical processor necessarily
All instructions execute at the exact same instant
Task switching converts programs into permanent storage
The operating system switches execution between tasks
questions.answer: The operating system switches execution between tasks
questions.explanation: Scheduling can share processor time among tasks, producing concurrent progress without simultaneous execution of all instructions.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A program runs without crashing but applies a discount twice. Which response is most useful?
options: Reinstall the keyboard driver first
Treat every numerical output as valid
Trace the calculation and compare it with the intended rule
Assume success because there is no syntax error
questions.answer: Trace the calculation and compare it with the intended rule
questions.explanation: Logical mistakes can produce incorrect results even when code is syntactically valid and executes successfully.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A backup exists but has never been restored in a test. What remains unverified?
options: Whether storing a backup always eliminates all data loss
Whether the saved data can actually be recovered as needed
Whether the file has a name
Whether the original data once existed
questions.answer: Whether the saved data can actually be recovered as needed
questions.explanation: A restore test checks the usability and completeness of the recovery process.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A maximum-finding algorithm starts its current maximum at zero. Why does it fail on a nonempty list containing only negative numbers?
options: Zero can remain the result even though it is not in the list
Negative numbers cannot be compared
The largest negative number is always zero
Initialisation does not affect a maximum search
questions.answer: Zero can remain the result even though it is not in the list
questions.explanation: The initial candidate must be compatible with the input domain, for example the list's first element.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: Discount rules use an if-elif chain: spend>=100 gets 10%, then spend>=200 gets 20%. Why does spending 250 receive only 10%?
options: Both discounts are always added
The comparison 250>=200 is false
An elif branch always overrides the first branch
The first true branch prevents the later branch from being checked
questions.answer: The first true branch prevents the later branch from being checked
questions.explanation: An if-elif chain selects its first satisfied condition, so more restrictive thresholds should be considered appropriately.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: An algorithm compares every list item with every other list item. If list length doubles, how does the number of comparisons grow approximately?
options: By one extra comparison
It remains constant
By a factor of four
By a factor of two
questions.answer: By a factor of four
questions.explanation: A pairwise nested traversal has a comparison count proportional to the square of the number of items.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A loop removes matching items from a list while advancing to the next index. Why can it skip an item?
options: Every removal restarts the loop automatically
Removal shifts later items left while the index still advances
Removing an item makes all remaining values equal
Indices remain attached permanently to their original elements
questions.answer: Removal shifts later items left while the index still advances
questions.explanation: An item can shift into the just-processed index and then be bypassed by the next increment.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A list contains mutable inner lists. Copying only the outer list does not isolate all later edits. Why?
options: The two outer lists can still refer to the same inner lists
The outer lists must have the same identity
A copy operation always makes data immutable
Nested data cannot be copied by any method
questions.answer: The two outer lists can still refer to the same inner lists
questions.explanation: A shallow copy duplicates the outer collection but preserves references to its nested objects.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: With left-to-right short-circuit AND, why check index<len(items) before accessing items[index]?
options: The index is automatically changed to a valid value
AND evaluates both sides regardless of the first result
A length check proves every list element is numeric
A failed bounds check can prevent the unsafe access from being evaluated
questions.answer: A failed bounds check can prevent the unsafe access from being evaluated
questions.explanation: Short-circuiting skips the second operand when the first is false, provided lower bounds and other preconditions also hold.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A function's result depends on a hidden global value that another function changes. Why is testing harder?
options: Global state guarantees every test is independent
The return type must change on every call
The same explicit arguments may produce different results as hidden state changes
Functions with global values cannot execute
questions.answer: The same explicit arguments may produce different results as hidden state changes
questions.explanation: Hidden dependencies make behaviour depend on more than the arguments visible at the call site.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A sorting program passes tests containing only distinct positive values. What is still poorly checked?
options: Whether the program's title is unique
Its behaviour on duplicates, negative values and empty input
Whether positive numbers can be represented at all
Whether every programming language sorts identically
questions.answer: Its behaviour on duplicates, negative values and empty input
questions.explanation: Successful tests establish behaviour for tested conditions, leaving other relevant input classes unresolved.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A query must show only classes whose average mark exceeds 70. Why use a condition on the grouped result?
options: The criterion concerns a group aggregate rather than each original mark
Filtering individual marks above 70 gives the same class averages
Averages cannot appear in database queries
Grouping automatically discards every class below the threshold
questions.answer: The criterion concerns a group aggregate rather than each original mark
questions.explanation: Filtering rows before averaging changes the data used; aggregate conditions are applied after groups are formed.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: An SQL field is NULL. Why is comparing it with =NULL not the proper test for missingness?
options: NULL is always identical to the number zero
NULL is always identical to an empty string
An equality comparison converts every NULL to false data permanently
NULL represents an unknown value and needs an IS NULL test
questions.answer: NULL represents an unknown value and needs an IS NULL test
questions.explanation: Ordinary comparisons with NULL evaluate to unknown in SQL's three-valued logic; IS NULL explicitly tests missingness.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A table has two rows matching a key, and another has three rows with that key. How many pairings does an equality join produce for that key?
options: Three
One
Six
Five
questions.answer: Six
questions.explanation: Each of the two rows pairs with each of the three matching rows, producing six combinations.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A database update is intended for one student but omits its WHERE condition. What is the main risk?
options: The update automatically guesses the intended student
Every row in the target table can receive the update
No row can change without a WHERE condition
Only the row with the smallest primary key changes
questions.answer: Every row in the target table can receive the update
questions.explanation: Without a restricting condition, an UPDATE applies its assignments to all rows in the target table.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A packet network can route around a failed link. Why does this not guarantee uninterrupted delivery in every failure?
options: Alternative paths may also be unavailable or congested
Rerouting requires all links to fail simultaneously
Every message must use one fixed physical path forever
Having two routers eliminates all possible failures
questions.answer: Alternative paths may also be unavailable or congested
questions.explanation: Redundancy improves resilience only while usable alternative capacity exists.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A connection includes a very fast local link and a much slower external link. Why may upgrading only the local link barely improve large downloads?
options: End-to-end speed equals the sum of every link's capacity
The fastest link alone sets the full download speed
A local upgrade automatically upgrades remote infrastructure
The external link can remain the limiting stage
questions.answer: The external link can remain the limiting stage
questions.explanation: Throughput is constrained by bottlenecks along the path, so improving a nonlimiting stage can have little effect.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A user signs in successfully but is denied access to staff records. Why is this not necessarily an error?
options: Permission checks apply only to anonymous users
The password must therefore have been incorrect
Identity verification does not imply permission for every resource
A successful login must grant all database rights
questions.answer: Identity verification does not imply permission for every resource
questions.explanation: Authentication establishes identity; authorisation determines what that identity is permitted to do.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: An attacker cannot read an encrypted connection but controls the receiving device after decryption. What remains possible?
options: The connection must have been unencrypted because an endpoint was compromised
The attacker can access plaintext at that endpoint
Encryption prevents all endpoint access forever
The endpoint never needs plaintext to use the message
questions.answer: The attacker can access plaintext at that endpoint
questions.explanation: Protecting transmission does not protect data from a compromised endpoint that processes the decrypted content.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: The largest value in an unsigned fixed-width integer field is incremented without overflow checking. Why can the result be incorrect?
options: The required value needs more bits than the field provides
The operation automatically increases the allocated bit width in every system
The largest value is followed by an exactly represented fraction
Unsigned fields cannot represent zero
questions.answer: The required value needs more bits than the field provides
questions.explanation: Fixed-width representations have a finite range; the outcome beyond that range depends on the system's overflow behaviour.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A lossy process removes image detail judged visually unimportant. Why might the output still be unsuitable for later scientific measurement?
options: Visual similarity guarantees identical numerical information
Lossy compression always preserves each original pixel
A smaller file automatically improves measurement precision
The discarded detail may matter to the measurement even if it is hard to notice
questions.answer: The discarded detail may matter to the measurement even if it is hard to notice
questions.explanation: An acceptable viewing approximation does not guarantee preservation of information needed for quantitative analysis.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A cache is enlarged, but a program rarely reuses recently accessed data. Why may the speed gain be small?
options: Cache size alone determines performance regardless of workload
A cache permanently increases the processor's instruction count
The access pattern may yield few useful cache hits
Larger caches necessarily slow every program
questions.answer: The access pattern may yield few useful cache hits
questions.explanation: A cache helps when requested data are present; benefits depend on workload and locality as well as capacity.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: A school system blocks legitimate users so often that they share one powerful staff account. What design problem should be addressed?
options: Stricter lockouts always improve actual security regardless of user behaviour
Access rules and recovery should support legitimate work without encouraging shared privileges
Shared administrator access is the safest solution for every user
Removing all authentication is the only possible improvement
questions.answer: Access rules and recovery should support legitimate work without encouraging shared privileges
questions.explanation: Security controls should provide workable authorised paths; shared privileged accounts weaken accountability and access separation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every member of set A is also in B, but B has extra members. Which statement follows?
options: A and B are disjoint
B is a proper subset of A
A equals B
A is a proper subset of B
questions.answer: A is a proper subset of B
questions.explanation: A is contained in B without being equal to it.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A real-valued rule contains the term 1/(x-3). Which input must be excluded?
questions.explanation: At x = 3 the denominator is zero, so the expression is undefined.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The graph of y = f(x) is changed to y = f(x)+4. What changes?
options: Every point moves upward by four units
Every point moves right by four units
All slopes double
The domain necessarily shrinks
questions.answer: Every point moves upward by four units
questions.explanation: Adding a constant to the output produces a vertical translation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An inequality is multiplied on both sides by a negative number. What must change?
options: The inequality becomes an equality
Only the larger side is multiplied
The inequality direction reverses
Both sides become zero
questions.answer: The inequality direction reverses
questions.explanation: Multiplication by a negative number reverses order on the number line.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An angle is increased by one full turn. What happens to its sine and cosine?
options: Both become zero
Both stay the same
Both change sign
Sine doubles while cosine stays fixed
questions.answer: Both stay the same
questions.explanation: Sine and cosine are periodic with a full-turn period.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A sequence increases by the same amount at every step. What feature does its term-number graph have?
options: A continuously doubling slope
A vertical line
A repeating circle
A constant slope
questions.answer: A constant slope
questions.explanation: A constant difference makes the term a linear function of its index.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A positive quantity grows by the same percentage each year. Which model is appropriate?
options: A fixed value with no change
A sequence with constant second difference necessarily
Geometric growth
A constant additive increase
questions.answer: Geometric growth
questions.explanation: Repeated multiplication by a fixed factor produces a geometric sequence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In expanding (1+x)^n for a positive integer n, why is the constant term 1?
options: It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
Every term contains x
The exponents must all be zero
All coefficients are equal to one
questions.answer: It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
questions.explanation: Only the product of all constant choices contributes to the x-to-the-zero term.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two distinct nonvertical lines have the same slope. What follows?
options: They are perpendicular
They meet exactly once
They must pass through the origin
They are parallel
questions.answer: They are parallel
questions.explanation: Equal slopes give the same direction; distinct intercepts keep the lines separate.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two circles subtend the same central angle. Why is the intercepted arc longer on the larger circle?
options: The arc becomes a diameter in every larger circle
Arc length is proportional to radius for a fixed angle
The angle necessarily becomes larger on the larger circle
Arc length is independent of radius
questions.answer: Arc length is proportional to radius for a fixed angle
questions.explanation: The relation between arc length, radius and angle makes arc length scale with radius when angle is fixed.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two vectors have equal magnitudes and opposite directions. What is their sum?
options: The zero vector
A vector twice as long
A unit vector
A scalar equal to their common magnitude
questions.answer: The zero vector
questions.explanation: Opposite equal vectors cancel component by component.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Values of f(x) approach 5 as x approaches 2, but f(2) is defined as 9. What is the limit at 2?
options: It must not exist
questions.explanation: A limit concerns nearby values, not the separately assigned value at the point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A graph has a jump at x = a. Why is the function not continuous there?
options: Its domain must contain only integers
Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
Its value must be negative
Its slope must be positive
questions.answer: Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
questions.explanation: Continuity requires the two-sided limit to exist and equal the function value.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A differentiable function has positive derivative throughout an interval. What does this imply?
options: Its values are all positive
It is constant
It must be linear
It is increasing on the interval
questions.answer: It is increasing on the interval
questions.explanation: Positive derivative gives increasing function values, regardless of their signs.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A nonnegative rate of water inflow is graphed against time. What does area under the graph represent?
options: The tank's initial volume alone
The elapsed time squared
Total water added over that time
The highest flow rate
questions.answer: Total water added over that time
questions.explanation: Integrating a rate over time gives the accumulated quantity.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A population's growth rate is proportional to its current size with a positive constant. What qualitative behaviour follows?
options: Exponential growth in the ideal model
Constant absolute growth
Linear decline
Immediate extinction
questions.answer: Exponential growth in the ideal model
questions.explanation: The differential equation dP/dt = kP gives exponential growth for positive k.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A continuous normal distribution is symmetric about its mean. What proportion lies above the mean?
options: All of it
None of it
A proportion determined only by its standard deviation
One half
questions.answer: One half
questions.explanation: Symmetry divides the total probability equally on either side, with zero probability at one exact value.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two events are mutually exclusive. What is impossible in one trial?
options: Their probabilities adding to less than one
Both occurring together
Either event occurring
Neither event occurring
questions.answer: Both occurring together
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events have an empty intersection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A bag contains red and blue counters. You learn the chosen counter is red. What happens to the relevant sample space?
options: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
It expands to all possible bags
Every original outcome remains equally relevant
It contains no outcomes
questions.answer: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
questions.explanation: Conditioning restricts attention to outcomes satisfying the given information.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For a continuous random variable, probability over an interval is represented by what feature of its density graph?
options: The curve's total length
The number of turning points
Area over that interval
The value at just the left endpoint
questions.answer: Area over that interval
questions.explanation: Density accumulates into probability through area, rather than a single graph height.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A student belongs to A or B, but not both. Which membership condition describes this?
options: Membership in the universal set only
Membership in their symmetric difference
Membership in their intersection
Membership in neither set
questions.answer: Membership in their symmetric difference
questions.explanation: The symmetric difference contains elements belonging to exactly one of the two sets.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two machines act in sequence: the first doubles an input, the second adds three. Why can reversing them change the result?
options: Addition always occurs before multiplication in any real process
Both machines must produce zero
The first machine has no output
The operations need not commute
questions.answer: The operations need not commute
questions.explanation: Doubling after adding three also doubles the added amount, unlike adding it afterward.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A quadratic's discriminant changes from positive to negative as a parameter varies. What changes?
options: Its leading coefficient must become zero
Every coefficient becomes negative
Two distinct real roots become no real roots
No real roots become two distinct real roots
questions.answer: Two distinct real roots become no real roots
questions.explanation: The discriminant's sign determines whether the roots are real and distinct, repeated, or nonreal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A sine equation has one solution in the first quadrant. Why can another occur in the second quadrant?
options: Supplementary angles have equal sine
Sine is one-to-one over a full turn
Cosine is positive in both quadrants
Every angle has the same sine
questions.answer: Supplementary angles have equal sine
questions.explanation: Reflection across the vertical axis preserves the unit-circle y-coordinate.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A complex number is multiplied by its conjugate. Why is the result real and nonnegative?
options: The imaginary part is always zero before multiplication
Conjugation changes its real part's sign
All complex products are nonnegative
It equals the square of its modulus
questions.answer: It equals the square of its modulus
questions.explanation: The imaginary cross terms cancel, leaving the sum of the squared real and imaginary parts.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A geometric sequence has ratio between zero and one. Why can the infinite sum be finite?
options: The terms eventually become negative
Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
There are only finitely many terms
Every term is zero
questions.answer: Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
questions.explanation: For absolute ratio below one, partial sums approach a finite limit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two committee roles are distinct. Why does assigning the same two people in exchanged roles create a different outcome?
options: The role assignment is part of the outcome
The membership becomes a different size
One person disappears
All arrangements are unordered
questions.answer: The role assignment is part of the outcome
questions.explanation: When positions or roles matter, permutations distinguish assignments with the same members.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two points lie on the same line parallel to another line. How do their perpendicular distances to the other line compare?
options: One distance must be zero
Distances depend only on x-coordinate
They are equal
The point farther right is always closer
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Parallel lines remain a constant perpendicular distance apart.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A line touches a circle at one point. How does it relate to the radius through that point?
options: It has the same length as the radius
It is perpendicular to the radius
It is parallel to the radius
It passes through the centre
questions.answer: It is perpendicular to the radius
questions.explanation: The tangent at a circle point is perpendicular to the radius there.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two nonzero vectors have zero dot product. What does this imply?
options: They are parallel in the same direction
They are equal
Their cross product must also be zero
They are perpendicular
questions.answer: They are perpendicular
questions.explanation: The dot product is proportional to the cosine of the angle, which is zero at a right angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two lines in three-dimensional space do not meet and are not parallel. What is possible?
options: They are the same line
Their direction vectors are zero
They are skew
They must lie in one plane
questions.answer: They are skew
questions.explanation: Skew lines are nonparallel, nonintersecting lines in different planes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The graph of absolute value of x has a sharp corner at zero. What is true there?
options: It is continuous but not differentiable
It is differentiable but not continuous
It has an infinite function value
It has the same tangent slope from both sides
questions.answer: It is continuous but not differentiable
questions.explanation: The left and right slopes differ although the function has no discontinuity.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function is increasing but its slope is becoming smaller. Which combination can describe it?
options: Negative first derivative and positive second derivative
Both derivatives negative necessarily
Zero first derivative throughout
Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.answer: Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.explanation: Increasing values require positive slope, while decreasing slope indicates concavity down.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A velocity-time graph has regions above and below the time axis. What does its signed integral represent?
options: Final acceleration
Net displacement
Total distance in every case
Maximum speed
questions.answer: Net displacement
questions.explanation: Positive and negative velocities contribute opposite signed displacements.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: F(x) is the area accumulated under a continuous function f from a fixed starting point to x. What does F'(x) measure?
options: The current value f(x)
The total area squared
Only the starting value of f
Always zero
questions.answer: The current value f(x)
questions.explanation: The derivative of accumulated area recovers the instantaneous integrand.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Events follow a constant-rate Poisson process. An observation interval doubles. What changes about the expected event count?
options: It stays constant
It becomes a negative number
It doubles
It halves
questions.answer: It doubles
questions.explanation: For a constant-rate process, the mean count is proportional to interval length.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two linear equations describe the same line. What is their solution set?
options: One point chosen by the larger coefficient
Infinitely many points on that line
No points
Exactly two points
questions.answer: Infinitely many points on that line
questions.explanation: Dependent equations impose the same condition rather than two independent constraints.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two counters are drawn without replacement from a mixed bag. Why can the second colour depend on the first?
options: The colours physically transform
All second draws are independent by definition
The first counter returns automatically
The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.answer: The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.explanation: Removing a counter changes the proportions remaining for the next selection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every value in a data set increases by the same constant. What happens to variance?
options: It becomes zero
It doubles
It stays unchanged
It rises by that constant
questions.answer: It stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The mean shifts by the same amount, leaving deviations from the mean unchanged.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The sampling method and confidence level stay the same, but a much larger random sample is taken. What usually happens to the interval estimating a mean?
options: It becomes narrower
It becomes wider solely because the sample is larger
It must have zero width
It loses its stated confidence level by definition
questions.answer: It becomes narrower
questions.explanation: Larger samples generally reduce standard error, giving more precise estimates under the model assumptions.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: To disprove the statement 'Every positive integer has property P', what is sufficient?
options: Many integers having P
One negative integer lacking P
No tested counterexample
One positive integer lacking P
questions.answer: One positive integer lacking P
questions.explanation: A single counterexample within the stated domain disproves a universal claim.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A piecewise function has equal left and right limits at a joining point, but its assigned value differs. What repairs continuity there?
options: Set the derivative to one without changing values
Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
Change every nearby value to zero
Remove both intervals entirely
questions.answer: Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
questions.explanation: A removable discontinuity is fixed by matching the point value to its existing limit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An upward-opening quadratic has two distinct real roots. Where is it negative?
options: Strictly between the roots
Outside both roots
Everywhere
Nowhere
questions.answer: Strictly between the roots
questions.explanation: The parabola lies below the axis between its crossings and above it outside them.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Multiplying a nonzero complex number by i changes its plane representation how?
options: Reflection only across the real axis
A quarter-turn clockwise with doubled modulus
A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
A doubling of modulus without rotation
questions.answer: A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
questions.explanation: Multiplication by i adds an angle of pi over two and has modulus one.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A series has terms that approach zero. Why does that alone not prove convergence?
options: A zero term forces every later term to vanish
The partial sums may still grow without bound
Every such series is finite
Terms approaching zero must alternate
questions.answer: The partial sums may still grow without bound
questions.explanation: Vanishing terms are necessary but not sufficient; the harmonic series is a standard counterexample.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair coin has produced several heads in independent tosses. Why is tails not made more likely on the next toss?
options: Tails becomes impossible after enough heads
The coin remembers its previous states
A balancing sequence is guaranteed immediately
The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
questions.answer: The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
questions.explanation: Independent trials retain the same probability regardless of previous outcomes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two lines have proportional x and y coefficients but nonproportional constants in their equations. What follows?
options: They intersect at the origin necessarily
They are perpendicular
They are distinct parallel lines
They are identical lines
questions.answer: They are distinct parallel lines
questions.explanation: Matching coefficient ratios give the same direction, while incompatible constants prevent intersection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A small study fails to reject no difference between two groups. Why is 'the groups are identical' too strong?
options: The test may lack power to detect a real difference
A nonsignificant result proves a large difference
All null hypotheses are true until rejected
Sample size cannot influence test sensitivity
questions.answer: The test may lack power to detect a real difference
questions.explanation: Nonrejection may reflect limited evidence or low power; it does not establish exact equality.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A binomial model has many trials but a very small success probability. Why may a symmetric normal approximation still be poor?
options: A large trial count always makes every distribution exactly normal
The binomial mean must be negative
The outcomes stop being discrete when probability is small
The distribution can remain strongly skewed if expected successes are few
questions.answer: The distribution can remain strongly skewed if expected successes are few
questions.explanation: Both expected successes and expected failures matter for a useful normal approximation; many trials alone are insufficient.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function oscillates between values near -1 and 1 arbitrarily close to a point without narrowing its range. What happens to its limit there?
options: The limit equals the point's assigned value
No single limit exists
The limit must be zero by averaging
The limit must be one
questions.answer: No single limit exists
questions.explanation: Persistent full-amplitude oscillation prevents values from approaching one number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function is differentiable at an interior point. Which conclusion is guaranteed?
options: It is continuous there
Its derivative is positive there
It is locally linear exactly
It has a local extremum there
questions.answer: It is continuous there
questions.explanation: Differentiability implies continuity, but does not determine slope sign or the presence of an extremum.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For f(x)=x cubed, the derivative is zero at zero. Why is zero not a local maximum or minimum?
options: The derivative is undefined there
The function is constant nearby
The function keeps increasing through it
The function is discontinuous there
questions.answer: The function keeps increasing through it
questions.explanation: A zero derivative alone is insufficient; the function increases on both sides of the stationary point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A continuous odd function is integrated from -a to a. Why is the integral zero?
options: Every antiderivative is constant
Opposite signed contributions cancel
The function must be zero everywhere
The interval has zero length
questions.answer: Opposite signed contributions cancel
questions.explanation: Odd symmetry gives equal-magnitude contributions of opposite sign on symmetric intervals.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In dP/dt = kP(1-P/K), with k and K positive, a population is slightly below K. What does the model predict?
options: It decreases away from K
It immediately jumps to zero
It grows exponentially without limit at all sizes
It increases toward K
questions.answer: It increases toward K
questions.explanation: For 0<P<K the growth rate is positive and becomes smaller near the stable equilibrium K.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function changes sign across a vertical asymptote. Why does this not guarantee a root between the endpoints?
options: The intermediate value theorem requires differentiability everywhere
An asymptote must itself be a zero
Continuity on the whole interval is missing
A sign change never gives any information
questions.answer: Continuity on the whole interval is missing
questions.explanation: The intermediate value theorem requires continuity; a discontinuity can separate opposite signs without a zero.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two successive iterates are close together. Why does that alone not prove an accurate root has been found?
options: An iteration can stagnate away from a root
Nearby iterates always prove a root
Every root has a derivative of zero
Iteration values must be integers
questions.answer: An iteration can stagnate away from a root
questions.explanation: Checking the residual and method behaviour is needed; a small step alone can reflect stagnation or numerical limitations.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rare condition has a test with some false positives. Why need a positive result not make the condition highly likely?
options: Test accuracy is irrelevant
A positive result proves the condition is absent
Rare conditions cannot be tested
The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.answer: The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.explanation: The posterior probability depends on both test performance and the prior prevalence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two random variables have finite means but are dependent. Which statement still holds?
options: They must have identical distributions
The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
Their variances always add without a covariance term
Their product mean always equals the product of their means
questions.answer: The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
questions.explanation: Linearity of expectation does not require independence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every observation is multiplied by a constant c. Why is variance multiplied by c squared?
options: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
The mean is always unchanged
Variance counts observations without using values
Only negative constants affect variance
questions.answer: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
questions.explanation: Variance averages squared deviations, so scaling values squares the scale factor.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rate rule is positive just below an equilibrium and negative just above it. What behaviour does this indicate for nearby solutions?
options: They remain at their starting values regardless of the rate
The rule has no equilibrium
They move toward the equilibrium
They move away from the equilibrium
questions.answer: They move toward the equilibrium
questions.explanation: The signs direct motion upward from below and downward from above, indicating local stability.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A trolley moves forward while its velocity-time graph slopes downward. What is happening?
options: It is slowing down
It is moving backward
Its acceleration is zero
Its distance travelled is decreasing
questions.answer: It is slowing down
questions.explanation: A downward slope means negative acceleration; with positive velocity this reduces speed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A passenger leans forward when a bus brakes. Why?
options: The seat increases the passenger's speed
The passenger loses mass
The passenger's body tends to keep moving
A forward force from gravity appears
questions.answer: The passenger's body tends to keep moving
questions.explanation: Inertia resists the change from the body's original forward motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A box remains stationary while you push it gently on a rough floor. What balances your push?
options: An upward force from the floor
Static friction
Kinetic friction
The box's weight alone
questions.answer: Static friction
questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to oppose the push until its limiting value is reached.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two carts initially at rest push apart on a frictionless track. What must their momenta do?
options: Have equal velocities
Point in the same direction
Increase the total momentum
Add to zero
questions.answer: Add to zero
questions.explanation: With no external horizontal force, total momentum remains its initial value of zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone moves at constant speed in a circle. Why is it accelerating?
options: Its speed must be increasing
Its kinetic energy must increase
Its velocity changes direction
Its mass changes continuously
questions.answer: Its velocity changes direction
questions.explanation: Velocity includes direction, which changes throughout circular motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical springs support equal loads, one singly and two in parallel. Which arrangement stretches less?
options: The parallel pair
The single spring
Both stretch equally
Neither arrangement can stretch
questions.answer: The parallel pair
questions.explanation: The parallel springs share the load, increasing the effective stiffness.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two points are at equal depth in connected water at rest. One is in a wide region and one in a narrow region. How do their pressures compare?
options: The narrow region must have higher pressure
The wide region must have higher pressure
Pressure depends only on the container's total volume
They are equal
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure depends on depth, density and surface pressure, not container width.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ice is melting at its melting point under constant pressure. Why can heat enter without raising temperature?
options: All added energy becomes light
Energy changes the phase
The ice has stopped absorbing energy
Its specific heat becomes zero
questions.answer: Energy changes the phase
questions.explanation: Latent heat changes intermolecular arrangement rather than increasing temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Gas expands and pushes a piston. What energy transfer occurs through the moving piston?
options: The gas does work on its surroundings
The surroundings always do positive work on the gas
The gas necessarily gains internal energy
No energy crosses the boundary
questions.answer: The gas does work on its surroundings
questions.explanation: An outward force acting through the piston's displacement transfers energy as work.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At the extreme position of a mass on an ideal spring, which quantity is zero?
options: Its acceleration magnitude
Its elastic potential energy
Its instantaneous speed
Its restoring force
questions.answer: Its instantaneous speed
questions.explanation: The mass reverses direction at the extreme, where its instantaneous velocity is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cork bobs as a water wave passes. What does this illustrate?
options: The cork must move permanently forward
Energy can travel without the cork travelling with the wave
All water travels at the wave speed
The wave carries no energy
questions.answer: Energy can travel without the cork travelling with the wave
questions.explanation: The disturbance propagates while material particles oscillate about local positions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two initially neutral objects become oppositely charged by rubbing. What was transferred between them?
options: Protons between nuclei
Whole positive nuclei only
Gravitational mass
Electrons
questions.answer: Electrons
questions.explanation: Charge separation in ordinary rubbing results from electron transfer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A positive test charge is released in a uniform electric field, with no other force. Which way does it initially accelerate?
options: Perpendicular to the field
It cannot accelerate
Along the field
Against the field
questions.answer: Along the field
questions.explanation: The electric force on a positive charge points along the electric field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One branch of two resistors in parallel is removed from an ideal battery. What happens to current in the remaining branch?
options: It stays the same
It doubles automatically
It falls to zero
It reverses direction
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: The remaining branch still has the same battery voltage across the same resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metal wire is made longer without changing material, temperature or cross-sectional area. Why does resistance increase?
options: The wire gains a larger cross-section
Its resistivity must decrease
Electrons stop carrying charge
Charge carriers encounter a longer conducting path
questions.answer: Charge carriers encounter a longer conducting path
questions.explanation: For fixed resistivity and area, resistance is proportional to length.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnet is held stationary inside a stationary coil. What induced emf results from this unchanged arrangement?
options: An emf that alternates automatically
Zero
A steady emf set only by magnet strength
An emf that grows with time
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Induction requires changing magnetic flux, not merely the presence of a magnetic field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Why does an ordinary transformer need changing current in its primary coil?
options: It needs changing magnetic flux
Its core must rotate
Direct current has no charge carriers
The secondary must touch the primary
questions.answer: It needs changing magnetic flux
questions.explanation: A changing primary current produces flux changes that induce an emf in the secondary.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens forms an image of a very distant object. Where is the image approximately formed?
options: At the lens centre
On the object's side as a virtual image
At the focal plane
At twice the focal length always
questions.answer: At the focal plane
questions.explanation: Nearly parallel incident rays converge near the principal focal plane.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two coherent light waves meet with crest aligned to crest. What happens locally?
options: Their wavelengths halve
Their amplitudes reinforce
Their frequencies cancel
Their speeds double
questions.answer: Their amplitudes reinforce
questions.explanation: The displacements add constructively when the waves are in phase.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radioactive sample contains fewer undecayed nuclei after one half-life. What happens to its activity?
options: It increases
It stays fixed until the last nucleus decays
It becomes independent of the number of nuclei
It decreases
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Activity is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei for a fixed decay constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A velocity-time graph crosses from positive to negative values. What occurs at the crossing?
options: Its distance travelled returns to zero
Its mass changes sign
The object reverses direction
Its acceleration must be zero
questions.answer: The object reverses direction
questions.explanation: The velocity changes sign, indicating reversal; acceleration is determined by the graph's slope.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two balls are launched horizontally from the same height with different speeds. Ignoring air resistance, which lands first?
options: They land together
The faster ball
The slower ball
The heavier ball regardless of speed
questions.answer: They land together
questions.explanation: Their initial vertical velocities and vertical accelerations are identical.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two touching blocks accelerate together on a smooth floor when one is pushed. Why are their net forces unequal if their masses differ?
options: Contact forces violate Newton's third law
The lighter block has no net force
Their velocities must be different
They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
questions.answer: They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives different net forces for different masses at the same acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball moves upward after being thrown, ignoring air resistance. Which description is correct?
options: Gravity does positive work during ascent
Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
Both energies increase
Mechanical energy decreases because speed decreases
questions.answer: Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
questions.explanation: Gravity converts kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy while total mechanical energy stays constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ultrasound pulse gives a later returning echo from interface B than from A in the same tissue. What does that imply?
options: B is farther from the probe
B must reflect more energy
B must be moving toward the probe
The transmitted pulse has a different frequency for each echo
questions.answer: B is farther from the probe
questions.explanation: With the same wave speed, greater round-trip travel time indicates a greater distance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two satellites have circular orbits around Earth. Why is the lower satellite faster?
options: The higher satellite is beyond gravity
The lower satellite must have greater mass
A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
The lower satellite has no gravitational potential energy
questions.answer: A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
questions.explanation: For a circular orbit, speed is proportional to the inverse square root of orbital radius.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two stars known to have equal luminosity appear with different brightnesses, with negligible absorption. What explains the fainter one?
options: It has lost its intrinsic luminosity by travelling
It is farther away
It necessarily has a lower surface temperature
It emits photons that slow down more
questions.answer: It is farther away
questions.explanation: Flux from a source of fixed luminosity falls with the square of distance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vacuum flask reduces heat transfer through its evacuated gap. Which process can still cross that gap?
options: Conduction through air
Convection of trapped gas
Bulk flow of liquid
Thermal radiation
questions.answer: Thermal radiation
