questions.explanation: Complementary measures can reduce different risks, without promising zero transmission.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A campaign reaches many students. Which additional measure better assesses its effect?
options: Relevant changes in understanding or behaviour
The number of colours on its posters
The length of the campaign title
The number of times organisers praise it
questions.answer: Relevant changes in understanding or behaviour
questions.explanation: Reach indicates exposure; outcomes indicate whether the intended change occurred.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: One cereal gives fibre per 30 g serving and another per 100 g. What is needed for a fair concentration comparison?
options: Compare the printed numbers directly
Choose whichever number is larger
Assume serving sizes are identical
Express both amounts per the same food mass
questions.answer: Express both amounts per the same food mass
questions.explanation: A common denominator is necessary to compare nutrient concentration.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A diet supplies a nutrient, but a clinical condition reduces its absorption. What does this illustrate?
options: Absorption cannot affect nutrient availability
Every consumed nutrient is fully retained
Reported intake alone may not establish nutritional adequacy
Food intake is never relevant
questions.answer: Reported intake alone may not establish nutritional adequacy
questions.explanation: The body must absorb and use nutrients as well as consume them.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: Two websites disagree about a nutritional claim. Which comparison is most useful?
options: Which page appears first in a screenshot
Evidence, expertise, methods and whether the claims are current
Which site has more animated graphics
Which headline sounds more certain
questions.answer: Evidence, expertise, methods and whether the claims are current
questions.explanation: Reliable assessment depends on the support for a claim, not its presentation alone.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A nutrition survey includes only students present at an optional fitness club. What limits its use for the whole school?
options: Participants may differ systematically from other students
Optional attendance ensures random sampling
Every student must have joined the club
The survey can only measure height
questions.answer: Participants may differ systematically from other students
questions.explanation: Selection into the club may produce a sample that does not represent the full school.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: Food diaries are often incomplete on weekends. Why could a weekday-only summary misrepresent usual intake?
options: Weekday records become invalid in every respect
Adding more weekdays necessarily recovers weekend patterns
Weekend eating patterns may differ systematically
All missing entries must represent no food eaten
questions.answer: Weekend eating patterns may differ systematically
questions.explanation: Systematically missing types of days can bias a summary of habitual intake.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: Two groups have the same mean nutrient intake, but one has a much wider spread. Why can their support needs differ?
options: Only the group with fewer people can have nutritional needs
The same mean can conceal different numbers with very low intakes
The shared mean proves that every individual has the same intake
Variation makes both means mathematically impossible
questions.answer: The same mean can conceal different numbers with very low intakes
questions.explanation: Population averages do not describe the full distribution or identify every individual's circumstances.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: One record gives a food mass in grams and another in ounces. What should happen before combining them?
options: Convert measurements to a consistent unit
Add the printed numbers directly
Discard the smaller number regardless of unit
Treat both numbers as calories
questions.answer: Convert measurements to a consistent unit
questions.explanation: Consistent units are necessary for meaningful aggregation and comparison.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: Students understand a new food label but cannot afford the foods it helps them identify. What distinction matters?
options: Understanding has no possible value
Affordability proves that the label is inaccurate
Knowledge and purchases are always the same outcome
Improved understanding is different from the ability to change behaviour
questions.answer: Improved understanding is different from the ability to change behaviour
questions.explanation: An intervention can improve one step in a causal chain while practical barriers limit later outcomes.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A class collects anonymous nutrition responses for a group project. Why report aggregate findings instead of speculating about individual respondents?
options: Aggregate data must contain no useful information
Personal speculation is required to compute a proportion
The educational purpose can be met without unnecessary personal identification
Anonymity guarantees every answer is accurate
questions.answer: The educational purpose can be met without unnecessary personal identification
questions.explanation: Purpose-limited reporting can communicate patterns while respecting participants' privacy.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A study links one food to better health, but its consumers also exercise more. What prevents a simple causal conclusion?
options: Food intake cannot ever be studied
The association proves exercise has no effect
A large sample automatically removes confounding
Exercise and other differences may confound the association
questions.answer: Exercise and other differences may confound the association
questions.explanation: Systematic differences between groups can offer alternative explanations.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A nutrition programme raises knowledge scores but leaves measured dietary intake unchanged. Which conclusion fits?
options: It proved that knowledge is irrelevant in every setting
It established harm to every participant
It improved measured knowledge without demonstrating dietary change
It proved full nutritional improvement
questions.answer: It improved measured knowledge without demonstrating dietary change
questions.explanation: Different outcomes must be distinguished rather than treating one as proof of another.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A screening threshold is lowered to detect more possible cases. What trade-off may result?
options: No change in who is referred
More false positives as sensitivity increases
Guaranteed improvement in every accuracy measure
Elimination of all false negatives and false positives
questions.answer: More false positives as sensitivity increases
questions.explanation: Threshold changes can increase detection while also flagging more people without the condition.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A new device reports a sudden change in average body measurements on the day it replaces the old device. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the devices give comparable measurements
Whether every person's body changed identically that day
Whether averages can ever be calculated
Whether all earlier records should be accepted as exact
questions.answer: Whether the devices give comparable measurements
questions.explanation: A change in measurement system can create an apparent change unrelated to biology.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: Participants selectively omit snacks they think researchers disapprove of. What bias is likely?
options: Perfect randomisation
Improved biochemical sensitivity
A guaranteed overestimate of snack intake
Social desirability affecting reported intake
questions.answer: Social desirability affecting reported intake
questions.explanation: Respondents may alter reports to present themselves in a favourable way.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A school compares different students each year and calls the difference individual improvement. Why is that interpretation weak?
options: All new students must be less healthy
One year's average proves every student's trajectory
Group composition changed, so individual change was not measured
Different groups cannot ever be compared
questions.answer: Group composition changed, so individual change was not measured
questions.explanation: Repeated population snapshots do not track the same individuals.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A poster says risk doubled but omits the original risk. What important information is missing?
options: Whether doubling is a relative comparison
The absolute size of the risk and its change
The colour of the source chart
The exact number of words in the poster
questions.answer: The absolute size of the risk and its change
questions.explanation: A relative increase can correspond to very different absolute changes depending on the baseline.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A method estimates body fat using assumptions that may not fit the person assessed. What follows?
options: Its estimate should be interpreted with awareness of those assumptions
The estimate is a direct count of every fat cell
The assumptions cannot influence the result
The estimate must equal true body fat exactly
questions.answer: Its estimate should be interpreted with awareness of those assumptions
questions.explanation: An indirect estimate depends on the model and measurement conditions used.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A nutrition service allocates identical support although assessed needs differ substantially. What should be reviewed?
options: Whether identical allocation always produces equal benefit
Whether assessment should be hidden from planners
Whether the easiest cases should receive everything
Whether resources match relevant differences in need
questions.answer: Whether resources match relevant differences in need
questions.explanation: Equitable support may require accounting for differing needs and barriers.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: With the same test accuracy, why can a positive result be less conclusive in a very low-prevalence population?
options: Sensitivity becomes automatically perfect
Prevalence changes the person's recorded height
False positives may form a larger share of all positive results
Low prevalence guarantees every positive is false
questions.answer: False positives may form a larger share of all positive results
questions.explanation: When true cases are rare, even a small false-positive rate can contribute many positive results.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A claim rests on testimonials from selected satisfied users, with no comparison group. What evidence is missing?
options: A photograph of the packaging
A systematic comparison that addresses alternative explanations
A more enthusiastic slogan
Proof that every testimonial is intentionally false
questions.answer: A systematic comparison that addresses alternative explanations
questions.explanation: Selected experiences cannot isolate an intervention's effect or establish typical outcomes.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A neighbourhood has poorer dietary indicators and fewer food outlets. What investigation would clarify the link?
options: Examine affordability, access and other relevant differences before assigning cause
Conclude residents simply lack motivation
Assume outlet count alone fully explains health
Treat all neighbourhoods as identical
questions.answer: Examine affordability, access and other relevant differences before assigning cause
questions.explanation: Multiple social and environmental factors can affect diet and should be examined together.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: Measurements, dietary reports and clinical findings each have limitations. Why can combining them strengthen assessment?
options: Combining them makes every result error-free
All methods measure exactly the same variable
The largest numerical result must determine the conclusion
Different methods can reveal or challenge each other's blind spots
questions.answer: Different methods can reveal or challenge each other's blind spots
questions.explanation: Complementary evidence supports a more complete interpretation while uncertainty remains.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A voluntary health survey quietly adds sensitive questions after consent was obtained for a different purpose. What should be addressed?
options: Whether more data always justifies the change
Whether consent can be assumed from attendance
Whether participants understand and agree to the expanded collection
Whether the questions fit on one screen
questions.answer: Whether participants understand and agree to the expanded collection
questions.explanation: Meaningful consent depends on the stated purpose and nature of the information collected.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A programme improves outcomes immediately, but the gains disappear after support ends. Which conclusion is most accurate?
options: Long-term follow-up adds no information
Initial effectiveness was not sustained under the later conditions
The initial measurements must be fabricated
The programme proved permanent success
questions.answer: Initial effectiveness was not sustained under the later conditions
questions.explanation: Follow-up distinguishes short-term change from sustained benefit.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A programme reports excellent results only for participants who stayed to the end, but many others left. What threatens the conclusion?
options: More charts can automatically remove the selection problem
Completers may differ systematically from those who left
Leaving proves that the programme failed for every person
The completers' measurements must all be fabricated
questions.answer: Completers may differ systematically from those who left
questions.explanation: Selective retention can make outcomes among completers unrepresentative of everyone who entered the programme.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A device produces almost identical readings each time but is consistently miscalibrated. What distinction does this illustrate?
options: High repeatability can coexist with poor accuracy
Repeatability proves the readings are unbiased
Calibration affects only the units printed on the case
Consistent error cancels automatically in every comparison
questions.answer: High repeatability can coexist with poor accuracy
questions.explanation: Repeated agreement does not establish closeness to the true value when systematic error persists.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A study compares replacing one snack with another, but an advertisement claims the second snack benefits anyone who adds it to an unchanged diet. Why is that inference weak?
options: A substitution study cannot measure any outcomes
The study proves that the added snack has the opposite effect
All diets contain exactly the same foods
Replacing a food and adding a food are different interventions
questions.answer: Replacing a food and adding a food are different interventions
questions.explanation: The effect of substitution depends on what is displaced and cannot automatically be transferred to additional consumption.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: Two groups show the same relative reduction in a measured risk but start at different baseline risks. Why can the absolute benefits differ?
options: Baseline risk is irrelevant once a percentage is given
The group with lower initial risk must have the larger absolute reduction
The same proportionate change acts on different starting amounts
Relative reductions always imply equal numbers of affected people
questions.answer: The same proportionate change acts on different starting amounts
questions.explanation: Absolute change depends on baseline risk as well as relative change.

questions.subject: Health Sciences
questions.q: A school programme improves one dietary indicator while worsening access for students with limited resources. What should an evaluation do?
options: Average the names of the outcomes without examining them
Consider both nutritional outcomes and unequal access effects
Declare success using only the favourable indicator
Assume access cannot affect health-related outcomes
questions.answer: Consider both nutritional outcomes and unequal access effects
questions.explanation: A programme's value depends on the pattern and distribution of its effects, not only its best-performing measure.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student checks whether a shared message is accurate before forwarding it. Which responsibility is being exercised?
options: Treating popularity as proof
Considering consequences before acting
Taking credit after success
Transferring every decision to others
questions.answer: Considering consequences before acting
questions.explanation: The curriculum distinguishes thoughtful preparation before an action from accountability afterward.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student accidentally damages borrowed equipment and informs its owner. What does the response demonstrate?
options: Accountability for the consequences of an action
A claim that intention removes every consequence
A refusal to acknowledge responsibility
Permission to use all property without consent
questions.answer: Accountability for the consequences of an action
questions.explanation: Acknowledging damage is part of responsibility after acting.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student is asked to keep donated money for a project. Which action best demonstrates amanah, or trustworthiness?
options: Borrow some secretly and replace it later
Spend it on a different project without asking
Record only the largest donations
Keep accurate records and use it only for the agreed purpose
questions.answer: Keep accurate records and use it only for the agreed purpose
questions.explanation: Entrusted resources should be handled faithfully according to their purpose.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: An unverified allegation about a classmate spreads online. Which response best protects the person's reputation?
options: Treat frequent sharing as confirmation
Add a dramatic headline to attract attention
Avoid repeating it and seek reliable clarification through an appropriate channel
Forward it with a question mark
questions.answer: Avoid repeating it and seek reliable clarification through an appropriate channel
questions.explanation: Repeating an unsupported allegation can spread harm even when presented as a question.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A learner says religious commitment requires rejecting careful study. What response fits the lesson on moderation?
options: Questions should be replaced by assumptions
Sound understanding and evidence support responsible practice
Study necessarily weakens commitment
The harshest interpretation is always the soundest
questions.answer: Sound understanding and evidence support responsible practice
questions.explanation: The lesson connects knowledge and understanding with avoiding excess and unsupported claims.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A community prioritises removing a dangerous obstacle from a public path. Which purpose does this most directly serve?
options: Protecting life and safety
Protecting wealth alone
Preserving a particular writing style
Increasing competition between neighbours
questions.answer: Protecting life and safety
questions.explanation: Removing a foreseeable danger directly supports the protection of life.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A learning project teaches students to examine evidence and avoid substances that impair judgement. Which purpose is most directly supported?
options: Increasing uncertainty in communication
Protecting property boundaries only
Replacing thought with imitation
Preserving intellect
questions.answer: Preserving intellect
questions.explanation: The preservation of intellect includes protecting and developing the capacity for sound judgement.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A seller accurately discloses a known defect before a buyer agrees. Which value is being applied?
options: Advantage through incomplete information
Treating consent as unnecessary
Honesty in transactions
Concealment for a good price
questions.answer: Honesty in transactions
questions.explanation: Disclosure enables an informed exchange and avoids deceptive gain.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: Neighbours organise different tasks to help a family after a house fire. What does this illustrate?
options: Avoiding responsibility because the need is shared
Cooperation in meeting a community need
Competition for exclusive credit
Assuming one person must do everything
questions.answer: Cooperation in meeting a community need
questions.explanation: Coordinated help applies social responsibility through practical cooperation.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student wants to enter a private room belonging to another person. Which action best respects privacy?
options: Seek permission before entering
Enter quietly without asking
Assume an unlocked door gives unlimited permission
Ask permission only after looking inside
questions.answer: Seek permission before entering
questions.explanation: Permission recognises the other person's control over private space.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A volunteer realises an agreed task cannot be finished on time. Which response best combines honesty and responsibility?
options: Promise completion while hiding the problem
Wait until others discover the delay
Blame someone who was not involved
Inform the organiser promptly and agree a realistic alternative
questions.answer: Inform the organiser promptly and agree a realistic alternative
questions.explanation: Early, truthful communication lets others address the consequences of the difficulty.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A learner quotes one sentence from a religious explanation without reading what surrounds it. What should be checked?
options: Only how many people shared it
Whether it confirms the learner's first impression
Its context and how it relates to the full discussion
Only whether the sentence is short
questions.answer: Its context and how it relates to the full discussion
questions.explanation: Context helps avoid assigning a meaning that the fuller discussion does not support.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: Two students disagree about an interpretation. Which response best supports constructive discussion?
options: Repeat the claim more loudly
Compare reasons respectfully and consult qualified guidance where needed
Attack each other's character
Assume disagreement proves bad intentions
questions.answer: Compare reasons respectfully and consult qualified guidance where needed
questions.explanation: Respectful reasoning distinguishes examining an idea from insulting a person.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student leaves a tap running although no water is needed. Which improvement reflects responsible use of resources?
options: Use the needed amount and stop avoidable waste
Keep it running because others also waste water
Avoid every use of water
Assume shared resources have no value
questions.answer: Use the needed amount and stop avoidable waste
questions.explanation: Responsible use meets needs without unnecessary waste.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student judging a contest discovers that a close friend is competing. What best protects fair judgement?
options: Give the friend extra marks privately
Lower the friend's score automatically
Ignore all judging criteria
Disclose the relationship and follow impartial judging arrangements
questions.answer: Disclose the relationship and follow impartial judging arrangements
questions.explanation: Transparency and impartial procedures address a possible conflict between friendship and responsibility.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student returns a borrowed book in good condition so others can use it. What links this action to trustworthiness?
options: A right to keep anything borrowed indefinitely
A need to receive public praise first
Permission to decide the owner's wishes without asking
Care for property placed in the student's custody
questions.answer: Care for property placed in the student's custody
questions.explanation: Trustworthiness includes taking reasonable care of something entrusted to a person and returning it as agreed.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A helper asks which form of assistance a neighbour actually needs. Why is this considerate?
options: It guarantees the neighbour must accept every offer
It makes listening unnecessary after the first offer
It connects help with the recipient's circumstances
It makes the helper's reputation the only aim
questions.answer: It connects help with the recipient's circumstances
questions.explanation: Considerate assistance attends to the person's real needs and respects their agency.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student prepares carefully for an examination while trusting in God. What balance is illustrated?
options: Effort removes all uncertainty from life
Reliance is accompanied by responsible effort
Reliance requires abandoning preparation
Preparation guarantees the exact result desired
questions.answer: Reliance is accompanied by responsible effort
questions.explanation: Responsible reliance does not replace taking appropriate available steps toward a worthwhile aim.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: Two friends want to end a disagreement. Which response most directly supports reconciliation?
options: Acknowledge harm and discuss how to repair the relationship
Repeat the accusation before checking it
Demand that only the less popular friend apologise
Retell the conflict to a wider audience for amusement
questions.answer: Acknowledge harm and discuss how to repair the relationship
questions.explanation: Reconciliation is supported by recognition of harm and constructive efforts to restore relations.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A family plans portions to reduce food being thrown away. What principle is applied?
options: Avoiding all enjoyment of food
Measuring generosity only by discarded leftovers
Buying more than needed to show responsibility
Using resources with care and avoiding waste
questions.answer: Using resources with care and avoiding waste
questions.explanation: Planning to use food well puts responsible stewardship into practice.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student forwards a false warning intending to help, then learns it caused distress. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Keep forwarding it because the intention was good
Delete only the student's own copy without clarification
Correct the misinformation and learn to verify future messages
Argue that good intention removes all responsibility
questions.answer: Correct the misinformation and learn to verify future messages
questions.explanation: Good intention matters, but does not remove the need to address avoidable harm.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A treasurer sees another worthy cause needing money. Why should they seek permission before redirecting entrusted funds?
options: Keeping records alone authorises any use
A worthy aim does not automatically change the terms of the trust
Only unsuccessful projects require permission
All charitable funds have identical purposes
questions.answer: A worthy aim does not automatically change the terms of the trust
questions.explanation: Trustworthiness includes respecting the agreed purpose as well as wanting a good outcome.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student neglects family responsibilities and health while pursuing an optional activity presented as devotion. What should be reconsidered?
options: The balance between commitments and the rights of others and oneself
Whether all family responsibilities should cease
Whether exhaustion alone proves sound judgement
Whether intentions make every choice proportionate
questions.answer: The balance between commitments and the rights of others and oneself
questions.explanation: Moderation involves recognising relevant responsibilities rather than allowing one activity to erase them.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A community compares two ways to improve a shared facility. One achieves the same benefit with substantially less avoidable harm. What consideration favours it?
options: Choosing the most difficult option for its own sake
Ignoring consequences once a benefit is named
Treating all methods as ethically identical
Achieving benefit while reducing harm
questions.answer: Achieving benefit while reducing harm
questions.explanation: Attention to consequences supports pursuing benefits without unnecessary harm.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: Two explanations make opposite claims from the same passage. What is the strongest first comparison?
options: The number of followers each speaker has
Which explanation was heard first
Their use of language, context and supporting evidence
The confidence of the speakers alone
questions.answer: Their use of language, context and supporting evidence
questions.explanation: A reasoned comparison examines the grounds of interpretation rather than popularity.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A class offers sympathy to a learner who cannot access an activity but makes no adjustment. What additional step would make support practical?
options: Give the learner a public label
Identify the barrier and arrange a suitable way to participate
Repeat sympathy without examining access
Assume the learner prefers exclusion
questions.answer: Identify the barrier and arrange a suitable way to participate
questions.explanation: Concern becomes practical support when it addresses the person's actual difficulty.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A buyer agrees to a price while the seller hides an important defect. Why is apparent agreement ethically insufficient?
options: Consent is undermined by withheld material information
Any stated price makes concealment irrelevant
A buyer's agreement proves full knowledge
Defects matter only after resale
questions.answer: Consent is undermined by withheld material information
questions.explanation: Informed exchange requires honesty about information material to the decision.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A project leader assigns a task to another student. What responsibility remains with the leader?
options: Assume delegation removes every responsibility
Redo every task without communication
Hold the student responsible for instructions never given
Provide clear expectations and appropriate follow-up
questions.answer: Provide clear expectations and appropriate follow-up
questions.explanation: Delegation should include clarity and oversight appropriate to the leader's role.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A learner makes a minor mistake during a discussion. Which correction best combines accuracy and respect?
options: Ignore the content and criticise appearance
Spread the mistake beyond the discussion
Explain the error constructively without personal ridicule
Turn the mistake into a public insult
questions.answer: Explain the error constructively without personal ridicule
questions.explanation: Correcting an idea need not damage a person's dignity.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: Many accounts repeat the same allegation copied from one unverified post. Does the number of repetitions establish independent evidence?
options: No; all allegations are necessarily false
No; repetition of one source is not independent corroboration
Yes; every repost is a new eyewitness
Yes; popularity establishes accuracy
questions.answer: No; repetition of one source is not independent corroboration
questions.explanation: Independent support requires more than repeated circulation of the same unsupported claim.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student memorises a rule but applies it without considering the facts of the situation. What is missing?
options: Understanding relevant context and the rule's purpose
The ability to repeat the exact wording faster
A larger audience for the decision
A guarantee that every situation is identical
questions.answer: Understanding relevant context and the rule's purpose
questions.explanation: Responsible application requires understanding both the principle and the circumstances.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: Everyone benefits from a shared study room, but each assumes someone else will maintain it. What arrangement best addresses the problem?
options: Leave all duties unnamed
Give access only to the first person arriving
Assume shared ownership prevents neglect
Agree clear, fair responsibilities for care
questions.answer: Agree clear, fair responsibilities for care
questions.explanation: Clear responsibilities reduce the tendency to leave common needs unattended.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: Someone labels every respectful disagreement as hostility. What distinction is being overlooked?
options: Respect requires never evaluating evidence
A confident claim cannot be questioned
Disagreeing with a claim is not necessarily attacking a person or faith
Every disagreement has the same motive
questions.answer: Disagreeing with a claim is not necessarily attacking a person or faith
questions.explanation: Constructive disagreement can examine ideas without expressing hostility.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student treats seeking qualified healthcare as incompatible with reliance on Allah. What response fits responsible action in the curriculum?
options: A good intention replaces qualified knowledge
Taking appropriate means can coexist with reliance on Allah
Reliance requires avoiding all practical means
Every illness should be judged by classmates
questions.answer: Taking appropriate means can coexist with reliance on Allah
questions.explanation: The lesson connects care for health with taking appropriate practical steps.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A volunteer makes several incompatible promises to appear helpful. What would better serve trustworthiness?
options: Assess capacity and make commitments that can be honoured
Promise everything and decide later
Keep only the most public promise
Assume enthusiasm substitutes for completion
questions.answer: Assess capacity and make commitments that can be honoured
questions.explanation: Responsible commitment includes considering feasibility before promising.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student follows an agreed rule only when the teacher is watching. What would better demonstrate integrity?
options: Following it only when a reward is announced
Treating secrecy as evidence that no duty exists
Keeping the commitment when supervision is absent too
Replacing the rule with a personal preference whenever alone
questions.answer: Keeping the commitment when supervision is absent too
questions.explanation: Integrity is reflected in consistency between acknowledged responsibilities and conduct beyond immediate supervision.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A community offers immediate supplies and then helps families regain stable livelihoods. Why combine these approaches?
options: Both approaches must have identical effects
They address urgent need and longer-term ability to meet needs
Immediate help prevents any later independence
Long-term support makes urgent needs irrelevant
questions.answer: They address urgent need and longer-term ability to meet needs
questions.explanation: Different forms of assistance can complement one another across immediate and continuing circumstances.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A volunteer accepts more commitments than can be fulfilled and repeatedly lets others down. What should change?
options: Make realistic commitments that can be honoured alongside existing duties
Promise more tasks to compensate without checking capacity
Assume good intentions fulfil every promise automatically
Hide the delays until someone complains
questions.answer: Make realistic commitments that can be honoured alongside existing duties
questions.explanation: Responsible commitment considers capacity and the rights of others who rely on the promise.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student discovers that a quotation used in an assignment has been attributed to the wrong author. What best reflects intellectual honesty?
options: Keep the error because the quotation sounds useful
Invent a supporting reference
Remove only the author's name while implying verification
Correct the attribution and explain the correction where needed
questions.answer: Correct the attribution and explain the correction where needed
questions.explanation: Accurate attribution and transparent correction protect trust in the use of knowledge.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A mediator hears only one participant before judging a dispute. Why seek the other account?
options: Listening automatically makes the dispute disappear
The second account must always override the first
Relevant facts and perspectives may otherwise be missed
Both accounts must be equally accurate in every detail
questions.answer: Relevant facts and perspectives may otherwise be missed
questions.explanation: Fair judgement requires a sufficient understanding of relevant evidence rather than immediate acceptance of one account.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student must help a team meet a deadline but discovers its report contains false evidence. What best balances cooperation and honesty?
options: Submit the false evidence to protect team loyalty
Abandon the team without explanation
Keep silent because deadlines outweigh truthfulness
Tell the team, correct the evidence and revise the plan together
questions.answer: Tell the team, correct the evidence and revise the plan together
questions.explanation: Cooperation does not require participation in deception; correction can preserve both integrity and collaboration.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: An argument cites only statements supporting its view and ignores directly relevant qualifications in the same source. What is the key weakness?
options: Qualifications never affect interpretation
The argument is valid if confidently delivered
The selection may distort the source's meaning
Short quotations are always false
questions.answer: The selection may distort the source's meaning
questions.explanation: Relevant qualifications can change the scope of a claim and must be considered.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A project causes harm that could reasonably have been identified during planning. Why is saying We did not intend harm incomplete?
options: Planning removes every possible uncertainty
Responsibility includes considering foreseeable consequences before acting
Intentions never matter at all
Every unexpected outcome is automatically blameworthy
questions.answer: Responsibility includes considering foreseeable consequences before acting
questions.explanation: The curriculum's pre-action responsibility includes assessing likely consequences, not intention alone.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A fundraiser uses deceptive claims to attract donations for a beneficial project. Which analysis is strongest?
options: A beneficial end does not make deceptive means acceptable
The donation total alone determines ethical quality
Any charitable label authorises misinformation
Donors' questions should be discouraged to protect the project
questions.answer: A beneficial end does not make deceptive means acceptable
questions.explanation: Ethical evaluation concerns the method as well as the intended benefit.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A false public accusation is privately withdrawn, but the original audience still believes it. What remains unresolved?
options: Whether the withdrawal used enough words
Whether the accusation attracted attention
Whether the accused knows the author's name
The public effect of the misinformation
questions.answer: The public effect of the misinformation
questions.explanation: Repair should address the audience and harm created, not just the author's private change of mind.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A person issues a sweeping religious judgement on an unfamiliar issue without studying relevant evidence. What is the most responsible alternative?
options: Treat personal confidence as sufficient evidence
Copy whichever judgement is most widely shared
Acknowledge the limit of knowledge and seek qualified analysis
Choose the harshest answer to avoid uncertainty
questions.answer: Acknowledge the limit of knowledge and seek qualified analysis
questions.explanation: Recognising one's limits prevents unsupported certainty from substituting for informed judgement.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: Two treasurers spend the same amount on an authorised purpose, but only one keeps verifiable records. Why do records matter?
options: They prove that no error can ever occur
They allow entrusted spending to be checked and explained
They make every possible decision automatically ethical
They replace the need for authorisation
questions.answer: They allow entrusted spending to be checked and explained
questions.explanation: Accountability requires an accessible basis for checking how a trust was fulfilled.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A transaction uses polite language while concealing the same unfair terms as before. What should evaluation focus on?
options: The actual terms and conduct, not wording alone
The politeness as conclusive proof of fairness
The length of the receipt
Whether the seller uses familiar phrases
questions.answer: The actual terms and conduct, not wording alone
questions.explanation: Ethical substance cannot be established solely by changing presentation.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A committee applies strict rules to strangers but overlooks identical conduct by friends. What principle is compromised?
options: The value of keeping records
The need for clear meeting times
The possibility of disagreement
Impartiality in applying relevant standards
questions.answer: Impartiality in applying relevant standards
questions.explanation: Changing standards because of personal relationships undermines fair treatment.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student takes reasonable precautions, but an unforeseeable event still disrupts a project. What distinction matters?
options: Good planning guarantees success
Uncertainty removes the duty to plan
Responsible preparation differs from control over every outcome
Any disruption proves there was no preparation
questions.answer: Responsible preparation differs from control over every outcome
questions.explanation: A person can act responsibly without being able to determine every external event.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student applies a conclusion from one case to another solely because both have the same label. What further comparison is needed?
options: Whether both stories are short
Whether the relevant facts and reasoning are actually similar
Whether the labels have the same number of letters
Whether the first case is more famous
questions.answer: Whether the relevant facts and reasoning are actually similar
questions.explanation: A sound comparison depends on relevant similarities, not superficial naming.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A charity can document its work without displaying identifiable recipients in distress. Why prefer that approach when it meets the same need?
options: It can provide accountability while respecting recipients' dignity
Accountability always requires public exposure
Recipients' privacy is irrelevant to charitable work
Documentation should be avoided altogether
questions.answer: It can provide accountability while respecting recipients' dignity
questions.explanation: Evidence of responsible work and respect for the people assisted can be pursued together.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A small, correctable classroom error leads to a response that creates much greater avoidable harm. What should be reassessed?
options: Whether every error deserves the strongest possible response
Whether correction should always be abandoned
Whether harm becomes beneficial when called discipline
Whether the response is proportionate to the issue and its consequences
questions.answer: Whether the response is proportionate to the issue and its consequences
questions.explanation: Reasoned judgement considers the scale and consequences of a response as well as its aim.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A speaker's account is emotionally moving but conflicts with verified facts. What is the sound approach?
options: Assume moving accounts are always false
Ignore every factual question to avoid disagreement
Respect the emotion while checking the factual claims
Treat emotion as a substitute for evidence
questions.answer: Respect the emotion while checking the factual claims
questions.explanation: Empathy and factual scrutiny can coexist; emotional impact alone does not establish truth.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: After correcting an error, a team changes its checking process to prevent recurrence. Why is this stronger than an apology alone?
options: It transfers responsibility to the checking form
It combines acknowledgement with practical prevention
It guarantees that no future mistake is possible
It removes the need to repair present harm
questions.answer: It combines acknowledgement with practical prevention
questions.explanation: Accountability can include repairing consequences and improving the process that allowed the error.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student praises openness in others but conceals a relevant mistake in their own report. What does a consistent ethical assessment require?
options: Assume a useful report cannot contain an ethical failure
Apply the same standard of honesty to the student's own conduct
Judge only other people's reports
Treat personal embarrassment as proof that concealment is right
questions.answer: Apply the same standard of honesty to the student's own conduct
questions.explanation: An ethical standard loses consistency when a person exempts their own relevant conduct without justification.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A committee invites comments only after an irreversible decision is made and calls this consultation. What is missing?
options: A meaningful opportunity for relevant views to influence the decision
A larger decorative notice about the completed decision
A guarantee that every view will be adopted
A requirement that nobody disagree
questions.answer: A meaningful opportunity for relevant views to influence the decision
questions.explanation: Consultation is meaningful when informed contributions can be considered before the decision is settled.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: An organiser delegates a purchasing task within an agreed budget and purpose. The delegate finds a cheaper unsuitable item. Why is price alone insufficient?
options: Any saving automatically fulfils the trust
The delegate gains ownership of all unused funds
A budget forbids comparing quality
The entrusted purpose and suitability still constrain the decision
questions.answer: The entrusted purpose and suitability still constrain the decision
questions.explanation: Acting within a trust means serving its authorised purpose, not optimising one measure while defeating that purpose.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: A student corrects an inaccurate instruction but knows some readers still have the old version. What further step addresses the remaining risk?
options: Blame readers for using the version originally provided
Delete the record of the instruction without informing anyone
Notify affected readers through an appropriate correction
Assume editing one copy removes every consequence
questions.answer: Notify affected readers through an appropriate correction
questions.explanation: Repair should consider how earlier information continues to affect people and take reasonable steps to prevent further harm.

questions.subject: Islamic Education
questions.q: Two projects have the same beneficial aim, but only one uses truthful evidence and respects entrusted resources. Why does the method matter?
options: Any benefit cancels all duties toward other people
A worthwhile aim does not by itself justify every means used
Shared intentions guarantee identical ethical conduct
Methods matter only if the project receives publicity
questions.answer: A worthwhile aim does not by itself justify every means used
questions.explanation: Ethical evaluation considers how an aim is pursued alongside the aim itself and its consequences.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every member of set A is also in B, but B has extra members. Which statement follows?
options: A and B are disjoint
B is a proper subset of A
A equals B
A is a proper subset of B
questions.answer: A is a proper subset of B
questions.explanation: A is contained in B without being equal to it.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A real-valued rule contains the term 1/(x-3). Which input must be excluded?
questions.explanation: At x = 3 the denominator is zero, so the expression is undefined.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The graph of y = f(x) is changed to y = f(x)+4. What changes?
options: Every point moves upward by four units
Every point moves right by four units
All slopes double
The domain necessarily shrinks
questions.answer: Every point moves upward by four units
questions.explanation: Adding a constant to the output produces a vertical translation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An inequality is multiplied on both sides by a negative number. What must change?
options: The inequality becomes an equality
Only the larger side is multiplied
The inequality direction reverses
Both sides become zero
questions.answer: The inequality direction reverses
questions.explanation: Multiplication by a negative number reverses order on the number line.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An angle is increased by one full turn. What happens to its sine and cosine?
options: Both become zero
Both stay the same
Both change sign
Sine doubles while cosine stays fixed
questions.answer: Both stay the same
questions.explanation: Sine and cosine are periodic with a full-turn period.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A sequence increases by the same amount at every step. What feature does its term-number graph have?
options: A continuously doubling slope
A vertical line
A repeating circle
A constant slope
questions.answer: A constant slope
questions.explanation: A constant difference makes the term a linear function of its index.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A positive quantity grows by the same percentage each year. Which model is appropriate?
options: A fixed value with no change
A sequence with constant second difference necessarily
Geometric growth
A constant additive increase
questions.answer: Geometric growth
questions.explanation: Repeated multiplication by a fixed factor produces a geometric sequence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In expanding (1+x)^n for a positive integer n, why is the constant term 1?
options: It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
Every term contains x
The exponents must all be zero
All coefficients are equal to one
questions.answer: It comes from choosing 1 from every factor
questions.explanation: Only the product of all constant choices contributes to the x-to-the-zero term.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two distinct nonvertical lines have the same slope. What follows?
options: They are perpendicular
They meet exactly once
They must pass through the origin
They are parallel
questions.answer: They are parallel
questions.explanation: Equal slopes give the same direction; distinct intercepts keep the lines separate.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A point moves so its distances from two fixed points have a constant sum greater than their separation. What path results?
options: A parabola with that same definition
An ellipse
A hyperbola
A straight line in all cases
questions.answer: An ellipse
questions.explanation: An ellipse is defined by a constant sum of distances to two foci.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two vectors have equal magnitudes and opposite directions. What is their sum?
options: The zero vector
A vector twice as long
A unit vector
A scalar equal to their common magnitude
questions.answer: The zero vector
questions.explanation: Opposite equal vectors cancel component by component.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Values of f(x) approach 5 as x approaches 2, but f(2) is defined as 9. What is the limit at 2?
options: It must not exist
questions.explanation: A limit concerns nearby values, not the separately assigned value at the point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A graph has a jump at x = a. Why is the function not continuous there?
options: Its domain must contain only integers
Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
Its value must be negative
Its slope must be positive
questions.answer: Nearby values do not approach one common value matching f(a)
questions.explanation: Continuity requires the two-sided limit to exist and equal the function value.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A differentiable function has positive derivative throughout an interval. What does this imply?
options: Its values are all positive
It is constant
It must be linear
It is increasing on the interval
questions.answer: It is increasing on the interval
questions.explanation: Positive derivative gives increasing function values, regardless of their signs.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A nonnegative rate of water inflow is graphed against time. What does area under the graph represent?
options: The tank's initial volume alone
The elapsed time squared
Total water added over that time
The highest flow rate
questions.answer: Total water added over that time
questions.explanation: Integrating a rate over time gives the accumulated quantity.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A survey measures a random sample of students to estimate the whole school's mean journey time. What is the sample mean used as?
options: An estimate of the population mean
A guaranteed exact value for every student's journey
The population size
Proof that all journeys take equally long
questions.answer: An estimate of the population mean
questions.explanation: A sample statistic provides an estimate of a population parameter, with sampling uncertainty.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A matrix has two rows and three columns. Why cannot it be added directly to a three-by-two matrix?
options: Only square matrices can ever be added
Every entry must be positive
Their entries must first be determinants
Matrix addition requires matching dimensions
questions.answer: Matrix addition requires matching dimensions
questions.explanation: Elementwise addition requires corresponding entries in matrices of the same shape.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two events are mutually exclusive. What is impossible in one trial?
options: Their probabilities adding to less than one
Both occurring together
Either event occurring
Neither event occurring
questions.answer: Both occurring together
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events have an empty intersection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A bag contains red and blue counters. You learn the chosen counter is red. What happens to the relevant sample space?
options: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
It expands to all possible bags
Every original outcome remains equally relevant
It contains no outcomes
questions.answer: It is restricted to outcomes consistent with red
questions.explanation: Conditioning restricts attention to outcomes satisfying the given information.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A scatter plot shows taller plants tending to have greater mass. What does a positive association establish by itself?
options: Every plant lies exactly on one straight line
Mass cannot influence any other measurement
Higher values tend to occur together
Height alone has been proved to cause all mass differences
questions.answer: Higher values tend to occur together
questions.explanation: Association describes the pattern in paired observations and alone does not establish causation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A student belongs to A or B, but not both. Which membership condition describes this?
options: Membership in the universal set only
Membership in their symmetric difference
Membership in their intersection
Membership in neither set
questions.answer: Membership in their symmetric difference
questions.explanation: The symmetric difference contains elements belonging to exactly one of the two sets.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two machines act in sequence: the first doubles an input, the second adds three. Why can reversing them change the result?
options: Addition always occurs before multiplication in any real process
Both machines must produce zero
The first machine has no output
The operations need not commute
questions.answer: The operations need not commute
questions.explanation: Doubling after adding three also doubles the added amount, unlike adding it afterward.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A quadratic's discriminant changes from positive to negative as a parameter varies. What changes?
options: Its leading coefficient must become zero
Every coefficient becomes negative
Two distinct real roots become no real roots
No real roots become two distinct real roots
questions.answer: Two distinct real roots become no real roots
questions.explanation: The discriminant's sign determines whether the roots are real and distinct, repeated, or nonreal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A sine equation has one solution in the first quadrant. Why can another occur in the second quadrant?
options: Supplementary angles have equal sine
Sine is one-to-one over a full turn
Cosine is positive in both quadrants
Every angle has the same sine
questions.answer: Supplementary angles have equal sine
questions.explanation: Reflection across the vertical axis preserves the unit-circle y-coordinate.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A complex number is multiplied by its conjugate. Why is the result real and nonnegative?
options: The imaginary part is always zero before multiplication
Conjugation changes its real part's sign
All complex products are nonnegative
It equals the square of its modulus
questions.answer: It equals the square of its modulus
questions.explanation: The imaginary cross terms cancel, leaving the sum of the squared real and imaginary parts.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A geometric sequence has ratio between zero and one. Why can the infinite sum be finite?
options: The terms eventually become negative
Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
There are only finitely many terms
Every term is zero
questions.answer: Later terms shrink sufficiently rapidly
questions.explanation: For absolute ratio below one, partial sums approach a finite limit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two committee roles are distinct. Why does assigning the same two people in exchanged roles create a different outcome?
options: The role assignment is part of the outcome
The membership becomes a different size
One person disappears
All arrangements are unordered
questions.answer: The role assignment is part of the outcome
questions.explanation: When positions or roles matter, permutations distinguish assignments with the same members.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two points lie on the same line parallel to another line. How do their perpendicular distances to the other line compare?
options: One distance must be zero
Distances depend only on x-coordinate
They are equal
The point farther right is always closer
questions.answer: They are equal
questions.explanation: Parallel lines remain a constant perpendicular distance apart.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A line touches a circle at one point. How does it relate to the radius through that point?
options: It has the same length as the radius
It is perpendicular to the radius
It is parallel to the radius
It passes through the centre
questions.answer: It is perpendicular to the radius
questions.explanation: The tangent at a circle point is perpendicular to the radius there.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two nonzero vectors have zero dot product. What does this imply?
options: They are parallel in the same direction
They are equal
Their cross product must also be zero
They are perpendicular
questions.answer: They are perpendicular
questions.explanation: The dot product is proportional to the cosine of the angle, which is zero at a right angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two lines in three-dimensional space do not meet and are not parallel. What is possible?
options: They are the same line
Their direction vectors are zero
They are skew
They must lie in one plane
questions.answer: They are skew
questions.explanation: Skew lines are nonparallel, nonintersecting lines in different planes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The graph of absolute value of x has a sharp corner at zero. What is true there?
options: It is continuous but not differentiable
It is differentiable but not continuous
It has an infinite function value
It has the same tangent slope from both sides
questions.answer: It is continuous but not differentiable
questions.explanation: The left and right slopes differ although the function has no discontinuity.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function is increasing but its slope is becoming smaller. Which combination can describe it?
options: Negative first derivative and positive second derivative
Both derivatives negative necessarily
Zero first derivative throughout
Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.answer: Positive first derivative and negative second derivative
questions.explanation: Increasing values require positive slope, while decreasing slope indicates concavity down.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A velocity-time graph has regions above and below the time axis. What does its signed integral represent?
options: Final acceleration
Net displacement
Total distance in every case
Maximum speed
questions.answer: Net displacement
questions.explanation: Positive and negative velocities contribute opposite signed displacements.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: F(x) is the area accumulated under a continuous function f from a fixed starting point to x. What does F'(x) measure?
options: The current value f(x)
The total area squared
Only the starting value of f
Always zero
questions.answer: The current value f(x)
questions.explanation: The derivative of accumulated area recovers the instantaneous integrand.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Matrices A and B can be multiplied in both orders. Why need AB not equal BA?
options: Both products must be undefined
All matrices represent the same transformation
Matrix multiplication generally depends on order
Only negative entries cause noncommutativity
questions.answer: Matrix multiplication generally depends on order
questions.explanation: Composing linear transformations in different orders can give different results.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two linear equations describe the same line. What is their solution set?
options: One point chosen by the larger coefficient
Infinitely many points on that line
No points
Exactly two points
questions.answer: Infinitely many points on that line
questions.explanation: Dependent equations impose the same condition rather than two independent constraints.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two counters are drawn without replacement from a mixed bag. Why can the second colour depend on the first?
options: The colours physically transform
All second draws are independent by definition
The first counter returns automatically
The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.answer: The bag's composition changes after the first draw
questions.explanation: Removing a counter changes the proportions remaining for the next selection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every value in a data set increases by the same constant. What happens to variance?
options: It becomes zero
It doubles
It stays unchanged
It rises by that constant
questions.answer: It stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The mean shifts by the same amount, leaving deviations from the mean unchanged.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A plot of log y against x is a straight line with positive slope. Which model for positive y is supported?
options: Exponential growth in x
A fixed additive increase in y per unit x
A constant value of y
A negative probability model
questions.answer: Exponential growth in x
questions.explanation: Taking logarithms turns an exponential relationship into a linear one; positive slope represents growth.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: To disprove the statement 'Every positive integer has property P', what is sufficient?
options: Many integers having P
One negative integer lacking P
No tested counterexample
One positive integer lacking P
questions.answer: One positive integer lacking P
questions.explanation: A single counterexample within the stated domain disproves a universal claim.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A piecewise function has equal left and right limits at a joining point, but its assigned value differs. What repairs continuity there?
options: Set the derivative to one without changing values
Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
Change every nearby value to zero
Remove both intervals entirely
questions.answer: Redefine the point value to equal the common limit
questions.explanation: A removable discontinuity is fixed by matching the point value to its existing limit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An upward-opening quadratic has two distinct real roots. Where is it negative?
options: Strictly between the roots
Outside both roots
Everywhere
Nowhere
questions.answer: Strictly between the roots
questions.explanation: The parabola lies below the axis between its crossings and above it outside them.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Multiplying a nonzero complex number by i changes its plane representation how?
options: Reflection only across the real axis
A quarter-turn clockwise with doubled modulus
A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
A doubling of modulus without rotation
questions.answer: A quarter-turn anticlockwise with unchanged modulus
questions.explanation: Multiplication by i adds an angle of pi over two and has modulus one.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A series has terms that approach zero. Why does that alone not prove convergence?
options: A zero term forces every later term to vanish
The partial sums may still grow without bound
Every such series is finite
Terms approaching zero must alternate
questions.answer: The partial sums may still grow without bound
questions.explanation: Vanishing terms are necessary but not sufficient; the harmonic series is a standard counterexample.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair coin has produced several heads in independent tosses. Why is tails not made more likely on the next toss?
options: Tails becomes impossible after enough heads
The coin remembers its previous states
A balancing sequence is guaranteed immediately
The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
questions.answer: The past sequence does not change the next toss's probability
questions.explanation: Independent trials retain the same probability regardless of previous outcomes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two lines have proportional x and y coefficients but nonproportional constants in their equations. What follows?
options: They intersect at the origin necessarily
They are perpendicular
They are distinct parallel lines
They are identical lines
questions.answer: They are distinct parallel lines
questions.explanation: Matching coefficient ratios give the same direction, while incompatible constants prevent intersection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A method produces 95% confidence intervals in repeated random sampling. What does 95% describe?
options: The long-run proportion of constructed intervals containing the fixed parameter
The proportion of individual observations inside every interval
A guarantee that this one interval contains exactly 95% of the population
The probability that the already observed sample mean will change
questions.answer: The long-run proportion of constructed intervals containing the fixed parameter
questions.explanation: Frequentist coverage concerns the procedure across repeated samples, not a probability distribution assigned to the fixed parameter.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Three vectors have zero scalar triple product. What geometric conclusion follows?
options: They necessarily form a cube
They are all unit vectors
They are mutually perpendicular and nonzero
They are coplanar or linearly dependent
questions.answer: They are coplanar or linearly dependent
questions.explanation: The scalar triple product measures signed parallelepiped volume, which vanishes for dependence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function oscillates between values near -1 and 1 arbitrarily close to a point without narrowing its range. What happens to its limit there?
options: The limit equals the point's assigned value
No single limit exists
The limit must be zero by averaging
The limit must be one
questions.answer: No single limit exists
questions.explanation: Persistent full-amplitude oscillation prevents values from approaching one number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A function is differentiable at an interior point. Which conclusion is guaranteed?
options: It is continuous there
Its derivative is positive there
It is locally linear exactly
It has a local extremum there
questions.answer: It is continuous there
questions.explanation: Differentiability implies continuity, but does not determine slope sign or the presence of an extremum.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For f(x)=x cubed, the derivative is zero at zero. Why is zero not a local maximum or minimum?
options: The derivative is undefined there
The function is constant nearby
The function keeps increasing through it
The function is discontinuous there
questions.answer: The function keeps increasing through it
questions.explanation: A zero derivative alone is insufficient; the function increases on both sides of the stationary point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A continuous odd function is integrated from -a to a. Why is the integral zero?
options: Every antiderivative is constant
Opposite signed contributions cancel
The function must be zero everywhere
The interval has zero length
questions.answer: Opposite signed contributions cancel
questions.explanation: Odd symmetry gives equal-magnitude contributions of opposite sign on symmetric intervals.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A line predicting y from x minimises vertical residuals. Why should its algebraic inverse not automatically be used as the best line predicting x from y?
options: Every regression line has slope one
Regression lines cannot be rearranged algebraically
The original correlation becomes zero on exchanging axes
The reversed prediction problem minimises different residuals
questions.answer: The reversed prediction problem minimises different residuals
questions.explanation: Least-squares regression is directional; switching response and predictor changes which errors are minimised.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: AB equals the identity for square matrices of the same size. What follows?
options: B must equal A
A's determinant is zero
B is the inverse of A
A must have all positive entries
questions.answer: B is the inverse of A
questions.explanation: A square matrix with an inverse product is nonsingular, and B is its inverse.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A square coefficient matrix is invertible. What follows for a linear system with that matrix and any right-hand side?
options: There is exactly one solution
There are always no solutions
There are always infinitely many solutions
Only a zero right-hand side is allowed
questions.answer: There is exactly one solution
questions.explanation: Multiplying by the inverse determines a unique solution vector.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rare condition has a test with some false positives. Why need a positive result not make the condition highly likely?
options: Test accuracy is irrelevant
A positive result proves the condition is absent
Rare conditions cannot be tested
The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.answer: The low base rate can make false positives numerous relative to true positives
questions.explanation: The posterior probability depends on both test performance and the prior prevalence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two random variables have finite means but are dependent. Which statement still holds?
options: They must have identical distributions
The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
Their variances always add without a covariance term
Their product mean always equals the product of their means
questions.answer: The mean of their sum equals the sum of their means
questions.explanation: Linearity of expectation does not require independence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Every observation is multiplied by a constant c. Why is variance multiplied by c squared?
options: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
The mean is always unchanged
Variance counts observations without using values
Only negative constants affect variance
questions.answer: Each deviation is scaled by c before being squared
questions.explanation: Variance averages squared deviations, so scaling values squares the scale factor.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A club contains many more beginners than experts. Experts are more likely to pass a test. Why can most passers still be beginners?
options: Conditional probabilities cannot differ between groups
Passing changes a beginner into an expert by definition
Group sizes as well as within-group pass rates determine passer counts
The experts' pass rate must be lower
questions.answer: Group sizes as well as within-group pass rates determine passer counts
questions.explanation: A larger starting group can contribute more successful people despite a lower individual success probability.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A learner wants to improve distance-running endurance. Which training best matches that aim?
options: Only practising a standing balance pose
Only practising one maximal throw
Only memorising competition rules
Progressive sustained aerobic activity
questions.answer: Progressive sustained aerobic activity
questions.explanation: Endurance training should develop the ability to sustain activity over time.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A comfortable exercise routine no longer challenges a learner. What principle supports a planned, gradual increase in demand?
options: Randomly changing every session
Avoiding all recovery
Progressive overload
Complete inactivity
questions.answer: Progressive overload
questions.explanation: Adaptation requires an appropriate challenge that progresses with capacity.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Why begin a sports session with gradually increasing movement?
options: To produce maximum fatigue immediately
To prepare the body for the activity ahead
To guarantee that no injury can occur
To replace every skill practice
questions.answer: To prepare the body for the activity ahead
questions.explanation: A gradual warm-up prepares movement and physiological responses without guaranteeing injury prevention.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Why include recovery between demanding training sessions?
options: Adaptation and restoration need time
Recovery permanently removes fitness
Every rest period causes immediate complete detraining
Muscles improve only during exhaustion
questions.answer: Adaptation and restoration need time
questions.explanation: Training stress and recovery together support adaptation.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A player changes direction quickly to follow an opponent. Which ability is most directly demonstrated?
options: Maximum static strength alone
Flexibility alone
Resting pulse rate
Agility
questions.answer: Agility
questions.explanation: Agility involves controlled changes of direction in response to the task.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A gymnast widens the base of support while holding a stationary position. What usually happens to stability?
options: It depends only on clothing colour
The centre of mass must leave the body
It increases if other conditions stay the same
It always disappears
questions.answer: It increases if other conditions stay the same
questions.explanation: A wider base provides a larger area within which the centre of mass can remain supported.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: During a controlled lowering of a weight, the active muscle lengthens. What kind of action is this?
options: Only a nerve reflex without muscle activity
Eccentric contraction
Concentric contraction
No muscular force
questions.answer: Eccentric contraction
questions.explanation: An eccentric action produces force while the muscle lengthens.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: During moderate running, breathing and heart rate rise. What is the main functional reason?
options: To support increased gas exchange and delivery to working tissues
To stop blood reaching muscles
To eliminate the need for cellular respiration
To reduce oxygen delivery to zero
questions.answer: To support increased gas exchange and delivery to working tissues
