questions.explanation: Working tissues require greater transport of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Two students compare shuttle-run results from different course lengths. What should they do first?
options: Assume the shorter course is always harder
Compare only their shoe brands
Ignore course length
Use the same test protocol before comparing results
questions.answer: Use the same test protocol before comparing results
questions.explanation: A meaningful comparison requires consistent conditions and procedures.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A coach says, Keep your eyes on the target during the pass. Why is this more useful than Do better?
options: It describes the player's personality
It removes the need to practise
It identifies a specific action to adjust
It guarantees immediate mastery
questions.answer: It identifies a specific action to adjust
questions.explanation: Specific feedback gives the learner a clear behaviour to work on.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Two defenders keep moving toward the same attacker, leaving space open. What is a useful response?
options: Both follow the ball regardless of team shape
Agree clear responsibilities and communicate switches
Stop communicating altogether
Blame the quieter player after each play
questions.answer: Agree clear responsibilities and communicate switches
questions.explanation: Coordinated responsibilities reduce duplicated coverage and unattended space.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A player notices damaged equipment before a lesson. What is the appropriate action?
options: Report it and avoid using it until checked
Hide the damage to keep the lesson moving
Test it at maximum force
Give it to a less experienced player
questions.answer: Report it and avoid using it until checked
questions.explanation: Reporting a hazard lets the responsible adult assess it before further use.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Two drinks have different bottle sizes. How can their sugar concentration be compared fairly?
options: Compare only sugar per bottle
Compare the size of their logos
Assume the larger bottle is less concentrated
Compare sugar per equal volume
questions.answer: Compare sugar per equal volume
questions.explanation: A common volume separates concentration from the amount in the container.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Which goal is easiest to evaluate after a month?
options: Always feel perfect
Never make a mistake
Complete the agreed training sessions and compare a standard endurance test
Become the best at everything
questions.answer: Complete the agreed training sessions and compare a standard endurance test
questions.explanation: A defined process and consistent outcome measure allow progress to be checked.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A learner needs a different way to perform a catching task. Which approach preserves the learning aim?
options: Replace feedback with public comparisons
Adapt equipment or rules while practising the same underlying skill
Exclude the learner from all practice
Assume the learner cannot improve
questions.answer: Adapt equipment or rules while practising the same underlying skill
questions.explanation: An appropriate adaptation can enable participation in the intended skill.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A working muscle's ATP demand rises. Why must ATP be continually regenerated?
options: ATP cannot be broken down
All ATP is stored permanently in DNA
ATP contains no transferable energy
Cells hold only a limited immediately available ATP supply
questions.answer: Cells hold only a limited immediately available ATP supply
questions.explanation: ATP is rapidly used and resynthesized to support continuing cellular work.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Alveoli have thin walls and a large total surface area. What does this arrangement improve?
options: Filtration of red blood cells
Production of bone tissue
Diffusion of respiratory gases
Storage of undigested food
questions.answer: Diffusion of respiratory gases
questions.explanation: A short diffusion distance and large surface support rapid oxygen and carbon-dioxide exchange.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Valves in veins close when blood begins moving backward. What function does this serve?
options: Separating plasma from cells
Maintaining one-way flow toward the heart
Increasing blood's oxygen content directly
Producing new red blood cells
questions.answer: Maintaining one-way flow toward the heart
questions.explanation: Venous valves prevent backflow, assisting return of blood under low pressure.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Blood glucose rises after a meal. In a healthy feedback system, what response helps lower it?
options: Increased insulin secretion
Increased glucose release from the liver only
Complete inhibition of cellular glucose uptake
Destruction of all glucagon receptors
questions.answer: Increased insulin secretion
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and storage, helping restore the regulated range.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A muscle pulls on a bone across a joint. Why is another muscle needed for the opposite movement?
options: Bones contract independently
A single tendon can reverse its attachment
Muscles have no force when shortening
Muscles actively pull rather than push
questions.answer: Muscles actively pull rather than push
questions.explanation: Antagonistic muscles create opposing joint movements by pulling in different directions.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A programme adds demanding sessions every day while performance and motivation decline. Which factor should be reviewed?
options: Whether training demand exceeds recovery
Whether the equipment has matching colours
Whether recovery can be removed completely
Whether every session must become harder
questions.answer: Whether training demand exceeds recovery
questions.explanation: Declining performance with rising load can indicate an imbalance between demand and recovery.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A swimmer improves swimming endurance but shows limited improvement in sprint starts. Why is this plausible?
options: Endurance training prevents all skill learning
Fitness transfers equally to every task
Sprint starts contain no physical skill
Different tasks require partly different adaptations
questions.answer: Different tasks require partly different adaptations
questions.explanation: Sustained swimming and explosive starts place different demands on the body and technique.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Why alternate work and recovery periods in an interval session?
options: To remove all physiological demand
To guarantee the same adaptation for every athlete
To manage repeated efforts at a chosen intensity
To make intensity impossible to control
questions.answer: To manage repeated efforts at a chosen intensity
questions.explanation: Recovery intervals allow planned repetition and control of demanding efforts.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Holding a small weight farther from the elbow makes the same arm position harder to maintain. Why?
options: The elbow becomes frictionless
The weight creates a larger moment about the elbow
The weight's mass has increased
Gravity has stopped acting
questions.answer: The weight creates a larger moment about the elbow
questions.explanation: A greater perpendicular distance increases the moment produced by the same force.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Why can flexing the knees during a controlled landing reduce average impact force for the same momentum change?
options: It increases the time over which the body slows
It removes all momentum before contact
It increases body mass
It prevents gravity from acting
questions.answer: It increases the time over which the body slows
questions.explanation: For the same impulse, extending stopping time reduces average force.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A short maximal sprint and a long steady run emphasise different energy contributions. Which conclusion is sound?
options: Only one pathway ever operates at a time
Long runs require no ATP
Sprints cannot use stored chemical energy
The relative contribution of energy pathways depends on intensity and duration
questions.answer: The relative contribution of energy pathways depends on intensity and duration
questions.explanation: Energy systems overlap, but their relative contributions vary with the task.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A learner's repeated balance-test scores vary greatly under otherwise similar conditions. What is the main concern?
options: The learner's height has certainly changed
The highest score must represent every attempt
The test may have low repeatability
The test must measure aerobic capacity
questions.answer: The test may have low repeatability
questions.explanation: Large unexplained variation weakens confidence in consistent measurement.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A coach uses a spelling test to rank football dribbling skill. What is wrong with the assessment?
options: Dribbling cannot be assessed
It does not directly measure the intended skill
It necessarily takes too little time
All written tests are unreliable
questions.answer: It does not directly measure the intended skill
questions.explanation: Validity concerns whether a measure supports the intended interpretation.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A learner relies on instructions after every movement and struggles alone. What change could support independence?
options: Gradually encourage self-evaluation and reduce constant prompting
Increase dependence on continuous commands forever
Remove all practice opportunities
Give only unrelated praise
questions.answer: Gradually encourage self-evaluation and reduce constant prompting
questions.explanation: Guided self-evaluation can help learners recognise and correct their own performance.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A player can pass accurately in isolation but struggles when opponents move. What practice best addresses the gap?
options: Repeat only identical unopposed passes indefinitely
Stop practising passes
Study only the history of the ball
Practise passing in progressively realistic decision situations
questions.answer: Practise passing in progressively realistic decision situations
questions.explanation: Game-like situations add perception and decision demands absent from isolated practice.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A team leads narrowly near the end of a game. Why might it favour controlled possession over risky long passes?
options: Because possession guarantees victory
Because scoring is no longer relevant
To reduce unnecessary loss of possession in that situation
Because long passes are always forbidden
questions.answer: To reduce unnecessary loss of possession in that situation
questions.explanation: Tactical choices depend on time, score and the risk of turnovers.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Two people have the same BMI but different muscle mass. What does this show?
options: Muscle has no mass
BMI alone does not distinguish fat from muscle
They necessarily have identical body composition
BMI directly measures every tissue
questions.answer: BMI alone does not distinguish fat from muscle
questions.explanation: BMI combines height and weight without separating the sources of body mass.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: After training, the same submaximal task requires a lower heart rate under comparable conditions. What is a plausible interpretation?
options: Improved cardiovascular efficiency
Proof that no energy is being used
Evidence that the heart has stopped adapting
Proof of superior fitness in every sport
questions.answer: Improved cardiovascular efficiency
questions.explanation: A trained cardiovascular system may meet the same demand with fewer beats; the observation has a limited scope.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A supplement advertisement promises instant fitness without exercise. What is the strongest first evaluation step?
options: Assume a celebrity endorsement proves it
Judge only the packaging
Treat repeated advertising as a controlled trial
Look for credible evidence and examine the claim's limits
questions.answer: Look for credible evidence and examine the claim's limits
questions.explanation: Evidence and plausible scope matter more than repetition or endorsement.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A captain gives every skilled player practice time but repeatedly excludes beginners. Which change better supports team development?
options: Assign roles only by friendship
Stop giving feedback to anyone
Provide meaningful practice opportunities with appropriate support
Keep beginners watching indefinitely
questions.answer: Provide meaningful practice opportunities with appropriate support
questions.explanation: Participation and suitable challenge allow less experienced players to develop.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Oxygen becomes unavailable to aerobic cells. Why does the mitochondrial electron-transport chain stall?
options: All glycolysis enzymes require oxygen directly
The Krebs cycle becomes a photosynthetic cycle
Its final electron acceptor is missing
Glucose cannot contain carbon anymore
questions.answer: Its final electron acceptor is missing
questions.explanation: Without oxygen accepting electrons, electron carriers cannot be efficiently reoxidised.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Why can fermentation sustain glycolysis when oxygen is absent?
options: It eliminates the need for enzymes
It regenerates NAD+
It produces oxygen for mitochondria
It makes ATP without any substrate
questions.answer: It regenerates NAD+
questions.explanation: Regeneration of NAD+ allows the oxidation step in glycolysis to continue.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Exercising tissue releases more carbon dioxide and becomes more acidic. How can this assist oxygen delivery?
options: Haemoglobin's oxygen affinity decreases locally
Haemoglobin binds oxygen irreversibly
Blood stops flowing to that tissue
Carbon dioxide replaces iron in every haem group
questions.answer: Haemoglobin's oxygen affinity decreases locally
questions.explanation: The Bohr effect promotes oxygen unloading where metabolic activity is high.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: The left ventricle has a thicker muscular wall than the right. What functional difference helps explain this?
options: It receives blood from the body directly through the vena cava
It contains less muscle to reduce pressure
It pumps only into the nearby lungs
It pumps through the higher-resistance systemic circuit
questions.answer: It pumps through the higher-resistance systemic circuit
questions.explanation: Systemic circulation requires greater pressure than pulmonary circulation.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A skeletal muscle sarcomere shortens while actin and myosin filament lengths stay constant. How?
options: Actin converts completely into myosin
The muscle loses all ATP
The filaments slide past each other
Both filaments are chemically dissolved
questions.answer: The filaments slide past each other
questions.explanation: Cross-bridge cycling increases filament overlap without shortening individual filaments.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A class improves after a new training plan, but also receives more practice time. What can be concluded about the plan alone?
options: The plan has been proved ineffective
Its separate effect is not isolated
The plan caused the entire improvement
Extra practice cannot influence performance
questions.answer: Its separate effect is not isolated
questions.explanation: Both changes could contribute, so the design does not isolate the plan's effect.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: An outdoor endurance test is repeated in much hotter weather. Why interpret the score change cautiously?
options: Environmental conditions can affect performance independently of fitness
Temperature changes the distance printed on the track
Fitness cannot change over time
Hot weather guarantees a better score
questions.answer: Environmental conditions can affect performance independently of fitness
questions.explanation: A change in testing conditions complicates attribution to training or fitness alone.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A player completes a skill faster but makes more errors. How should progress be evaluated?
options: Use speed alone in every sport
Ignore errors if movement looks confident
Assume any increase in speed means mastery
Assess both speed and accuracy against the task's demands
questions.answer: Assess both speed and accuracy against the task's demands
questions.explanation: Skill quality depends on successful execution as well as time taken.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A jump result improves by less than the measuring device's usual variation. What is the most defensible interpretation?
options: The device must be deliberately misleading
The learner has certainly become less fit
The apparent improvement may not exceed measurement noise
The improvement proves a major adaptation
questions.answer: The apparent improvement may not exceed measurement noise
questions.explanation: A change smaller than typical measurement variation is uncertain without stronger evidence.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Two learners follow the same workload, but one recovers well and the other struggles. What follows?
options: Recovery differences are irrelevant to planning
The same external workload can create different internal demands
Identical schedules guarantee identical adaptation
The struggling learner should always double the load
questions.answer: The same external workload can create different internal demands
questions.explanation: Capacity and context differ, so responses should inform individual adjustments.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A skater pulls the arms inward while spinning with little external torque. Why does rotation speed increase?
options: Moment of inertia decreases while angular momentum is approximately conserved
Angular momentum must vanish
Body mass increases
Gravity supplies a large twisting force
questions.answer: Moment of inertia decreases while angular momentum is approximately conserved
questions.explanation: Reducing the distribution of mass away from the axis increases angular speed for the same angular momentum.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A player lowers the centre of mass for stability, but must then jump quickly. What should guide the movement choice?
options: Assume the lowest possible position is always best
Ignore the opponent and task
Use one posture for every situation
Balance stability needs with the demands of the next action
questions.answer: Balance stability needs with the demands of the next action
questions.explanation: A stable posture can involve a trade-off with movement readiness depending on the action required.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A player executes well in drills but chooses poor options in matches. Which assessment would best identify the problem?
options: Count only training attendance
Repeat a vocabulary test
Observe perception and decisions in representative game situations
Measure only maximum grip strength
questions.answer: Observe perception and decisions in representative game situations
questions.explanation: Match decisions require reading the situation and selecting an action, not just executing a rehearsed movement.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: To compare two training methods, what is especially important besides consistent outcome tests?
options: Selecting only the best result from one group
Comparable starting ability and training exposure
Matching shirt colours
Giving one group much more practice without accounting for it
questions.answer: Comparable starting ability and training exposure
questions.explanation: Baseline and exposure differences can otherwise explain the result attributed to training method.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A coach claims one technique suits every athlete because it worked for a champion. What is the weakness?
options: One successful example does not establish universal suitability
Champions never use effective techniques
Technique cannot be examined scientifically
All individual differences are irrelevant
questions.answer: One successful example does not establish universal suitability
questions.explanation: A single case cannot establish that the method fits different bodies, skills and tasks.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Students who train more also report better wellbeing. Which statement is best supported by this observation alone?
options: Training is the only possible cause
Wellbeing can never influence participation
Every nonparticipant has poor wellbeing
Training and reported wellbeing are associated
questions.answer: Training and reported wellbeing are associated
questions.explanation: An association alone does not exclude reverse causation or other influences.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A team increases tactical practice near a tournament while managing physical load. What is the rationale?
options: The same maximal workload is required daily
Tactics and physical demands are unrelated
Training emphasis can change with the phase and competition demands
Physical preparation becomes permanently unnecessary
questions.answer: Training emphasis can change with the phase and competition demands
questions.explanation: Planning can vary emphasis over time while preserving readiness and recovery.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: An adapted task uses a lighter ball to assess the same throwing technique. What makes the comparison defensible?
options: The lighter ball automatically earns a higher score
The assessment criteria focus on the shared skill and document the adaptation
All scores must be identical
Equipment differences must be hidden
questions.answer: The assessment criteria focus on the shared skill and document the adaptation
questions.explanation: Transparent adaptations can maintain the intended learning target while changing access conditions.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A learner meets every attendance goal but shows little skill improvement. What should be reconsidered?
options: Whether practice quality and outcome measures match the learning goal
Whether attendance alone proves mastery
Whether feedback should be banned
Whether every session should be cancelled
questions.answer: Whether practice quality and outcome measures match the learning goal
questions.explanation: Participation is a process measure; improvement also depends on the content and quality of practice.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A team can exploit an opponent's misunderstanding of an agreed safety rule. Which response best combines fairness and responsibility?
options: Keep the misunderstanding secret to gain advantage
Encourage more confusion
Treat winning as overriding every agreed safeguard
Clarify the rule before continuing play
questions.answer: Clarify the rule before continuing play
questions.explanation: Clarification supports informed, fair participation under the shared rules.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A mitochondrial membrane becomes freely permeable to protons while electron transfer can continue. What happens to ATP synthesis by ATP synthase?
options: It moves into the nucleus
It decreases as the proton gradient dissipates
It increases without limit
It becomes independent of the gradient
questions.answer: It decreases as the proton gradient dissipates
questions.explanation: ATP synthase relies on the proton-motive force; a proton leak uncouples it from electron transport.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A germinating seed mainly oxidises stored fats. Why is its respiratory quotient often below one?
options: Fat oxidation uses more oxygen relative to carbon dioxide released
Fat contains no carbon
Respiration cannot use oxygen in seeds
All carbon dioxide is converted into nitrogen
questions.answer: Fat oxidation uses more oxygen relative to carbon dioxide released
questions.explanation: Reduced lipid molecules require relatively more oxygen, giving CO2 produced divided by O2 consumed below one.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: A stronger stimulus causes more frequent action potentials rather than proportionately taller action potentials in one axon. Why?
options: Axons cannot transmit repeated signals
Stimulus strength changes the genetic code each time
Stronger stimuli eliminate refractory periods
Individual action potentials are all-or-none events
questions.answer: Individual action potentials are all-or-none events
questions.explanation: Stimulus intensity can be encoded by firing frequency while action-potential amplitude remains broadly fixed.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: ATP becomes unavailable in a contracted muscle fibre. Why can cross-bridges remain attached?
options: Myosin is never attached during contraction
Calcium immediately removes every cross-bridge
ATP binding is needed to detach myosin from actin
ATP destroys all actin filaments
questions.answer: ATP binding is needed to detach myosin from actin
questions.explanation: ATP binding releases the myosin head from actin; depletion prevents normal detachment.

questions.subject: Physical & Health Education
questions.q: Blood hormone level is high but target cells lack functional receptors. Why might the expected response be absent?
options: All cells respond identically to every hormone
Hormone presence alone does not ensure signal reception
Hormones act without any molecular interaction
The hormone must instantly turn into DNA
questions.answer: Hormone presence alone does not ensure signal reception
questions.explanation: Target response depends on functional receptors and downstream signalling.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A trolley moves forward while its velocity-time graph slopes downward. What is happening?
options: It is slowing down
It is moving backward
Its acceleration is zero
Its distance travelled is decreasing
questions.answer: It is slowing down
questions.explanation: A downward slope means negative acceleration; with positive velocity this reduces speed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A passenger leans forward when a bus brakes. Why?
options: The seat increases the passenger's speed
The passenger loses mass
The passenger's body tends to keep moving
A forward force from gravity appears
questions.answer: The passenger's body tends to keep moving
questions.explanation: Inertia resists the change from the body's original forward motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A box remains stationary while you push it gently on a rough floor. What balances your push?
options: An upward force from the floor
Static friction
Kinetic friction
The box's weight alone
questions.answer: Static friction
questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to oppose the push until its limiting value is reached.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two carts initially at rest push apart on a frictionless track. What must their momenta do?
options: Have equal velocities
Point in the same direction
Increase the total momentum
Add to zero
questions.answer: Add to zero
questions.explanation: With no external horizontal force, total momentum remains its initial value of zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone moves at constant speed in a circle. Why is it accelerating?
options: Its speed must be increasing
Its kinetic energy must increase
Its velocity changes direction
Its mass changes continuously
questions.answer: Its velocity changes direction
questions.explanation: Velocity includes direction, which changes throughout circular motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A star's thermal spectrum peaks at a shorter wavelength than another star's. What can be inferred about its surface temperature?
options: It is hotter
It is cooler
It must have the same temperature
Its temperature cannot affect the spectrum
questions.answer: It is hotter
questions.explanation: Wien's displacement relation associates shorter peak wavelengths with higher absolute temperatures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sealed hydraulic system has connected pistons of different areas. Why can the larger piston exert more force?
options: Pressure must be larger at the larger piston
The fluid creates extra energy
The smaller piston has no displacement
The same pressure acts over a larger area
questions.answer: The same pressure acts over a larger area
questions.explanation: Transmitted pressure is the same at equal depth, while force equals pressure times area.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ice is melting at its melting point under constant pressure. Why can heat enter without raising temperature?
options: All added energy becomes light
Energy changes the phase
The ice has stopped absorbing energy
Its specific heat becomes zero
questions.answer: Energy changes the phase
questions.explanation: Latent heat changes intermolecular arrangement rather than increasing temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Gas expands and pushes a piston. What energy transfer occurs through the moving piston?
options: The gas does work on its surroundings
The surroundings always do positive work on the gas
The gas necessarily gains internal energy
No energy crosses the boundary
questions.answer: The gas does work on its surroundings
questions.explanation: An outward force acting through the piston's displacement transfers energy as work.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At the extreme position of a mass on an ideal spring, which quantity is zero?
options: Its acceleration magnitude
Its elastic potential energy
Its instantaneous speed
Its restoring force
questions.answer: Its instantaneous speed
questions.explanation: The mass reverses direction at the extreme, where its instantaneous velocity is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cork bobs as a water wave passes. What does this illustrate?
options: The cork must move permanently forward
Energy can travel without the cork travelling with the wave
All water travels at the wave speed
The wave carries no energy
questions.answer: Energy can travel without the cork travelling with the wave
questions.explanation: The disturbance propagates while material particles oscillate about local positions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two initially neutral objects become oppositely charged by rubbing. What was transferred between them?
options: Protons between nuclei
Whole positive nuclei only
Gravitational mass
Electrons
questions.answer: Electrons
questions.explanation: Charge separation in ordinary rubbing results from electron transfer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A positive test charge is released in a uniform electric field, with no other force. Which way does it initially accelerate?
options: Perpendicular to the field
It cannot accelerate
Along the field
Against the field
questions.answer: Along the field
questions.explanation: The electric force on a positive charge points along the electric field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One branch of two resistors in parallel is removed from an ideal battery. What happens to current in the remaining branch?
options: It stays the same
It doubles automatically
It falls to zero
It reverses direction
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: The remaining branch still has the same battery voltage across the same resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metal wire is made longer without changing material, temperature or cross-sectional area. Why does resistance increase?
options: The wire gains a larger cross-section
Its resistivity must decrease
Electrons stop carrying charge
Charge carriers encounter a longer conducting path
questions.answer: Charge carriers encounter a longer conducting path
questions.explanation: For fixed resistivity and area, resistance is proportional to length.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnet is held stationary inside a stationary coil. What induced emf results from this unchanged arrangement?
options: An emf that alternates automatically
Zero
A steady emf set only by magnet strength
An emf that grows with time
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Induction requires changing magnetic flux, not merely the presence of a magnetic field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Why does an ordinary transformer need changing current in its primary coil?
options: It needs changing magnetic flux
Its core must rotate
Direct current has no charge carriers
The secondary must touch the primary
questions.answer: It needs changing magnetic flux
questions.explanation: A changing primary current produces flux changes that induce an emf in the secondary.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens forms an image of a very distant object. Where is the image approximately formed?
options: At the lens centre
On the object's side as a virtual image
At the focal plane
At twice the focal length always
questions.answer: At the focal plane
questions.explanation: Nearly parallel incident rays converge near the principal focal plane.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two coherent light waves meet with crest aligned to crest. What happens locally?
options: Their wavelengths halve
Their amplitudes reinforce
Their frequencies cancel
Their speeds double
questions.answer: Their amplitudes reinforce
questions.explanation: The displacements add constructively when the waves are in phase.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radioactive sample contains fewer undecayed nuclei after one half-life. What happens to its activity?
options: It increases
It stays fixed until the last nucleus decays
It becomes independent of the number of nuclei
It decreases
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Activity is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei for a fixed decay constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A velocity-time graph crosses from positive to negative values. What occurs at the crossing?
options: Its distance travelled returns to zero
Its mass changes sign
The object reverses direction
Its acceleration must be zero
questions.answer: The object reverses direction
questions.explanation: The velocity changes sign, indicating reversal; acceleration is determined by the graph's slope.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two balls are launched horizontally from the same height with different speeds. Ignoring air resistance, which lands first?
options: They land together
The faster ball
The slower ball
The heavier ball regardless of speed
questions.answer: They land together
questions.explanation: Their initial vertical velocities and vertical accelerations are identical.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two touching blocks accelerate together on a smooth floor when one is pushed. Why are their net forces unequal if their masses differ?
options: Contact forces violate Newton's third law
The lighter block has no net force
Their velocities must be different
They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
questions.answer: They share acceleration, so net force is proportional to mass
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives different net forces for different masses at the same acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball moves upward after being thrown, ignoring air resistance. Which description is correct?
options: Gravity does positive work during ascent
Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
Both energies increase
Mechanical energy decreases because speed decreases
questions.answer: Kinetic energy decreases while gravitational potential energy increases
questions.explanation: Gravity converts kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy while total mechanical energy stays constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A skater pulls in their arms while experiencing negligible external torque. Why do they spin faster?
options: Their moment of inertia decreases while angular momentum stays constant
Their angular momentum increases spontaneously
Their mass decreases
Their rotational kinetic energy must remain constant
questions.answer: Their moment of inertia decreases while angular momentum stays constant
questions.explanation: Conservation of angular momentum links smaller moment of inertia to greater angular speed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two satellites have circular orbits around Earth. Why is the lower satellite faster?
options: The higher satellite is beyond gravity
The lower satellite must have greater mass
A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
The lower satellite has no gravitational potential energy
questions.answer: A smaller orbital radius requires a larger circular-orbit speed
questions.explanation: For a circular orbit, speed is proportional to the inverse square root of orbital radius.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Steady incompressible flow enters a narrower section of a pipe. What happens to average flow speed?
options: It must become zero
It increases
It decreases
It stays constant while volume flow increases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Conservation of volume flow requires area times average speed to remain constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vacuum flask reduces heat transfer through its evacuated gap. Which process can still cross that gap?
options: Conduction through air
Convection of trapped gas
Bulk flow of liquid
Thermal radiation
questions.answer: Thermal radiation
questions.explanation: Radiation does not require matter, whereas gas conduction and convection are suppressed by the vacuum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal gas expands adiabatically while doing work. Why does its temperature decrease?
options: Its number of molecules decreases necessarily
Adiabatic expansion means constant temperature
The work comes from its internal energy
Heat flows into it faster than work leaves
questions.answer: The work comes from its internal energy
questions.explanation: With no heat input, work done by the gas reduces its internal energy and temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal spring oscillator's amplitude doubles while its mass and spring constant stay fixed. What happens to its period?
options: It stays the same
It doubles
It halves
It becomes four times larger
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: The ideal spring period depends on mass and stiffness, not amplitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in its second harmonic. What appears in addition to the end nodes?
options: An antinode at its midpoint
No internal nodes
A travelling crest fixed at one end
A node at its midpoint
questions.answer: A node at its midpoint
questions.explanation: The second harmonic contains two loops separated by a central node.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charge moves along an equipotential surface. What work does the electric field do?
options: Work equal to charge times field strength
Zero
Positive for every charge
Negative for every charge
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Electric work depends on the potential difference, which is zero along an equipotential.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An isolated conductor reaches electrostatic equilibrium. Why is its interior electric field zero?
options: Free charges redistribute until the internal field cancels
The conductor contains no electrons
The conductor's potential must be zero
All external electric fields disappear everywhere
questions.answer: Free charges redistribute until the internal field cancels
questions.explanation: A nonzero internal field would keep free charges moving, contradicting electrostatic equilibrium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A real battery supplies a larger current. Why can its terminal voltage fall?
options: External resistance creates charge
The battery's internal current becomes zero
More voltage is lost across its internal resistance
Its emf must instantly become zero
questions.answer: More voltage is lost across its internal resistance
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage during discharge equals emf minus the internal voltage drop.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At a junction, one entering current becomes two outgoing currents. Why must their sum equal the entering current in steady state?
options: Both outgoing currents must be equal
Charge does not accumulate at the junction
Energy is created at the junction
Resistance is always equal in both branches
questions.answer: Charge does not accumulate at the junction
questions.explanation: Current conservation follows from charge conservation when there is no accumulating charge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnet approaching a conducting loop experiences resistance to its motion. What explains this?
options: The loop creates energy from nothing
The loop always attracts every magnetic pole
Induced current cancels the magnet's mass
The induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux
questions.answer: The induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux
questions.explanation: Lenz's law makes the induced effect oppose the flux change, requiring mechanical work.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal capacitor is driven by a sinusoidal supply of unchanged voltage amplitude but higher frequency. What happens to current amplitude?
options: It remains zero
It reverses into direct current
It increases
It decreases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Capacitive reactance decreases as frequency rises, allowing greater current amplitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnifying glass is used with an object inside its focal length. What image does the eye view?
options: An upright magnified virtual image
An inverted reduced real image
A real image at the lens centre
An upright image on a screen behind the lens
questions.answer: An upright magnified virtual image
questions.explanation: A converging lens used inside its focal distance produces an upright enlarged virtual image.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a double-slit experiment, the screen moves farther away while wavelength and slit spacing stay fixed. What happens to fringe spacing?
options: It decreases
It stays fixed
All bright fringes vanish
It increases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Fringe spacing is proportional to the screen distance under the small-angle approximation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A laboratory observes a clock moving steadily at a large fraction of light speed. How does the moving clock's elapsed time compare between two ticks with the lab interval?
options: The moving clock runs backward
Less time elapses on the moving clock
More time elapses on the moving clock
Both intervals must be equal because the clock is mechanical
questions.answer: Less time elapses on the moving clock
questions.explanation: The clock records proper time along its path; the laboratory describes a longer interval between those events.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ruler has a fixed positive zero error. Repeating a length measurement many times gives closely grouped results. What remains unresolved?
options: The systematic offset
Random scatter only
Whether the ruler has markings
The object's physical length changes
questions.answer: The systematic offset
questions.explanation: Repeated readings can improve precision without removing a fixed systematic error.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person stands on a scale in a lift moving upward but slowing down. How does the reading compare with their weight?
options: It equals weight because motion is upward
It is zero in every slowing lift
It is smaller
It is larger
questions.answer: It is smaller
questions.explanation: Upward motion with decreasing speed means downward acceleration, so the normal force is below weight.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rigid wheel rolls without slipping at constant speed on a level surface with no resistive losses or applied horizontal forces. What static friction is required?
options: A force that continually increases its speed
Zero
A force equal to its weight
The maximum possible static friction
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Static friction supplies only the force needed by the dynamics; ideal steady rolling needs none here.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere and a hoop roll without slipping down the same incline from rest. Why does the sphere arrive first in the ideal model?
options: It experiences no gravitational force
Its centre of mass loses more height
The hoop must slide rather than roll
A smaller fraction of its energy goes into rotation
questions.answer: A smaller fraction of its energy goes into rotation
questions.explanation: The sphere has a smaller moment-of-inertia-to-mass-radius-squared ratio, giving greater translational acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A satellite is moved into a larger circular orbit. Which combination describes its new state?
options: Lower speed and lower total mechanical energy
Unchanged speed and unchanged total mechanical energy
Lower speed and greater total mechanical energy
Higher speed and greater total mechanical energy
questions.answer: Lower speed and greater total mechanical energy
questions.explanation: Larger circular orbits have lower orbital speed but less negative total mechanical energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metal plate with a circular hole is heated uniformly. Which prediction is consistent with uniform expansion?
options: The hole enlarges as though the missing metal also expanded
The hole shrinks because metal expands inward only
The hole area stays fixed
The hole closes if the plate is thick
questions.answer: The hole enlarges as though the missing metal also expanded
questions.explanation: All linear dimensions scale upward under unconstrained uniform expansion, including the hole diameter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal gas completes a full cycle and performs positive net work. What must be true of net heat transfer?
options: Net heat leaves the gas
Net heat is zero
Internal energy increases each cycle
Net heat enters the gas
questions.answer: Net heat enters the gas
questions.explanation: The internal-energy change over a complete cycle is zero, so net heat input equals net work output.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In ideal spring motion, when is acceleration magnitude greatest while kinetic energy is least?
options: At every position equally
At either extreme displacement
At equilibrium only
Halfway in time between equilibrium and an extreme always
questions.answer: At either extreme displacement
questions.explanation: Restoring acceleration is proportional to displacement, while speed is zero at the extremes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A driven oscillator has modest damping. Increasing damping near resonance most directly does what to its response curve?
options: Lowers and broadens the resonance peak
Raises and narrows the resonance peak
Removes all forcing frequencies
Makes amplitude independent of the drive
questions.answer: Lowers and broadens the resonance peak
questions.explanation: Damping dissipates energy, reducing resonant amplitude and making the response less sharply selective.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At the midpoint between equal positive charges, electric field is zero. What about electric potential, taking zero at infinity?
options: It is negative
It is undefined because fields cancel
It is positive
It is zero because field is zero
questions.answer: It is positive
questions.explanation: Vector fields cancel at the midpoint, but the two positive scalar potentials add.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A closed surface encloses equal positive and negative charges. What follows from zero net enclosed charge?
options: No field line crosses the surface
Net electric flux is zero, but local fields need not be zero
The field is zero at every point on the surface
Potential is zero everywhere inside
questions.answer: Net electric flux is zero, but local fields need not be zero
questions.explanation: Gauss's law constrains net flux, not the field at each location.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical resistors are first in series and then in parallel across the same ideal voltage source. Which arrangement uses greater total power?
options: Series
Both use equal power
Neither can dissipate power
Parallel
questions.answer: Parallel
questions.explanation: Parallel connection has lower equivalent resistance, so total power V squared divided by resistance is greater.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A loop rotates in a uniform magnetic field at constant angular speed. At maximum flux, what is its instantaneous induced emf?
options: Equal to the flux
Infinite
Zero
Maximum magnitude
questions.answer: Zero
questions.explanation: Emf depends on the rate of change of flux, which is zero at a smooth flux maximum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A telescope's aperture is increased with the wavelength unchanged. Why can it resolve closer angular details?
options: The diffraction pattern becomes narrower
The incoming wavelength increases
The stars move farther apart
The focal length must become zero
questions.answer: The diffraction pattern becomes narrower
questions.explanation: A larger aperture reduces the diffraction-limited angular spread.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sample is chemically combined into a new compound. In the standard school model, what happens to its nuclear half-life?
options: It halves because bonds form
It doubles because electrons are shared
It follows the compound's boiling point
It remains essentially unchanged
questions.answer: It remains essentially unchanged
questions.explanation: Ordinary chemical changes affect electronic bonding, not the nuclear decay constant in this model.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A positive charge is released from rest where electric potential decreases toward the right. What initially happens?
options: It accelerates right and potential energy increases
It accelerates right and electric potential energy decreases
It accelerates left and electric potential energy decreases
It stays still because potential is a scalar
questions.answer: It accelerates right and electric potential energy decreases
questions.explanation: Electric field points toward decreasing potential, and a positive charge lowers its potential energy as it accelerates that way.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charged parallel-plate capacitor is isolated, then a dielectric is inserted. Which pair decreases?
options: Voltage and stored electrical energy
Charge and capacitance
Capacitance and voltage
Charge and stored electrical energy
questions.answer: Voltage and stored electrical energy
questions.explanation: With charge fixed, increased capacitance lowers both Q/C and Q squared divided by twice the capacitance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A glass converging lens is immersed in a liquid whose refractive index is closer to that of glass than air's is. What happens to its converging power?
options: It is fixed by shape alone
It becomes infinite
It decreases
It increases
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: Reduced relative refractive index weakens refraction at the lens surfaces.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A proton and an alpha particle enter the same uniform magnetic field perpendicularly with equal speeds. Which has the larger circular radius?
options: Neither follows a curved path
The alpha particle
The proton
Their radii are equal
questions.answer: The alpha particle
questions.explanation: Radius is proportional to mass divided by charge at fixed speed and field; an alpha particle has about twice the proton's mass-to-charge ratio.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron and a proton have equal nonrelativistic kinetic energies. Which has the longer de Broglie wavelength?
options: The proton
They have equal wavelengths
Wavelength depends only on charge
The electron
questions.answer: The electron
questions.explanation: At fixed kinetic energy, the lighter particle has smaller momentum and therefore larger wavelength.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A student studies an old coastal settlement using pottery and trade records. Why use both?
options: Written records always make objects irrelevant
Objects prove every recorded claim is correct
They provide different kinds of evidence about life and exchange
They must describe exactly the same event
questions.answer: They provide different kinds of evidence about life and exchange
questions.explanation: Material and written sources can complement each other while requiring interpretation.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: An inland settlement develops near a reliable water source in an arid region. Which explanation is most plausible?
options: All settlements require identical locations
Water availability supports settlement and livelihoods
The source guarantees unlimited population growth
Rainfall becomes irrelevant everywhere
questions.answer: Water availability supports settlement and livelihoods
questions.explanation: Access to water is an important constraint on settlement in dry environments.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A region develops tourism and manufacturing alongside one major export industry. What is the intended economic effect?
options: Reduce dependence on a single source of activity
Make every industry face identical risks
Eliminate the need for trade
Guarantee constant income in every year
questions.answer: Reduce dependence on a single source of activity
questions.explanation: Diversification spreads activity across sectors, though it does not remove all risk.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: The same journey occupies more centimetres on a larger-scale map. What remains unchanged?
options: The level of detail on both maps
The map distance in centimetres
The size of every printed symbol
The real distance of the journey
questions.answer: The real distance of the journey
questions.explanation: Scale changes the representation, not the underlying distance.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A historic building is repaired using documented evidence of its original features. Why keep those records?
options: To replace the need for careful conservation
To claim no change ever occurred
To explain what is original and what was restored
To prove all repairs are invisible
questions.answer: To explain what is original and what was restored
questions.explanation: Documentation helps distinguish surviving evidence from later interventions.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A visitor encounters an unfamiliar custom. Which response best supports understanding?
options: Avoid all contact with the community
Ask respectfully about its meaning and context
Assume unfamiliar means inferior
Treat one person's explanation as every person's view
questions.answer: Ask respectfully about its meaning and context
questions.explanation: Respectful enquiry helps interpretation without stereotyping.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Students identify an access problem and submit a practical proposal through the school's feedback process. What are they demonstrating?
options: Constructive participation in community improvement
A guarantee that their proposal must be adopted
Withdrawal from shared responsibility
Proof that no other view matters
questions.answer: Constructive participation in community improvement
questions.explanation: They are contributing evidence and a proposal to a shared decision process.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Two classmates disagree over use of a shared room. What is a useful first step?
options: Assume the louder speaker is correct
Repeat accusations before hearing details
Let a rumour decide the issue
Clarify each person's needs and the actual source of disagreement
questions.answer: Clarify each person's needs and the actual source of disagreement
questions.explanation: Understanding needs and facts creates a basis for a workable resolution.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Two learners need different supports to access the same activity. What can fair treatment require?
options: Automatic exclusion of the learner needing more help
A reward based only on who asks first
Different support that enables comparable participation
Identical support regardless of barriers
questions.answer: Different support that enables comparable participation
questions.explanation: Fairness can require attention to relevant differences in need.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A student plans spending before receiving a fixed allowance. Which choice best protects essential expenses?
options: Ignore small repeated expenses
Reserve amounts for necessities before optional purchases
Spend first and estimate needs later
Treat expected gifts as guaranteed income
questions.answer: Reserve amounts for necessities before optional purchases
questions.explanation: Planning around essential commitments helps keep spending within available resources.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A product is inexpensive but its advertised environmental claim has no supporting evidence. What should a buyer examine?
options: The basis and scope of the claim
Only the green colour of the label
Whether the slogan is memorable
Whether a friend repeats the advertisement
questions.answer: The basis and scope of the claim
questions.explanation: An ethical claim should be evaluated through evidence rather than appearance.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A disruption in one country's production delays goods elsewhere. What does this illustrate?
options: Complete economic isolation
That local choices have no external effects
That every product has one domestic input
Interdependence through supply chains
questions.answer: Interdependence through supply chains
questions.explanation: Connected production and trade can transmit disruptions across borders.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A student wants to post a photograph identifying classmates. What is the responsible first consideration?
options: Whether it can be edited to look brighter
Whether the uploader owns a newer phone
Whether the people shown have agreed to that sharing
Whether the image will receive many likes
questions.answer: Whether the people shown have agreed to that sharing
questions.explanation: Responsible sharing considers the people affected and their privacy.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A school fixes leaks before increasing its water supply. What is the immediate benefit?
options: Making all consumption unnecessary
Reducing avoidable losses from existing supply
Creating water without an input
Removing every future water need
questions.answer: Reducing avoidable losses from existing supply
questions.explanation: Repairing leaks improves use of the water already supplied.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A volunteer project falls short of its target. Which response supports learning?
options: Compare plans with outcomes and identify improvements
Hide the result because it was disappointing
Assume every part of the plan was wrong
Repeat the plan without reviewing evidence
questions.answer: Compare plans with outcomes and identify improvements
questions.explanation: Reflection uses experience to understand what worked and what needs change.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A baker buys flour and sells bread to a household. Why count the final bread value rather than adding both sales to GDP?
options: Flour has no market value
Only imported ingredients count in GDP
All business purchases are excluded from production
The bread value already includes the flour used
questions.answer: The bread value already includes the flour used
questions.explanation: Counting intermediate inputs again would double-count value embodied in the final product.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A wage stays fixed while the price of the household's consumption basket rises. What happens to that wage's purchasing power?
options: It stays fixed because the wage is unchanged
It becomes independent of prices
It falls
It rises by the inflation rate
questions.answer: It falls
questions.explanation: A fixed money income buys fewer goods when relevant prices rise.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A shop accepts money even though it does not want the buyer's goods. Which problem does this solve?
options: The existence of opportunity cost
The need for a double coincidence of wants
The possibility of any price change
The need to produce goods before exchanging them
questions.answer: The need for a double coincidence of wants
questions.explanation: Money as a medium of exchange allows trade without matching two barter wants.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Workers produce more real output per hour after effective training. What has increased?
options: Labour productivity
The number of hours in every working day
The unemployment rate by definition
Inflation by definition
questions.answer: Labour productivity
questions.explanation: Productivity relates output to inputs, so greater real output per hour represents a productivity gain.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A currency appreciates while exporters' domestic-currency prices stay unchanged. What happens to their goods' foreign-currency prices?
options: They fall
They remain unchanged by definition
They become equal across all products
They rise
questions.answer: They rise
questions.explanation: Foreign buyers need more of their currency to purchase the same domestic-currency-priced goods.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Two accounts of the same event emphasise different participants. What should a historian examine?
options: Which account is longer as the only criterion
Whether disagreement makes both useless
Which account has a more attractive cover
Each author's position, purpose and supporting evidence
questions.answer: Each author's position, purpose and supporting evidence
questions.explanation: Perspective and purpose can shape selection and emphasis without making a source wholly unusable.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A town's population rises faster than its transport capacity. What consequence is plausible?
options: A guaranteed fall in all travel demand
No change in infrastructure needs
Greater pressure on existing routes and services
Automatic elimination of congestion
questions.answer: Greater pressure on existing routes and services
questions.explanation: Population growth can increase demand when service capacity does not keep pace.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A community uses its limited project budget for a park instead of a library extension. What is the relevant opportunity cost?
options: The total value of all possible projects combined
The benefit forgone from the next-best alternative
Every past expense on the library
The park's name
questions.answer: The benefit forgone from the next-best alternative
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost concerns the best alternative sacrificed by the choice.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: One district has more total water use but a larger population. What is needed to compare average use per resident?
options: Relate water use to population in each district
Rank only the total volumes
Ignore household numbers and population
Assume larger districts are always less efficient
questions.answer: Relate water use to population in each district
questions.explanation: Per-person comparisons require a common population basis.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: An oral account recalls a local tradition from decades earlier. How should it be used?
options: Treat memory as a flawless recording
Reject all spoken evidence automatically
Assume one speaker represents every resident
Value the perspective while checking details against other evidence
questions.answer: Value the perspective while checking details against other evidence
questions.explanation: Oral history offers experience and meaning, but memory and perspective require scrutiny.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Two clubs each demand exclusive use of one room, but one needs quiet and the other needs storage. What may unlock agreement?
options: Assume their needs are identical
Choose the club with the longest name
Address the different underlying needs instead of only the demands
Repeat the original demands more forcefully
questions.answer: Address the different underlying needs instead of only the demands
questions.explanation: Understanding interests can reveal solutions unavailable when attention stays on fixed positions.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A popular proposal benefits most students but prevents a small group from participating. What should be examined?
options: Whether benefits remove the need for consultation
Both overall benefit and the excluded group's rights and access
Popularity as the only ethical test
Whether the excluded group is too small to matter
questions.answer: Both overall benefit and the excluded group's rights and access
questions.explanation: Ethical evaluation should consider affected minorities as well as aggregate advantage.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A factory's low price excludes the cost of pollution borne by nearby residents. What does this illustrate?
options: A cost imposed on others outside the market price
Proof that production has no benefits
A direct wage payment to residents
A guarantee that the product is scarce
questions.answer: A cost imposed on others outside the market price
questions.explanation: External costs are consequences borne by people other than the immediate buyer or seller.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A device is cheap to buy but requires an expensive monthly subscription. What comparison is more informative?
options: Purchase price alone
The number of accessories in the box
The size of the initial discount alone
Total cost over the intended period of use
questions.answer: Total cost over the intended period of use
questions.explanation: Recurring charges can materially change the cost of ownership.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Several websites repeat an identical story from one source. What should a reader seek?
options: The shortest version of the story
A more emotional presentation
Independent evidence rather than more copies
The greatest number of matching headlines
questions.answer: Independent evidence rather than more copies
questions.explanation: Repeated publication of one claim does not create independent confirmation.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A student generalises about a whole culture from one encounter. What is the problem?
options: Cultures cannot have shared practices
Individual behaviour may not represent the group's diversity
Every encounter must be ignored
All members of a culture behave identically
questions.answer: Individual behaviour may not represent the group's diversity
questions.explanation: A single example is insufficient to characterise a diverse group.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A transport survey is conducted only online, excluding residents without access. What should improve the process?
options: Provide additional ways for affected residents to respond
Assume online respondents represent everyone
Remove questions about access
Use only the fastest responses
questions.answer: Provide additional ways for affected residents to respond
questions.explanation: Inclusive consultation needs routes that reach people affected by the decision.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A reusable item requires more resources to manufacture than a disposable one. What determines whether reuse has an overall benefit?
options: The reusable label alone
Its purchase colour
Manufacturing impact alone in every case
Manufacturing, repeated use and end-of-life impacts over its actual lifespan
questions.answer: Manufacturing, repeated use and end-of-life impacts over its actual lifespan
questions.explanation: Lifecycle comparison considers impacts across production, use and disposal.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A mediator helps two groups reach an agreement without imposing a decision. What is central to the role?
options: Speaking only to the stronger group
Replacing all discussion with an order
Facilitating communication and a mutually acceptable solution
Privately deciding which side deserves punishment
questions.answer: Facilitating communication and a mutually acceptable solution
questions.explanation: Mediation supports the parties in developing an agreement rather than imposing one.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A volunteering project reports many hours but cannot show who benefited. What additional evidence is needed?
options: A new project logo
Outcomes related to the project's stated purpose
Longer descriptions of the volunteers' effort
More photographs of the organisers
questions.answer: Outcomes related to the project's stated purpose
questions.explanation: Activity measures alone do not establish the intended community benefit.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A tariff raises the domestic price of an imported input used by local manufacturers. What possible consequence should be considered?
options: Export competitiveness must increase with input prices
The tariff can affect only foreign firms
Higher costs may reduce those manufacturers' competitiveness
Every domestic producer must benefit equally
questions.answer: Higher costs may reduce those manufacturers' competitiveness
questions.explanation: Protection for one industry can impose higher input costs on downstream domestic industries.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Real GDP rises while unpaid household care falls and pollution rises. What is the sound conclusion?
options: Pollution automatically reduces measured GDP by its full harm
GDP growth alone does not establish improved overall welfare
Overall welfare must rise by the GDP growth rate
Unpaid household care is fully counted in GDP
questions.answer: GDP growth alone does not establish improved overall welfare
questions.explanation: GDP measures market production broadly, not every contribution to or cost of well-being.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Unemployment-benefit payments rise during a downturn under existing rules. Why is this an automatic stabiliser?
options: Transfers support disposable income without a fresh policy vote
Transfers directly count as government production in GDP
Every recipient stops being unemployed when paid
Benefits necessarily eliminate the output gap
questions.answer: Transfers support disposable income without a fresh policy vote
questions.explanation: The existing system offsets part of the fall in private income and spending.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A currency depreciates and domestic import prices rise. Why might domestic inflation increase?
options: Depreciation necessarily lowers every domestic production cost
The exchange-rate change directly reduces every tax rate
Imported goods stop entering the consumption basket
Imported final goods and imported inputs can become more expensive
questions.answer: Imported final goods and imported inputs can become more expensive
questions.explanation: Higher import costs can affect both consumer prices and firms' production costs.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A country buys more abroad than it earns in current-account receipts. How can it finance the gap?
options: Only by increasing current receipts on paper
By making all financial transactions disappear
By net borrowing, selling assets or reducing external assets
Only by recording the imports as exports
questions.answer: By net borrowing, selling assets or reducing external assets
questions.explanation: A current-account deficit is matched by financing transactions, subject to the accounting convention and statistical discrepancy.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: No surviving record mentions a small trading activity. Why is concluding it never occurred too strong?
options: Records may be incomplete or selectively preserved
Every unrecorded event definitely occurred
All records are equally comprehensive
Silence proves the activity was illegal
questions.answer: Records may be incomplete or selectively preserved
questions.explanation: The surviving record's limits must be considered before treating silence as proof of absence.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Average income rises, but gains are concentrated in a small group. What can the average conceal?
options: The exact income of every household
A guarantee that all households gained equally
Proof that total income fell
Unequal distribution of improvements
questions.answer: Unequal distribution of improvements
questions.explanation: An average can rise while many individuals see little or no improvement.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Coastal development and habitat loss occur together in several locations. What strengthens a causal analysis?
options: Assume correlation alone proves every loss was caused by development
Ignore locations that do not fit the claim
Examine timing, mechanisms and alternative influences
Rely only on a shared location name
questions.answer: Examine timing, mechanisms and alternative influences
questions.explanation: Causal reasoning needs evidence about how and when changes occur and what else may explain them.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A restoration proposal increases visitor capacity but may damage original material. What should guide evaluation?
options: Reject every form of public access automatically
Compare access benefits with conservation impacts and less damaging alternatives
Assume more visitors always justify any alteration
Preserve tourism income as the only criterion
questions.answer: Compare access benefits with conservation impacts and less damaging alternatives
questions.explanation: Heritage decisions require consideration of both use and the evidence being preserved.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A region diversifies into several industries that all depend on the same fragile resource. What limitation remains?
options: The industries may still be exposed to a shared disruption
The number of industries guarantees independence
Diversification necessarily increases every risk
A shared input cannot affect multiple sectors
questions.answer: The industries may still be exposed to a shared disruption
questions.explanation: Sector variety does not remove risks that affect a common dependency.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: An adviser recommends a supplier while secretly receiving payment from that supplier. Why does disclosure matter even if the product is adequate?
options: Adequate quality makes every hidden incentive irrelevant
Disclosure automatically proves the recommendation is wrong
Only an expensive product can create a conflict
The incentive can influence judgement and should be visible to decision-makers
questions.answer: The incentive can influence judgement and should be visible to decision-makers
questions.explanation: Transparency allows others to assess an incentive that may compromise impartial advice.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A shared environmental problem affects everyone, but communities differ greatly in resources and contribution to it. What should a fair response consider?
options: Only the preferences of the wealthiest participants
Whether responsibility can be avoided by everyone
Capacity, contribution and need when allocating responsibilities
Identical burdens as the only possible form of fairness
questions.answer: Capacity, contribution and need when allocating responsibilities
questions.explanation: Relevant differences can matter when distributing duties and support.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Violence stops, but the underlying dispute and distrust remain. What distinction is important?
options: All underlying causes must already have disappeared
Ending immediate violence does not necessarily resolve its causes
A ceasefire guarantees lasting reconciliation
Dialogue is unnecessary once fighting stops
questions.answer: Ending immediate violence does not necessarily resolve its causes
questions.explanation: Sustainable peace may require addressing grievances and relationships beyond stopping immediate violence.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.topic: Responsible finances: nominal and real value
questions.q: Savings grow slowly while prices rise faster. What happens to their purchasing power?
options: It can fall despite the balance increasing
It must rise because the number is larger
It stays fixed whenever the account is safe
It doubles whenever interest is paid
questions.answer: It can fall despite the balance increasing
