questions.explanation: Purchasing power depends on growth relative to prices, not the nominal balance alone.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A community project maximises attendance by removing activities that help a smaller high-need group. What is the concern?
options: Higher attendance proves every need is better served
The smaller group's outcomes cannot be measured
Any numerical target is inherently useless
The attendance target may displace the project's real purpose
questions.answer: The attendance target may displace the project's real purpose
questions.explanation: A convenient metric can diverge from the underlying objective it is meant to represent.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A consultation receives many responses from one well-organised group and few from others. What should decision-makers avoid?
options: Seeking missing perspectives
Publishing the consultation method
Treating response volume as automatically representative of all affected people
Reading the detailed responses
questions.answer: Treating response volume as automatically representative of all affected people
questions.explanation: Participation patterns may reflect organisation and access rather than the distribution of all views.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A student says respecting cultural difference means no practice can ever be questioned. What is a stronger approach?
options: Assume context removes every ethical question
Seek contextual understanding while evaluating effects on people respectfully
Treat all unfamiliar practices as wrong
Replace reasoning with ridicule
questions.answer: Seek contextual understanding while evaluating effects on people respectfully
questions.explanation: Respectful understanding and critical ethical examination can coexist.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A policy reduces waste at one site but shifts disposal to another. What should evaluation include?
options: The total effects across the affected system
Only the most improved location
Only the policy's original intention
The number of announcements issued
questions.answer: The total effects across the affected system
questions.explanation: A local improvement may conceal displacement rather than an overall reduction.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A shared conservation scheme benefits everyone, including those who contribute nothing. What challenge can arise?
options: Shared benefits guarantee sufficient contributions
Noncontributors receive no possible benefit
Cooperation cannot ever address the problem
Individuals may rely on others' contributions, weakening the scheme
questions.answer: Individuals may rely on others' contributions, weakening the scheme
questions.explanation: Free riding can underprovide a shared benefit unless cooperation or arrangements sustain contributions.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: New credible evidence changes the expected effects of a proposal a student supported. What is the most responsible response?
options: Change the topic to the opponent's personality
Assume revising a view always shows dishonesty
Reassess the position and explain any revision
Reject the evidence to preserve consistency
questions.answer: Reassess the position and explain any revision
questions.explanation: Reasoned judgement should respond to relevant evidence rather than defend a position regardless of facts.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: An economy raises investment by cutting current consumption. Why is faster future growth not guaranteed merely by a larger investment total?
options: The total guarantees equal benefits to every resident
The productivity and effective use of the investment also matter
Any investment automatically reduces future capacity
Consumption and investment use unrelated resources
questions.answer: The productivity and effective use of the investment also matter
questions.explanation: Wasteful or poorly used investment may deliver little additional productive capacity despite its current resource cost.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: Trade raises total potential gains, but workers in an import-competing industry lose jobs. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Aggregate gains can coexist with concentrated adjustment costs
Those job losses prove that no consumer can gain
Comparative advantage guarantees no worker ever changes jobs
Total gains guarantee automatic compensation to every loser
questions.answer: Aggregate gains can coexist with concentrated adjustment costs
questions.explanation: Efficiency gains do not determine how benefits and costs are distributed or whether compensation occurs.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A country has positive gross investment but depreciation is larger. What follows for its produced capital stock, other changes excluded?
options: It rises because gross investment is positive
It stays fixed because depreciation is only a price index
It becomes identical to current consumption
It declines because net investment is negative
questions.answer: It declines because net investment is negative
questions.explanation: Net investment subtracts depreciation from gross investment; a negative amount means capital is not fully replaced.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: A central bank defends a currency facing downward pressure by selling foreign reserves and buying domestic currency. What constraint can eventually bind?
options: The exchange rate no longer needs any supporting transactions
A fixed rate guarantees investors cannot sell domestic assets
Its available foreign reserves can be depleted
Its purchases create unlimited foreign reserves automatically
questions.answer: Its available foreign reserves can be depleted
questions.explanation: Defending the rate in this direction uses foreign assets, so persistent pressure can exhaust the reserve buffer.

questions.subject: Social Studies & Moral Education
questions.q: An economy keeps adding physical capital per worker with unchanged technology. Why can growth from this source slow?
options: Technology automatically deteriorates as investment rises
Diminishing returns can reduce the extra output from each additional unit of capital
More capital necessarily makes every worker less productive
Depreciation must fall to zero
questions.answer: Diminishing returns can reduce the extra output from each additional unit of capital
questions.explanation: With other factors fixed, capital deepening commonly delivers diminishing additions to output per worker.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two equal pizzas are cut into four and eight equal slices. Which single slice is larger?
options: A slice from the four-piece pizza
A slice from the eight-piece pizza
They are equal
Size cannot be compared
questions.answer: A slice from the four-piece pizza
questions.explanation: Dividing the same whole into fewer equal parts makes each part larger.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A temperature rises from -4 degrees to -1 degree. Which statement is correct?
options: It fell by three degrees
It rose by five degrees
It did not change
It rose by three degrees
questions.answer: It rose by three degrees
questions.explanation: Moving from -4 to -1 is a positive change of three.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A shop raises a price by 10 percent, then cuts the new price by 10 percent. Compared with the original, the final price is what?
options: Exactly equal
Twice as high
Lower
Higher
questions.answer: Lower
questions.explanation: The reduction is taken from the larger updated price, giving 99 percent of the original.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A paint mix uses two parts blue for every one part yellow. Which describes the blue share?
options: Twice the whole mixture
Two thirds of the mixture
One half of the mixture
One third of the mixture
questions.answer: Two thirds of the mixture
questions.explanation: There are three total parts, of which two are blue.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Every member of a group receives the same two extra marks. What happens to the group's average?
options: It rises by two
It stays unchanged
It doubles
It falls by two
questions.answer: It rises by two
questions.explanation: Adding the same amount to every value adds that amount to the mean.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two equal-distance journeys take different times. Which has the greater average speed?
options: The journey taking more time
They must have equal speed
The one starting later regardless of time
The journey taking less time
questions.answer: The journey taking less time
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time, so the shorter time gives the greater speed.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Which is larger: 0.8 or 0.75?
options: They are equal
The longer decimal must be larger
questions.explanation: Eight tenths equals eighty hundredths, which exceeds seventy-five hundredths.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A distance is rounded to 50 km to the nearest 10 km. Which actual distance could produce this result?
options: 39 km
53 km
44 km
61 km
questions.answer: 53 km
questions.explanation: A distance of 53 km is closer to 50 than to the neighbouring multiples of ten.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A square's side length doubles. What happens to its area?
options: It becomes four times as large
It doubles
It stays the same
It becomes eight times as large
questions.answer: It becomes four times as large
questions.explanation: Both dimensions double, multiplying area by four.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A small class and a large class each have half their students absent. What can be concluded?
options: The numbers absent must match
The smaller class has more absent students
Both classes have no one present
The larger class has more absent students
questions.answer: The larger class has more absent students
questions.explanation: The same fraction of a larger total represents a larger number.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A recipe is doubled with all ingredient proportions preserved. What happens to the amount of flour?
options: It halves
It depends only on oven temperature
It doubles
It stays fixed
questions.answer: It doubles
questions.explanation: Scaling a recipe uniformly doubles each ingredient.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: The same job is shared by more equally productive workers with no interference. What tends to happen to completion time?
options: It becomes negative
It decreases
It increases
It stays fixed
questions.answer: It decreases
questions.explanation: A larger combined work rate reduces the time needed for the fixed job.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A taxi fare includes a fixed starting fee plus a charge per kilometre. Why does doubling distance not usually double the total fare?
options: The starting fee is paid only once per trip
The kilometre charge disappears
The starting fee doubles for every kilometre
The longer trip must be free
questions.answer: The starting fee is paid only once per trip
questions.explanation: Only the distance-dependent part doubles; the fixed part does not.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A drink at 20 degrees is mixed with an equal amount of the same drink at 40 degrees, with no heat loss. What temperature is expected?
options: 60 degrees
20 degrees
40 degrees
30 degrees
questions.answer: 30 degrees
questions.explanation: Equal amounts of the same substance balance at the average initial temperature.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A fixed prize is divided equally among more winners. What happens to each winner's share?
options: It stays the same
It exceeds the total prize
It becomes smaller
It becomes larger
questions.answer: It becomes smaller
questions.explanation: A fixed total divided by a larger number gives smaller equal shares.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two runners cover the same route. One runs every segment faster. Who must finish sooner if neither stops?
options: It depends only on their names
The runner faster on every segment
The slower runner
They must tie
questions.answer: The runner faster on every segment
questions.explanation: Taking less time on every segment gives less total time.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A map scale doubles the drawing length for every real-world distance. What happens to a route's drawn length?
options: It doubles
It halves
It stays fixed
It becomes four times longer
questions.answer: It doubles
questions.explanation: A uniform linear scale change applies directly to every drawn distance.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A larger pack costs less per kilogram than a smaller pack. Which claim follows?
options: The larger pack must have the lower total price
The smaller pack contains more mass
Buying the larger pack is always necessary
The larger pack offers a lower unit price
questions.answer: The larger pack offers a lower unit price
questions.explanation: Lower unit cost does not necessarily mean lower total spending or better suitability.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A success rate rises from 40 percent to 50 percent. What is the increase in percentage points?
questions.explanation: Percentage-point change is the difference between the two percentages.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A fund is split in proportion to group sizes. Group A has twice as many members as B. What should A receive?
options: All the fund
Twice B's allocation
The same as B
Half B's allocation
questions.answer: Twice B's allocation
questions.explanation: Proportional allocation preserves the ratio of the group sizes.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: All library volunteers wear badges. Maya is a library volunteer. What follows?
options: Maya wears a badge
Everyone with a badge is a volunteer
Maya is the only volunteer
Maya works every day
questions.answer: Maya wears a badge
questions.explanation: The universal rule applies to Maya because she belongs to the stated group.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: If the alarm is armed, a red light is on. The red light is off. What follows if the rule holds?
options: The alarm is definitely armed
The alarm has no battery necessarily
The light must be blue
The alarm is not armed
questions.answer: The alarm is not armed
questions.explanation: A missing necessary consequence rules out the condition that would require it.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Some students in a class play chess. Does that prove all students play chess?
options: No student can play chess
Exactly half must play
No; the others may or may not play
Yes; some always means all
questions.answer: No; the others may or may not play
questions.explanation: An existential statement gives no universal conclusion about the remaining students.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A pass allows either the morning session or the evening session, but not both. Noor attends the morning session. What is permitted by this pass?
options: Any number of sessions
No evening attendance
Both sessions
Evening attendance only
questions.answer: No evening attendance
questions.explanation: The stated exclusive choice is used by attending the morning session.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Entry requires a valid ticket. Arun has no valid ticket. What follows under this rule?
options: Arun does not qualify for entry
Arun must be admitted
Arun is the event organiser
Arun has already attended
questions.answer: Arun does not qualify for entry
questions.explanation: Lacking a required condition prevents eligibility under the stated rule.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: No bicycles are allowed in the lift. This object is a bicycle. What does the rule imply?
options: It is allowed if blue
All vehicles are banned
Only this bicycle is banned
It is not allowed in the lift
questions.answer: It is not allowed in the lift
questions.explanation: The prohibition applies to every member of the bicycle category.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A claim says every door is locked. What single observation disproves it?
options: Two locked doors
A door's colour
One unlocked door
One locked door
questions.answer: One unlocked door
questions.explanation: A universal claim fails if any member is a counterexample.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A code is accepted only if it has six digits. Which code definitely fails this length rule?
options: A six-digit code ending with nine
A code with five digits
A code with six digits
A six-digit code beginning with zero
questions.answer: A code with five digits
questions.explanation: A five-digit code lacks the required length, regardless of its content.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Some artists are teachers. What must also be true?
options: Some teachers are artists
All teachers are artists
No teacher is an artist
Every artist teaches
questions.answer: Some teachers are artists
questions.explanation: The people in the overlap establish the reversed existential statement.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A box contains at least one red ball. Can you conclude it contains a blue ball?
options: Yes; every red ball implies a blue ball
Yes; there must be equal colours
No; blue balls are impossible
No; that information is not given
questions.answer: No; that information is not given
questions.explanation: Knowing one colour occurs neither proves nor rules out another colour.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A finishes before B, and B before C. Who finishes before C?
options: C
No one
A
Only B, never A
questions.answer: A
questions.explanation: The order A before B before C places A before C as well.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Three people sit in a row. Lina is between Omar and Sara. Who occupies the middle seat?
options: No one
Lina
Omar
Sara
questions.answer: Lina
questions.explanation: Being between the other two in a three-seat row fixes Lina in the middle.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A meeting is moved one day later from Tuesday. On which day is it now?
options: Wednesday
Monday
Thursday
Tuesday
questions.answer: Wednesday
questions.explanation: One day after Tuesday is Wednesday.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Ravi is older than Ben but younger than Chen. Who is oldest?
options: Ravi
Ben
They are equal in age
Chen
questions.answer: Chen
questions.explanation: The age order is Chen, Ravi, then Ben.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: You overtake the person in second place in a race. What place do you take immediately?
options: Third
Last
Second
First
questions.answer: Second
questions.explanation: You occupy the overtaken runner's position; the leader remains ahead.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A clock shows 10:50, and an event begins in twenty minutes. What time is that?
questions.explanation: Ten minutes reach the next hour, followed by ten more minutes.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A must happen before B, while C has no stated timing restriction. What is certain?
options: A cannot occur after B
C must occur first
C must occur last
B must immediately follow A
questions.answer: A cannot occur after B
questions.explanation: Only the relative order of A and B is constrained.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Five objects are ordered from lightest to heaviest. Which position remains unchanged when the order is reversed?
options: First
Second
Fourth
Third
questions.answer: Third
questions.explanation: The middle position in an odd-length list remains the middle under reversal.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: One meeting runs from 2 to 3 and another from 2:30 to 3:30. What is true?
options: They overlap for two hours
They start together
They overlap for half an hour
They do not overlap
questions.answer: They overlap for half an hour
questions.explanation: Both meetings are running from 2:30 to 3.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A shortlist requires at least three reviewers. It currently has two. What is the smallest addition needed?
options: No reviewer
One reviewer
Two reviewers
Three reviewers
questions.answer: One reviewer
questions.explanation: Adding one raises the total to the required minimum of three.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A notice says, 'The garden reopens after repairs are completed.' Repairs are still underway. What is supported?
options: The reopening condition has not yet been met
The garden must have reopened yesterday
Repairs are unnecessary
The garden will never reopen
questions.answer: The reopening condition has not yet been met
questions.explanation: Ongoing repairs mean completion, the stated reopening condition, has not occurred.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: In 'The river bank was muddy', what does 'bank' refer to?
options: A financial institution
A store of batteries
A group of aircraft
The land beside the river
questions.answer: The land beside the river
questions.explanation: The river and mud context selects the geographical meaning.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A sentence says, 'The route is shorter; however, it is steeper.' What relationship does 'however' signal?
options: An exact repetition
A chronological sequence only
A contrast between advantages and disadvantages
A cause of the shorter distance
questions.answer: A contrast between advantages and disadvantages
questions.explanation: The connector introduces a contrasting consideration about the same route.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: In 'Nadia handed the book to Leila because Leila had requested it', what does 'it' refer to?
options: The act of handing
The book
Nadia
Leila
questions.answer: The book
questions.explanation: The requested object named in the sentence is the book.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Which best restates 'Entry is free for children under twelve'?
options: Children younger than twelve pay no entry fee
All visitors enter free
Only twelve-year-olds enter free
Children must pay twice
questions.answer: Children younger than twelve pay no entry fee
questions.explanation: The paraphrase preserves both the age condition and the free-entry meaning.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A sentence reads, 'The path flooded, so the walk was cancelled.' What caused the cancellation according to the sentence?
options: The length of the walk
A ticket discount
An earlier cancellation
The flooded path
questions.answer: The flooded path
questions.explanation: The connector 'so' presents the cancellation as a consequence of flooding.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A reviewer writes, 'The design is promising, though the instructions need work.' What is the tone?
options: Complete rejection
Indifference with no evaluation
Qualified approval
Unqualified praise
questions.answer: Qualified approval
questions.explanation: The reviewer expresses approval while identifying a limitation.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A report says 'Most respondents preferred option A.' Which conclusion goes too far?
options: A was preferred by a majority
Every respondent preferred A
More than half preferred A
Some respondents preferred A
questions.answer: Every respondent preferred A
questions.explanation: Most indicates a majority, not unanimity.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A debate asks whether a bridge can support heavy buses. Which evidence is most relevant?
options: Its tested load capacity
Its paint colour
Its name's popularity
The number of letters in its name
questions.answer: Its tested load capacity
questions.explanation: Load capacity directly bears on whether the bridge can support the proposed vehicles.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A sign says 'Students may borrow two books.' Which question remains unanswered?
options: Whether borrowing is mentioned
Whether the objects are books
Whether students are named
Whether two is the maximum or simply an allowed amount
questions.answer: Whether two is the maximum or simply an allowed amount
questions.explanation: The wording permits two but does not explicitly state a maximum.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A graph's vertical axis shows litres and its horizontal axis shows minutes. What could the graph describe?
options: Cost per kilogram
Age versus height
Water volume over time
Temperature over distance
questions.answer: Water volume over time
questions.explanation: The axis labels identify the measured quantity and its time variable.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A class has 12 students in one group and 8 in another, with no overlap and everyone included. How many students are there?
questions.explanation: Disjoint groups covering the class are added to obtain the total.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A table gives sales for Monday and Wednesday but leaves Tuesday blank. What should Tuesday's blank mean without further instructions?
options: Missing information
Zero sales necessarily
The same as Monday
The largest sales of the week
questions.answer: Missing information
questions.explanation: A blank is not a numerical value unless the table defines it that way.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Five numbers are sorted from smallest to largest. Which determines their median?
options: The first number
The sum of all five
The largest number
The third number
questions.answer: The third number
questions.explanation: For five ordered observations, the middle observation is the median.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two sets have the same minimum but different maxima. Which has the larger range?
options: Both have equal range
Range depends only on the mean
The set with the larger maximum
The set with the smaller maximum
questions.answer: The set with the larger maximum
questions.explanation: With the minimum fixed, a larger maximum increases maximum minus minimum.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A survey records more votes for B than for A, and more for A than C. Which received the most among these three?
options: They tied
B
A
C
questions.answer: B
questions.explanation: The stated order of counts places B above A and C.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: One category fills half of a pie chart showing all responses. What does it represent?
options: Half of the responses
Half of each person's opinion
Twice all responses
An unknown share regardless of the chart
questions.answer: Half of the responses
questions.explanation: A pie chart represents parts of one whole; half the circle is half the total.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A scale shows whole kilograms only. Why might two different masses display the same reading?
options: The masses must be physically identical
The scale measures colour instead
Rounding always changes every value differently
Both round to the same displayed value
questions.answer: Both round to the same displayed value
questions.explanation: Limited resolution can map nearby actual measurements to the same displayed result.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Ten complaints come from 100 customers at one shop and ten from 1,000 at another. Which has the higher complaint rate?
options: Both rates are equal
Neither rate can be compared
The first shop
The second shop
questions.answer: The first shop
questions.explanation: The same complaint count represents a larger fraction of the smaller customer base.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A table shows attendance rising each month for four months. What is directly supported?
options: No month ever had absences
Attendance rose during those four months
Attendance will rise forever
The rise was caused by advertising
questions.answer: Attendance rose during those four months
questions.explanation: The observed period supports a past trend without proving future behaviour or causation.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: You face north and turn right once through a quarter-turn. Which way do you face?
options: East
West
South
North
questions.answer: East
questions.explanation: A clockwise quarter-turn from north points east.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two people leave the same point, one walking east and one west at equal speed. What happens to their separation?
options: It remains zero
It decreases
It alternates between zero and one metre
It increases
questions.answer: It increases
questions.explanation: Walking away in opposite directions increases the distance between them.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A vertical mirror reverses the apparent side of a badge worn on someone's left in a front-facing view. Where does it appear in the reflected view?
options: At the person's feet
Behind the mirror with no image
On the viewer's right
On the viewer's left always
questions.answer: On the viewer's right
questions.explanation: In a front-facing reflected view, the person's left appears on the viewer's right.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A paper triangle is rotated without resizing. Which property stays unchanged?
options: Its position relative to the page corner
Its side lengths
Its orientation on the page
The direction its top vertex points
questions.answer: Its side lengths
questions.explanation: Rigid rotation preserves distances and therefore side lengths.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A square is folded along a diagonal so matching edges align. What does this show about the diagonal?
options: It is a line of reflection symmetry
It is shorter than every side
It divides the square into unequal areas
It changes the number of corners before folding
questions.answer: It is a line of reflection symmetry
questions.explanation: The two halves reflect onto each other across the diagonal.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two faces of a cube share an edge. How are they related?
options: They are opposite
They are the same face
They never meet
They are adjacent
questions.answer: They are adjacent
questions.explanation: Sharing an edge defines adjacent faces of a cube.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: You walk five metres east and then five metres west along the same line. Where do you finish?
options: Five metres north
Ten metres west
At the starting point
Ten metres east
questions.answer: At the starting point
questions.explanation: Equal opposite displacements cancel.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two identical squares share a full side without overlapping. What outer shape do they form?
options: A circle
A rectangle twice as long as it is wide
A larger square
A triangle
questions.answer: A rectangle twice as long as it is wide
questions.explanation: Joining along one full side doubles one dimension while preserving the other.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A rectangle is cut into two smaller rectangles. Why can the sum of their perimeters exceed the original perimeter?
options: The cut adds new boundary edges
Cutting creates extra area
The original edges disappear
Each new rectangle must have zero width
questions.answer: The cut adds new boundary edges
questions.explanation: The two sides along the cut are counted as additional boundaries.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A rectangular sign looks narrower when viewed more obliquely from the side. Does that mean its physical width changed?
options: Yes; viewing compresses the material
Yes; its area must halve
No; its image must have identical width from every angle
No; the projected view changed
questions.answer: No; the projected view changed
questions.explanation: Perspective changes apparent width without changing the object's dimensions.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A stated rule adds three each time: 2, 5, 8. What is the next term?
questions.explanation: Applying the given rule adds three to eight.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A signal repeats red, blue, red, blue. Under this rule, what follows the next red?
options: No signal
Blue
Red again
Green
questions.answer: Blue
questions.explanation: The specified alternating pattern places blue after red.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A sequence begins 1, 3, 6, 10, adding consecutive integers 2, 3, 4. What comes next under that rule?
questions.explanation: The next increment is five, giving fifteen.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A code shifts each letter one place forward in the alphabet. How is CAT encoded?
options: BZS
DBT
CBU
DBU
questions.answer: DBU
questions.explanation: C becomes D, A becomes B, and T becomes U under the same rule.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Lights cycle A, B, C, A, B, C. Which appears immediately after C?
options: C
D
A
B
questions.answer: A
questions.explanation: The defined three-item cycle restarts with A after C.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A rule doubles a number at every step: 3, 6, 12. What follows?
questions.explanation: The next term is twice twelve.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A rule claims every listed number is even. Which entry breaks it?
questions.explanation: Fifteen is not divisible by two, unlike the other entries.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Choose the item that does not have exactly four sides.
options: Square
Rectangle
Rhombus
Triangle
questions.answer: Triangle
questions.explanation: A triangle has three sides, while the other named polygons have four.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A machine triples its input and then adds one. Which output could come from an input of two?
questions.explanation: Tripling two gives six, then adding one gives seven.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A short sequence has no stated rule and several rules fit it. What is the best conclusion about the next term?
options: Only one rule can fit any finite list
It is not uniquely determined from the list alone
It must be the smallest positive integer
The longest rule is always correct
questions.answer: It is not uniquely determined from the list alone
questions.explanation: A finite set of terms can be continued by multiple rules unless constraints specify one.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A room has 30 seats and 32 attendees. What is needed to seat everyone at once?
options: At least two extra seats
Two fewer seats
No change
Exactly thirty extra seats
questions.answer: At least two extra seats
questions.explanation: The seating shortfall is the difference between attendees and seats.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A task needs two full days and must finish by Friday evening. Which start guarantees enough time if work is continuous on those days?
options: Friday evening
Saturday morning
Friday afternoon
Thursday morning
questions.answer: Thursday morning
questions.explanation: Thursday and Friday provide the two required days before the deadline.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A printer produces pages faster than a single binder can bind them. Where will unfinished work tend to accumulate?
options: After all binding is complete
Nowhere because speeds do not matter
Before the binder
Before the printer only
questions.answer: Before the binder
questions.explanation: The slower binding stage limits throughput, creating a queue of printed pages.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A candidate meets the age rule but fails a mandatory qualification rule. Are all entry requirements met?
options: The qualification rule disappears
No
Yes, because one rule is enough
Yes, if the age is much higher
questions.answer: No
questions.explanation: Mandatory requirements must all be satisfied.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two routes take equal time, but one costs less and all other relevant features are equal. Which better meets a lower-cost objective?
options: The cheaper route
The dearer route
Neither can be compared
The route with the longer name
questions.answer: The cheaper route
questions.explanation: When time and other criteria match, lower cost directly serves the stated objective.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: An outdoor activity depends on dry weather. What plan best reduces disruption if rain occurs?
options: Ignore the forecast
Assume rain is impossible
Remove the activity's schedule
Arrange a suitable indoor alternative
questions.answer: Arrange a suitable indoor alternative
questions.explanation: A fallback addresses the identified dependency and provides a usable alternative.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: You must decide whether a bag fits in a storage box. Which missing information is most useful?
options: The bag owner's age
The box's colour
Their relevant dimensions
Their brand names
questions.answer: Their relevant dimensions
questions.explanation: Fit depends on the spatial dimensions of both objects.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A cake must cool before icing. Why might icing first cause a scheduling problem?
options: Icing makes baking unnecessary
It violates a required task order
Cooling always takes zero time
Both steps require no time
questions.answer: It violates a required task order
questions.explanation: The cooling dependency must be completed before icing can properly proceed.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A shop starts with ten items, sells three and receives no stock. What is left?
options: Seven items
Thirteen items
Three items
Ten items
questions.answer: Seven items
questions.explanation: Sales remove three from the initial stock of ten.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two batteries are compared for running time. Why use the same device settings?
options: To make their brand labels identical
To prevent measuring time
To guarantee equal results
To control differences in power demand
questions.answer: To control differences in power demand
questions.explanation: Matching conditions helps attribute run-time differences to the batteries.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Ice-cream sales and swimming accidents both rise in hot months. What is a plausible shared factor?
options: Accidents always cause ice-cream purchases
The two counts must be identical
Hot weather increases both activities
Ice cream necessarily causes accidents
questions.answer: Hot weather increases both activities
questions.explanation: A common seasonal factor can explain an association without direct causation.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A survey about all students asks only members of the football team. What is a concern?
options: Any sample gives exactly the same result
The sample may not represent all students
The sample automatically includes everyone
Team members cannot answer questions
questions.answer: The sample may not represent all students
questions.explanation: One subgroup may differ systematically from the wider student population.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A new poster is put up and attendance rises. What cannot be established from this alone?
options: That the poster caused the rise
That attendance rose
That a poster was put up
That the events occurred in that order
questions.answer: That the poster caused the rise
questions.explanation: Other factors could explain the increase, so timing alone does not establish causation.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: To check tomorrow's school opening time, which source is most directly relevant?
options: An old unrelated school's timetable
A visitor's guess
A map showing road colours
The school's current official notice
questions.answer: The school's current official notice
questions.explanation: A current notice from the responsible institution addresses the specific schedule.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Which claim can be checked by a clear observation?
options: This bottle has perfect beauty
Everyone should admire this bottle
This bottle holds more than one litre
This bottle is the best in every possible sense
questions.answer: This bottle holds more than one litre
questions.explanation: Capacity has an operational measurable criterion, unlike unrestricted subjective judgements.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A plant wilts after being moved. Which question best checks an alternative to 'moving caused damage'?
options: How many letters are in its label?
Did watering or light conditions also change?
What is the pot's nickname?
Who first used the word plant?
questions.answer: Did watering or light conditions also change?
questions.explanation: Changes in water or light provide plausible competing causes of wilting.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Which better supports a claim that a repair solved a recurring fault?
options: Repeated checks under the conditions that previously triggered it
A new sticker on the device
The repairer's confidence alone
A single unrelated photograph
questions.answer: Repeated checks under the conditions that previously triggered it
questions.explanation: Testing the relevant failure conditions gives direct evidence of improved functioning.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Which statement expresses a preference rather than a measured fact?
options: The box weighs two kilograms
The trip lasted thirty minutes
The room has four windows
I like the blue design more
questions.answer: I like the blue design more
questions.explanation: Liking one design is a personal evaluation, unlike the observable measurements and count.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two plans have the same benefit, but one has a lower chance of failure and no other disadvantage. Which better fits a reliability goal?
options: Both necessarily have identical reliability
The plan chosen at random must be safer
The lower-risk plan
The higher-risk plan
questions.answer: The lower-risk plan
questions.explanation: With other factors equal, a lower failure probability improves reliability.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A prediction is repeatedly contradicted by reliable observations. What is the most reasonable response?
options: Stop distinguishing predictions from evidence
Reconsider the prediction or its assumptions
Discard every observation automatically
Call the prediction proven
questions.answer: Reconsider the prediction or its assumptions
questions.explanation: Reliable contrary evidence is a reason to revise or investigate the underlying explanation.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A group of 30 averages 80 and a group of 10 averages 60. Why is the combined average closer to 80?
options: More observations come from the first group
Every group has equal weight regardless of size
Averages cannot be combined
The higher average always wins completely
questions.answer: More observations come from the first group
questions.explanation: The combined mean weights each group's mean by its number of observations.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A price is discounted by 20 percent, then a further 10 percent of the reduced price. What total discount results?
options: 30 percent
10 percent
32 percent
28 percent
questions.answer: 28 percent
questions.explanation: The retained fraction is 0.8 times 0.9, or 0.72 of the original.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A mixture has equal red and blue beads. Only red beads are added. What happens to the blue proportion?
options: It stays at one half
The blue count must decrease
It decreases although the blue count stays fixed
It increases because total count rises
questions.answer: It decreases although the blue count stays fixed
questions.explanation: A fixed blue count divided by a larger total gives a smaller proportion.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A machine's production rate doubles, but the required batch size also doubles. What happens to production time, ignoring setup?
options: It quadruples
It stays the same
It doubles
It halves
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.explanation: Time is quantity divided by rate, so doubling both leaves the ratio unchanged.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two trains move in the same direction at equal speeds. What happens to the distance between them if neither changes speed?
options: It stays constant
It increases at twice their speed
It decreases at their shared speed
It must become zero
questions.answer: It stays constant
questions.explanation: Their relative velocity is zero, so separation does not change.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A cyclist travels equal distances at a slow speed and a fast speed. Why is average speed below the simple mean of the speeds?
options: The distances cannot be equal
The fast segment contributes no distance
Average speed depends only on the fastest segment
More travel time is spent at the slower speed
questions.answer: More travel time is spent at the slower speed
questions.explanation: Equal-distance averaging weights the slower leg more heavily in time.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two salt solutions of concentrations 10 and 30 percent are mixed with no salt or water lost. Which concentration is impossible?
options: 20 percent
25 percent
40 percent
15 percent
questions.answer: 40 percent
questions.explanation: A mixture's concentration lies between those of its components.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A 50-unit voucher and a 10-percent discount apply separately to a 400-unit purchase. Which saves more?
options: Neither reduces the price
The voucher
The percentage discount
They save equal amounts
questions.answer: The voucher
questions.explanation: Ten percent of 400 is 40, which is less than the voucher's 50.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: All dimensions of a rectangular box are tripled. By what factor does its volume grow?
questions.explanation: Three independent length factors each triple, giving 3 cubed.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two services charge the same per-use amount but different joining fees. What stays constant as equal usage increases?
options: The ratio of their total charges
Their total charges
The lower fee becomes the higher fee
The difference in their total charges
questions.answer: The difference in their total charges
questions.explanation: The identical variable parts cancel when total charges are subtracted.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: The sum of two integers is odd. What must be true?
options: Both are even
One must be zero
One is odd and the other even
Both are odd
questions.answer: One is odd and the other even
questions.explanation: Equal parity gives an even sum; opposite parity gives an odd sum.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: An integer is divisible by both 3 and 4. What must divide it?
questions.explanation: Because 3 and 4 are coprime, their least common multiple is 12.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: An integer leaves remainder 2 when divided by 5. What remainder does adding 3 produce?
questions.explanation: Adding three completes the next multiple of five.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Three consecutive integers are added. Which of the following must be true?
options: Their sum is always odd
Their sum is always prime
Their sum is divisible by 4
Their sum is divisible by 3
questions.answer: Their sum is divisible by 3
questions.explanation: Writing them as n-1, n and n+1 gives a sum of 3n.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: For a positive proper fraction, the same positive amount is added to numerator and denominator. What happens to its value?
options: It becomes greater than one immediately
It remains exactly unchanged
It moves closer to one
It decreases toward zero
questions.answer: It moves closer to one
questions.explanation: The numerator's shortfall below the denominator stays fixed while the denominator grows.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A cost is just under 20 per item and 50 items are bought. Which is the best bound on the total?
options: Under 20
Just under 1,000
Just over 1,000
Exactly 500
questions.answer: Just under 1,000
questions.explanation: Fifty times a value just below twenty is just below one thousand.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: An amount has fallen to 80 percent of its original value. To restore the original, what percentage increase on the reduced amount is needed?
options: 25 percent
20 percent
10 percent
80 percent
questions.answer: 25 percent
questions.explanation: The missing 20 original units are one quarter of the remaining 80.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Both terms of a nonzero ratio are multiplied by the same positive number. What happens to the ratio?
options: It doubles regardless of multiplier
It becomes one
It reverses
It is unchanged
questions.answer: It is unchanged
questions.explanation: The common scale factor cancels in the quotient.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Four values have mean 10. A fifth value greater than 10 is added. What happens to the mean?
options: It becomes the added value
It decreases
It increases but remains below the added value
It stays at 10
questions.answer: It increases but remains below the added value
questions.explanation: A weighted average lies between the original mean and the new larger observation.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A total is split into two parts. Five is added to one part and five removed from the other. What remains unchanged?
options: Both individual parts
The total
The ratio in every case
The difference
questions.answer: The total
questions.explanation: Equal opposite changes cancel when the parts are added.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: All tutors are graduates, and no graduates are trainees. What follows?
options: No tutors are trainees
All trainees are tutors
Some tutors are trainees
All graduates are tutors
questions.answer: No tutors are trainees
questions.explanation: Tutors belong within the graduate group, which excludes trainees.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: If a file is encrypted, it asks for a key. This file asks for a key. What can be concluded?
options: It is certainly encrypted
It certainly is not encrypted
It cannot be opened under any circumstances
It may be encrypted, but the rule alone does not prove it
questions.answer: It may be encrypted, but the rule alone does not prove it
questions.explanation: Other kinds of files could also ask for a key; the converse is not given.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: At least one of A and B is true. A is false. What follows?
options: Both are false
Nothing at all follows about B
B is true
B is false
questions.answer: B is true
questions.explanation: The inclusive-or statement requires B when A is ruled out.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: All poets in a club are readers, and some readers are swimmers. Must any poet be a swimmer?
options: No poet can swim
No; the stated groups need not overlap that way
Yes; all poets must swim
Yes; exactly one poet swims
questions.answer: No; the stated groups need not overlap that way
questions.explanation: The swimming readers could all be outside the poet subgroup.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A rule says it is not true that neither option is available. What must be the case?
options: At least one option is available
Both options are unavailable
Exactly one option is available
Both options are available necessarily
questions.answer: At least one option is available
questions.explanation: Negating 'neither' yields an inclusive choice of one or both being available.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A device runs only if its safety latch is closed. It is running. What follows?
options: The latch is open
Every closed latch means the device runs
The device has no power supply
The latch is closed
questions.answer: The latch is closed
questions.explanation: A closed latch is necessary for running, so observed running implies that condition.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: All vehicles need permits except emergency vehicles. A vehicle has no permit. Can it be judged noncompliant without knowing its type?
options: No, because permits are never needed
Yes, unless it is red
No, because an exception may apply
Yes, every permitless vehicle violates the rule
questions.answer: No, because an exception may apply
questions.explanation: The type determines whether the vehicle belongs to the stated exception.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Which pair of statements cannot both hold for the same nonempty group?
options: One passed; another passed
All members passed; one member failed
Some passed; some failed
No member passed; all failed
questions.answer: All members passed; one member failed
questions.explanation: A failing member directly contradicts the claim that every member passed.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: All unicorns in a story are silver. Does this statement by itself prove the story contains a unicorn?
options: No
Yes, exactly one
Yes, at least two
Yes, infinitely many
questions.answer: No
questions.explanation: A universal conditional can hold even when its subject category is empty.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Exactly one of two switches is on. The first is on. What follows?
options: The second is on
The second has no state
Both must change immediately
The second is off
questions.answer: The second is off
questions.explanation: The exactly-one requirement excludes the second being on as well.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: P is ahead of Q, R is behind Q, and S is ahead of P. Who is first among these four?
options: Q
R
S
P
questions.answer: S
questions.explanation: The constraints give S before P before Q before R.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Four seats form a row. A occupies an end, and B sits immediately to A's right. Where must A sit?
options: Any seat
The left end
The right end
Either middle seat
questions.answer: The left end
questions.explanation: An immediate seat to the right exists for the left end but not the right end.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: X must precede Y, and Z must follow X but may precede Y. Which sequence is allowed?
options: X, Z, Y
Z, X, Y
Y, X, Z
Y, Z, X
questions.answer: X, Z, Y
questions.explanation: X first satisfies both dependencies, while Z before Y is permitted.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A 40-minute appointment begins at 10:20. The next begins at 11:00. What gap is there?
options: A 20-minute gap
A 40-minute overlap
A 10-minute gap
No gap and no overlap
questions.answer: No gap and no overlap
questions.explanation: The first appointment ends exactly when the next begins.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: An event occurs every seven days, beginning on a Thursday. On which weekday do later occurrences fall?
options: Wednesday
The weekday changes each week
Thursday
Friday
questions.answer: Thursday
questions.explanation: A seven-day interval is one full weekday cycle.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: One sibling is four years older than another. What happens to their age difference after ten years?
options: It doubles
It stays four years
It grows to fourteen years
It falls to zero
questions.answer: It stays four years
questions.explanation: Both ages increase by the same amount, preserving their difference.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Four people sit around a round table. Why can rotating the whole seating arrangement leave it equivalent when seats are unlabelled?
options: Relative neighbours remain the same
Everyone changes identity
Opposite pairs become adjacent
The number of people changes
questions.answer: Relative neighbours remain the same
questions.explanation: A common rotation preserves all relative positions when absolute seat labels do not matter.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: In a race with no ties, Ana is third from the front and fourth from the back. How many runners are there?
options: Seven
Five
Twelve
Six
questions.answer: Six
questions.explanation: Count the two runners ahead, Ana, and the three behind.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A single room hosts three one-hour sessions with no overlap and no breaks. What minimum room time is needed?
options: Two hours
Four hours
Three hours
One hour
questions.answer: Three hours
questions.explanation: A single room must host the sessions sequentially, so their durations add.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Tasks B and C can run together but both require A to finish first. Why does starting B earlier than A's finish fail?
options: All tasks must run alphabetically
It breaks B's prerequisite
Parallel tasks must always have equal duration
C must finish before A
questions.answer: It breaks B's prerequisite
questions.explanation: B cannot begin until its dependency A is complete.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A report says, 'The treatment helped some participants, but the sample was small.' What conclusion best respects both clauses?
options: The result is promising but limited in generalisability
The treatment helps everyone
The treatment never helps
The sample size proves the result is false
questions.answer: The result is promising but limited in generalisability
questions.explanation: The reported benefit is limited by the evidence's small scope.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A speaker gives a claim, a supporting example, then a warning about exceptions. What role does the warning play?
options: It supplies an unrelated definition
It proves the example never occurred
It removes the claim's subject
It limits the claim's scope
questions.answer: It limits the claim's scope
questions.explanation: An exception warning qualifies where the claim should be applied.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A school argues that extending library hours will increase access. Which assumption is most relevant?
options: Books must become shorter
All staff prefer mornings
Some students can use the additional hours
Every student owns a car
questions.answer: Some students can use the additional hours
questions.explanation: Extra hours increase usable access only if some intended users can attend then.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A claim says a clearer form reduces errors. Which finding strengthens it most?
options: The form uses more paper
Comparable users make fewer errors with the new form in a controlled trial
The new form has a fashionable colour
Its designer likes it
questions.answer: Comparable users make fewer errors with the new form in a controlled trial
questions.explanation: A controlled comparison of error rates directly tests the claimed effect.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A shop claims a promotion caused higher sales. Which finding weakens that interpretation?
options: Sales rose equally at comparable shops without the promotion
Customers noticed the promotion
The shop displayed new signs
The promotion happened before the increase
questions.answer: Sales rose equally at comparable shops without the promotion
questions.explanation: A similar increase without the intervention suggests another common explanation.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: No complaint was recorded. Why does this not prove every user was satisfied?
options: Every user must have complained secretly
Records always contain errors
Satisfaction cannot exist
Some dissatisfied users may not have complained
questions.answer: Some dissatisfied users may not have complained
questions.explanation: Lack of complaints does not capture unreported dissatisfaction.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A claim says a product is 'twice as effective' without naming an outcome. What is missing?
options: The number of words in the slogan
A guarantee that it is expensive
A defined measure of effectiveness
The product's colour only
questions.answer: A defined measure of effectiveness
questions.explanation: A numerical comparison needs an operational outcome and comparison basis.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Which preserves 'Applications received after Friday may not be considered'?
options: Only applications received on Friday are considered
Late applications risk being excluded
All late applications are definitely accepted
All applications are rejected on Friday
questions.answer: Late applications risk being excluded
questions.explanation: The original expresses a possibility of exclusion, not an absolute universal rule.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A record states that a door opened at noon. Which adds interpretation beyond the record?
options: Someone opened it to welcome a visitor
The door opened
The opening was at noon
The event was recorded
questions.answer: Someone opened it to welcome a visitor
questions.explanation: A purpose and visitor are not established merely by the observed opening.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A school is compared with a team to argue that cooperation matters. Why should the analogy be limited?
options: Analogies prove all properties identical
Teams cannot cooperate
Schools contain no groups
The two settings differ in goals and responsibilities
questions.answer: The two settings differ in goals and responsibilities
questions.explanation: Shared features can illuminate one point without transferring every characteristic.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A bar chart begins its vertical axis near the smallest value rather than zero. What risk arises?
options: The ordering must reverse
The totals necessarily double
Small differences may look exaggerated
All data values become zero
questions.answer: Small differences may look exaggerated
questions.explanation: Truncating a bar baseline can visually magnify relative height differences.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Most invited people ignore a survey, while highly dissatisfied users respond. What bias may result?
options: Nonrespondents are automatically neutral
Dissatisfaction is overrepresented
Satisfaction is necessarily overrepresented
The survey becomes a census
questions.answer: Dissatisfaction is overrepresented
questions.explanation: Response patterns related to the outcome can distort the sample's apparent distribution.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A club says female membership rose from 40 to 50 percent. What cannot be determined without total membership counts?
options: Whether the number of female members increased
Whether the share increased
Whether the old share was below half
Whether the new share is half
questions.answer: Whether the number of female members increased
questions.explanation: A higher proportion can accompany a smaller absolute number if the total falls enough.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A survey counts 20 people who swim and 15 who cycle, with some doing both. Why might adding 20 and 15 overcount distinct people?
options: Swimmers cannot cycle
Every cyclist is counted zero times
The survey must contain exactly 35 people
People in both groups are counted twice
questions.answer: People in both groups are counted twice
questions.explanation: Adding overlapping category totals repeats members in the intersection.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A data set's largest value becomes much larger, while order stays unchanged. Why can the median stay fixed?
options: The largest value is excluded from all statistics
The data set gains a new observation
Its central position is unchanged
The mean must also stay fixed
questions.answer: Its central position is unchanged
questions.explanation: Changing an extreme value without moving the central observations need not alter the median.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A chart shows total tickets sold up to each day. Why does a steeper section indicate stronger daily sales?
options: Earlier tickets are being counted negatively
The total is increasing faster there
The ticket price must be higher
The cumulative total is falling
questions.answer: The total is increasing faster there
questions.explanation: The slope of cumulative sales reflects the rate of new sales.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two random samples from the same population give slightly different averages. What is a reasonable explanation?
options: Random sampling variation
The population must have changed completely
One sample is necessarily fabricated
Averages cannot be measured
questions.answer: Random sampling variation
questions.explanation: Different randomly selected members can yield different estimates even from the same population.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Town A has more cases than town B but a much larger population. What is needed for a fair incidence comparison?
options: Only total cases
Town names
The number of streets alone
Cases relative to population over the same period
questions.answer: Cases relative to population over the same period
questions.explanation: A comparable incidence rate uses population and a common time frame.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: An advert says '90 percent improved' but gives no sample size. Why does sample size matter?
options: A sample size determines everyone's individual result
Ninety percent always means ninety people
It affects how much evidence the percentage represents
Percentages are invalid for all small groups
questions.answer: It affects how much evidence the percentage represents
questions.explanation: The same percentage may summarize very different amounts of evidence.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A machine's output doubled once after a repair. Why is predicting repeated doubling every week unjustified?
options: A weekly forecast must always be linear
One change does not establish a continuing growth rule
Repairs can never increase output
Doubling is mathematically impossible
questions.answer: One change does not establish a continuing growth rule
questions.explanation: A one-time intervention does not demonstrate an ongoing exponential process.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: You face east, turn left, then make a half-turn. Which way do you face?
options: South
North
East
West
questions.answer: South
questions.explanation: The left turn faces north, and the half-turn then faces south.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A person completes one full lap of a circular track. What is zero?
options: Distance travelled
Time taken necessarily
Average speed
Net displacement
questions.answer: Net displacement
questions.explanation: Returning to the start gives zero displacement despite positive distance travelled.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A shape is reflected twice across the same mirror line. What is the final result?
options: A larger shape
A shift parallel to the mirror
The original position and orientation
A quarter-turn
questions.answer: The original position and orientation
questions.explanation: A reflection is its own inverse, so applying it twice restores the original.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: On a cube, face A is opposite B. Can A and B share an edge?
options: Only when viewed from above
No
Yes, always
Only if the cube is rotated
questions.answer: No
questions.explanation: Opposite cube faces are separated and do not meet along an edge.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two squares in a cube net fold onto the same face position. What does this imply?
options: The arrangement is not a valid nonoverlapping cube net
The cube gains a seventh face
Every net behaves this way
The squares become triangles
questions.answer: The arrangement is not a valid nonoverlapping cube net
questions.explanation: A valid cube net must cover each face once without overlapping.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two differently shaped objects cast the same silhouette from one direction. What follows?
options: The objects must be identical
Their volumes must match
All their other views must match
That one view is insufficient to distinguish their full shapes
questions.answer: That one view is insufficient to distinguish their full shapes
questions.explanation: Projection loses depth information, so different three-dimensional objects can share one silhouette.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A floor is covered with identical square tiles without gaps. One tile is removed. What shape is the uncovered region?
options: A triangle
The whole floor
A square of one tile's area
A circle
questions.answer: A square of one tile's area
questions.explanation: Removing one tile exposes exactly the region it occupied.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A non-square rectangle is reflected across a diagonal. Why does it not generally map onto itself?
options: Reflection changes all angles
The unequal side lengths are exchanged
All rectangles lack any symmetry
The diagonal is outside the rectangle
questions.answer: The unequal side lengths are exchanged
questions.explanation: Diagonal reflection would interchange unequal dimensions, unlike a square.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A right circular cylinder is sliced parallel to its circular base. What is the section?
options: A circle
A triangle
A parabola
A single point in every interior slice
questions.answer: A circle
questions.explanation: A plane parallel to the base cuts the cylinder in a congruent circular section.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: On a rectangular street grid, two shortest routes connect the same corners using only east and north steps. Why can their lengths match despite different turns?
options: Turns add no time in any transport system
They must visit every same street
Their endpoints are irrelevant
They use the same total eastward and northward distances
questions.answer: They use the same total eastward and northward distances
questions.explanation: For monotone shortest grid routes, total horizontal and vertical distances are fixed.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A rule alternates adding two and doubling. Starting with 3 gives 3, 5, 10, 12. What follows?
questions.explanation: After adding two to ten, the next prescribed operation is doubling twelve.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A sequence of arrows rotates clockwise by a quarter-turn each step. After four steps, how does an arrow compare with its start?
options: It points one quarter-turn left
It points in the original direction
It points opposite
It is reflected
questions.answer: It points in the original direction
questions.explanation: Four quarter-turns make a complete rotation.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A process transfers one counter from box A to box B each turn. Which quantity is invariant?
options: The total in both boxes
The number in A
The number in B
The difference between their counts
questions.answer: The total in both boxes
questions.explanation: Each transfer subtracts one from one box and adds one to the other.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A code writes each word backward. A coded word is LEVEL. What was the original?
options: LEVER
VELLE
EVELL
LEVEL
questions.answer: LEVEL
questions.explanation: LEVEL is a palindrome, so reversing it leaves it unchanged.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A substitution code always maps the same letter to the same symbol. A word has its first and third letters equal. What must be true of its code?
options: The second and fourth symbols match necessarily
The code has fewer symbols than letters
The first and third symbols match
Every symbol matches
questions.answer: The first and third symbols match
questions.explanation: A consistent letter substitution preserves repeated-letter positions.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: The terms 2, 4, 8 fit doubling, but the next observed term is 14. What should happen to the doubling hypothesis?
options: The fourth term should be ignored automatically
It should be rejected for the full observed sequence
It is proven by the first three terms
Fourteen must be renamed sixteen
questions.answer: It should be rejected for the full observed sequence
questions.explanation: The new term contradicts the predicted doubling continuation.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Each new term is the sum of the preceding two. The latest terms are 5 and 8. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The stated recurrence adds the two latest terms.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A custom operation a star b means a plus twice b. Why need swapping a and b change the result?
options: Every custom operation is commutative
The symbols cannot represent numbers
The result must always be zero
The two positions have different weights
questions.answer: The two positions have different weights
questions.explanation: The second input is doubled, so exchanging unequal inputs generally changes the result.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Numbers are grouped by remainder when divided by three. Which belongs with 1, 4 and 7?
questions.explanation: All members of the group leave remainder one on division by three.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A proposed rule says doubling any positive integer produces a number ending in zero. Which input disproves it?
questions.explanation: Doubling three gives six, which does not end in zero.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: One task takes six hours. Two prerequisite-free tasks of two hours each can run alongside it. What is the shortest total duration with enough workers?
options: Six hours
Ten hours
Four hours
Two hours
questions.answer: Six hours
questions.explanation: Parallel scheduling cannot finish before the longest independent task, and all shorter tasks fit within it.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A bus has 40 seats and makes two trips, with no standing allowed. What maximum number of one-trip passengers can it carry?
questions.explanation: Each trip supplies forty seats, so two trips supply eighty passenger places.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A plan must cost at most 100 and finish within two days. Plan X costs 90 but needs three days. What follows?
options: It is automatically the best plan
The time limit becomes three days
It fails one mandatory constraint
It qualifies because it is cheap
questions.answer: It fails one mandatory constraint
questions.explanation: Meeting the budget does not compensate for violating a mandatory deadline.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two independent power supplies can each run a device alone. Why can using both as backups improve reliability?
options: Both must fail whenever one fails
Either can maintain operation if the other fails
Their failures become impossible
The device uses no energy
questions.answer: Either can maintain operation if the other fails
questions.explanation: Redundancy allows continued operation after a single-source failure, subject to independence and switching assumptions.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A game offers a small chance of a large prize. Why can that chance alone not establish that playing has positive expected value?
options: Prize size, probability and cost all matter
Large prizes always make games profitable
Costs do not affect expected value
The chance of winning must be one
questions.answer: Prize size, probability and cost all matter
questions.explanation: Expected net value weights outcomes by probabilities and subtracts the cost.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A nonrefundable fee has already been paid for a project. When comparing future options, why may that fee be excluded from their difference?
options: Past costs were never real
Every paid project must continue
Future costs are always zero
It is the same unavoidable past cost for both options
questions.answer: It is the same unavoidable past cost for both options
questions.explanation: A sunk cost cannot be changed by the current choice, so it does not distinguish future alternatives.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A student chooses one of two simultaneous workshops. What is an opportunity cost of the choice?
options: Only the chosen room's temperature
The cost of an unrelated past event
The benefit of the workshop forgone
The benefits of both workshops added
questions.answer: The benefit of the workshop forgone
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative given up.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two plans have similar expected results, but one fails badly under a plausible delay while the other still works. Which is more robust to that delay?
options: Neither can be compared without changing the delay
The second plan
The first plan
Both are equally robust by definition
questions.answer: The second plan
questions.explanation: Robustness concerns maintaining acceptable performance when conditions vary.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: You can buy a measurement before choosing a box size. When is it most useful?
options: When it may change the choice and avoid a costly mismatch
When it cannot affect any decision
When the choice is already irreversible
When the measurement is unrelated to size
questions.answer: When it may change the choice and avoid a costly mismatch
questions.explanation: Information has decision value when it can improve the selected action.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two teaching methods are compared using classes that differed greatly before teaching began. What complicates the comparison?
options: Only the method can explain any difference
The methods must be identical
Learning cannot be observed
Initial differences may explain later outcomes
questions.answer: Initial differences may explain later outcomes
questions.explanation: Pre-existing group differences can confound the apparent effect of the teaching method.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: People who exercise more also report better sleep. Why is a causal conclusion uncertain from an observational survey alone?
options: All surveys are fabricated
Two variables can never be related
Other factors may influence both exercise and sleep
Exercise cannot affect sleep
questions.answer: Other factors may influence both exercise and sleep
questions.explanation: An association may reflect confounders or reverse causation rather than the proposed direction alone.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A review site shows only comments from buyers who chose to post. What limitation follows?
options: The product has no users
The comments may not represent all buyers
Every buyer posted
All comments must be false
questions.answer: The comments may not represent all buyers
questions.explanation: Self-selection may overrepresent especially motivated or extreme experiences.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A participant is selected after an unusually poor performance and later improves. Why need the intervention not explain all improvement?
options: An extreme result may partly reflect temporary variation
Improvement proves the intervention failed
Scores can never vary naturally
The second result is necessarily false
questions.answer: An extreme result may partly reflect temporary variation
questions.explanation: Extreme observations often move closer to typical performance on repeat measurement even without an intervention.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: An argument says online registration will reduce queues. Which assumption is required for the proposed mechanism?
options: Every visitor has the same phone
The event has no staff
Printed tickets are impossible
Enough visitors will use it before arriving
questions.answer: Enough visitors will use it before arriving
questions.explanation: Queue reduction through advance registration requires meaningful uptake of the advance process.

questions.subject: Aptitude
